confirmed.title: Happening-now progress bar still refills from empty whenever the rain hint changes
confirmed.symptom: On days with a rain forecast of 40% or more in the next 3 hours, the 'Happening now' bar blanks and refills from 0 mid-block. This is the same 'progress bar keeps reloading' glitch the owner reported. It happens at each hour rollover and after each weather refresh that changes the percentage. It also happens when the hint appears or disappears, and once at page load when the weather arrives after the first paint.
confirmed.trigger: Senior: ?now=1-1950 (Evening worship 7:15-8:30). Inject weatherData with precip 60 at hours 20 and 21 and step the minute 19:50 to 20:10: at 20:00 the hint text changes 'near 8pm' to 'this hour' and the bar is a new element. In the same setup, calling repaintWeather() with a changed % or with the rain cleared also swaps the bar. Junior: Sunday 'Registration 2:00-4:00pm' at 3:00 behaves the same. Repro: node p15_rain.cjs senior.
confirmed.evidence: p15_rain.cjs senior: 'BAR RE-CREATED (refills from 0)' with hint '60% chance of rain near 8pm -> 60% chance of rain this hour' at minute 1200. 'weather refresh changed rain % 50->70' gave barRecreated:true, and 'rain hint disappears' gave barRecreated:true. A fresh jelly-progress keeps changing pixels for more than 40 frames (p9_connect.cjs, 40 distinct canvas states), so every re-creation shows a fill animation of about 0.7 s or longer. Junior reproduced the hour-rollover case (minute 900, 'Registration').
confirmed.rootCause: renderNowBanner's shape check (app.js:825) strips only the bar's value attribute. nowBannerHtml (app.js:755-760) places upcomingRainHint() inside the same markup string, so any change to the hint text changes the shape. The early return is skipped and setHtmlIfChanged rebuilds the whole banner, including a new jelly-progress. The same path also fires when mealCleanupNote text changes, for example a remote team rename. The bar is also absent while a live Big Board hides the banner (app.js:813-817 clears innerHTML), so it fills from 0 again after every live game or game-view toggle.
confirmed.proposedFix:
Make the bar a persistent node that is never part of the replaced markup. Either (a) strip the `
...
` from `shape` and patch `.now-wx` in place on the early-return path, or (b) split the banner into stable children (eyebrow, body, bar) and update only the changed pieces. For the live-board case, set `el.hidden = true` and keep the children instead of `innerHTML = ''`, so the bar does not refill from 0 when a live game ends.

verdict.location: app.js:808-834 (renderNowBanner, shape at 825); app.js:743-760 (nowBannerHtml main()); app.js:515-529 (upcomingRainHint)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced twice. (1) Their p15_rain.cjs senior prints BAR RE-CREATED at minute 1200 ('near 8pm' -> 'this hour'), and again for a weather refresh that changes the percentage and for the hint disappearing. (2) My own probe (hunt/home-live-verify/v1_rain.cjs): bar settled at shownFrac 0.59, then renderAll() at 20:00 made a new element whose shownFrac was 0.024, 0.109, 0.183 ... 0.59 over about 25 frames (~0.4 s). So a visible empty-to-full sweep, the exact glitch the owner reported. The control (idle renderAll, same hint) kept the bar. v1b_rain_cases.cjs on the live build: rain appears, % changes, rain moves later and rain clears all gave barKept:false for the senior-worship layout and the junior elective layout. The slim competitions layout has no bar, so it is unaffected. Root cause is right: the shape check strips only value=, and the hint lives inside the same markup string. It only fires on days with a forecast of 40% or more (WEATHER_RAIN_MIN) within three hours, at hour rollovers and 30-min weather refreshes that change the %, so rain days only. The claim that the bar refills after a live Big Board hides the banner is a banner re-appearing, which is natural and not worth fixing.

confirmed.title: Big Board loses its final-minute and final-ten red clock, heartbeat and glow on every renderAll
confirmed.symptom: In the last 10 seconds of a live game, any incoming snapshot (a goal, another editor's save, an announcement) turns the red heartbeat clock back to normal text colour and switches the board glow off. It stays that way for up to 500 ms, then jumps back with the heartbeat and glow restarted from phase 0. The last-minute amber pulse is restarted the same way. Visible on the home Big Board for viewers and editors.
confirmed.trigger: Junior: a live-tracker game (jeb-ball) or a tally game with a clock (counselor-hide-seek) with a running clock inside its last 10 s. Call renderAll() with any real change. Repro: node p22_final10.cjs light (and dark), or p2_live.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: p22_final10.cjs: steady state has clock colour oklch(0.577 0.215 27) (red), animation clock-heartbeat, board animation board-glow. Right after renderAll: colour oklch(0.26 ...) (default text), clock animation none, board animation none. This is unchanged at +250 ms and restored at +650 ms. Dark scheme is the same (colour flips to oklch(0.96 ...)). p2_live.cjs C and D show clsImmediately = 'board-clock | big-board viewer' with no clock-final-ten or board-final-ten classes, and sameBoard:false.
confirmed.rootCause: renderLiveHome rewrites the whole board with innerHTML (app.js:5688). liveTrackerHTML and tallyBoardHTML emit only `board-clock-zero` in markup. `clock-final-min`, `clock-final-ten` and `board-final-ten` are applied only by tickBoardClocks (app.js:3529-3533), which runs every 500 ms. So a freshly rebuilt board is missing them until the next tick. The new nodes also restart their CSS animations from 0.
confirmed.location: app.js:5664-5751 (renderLiveHome), app.js:5776 (tallyBoardHTML), app.js:6635 (liveTrackerHTML), app.js:3511-3535 (tickBoardClocks); same pattern wherever the board is rebuilt in the game view
confirmed.proposedFix: Factor the class logic out of tickBoardClocks into one helper, for example `clockStateClasses(clock, rem)`, and call it both when building the markup and in the tick. A rebuilt board is then born in its final state. Better still, avoid rebuilding the board when only unrelated state changed: wrap the innerHTML in setHtmlIfChanged keyed on the markup with the clock text and state classes excluded, so the animation phase survives.

verdict.location: app.js:3511-3535 (tickBoardClocks), app.js:5688 (renderLiveHome), liveTrackerHTML ~6670, tallyBoardHTML ~5790, game-view clock box app.js:6504 and 6736
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. p22_final10.cjs light: steady state is colour oklch(0.577 0.215 27) with clock-heartbeat and board-glow. Right after renderAll it is the default text colour with animation none, still unchanged at +250 ms, and restored by +650 ms. My own v2_final10.cjs gave the same for viewer and editor on the home Big Board. It also reproduces in the game view's clock box (gv_after_sync cls 'board-clock' with anim none, restored at +250 ms). Cause is as stated: markup carries only board-clock-zero, and clock-final-min, clock-final-ten and board-final-ten are added only by the 500 ms tick. renderAll runs only on real synced changes, because echo snapshots are skipped in applyRemoteState, so a score tap inside the last 10 s of a clocked game is needed. That is why I rate it low, not med: a brief flicker (0 to 500 ms, mean 250 ms) at a high-attention moment but a rare coincidence.

confirmed.title: Live-now card's red pulse ring restarts on every renderAll
confirmed.symptom: The 2 s ring around a 'LIVE' card is cut off and restarts each time any snapshot lands. During active scoring (an editor tapping every few seconds) the ring never completes its cycle and looks like it is twitching.
confirmed.trigger: Junior: start a bracket on a game without liveTracker (ladder-ball), or have a second live game. Call renderAll(). A live-tracker game on its own is shown as a Big Board, not a card. Repro: node p2_live.cjs viewer junior light (A and B) and p20_ring.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: p2_live A: sameNode:false, pulse currentTime 2000 ms before and 17 ms after. B: sampled 0-16 ms after each renderAll, 400 ms apart, the phase is [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] where a steady ring would read 400, 800, 1200 and so on. p20_ring.cjs: box-shadow spread 5.26 px at alpha 0.11 just before, then 0 px at alpha 0.45 in the same frame after renderAll, so the ring snaps away.
confirmed.rootCause: renderLiveHome does `wrap.innerHTML = boardHTML + games.map(...)` unconditionally (app.js:5688). Each .live-home-card button is re-created, which restarts its `animation: live-pulse 2s infinite`. setHtmlIfChanged (v183) is not used here.
confirmed.proposedFix: Build the markup string first and write it with setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html), wiring listeners only when it returns true. For the board, exclude the ticking clock text from the compared string (or patch it in place) so a clock tick does not count as a change. Shares one fix with the lost-tap and cannon findings.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. p2_live.cjs A: sameNode:false, pulse currentTime 2017 ms before and 17 ms after. B: phase [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] sampled after each renderAll, where a steady ring would read 400, 800, 1200 and so on. p20_ring.cjs: box-shadow spread 5.4 px at alpha 0.10 before, 0 px at alpha 0.45 in the same frame after the render. The keyframe is a 2 s infinite ring that is invisible from 70% to 100%, so the effect is an irregular ring that restarts on every real change, not a flash. Subtle but real, and it shares one root cause with the cannon, press and final-ten findings.

confirmed.title: Tapping a Live-now card or home Big Board does nothing if a snapshot lands during the press
confirmed.symptom: A spectator taps the live card or board to open the game. If any renderAll runs between pointerdown and pointerup, nothing opens. The tap is silently dropped.
confirmed.trigger: Junior with a live ladder-ball card (or a kickball Big Board). Hold the pointer down, call renderAll() (any remote snapshot), release. Repro: node p14_press.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: p14_press.cjs: card: control tap opens game 'ladder-ball'; tap with renderAll between down and up leaves state.ui.gameId = null. Board: control opens 'kangaroo-kickball'; with a snapshot between down and up, null. The tap fails because the pressed element is replaced.
confirmed.rootCause: Same unconditional innerHTML rebuild in renderLiveHome (app.js:5688). The element that received pointerdown is detached before pointerup, so no click is dispatched. A press lasts about 100 ms and snapshots arrive every few seconds during live scoring, so only a small share of taps are lost.
confirmed.proposedFix: Same fix as the pulse-restart finding: setHtmlIfChanged or in-place patching so unchanged live cards keep their nodes. Alternatively use one delegated click handler on the stable #live-home wrapper instead of per-node listeners.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced for a mouse, and NOT for touch, so this is overstated for a phone app. My v3_press_touch.cjs (stable card position, scrolled into view) on the live build: mouse with renderAll between down and up gives null for both the card and the board, while the control opens the game. Touch via CDP touchStart, renderAll, touchEnd opens the game for both, because Chromium hit-tests the tap gesture at tap time and hits the new node. WebKit also synthesizes the click from the tap point at tap time. So phones are not affected, only desktop or laptop mouse users with a roughly 100 ms press window. Their p14 harness is unreliable: on the patched build it still prints null because the card has drifted after the earlier smooth scrollIntoView. My probe, with a stable layout, passes on the patched build. The proposed alternative fix, a delegated listener on #live-home, does not work: with the mousedown node detached, Chromium dispatches no click at all (a document-level capture listener saw nothing).
verdict.refinedFix: The only working fix is not replacing unchanged nodes, which is the same renderLiveHome change as livehome-card-pulse-restart (liveKey skip). Verified in a scratch copy: with that change the mouse tap with a snapshot between down and up opens the game for both the card and the board. Drop the delegated-listener alternative. A real score change mid-press will still replace the node, which is inherent and negligible.

confirmed.title: Goal emoji cannons and the score pop are wiped by the next renderAll
confirmed.symptom: On the home Big Board, the 24-emoji cannon volley (1-1.8 s) and the score-pop vanish instantly if any other snapshot or tick-driven render arrives within about 2 s of the goal.
confirmed.trigger: Junior kickball board on the home screen. Raise a team's hr in state.live and call renderAll(), then call renderAll() again 0.4 s later. Repro: node p10_cannon.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: p10_cannon.cjs: cannonsAtGoal 24 and scorePopAtGoal 1. After 400 ms, still 24. After the next renderAll, cannonsAfterNextRender 0 and scorePopAfterNextRender 0.
confirmed.rootCause: boardCelebrate appends the cannon spans to the .big-board element itself and removes them with a 2100 ms timer (app.js:6587-6620). renderLiveHome replaces that element on every render, taking the particles and the .score-pop class with it.
confirmed.proposedFix: Stop rebuilding the board when nothing about it changed (same fix as the pulse finding). Also host the cannons in a persistent overlay (a sibling of the board inside #live-home, or #joy-layer positioned from the board's rect) so a rebuild cannot erase them.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with p10_cannon.cjs on the live build: cannonsAtGoal 24 and scorePopAtGoal 1, 24 still at +400 ms, then cannonsAfterNextRender 0 and scorePopAfterNextRender 0 after an unrelated renderAll. The cannons are children of the .big-board that renderLiveHome replaces. It needs another real change within about 2 s of a goal, for example the next tap, an inning change or an announcement. Rare, so low.
verdict.refinedFix: Same renderLiveHome liveKey skip as livehome-card-pulse-restart. Tested: cannonsAfterNextRender 24 and scorePopAfterNextRender 1 on the patched build. Do not move the cannons into an overlay: they live inside .big-board, which is overflow:hidden, so an overlay would change how they are clipped. A real score change in the markup still rebuilds the board and clears in-flight cannons, which is acceptable.

confirmed.title: Sparkle burst fires on editor devices when a game clock hits zero, with no user action
confirmed.symptom: When a synced game clock expires (the alarm sounds), every editor device throws a 16-particle 'big' sparkle burst from wherever the last tap was, or from screen centre if there was none. It is a celebration with no save behind it. Viewers see nothing.
confirmed.trigger: Editor device with a running synced clock reaching 0:00. In no-sync mode set window.FIREBASE_CONFIG = {} so settleExpiredClocks may write. Repro: node p6_joy.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: p6_joy.cjs: editor: particles before expiry 0, peak 16 within about 2.6 s, lastTap {x:null,y:null} (centre of screen), clock.running false afterwards. Viewer: peak 0.
confirmed.rootCause: tickBoardClocks calls settleExpiredClocks (app.js:3482), which runs setClock (app.js:6425). setClock calls touchData (app.js:2075), which calls joyCelebrate (app.js:2079 and 8078). joyCelebrate has no check that the write came from a user gesture. Every editor device settles the clock, so each one bursts.
confirmed.proposedFix: Let joyCelebrate fire only when a pointer or keyboard event happened in the last ~1.5 s. Record the time in the existing pointerdown handler, which already tracks joyLastTap. That also protects any future automated writes. Alternatively give settleExpiredClocks a quiet write path that skips touchData's celebration.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with p6_joy.cjs on the live build: the editor peaks at 16 joy particles within about 2.6 s of expiry with no tap, and the viewer sees 0. The chain is as stated: settleExpiredClocks, setClock, touchData, joyCelebrate, joyBurst(joyLastTap). In production the burst starts at the last pointer position (likely the Start button), not the screen centre as in the headless run. Every editor device with the app open does the same. Cosmetic, editors only. It also stamps 'Data last updated', but that is out of scope here.

confirmed.title: Toasts stack without limit and can cover most of the screen
confirmed.symptom: One remote snapshot that moves several teams' points produces one toast per team, all at once, for 4-5.5 s each. Nine toasts filled a 598 px column of an 844 px phone. The toasts take taps (pointer-events:auto), and the first one sits directly over the 'tap to refresh' update bar.
confirmed.trigger: Any phone with notifications on. Following a team turns that on automatically (enableNotify in the team picker). Then receive a remote snapshot that changes several teams: a placement save moves 3 teams, a new-week reset or restore moves all 6, and waking a phone after a long sleep replays the catch-up. Repro: node p7_toast.cjs light, and node p19_overlap.cjs for the update banner.
confirmed.evidence: p7_toast.cjs: n = 9 toasts, rail top 228 to bottom 826 (598 px of an 844 px viewport), 2 still visible at about 4.6 s. p19_overlap.cjs: with the update banner at y 748-828, the bottom toast at y 747-826 spans the same x range, so toastOverlapsUpdateBanner is true for that toast.
confirmed.rootCause: notifyPointChanges (app.js:3272-3285) calls showToast once per changed team with no coalescing. jelly-toaster has no cap (vendor/jelly.js:1262 push appends). The toaster and the update bar share the same bottom-right corner (toaster z-index 10002, update bar z-index 60).
confirmed.location: app.js:3272-3296 (notifyPointChanges, notifyMatchupChanges), app.js:3198 (showToast), vendor/jelly.js ~1262 (jelly-toaster push), styles.css:4258 (.update-banner)
confirmed.proposedFix: Coalesce each snapshot's point alerts into one toast, for example '+5 Maples, +4 Turkey, +3 Foxes', and keep the 'Your team' toast separate. Cap visible toasts at about 3 by removing the oldest in showToast. Lift the toaster above the update bar, or hide the bar while toasts show.

verdict.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed, but the headline is overstated. p7_toast.cjs reproduces 9 toasts and 598 px of an 844 px viewport, but that needs all 6 teams changing (new-week reset or restore) plus the 'Following' toast and two manual toasts. My v6_toast.cjs with a realistic placement-style save moving 3 teams gives 3 toasts at 172 px (20% of the viewport), each lasting 4 to 5.5 s. p19_overlap.cjs confirms that the bottom toast (y 747-826) sits over the update bar (y 748-828), but both being up at once is rare. Stacking is uncapped and uncoalesced, so it is worth a small fix, at low severity.
verdict.refinedFix: In notifyPointChanges, show one toast for all non-mine changes and keep 'Your team scored!' separate, for example `📈 🍁 Maples +5 · 🦃 Turkey +4 · 🦊 Foxes +3`. Keep the per-team maybeNativeNotification for mine. Cap visible toasts at about 3 in showToast. Raise the toaster clear of the update bar, or hide the bar while toasts are up. Do this together with the esc() removal in toast-double-escaped-text, so the coalesced text is not double-escaped. Risk: joining team names makes one long toast, so check the wrapping on a 320 px phone.

confirmed.title: Toasts and OS notifications show ''' and '&' for names with apostrophes or ampersands
confirmed.symptom: A team or game name with an apostrophe or ampersand reads wrongly in point and 'up next' toasts and OS notifications, for example "Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts".
confirmed.trigger: Rename a team to "Pete's Pandas & Co" or have a game named "Let's Go". Fire notifyPointChanges or notifyMatchupChanges. Repro: node p13_esc.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: p13_esc.cjs toast texts: "🦃 Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts (now 12)" and "Up next: 🦃 Pete's Pandas & Co vs 🍁 Methodic Mediocre Maples — Let's Go <Ball>". Current default junior team names have no special characters, so it appears only after a rename or a game name that contains an apostrophe or ampersand.
confirmed.rootCause: msg is built with esc(team.name) and esc(game.name) (app.js:3277 and 3292), but it is passed to showToast and maybeNativeNotification. Both are text sinks (jellyToast uses textContent; showNotification takes plain text), so the HTML escaping is displayed literally.
confirmed.proposedFix: Drop esc() when building toast and notification text. Escape only where markup is actually generated.

verdict.location: app.js:3279 and app.js:3293 (esc() inside toast and notification text)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with p13_esc.cjs on the live build: toast text reads "Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts" and "Let's Go <Ball>". jellyToast sets textContent, the legacy #toast-container fallback also uses textContent, and showNotification takes plain text, so every sink is a text sink and esc() is wrong. None of the current default names contain ' or &. The only default with an apostrophe is senior 'Let's Make a Deal', a placement game that never reaches notifyMatchupChanges. So it only shows after an editor renames a team or game. Hence visibleToUsers false for the default data.
verdict.refinedFix: Remove the three esc() calls: `${team.name}` at 3279, and `${teamName(aId)}`, `${teamName(bId)}` and `${game.name}` at 3293. Tested in a scratch copy: toast text is "Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts" and "Let's Go <Ball>". No markup is generated from those strings, so nothing becomes an injection path. grep showed these are the only two esc() uses feeding showToast or maybeNativeNotification.

confirmed.title: Notice board, My electives, standings rows and catch-up hint are rebuilt on every renderAll and 30 s tick, dropping selection
confirmed.symptom: Text a counselor has selected in the notice board (for example the cleanup assignments) is deselected within 30 s or on the next snapshot. The same holds for text selected in the My electives card and the standings rows. No animation or scroll jump results; scroll position was stable in tests.
confirmed.trigger: Posted notice, then select text and call renderAll() or the tick set. Repro: node p18_scroll.cjs (selection) and node p1_census.cjs (mutation census).
confirmed.evidence: p18_scroll.cjs: selection 'Where your team cleans' before, '' after renderAll. Scroll Y was unchanged (135 to 135 and 2157 to 2157). p1_census.cjs: #notice-board adds and removes a div.notice-card on every renderAll and every tick. #my-electives-card is rebuilt on every renderAll and tick. #standings-tbody is fully rebuilt on every renderAll. No new animations were created in any idle scenario. Rebuilds of the standings table, #catchup-hint and My electives under idle renderAll with a card open created no animations (p4_cards.cjs).
confirmed.rootCause: renderNoticeBoard (app.js:690-691) and renderMyElectives (app.js:4618-4630) assign innerHTML unconditionally. renderStandings (app.js:4296-4333) clears tbody and re-creates every row each time. These were not moved to setHtmlIfChanged in v183.
confirmed.proposedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged for the notice board and My electives. For standings, rebuild a row only when its row HTML or its pulse flag changed, or skip the whole tbody write when nothing changed (the points-pulse logic needs the fresh rows only when a pulse is due).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. p18_scroll.cjs: selecting the notice-card text and calling renderAll leaves an empty selection. p1_census.cjs editor: #notice-board, #my-electives-card, #standings-tbody and #catchup-hint are rebuilt on every renderAll, and notice-board and my-electives also on the 30 s tick. No new animations are created and no jelly nodes are involved (notice-card has no entrance animation; chips and buttons paint on frame 0 in p9). Scroll is stable. So the only effect is that text a counselor has selected or is long-pressing is dropped. Plain-text nodes, as the task brief already judged, but the selection loss is real. Low.
verdict.refinedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged in renderNoticeBoard (`setHtmlIfChanged(el, html || '')`) and renderMyElectives (build the template string, then `setHtmlIfChanged(card, ...)`). Tested in a scratch copy: all 436 tests pass, the selection survives renderAll, and idle renders create no nodes. Neither container holds inputs or jelly components, so there is no typed-value or toggled-attribute risk. For standings, build each row as a string (the className and pulse logic is already per-row), `setHtmlIfChanged(tbody, rowsHtml)`, and keep the changedTeams and lastPointsByTeam bookkeeping outside it. See the extra finding about points-pulse: a pulse row's markup differs from the next idle render, so that render still rewrites it.

confirmed.title: A remote announcement moves the caret to the end of the editor's half-typed announcement
confirmed.symptom: An editor typing in the announcement composer, with the caret mid-text, has the caret jump to the end when another announcement arrives. The text and focus are kept.
confirmed.trigger: Editor opens the composer, types text and places the caret at position 7, then a remote announcement arrives (renderAnnouncements with new content). Repro: node p12_misc.cjs editor junior.
confirmed.evidence: p12_misc.cjs: input was re-created (sameInput:false), focusAfter:true, value preserved, caret [19,19] after being [7,7] before.
confirmed.rootCause: renderAnnouncements rebuilds the markup and restores value and focus, but not selectionStart or selectionEnd (app.js:7546-7556). It also calls focus(), which on iOS can reopen the keyboard or scroll.
confirmed.proposedFix: Save and restore selectionStart and selectionEnd. Better, insert the new banner nodes before the composer and leave the composer element untouched when only the banners changed.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v12_caret.cjs, live build). Caret at 7 in 'Dinner is at six pm tonight' goes to 27 after a remote announcement arrives; value and focus are kept. I also measured a second, related case: with the composer focused but EMPTY, focus is dropped after a remote announcement (`if (newInput && draft)` gates the focus() call too), which on a phone dismisses the keyboard. Editors only, and only while the composer is open when someone else posts.

confirmed.title: Schedule sheet rows re-run their rise-in if a snapshot or tick lands within 0.9 s of a day-chip tap
confirmed.symptom: After tapping a day chip in the open Full-schedule sheet, a renderAll or 30 s tick that lands during the 900 ms stagger window makes the heading, timeline and calendar button re-run joy-rise from invisible. Rare and brief.
confirmed.trigger: Open the schedule sheet, tap a day chip, then call renderAll() 350 ms later. Repro: node p12_misc.cjs (schedule-sheet section).
confirmed.evidence: p12_misc.cjs: joyRiseRunningAt350ms 3, joyRiseREPLAYEDbySyncInWindow 3. In the same run, an idle renderAll with no tap created no animations, and scroll position stayed correct. p12b_sched.cjs and p12c_sched.cjs: scrollTop stayed at 400 or 500 through renderAll, refreshOpenSchedule and the real 30 s interval.
confirmed.rootCause: refreshOpenSchedule (app.js:7879-7882) rebuilds `wrap.innerHTML` (app.js:969) every render and tick while `.joy-stagger` is still on #schedule-body (set for 900 ms by joyStagger, app.js:8057-8063). The new children replay `.joy-stagger > *` animations.
confirmed.proposedFix: Skip renderScheduleBody while the stagger class is present, or use setHtmlIfChanged on #schedule-body so an unchanged timeline is not rewritten.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (p12_misc.cjs live build): joyRiseRunningAt350ms 3, joyRiseREPLAYEDbySyncInWindow 3, and the schedule body is fully rebuilt by every renderAll and 30 s tick while the sheet is open (rowsRecreatedOnRenderAll true). The idle rebuild creates no animations outside the 900 ms stagger window, and scroll is unaffected. The scrollKept [400,0] in their output is the chip tap resetting scrollTop, not a sync effect. Needs a real snapshot inside the sub-second window after a day-chip tap, so low.
verdict.refinedFix: Build the markup into a string and use setHtmlIfChanged: `const bodyHtml = `...`; if (!setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, bodyHtml)) return;` before wiring #sched-ics-btn. Tested in a scratch copy: rows are not recreated on renderAll, replays during the stagger drop from 3 to 0, and all tests pass. The ICS button listener is wired only on a write, and its closure over dow and day is safe because the day title is in the markup, so a day change always rewrites. The NOW pill still updates because it is in the markup.

confirmed.title: Standings points-pulse is cut off mid-flight by the next renderAll
confirmed.symptom: A row that just gained points flashes a blue tint fading out over 0.6 s. If any other real snapshot lands inside that window, the tint vanishes instantly (a faint flicker) instead of finishing its fade.
confirmed.trigger: Viewer with Standings open. Remote change gives a team points, then another renderAll() about 200 ms later (the next editor tap or an announcement).
confirmed.evidence: hunt/home-live-verify/v_pulse_cut.cjs: right after the first render the row has class 'points-pulse' and td background oklab(... / 0.105) at +200 ms. In the same frame after the second renderAll the row has no 'points-pulse' class and the background is rgba(0,0,0,0). Measured in Chromium, 390x844.
confirmed.rootCause: renderStandings rebuilds every tr and applies points-pulse only when pulseFromRemote and the points changed in THIS render, so the next render recreates the rows without the class and kills the running animation.
confirmed.proposedFix: Remember when each team's pulse started (for example a module-level `pulseAt[team.id] = Date.now()` set where the class is added) and keep adding 'points-pulse' to that row for 600 ms. Or skip the tbody write when the row markup is unchanged. Note the animation will still restart on a re-created row, so prefer the skip.

confirmed.title: Announcement composer loses focus (keyboard dismisses) when a remote announcement arrives while it is empty

confirmed.title: Every renderAll re-creates the whole open game view (all Jelly controls, back pill, rules)
confirmed.symptom: While any game is open, every remote snapshot, clock action or tap tears down and rebuilds the entire game card. The "← games" back pill slides in again, "How to play" snaps shut, and all Jelly buttons and selects are re-created. Players see the pill blink on every goal and every editor tap.
confirmed.trigger: Open any game, then call renderAll() or deliver a remote snapshot that changes anything (a Quick Points bonus on another team is enough). Editor taps do it too: team chip, clock Start/Pause/Reset, ladder score-round. Viewer watching a Big Board: any remote goal.
confirmed.evidence: p1_census, editor, idle renderAll. Nodes added and Jelly elements added: tally axe-throwing 242 / 102 (38 jelly-button, 9 jelly-select, 54 jelly-option); counselor-hide-seek 283 / 102; pictionary 220 / 72; placement shields 92 / 45; bracket 31-37 / 3. Back button, input and Save button are never the same node (sameBack/sameInput/sameSave false). Every run shows a fresh running animation `button#back-btn.back-pill :: back-pill-in`. p6b with a real handleRemoteSnapshot (a bonus on t3 only): game view rebuilt, rules <details> closed, back-pill-in replayed. p9 shows the same on every chip tap and clock tap. p26 viewer remote goal: back-pill-in plus 135 nodes. p2/p15: Jelly canvases paint synchronously (no blank frames), so the cost is replay and CPU, not a blank flash. Scroll jump on rebuild is 0.
confirmed.rootCause: renderGameView does `view.innerHTML = html` and then re-renders #clock-area, #tools-area and #entry-area unconditionally. The setHtmlIfChanged treatment from v183 was never applied here, and the whole game view re-renders on every renderAll. `.back-pill` has `animation: back-pill-in ... both`, so each re-creation replays the slide-in.
confirmed.proposedFix: Make renderGameView incremental. (1) Rebuild the header, back button and rules <details> only when g.id changes (track lastGameViewId) and leave them alone otherwise. (2) Write #clock-area, #tools-area and #entry-area through setHtmlIfChanged and bind listeners only when it returns true. Pass `entry.__dom`-style state so a focused input or open select is not lost. (3) As a stopgap, play back-pill-in only on first show: add the animation via a class that joySlideIn-style code adds and removes on open, not as a permanent rule.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p1_census (editor): every idle renderAll with a game open re-creates the whole view (shields 92 nodes/45 jelly, axe-throwing 242/102, pictionary 220/72, kickball 34/3). Back button, input and Save are never the same node, rules <details> closes, and a fresh back-pill-in runs. My own probe (v1_pill, jeb-ball, scrolled to the game) sampled the pill's opacity per frame after renderAll: 0,0,0,0.26,0.49,...,1 for editor, and 0,0,0.26,... for viewer. That is a real fade-from-invisible blink. p6b with a real handleRemoteSnapshot (a bonus on t3 only) rebuilds the view (the snapshot is a genuine signature change, so applyRemoteState calls renderAll). p9 shows the same on team-chip taps and clock Start/Pause/Reset (222-234 nodes and back-pill-in each). p26 shows the viewer remote goal rebuilding 135 nodes. Jelly canvases paint synchronously (p2/p15: pixel counts never drop to 0), so no blank flash on the controls, only replay and CPU. Two corrections to the claim: (1) the editor's own goal tap is NOT a rebuild (p9 'goal +1 (in-place)' adds only the 24 cannons, and inning+ adds 0 nodes), so 'every goal' is true only for viewers receiving it remotely; (2) v183 never touched renderGameView or renderLiveHome (git show 554fbe1; setHtmlIfChanged is used only by the footer, follow card, bonuses, verse, cleanup and day panels). Root cause as stated is right: `view.innerHTML = html` at app.js:5567 plus unconditional re-render of clock/tools/entry areas. This is the same class of bug the owner reported with the progress bar, and it is the common root of findings 2, 3, 9 and 10.
verdict.refinedFix: Do it in stages, cheapest and safest first. (A) styles.css:1441: delete the permanent `animation: back-pill-in ...` from `.back-pill` (and its reduced-motion override). The open already plays joySlideIn(#game-view). Verified: with `.back-pill{animation:none}` the opacity stays 1 across a rebuild. (B) In renderGameView split the markup into a stable head (back pill, title, messtival tag, rules <details>) and the three areas (#clock-area/#tools-area/#entry-area, created once). Rebuild the head only when a key changes, e.g. `headKey = [g.id,g.name,g.emoji,g.location,g.session,g.messtival,backDay&&backDay.name,JSON.stringify(g.rules)].join('|')`, stored on the view; capture `lastGameViewId` before it is overwritten at app.js:5538 to detect the id change. Do NOT use setHtmlIfChanged for the head: a user-opened <details> gains an `open` attribute, so `el.__dom !== el.innerHTML` reads as 'DOM altered' and the rules would still be rebuilt shut. (C) Only then make the three areas skip identical markup, and be careful: (i) renderTally/renderPlacement/renderTournament/renderLiveWatch/renderTools bind handlers that close over `draft = state.drafts[g.id]`, `state.brackets[g.id]`, etc. applyRemoteState replaces `state[k]` with fresh objects on every non-echo snapshot, so if markup is identical and the rebuild is skipped, the old handlers keep writing into orphaned objects and saveState() pushes a state that lacks the edit, which silently loses scores (the CLAUDE.md 'closures over replaced state objects' invariant). Re-resolve at event time (`const draft = () => state.drafts[g.id]`) or keep rebuilding those areas. (ii) setHtmlIfChanged never skips for any area containing a ticking clock (tickBoardClocks rewrites textContent every 500 ms, verified: #live-home innerHTML changes with no render), so tracker games' boards won't benefit; compare against the last html string only (drop the __dom check) for those, or split the clock out. (iii) Focus/typed values survive because renderAll is already deferred while a field is focused. Re-run tests/render-stability.test.js and add a game-view case.

confirmed.title: Each renderAll with a game open costs 50-130 ms of main-thread work
confirmed.symptom: On a real phone every remote update or tap re-render during a game is a visible hitch (several hundred ms). Scoring a rapid sequence feels laggy.
confirmed.trigger: Open a tally or placement game and call renderAll() (any remote snapshot).
confirmed.evidence: p3_cost, median over 15 renders (max). No game open: 1.2 ms (2.1). Placement shields: 56 ms (98). Tally axe-throwing: 88 ms (130). counselor-hide-seek: 75 ms (152). pictionary: 47 ms (74). Bracket kangaroo: 5.4 ms. That is desktop headless Chromium; phones are typically 4-6x slower. The cost tracks the number of jelly-select and jelly-option elements: a placement view has 6 jelly-selects and costs about 56 ms.
confirmed.rootCause: Same unconditional rebuild as gameview-full-rebuild-every-render. The expensive parts are the medal pickers (3 jelly-select, 18 jelly-option) and the counter jelly-buttons, re-created on every render.
confirmed.proposedFix: Fixed by the same incremental render. Additionally keep the medal pickers out of the rebuild: update the existing selects' value attributes in place when draft.medals changes.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p3_cost: no game 1.3 ms; shields 45 ms; axe-throwing 69 ms (max 105); counselor-hide-seek 68 ms; pictionary 52 ms; kangaroo-kickball 6 ms. My v2_cost with CDP CPU throttling gives a measured phone proxy: at 4x, axe-throwing is 491 ms median (629 max) and shields 270 ms (315 max) per renderAll. That is a main-thread freeze of roughly a quarter to half a second whenever a remote update lands while an editor has a tally/placement game open (CPU throttling only approximates a phone). Viewers' watch views are cheap (kickball 6 ms, p26 viewer goal 8 ms), so the pain is editor-side. Same root cause as finding 1, not an independent defect; fixing 1 plus the tally split (finding 3) removes it. Kept at med only because the audience is the handful of editors.
verdict.refinedFix: No separate fix: it falls out of the incremental render in gameview-full-rebuild-every-render, whose cost is dominated by the three jelly-selects/18 jelly-options in the medal picker and the counter jelly-buttons. Highest-yield first step: keep the medal picker (medalPickerHTML, app.js:5950) out of rebuilds when picks are unchanged (see tally-medals fix) and skip the entry-area rebuild when markup is identical, with the closure caveat noted in finding 1.

confirmed.title: Every tally keystroke or +N tap rebuilds the medal pickers (about 50 ms, 21 Jelly elements)
confirmed.symptom: Typing a score or tapping +1/+5 is laggy on a phone (50-65 ms desktop, so 200-300 ms on a phone). The medal selects are torn down and re-created each time even though nothing in them changed.
confirmed.trigger: Axe Throwing / Counselor Hide and Seek: tap a +1/+5 counter or type in a score field.
confirmed.evidence: p8_tally: counter tap handler 65 ms, with 31 nodes added and 21 of them jelly (3 jelly-select + 18 jelly-option). Three taps 148 ms. Keystrokes 64, 45, 43, 41 ms. The input stays focused (clean).
confirmed.rootCause: updateTallyMedals always does `wrap.innerHTML = ...` including medalPickerHTML and re-binds the selects, even when ranking and picks are unchanged.
confirmed.proposedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html) and bind the select listeners only when it returns true. Better, skip the call when the ranked order and picks are the same as last time.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p8_tally: counter tap handler 55 ms with 31 nodes added, 21 of them Jelly; keystrokes 38-41 ms each; the input stays focused. Code confirms updateTallyMedals always does `wrap.innerHTML = ...` including medalPickerHTML and re-binds the selects (app.js:6147). The auditor's proposed fix does not work as written: I measured (v3_select) that between keystrokes the WHOLE #tally-medals html differs on every keystroke (the rank pills carry the scores) while the picker sub-markup is identical (fullDiffers12=true, pickerDiffers12=false), so `setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html)` on the whole wrap would still rebuild every keystroke. I validated a corrected version by monkeypatching updateTallyMedals in the page: pills in their own div, picker in its own div written through setHtmlIfChanged. Keystrokes dropped from 38-40 ms to 0.4-0.6 ms once picks were stable (the first one still rebuilds because the auto picks changed), and a manual pick followed by a score change still resets to the auto pick (jelly-select reflects `value` to an attribute, so setHtmlIfChanged sees its DOM as altered and rebuilds).
verdict.refinedFix:
In updateTallyMedals, give #tally-medals two children, e.g. `
` (build them once; readMedalPicks(document.getElementById('tally-medals')) still finds [data-medal] inside). Write the pills + tieNote into #tally-ranking with plain innerHTML (plain text, no Jelly). Write `

...

${medalPickerHTML(picks, g)}` into #tally-picker via `if (setHtmlIfChanged(picker, html)) picker.querySelectorAll('[data-medal]').forEach(sel => sel.addEventListener('change', ...))` and bind the change handler only on a fresh write. Keep resolving `draft` as `state.drafts[g.id]` at call time (it already is). The existing manual-pick behaviour is preserved (verified).

confirmed.title: Opening a game scrolls too far: back pill and title end up clipped above the screen
confirmed.symptom: Tap a tall game (tally, Pictionary) in the Competitions list: the page whips down and settles with the "← games" pill and the top of the title cut off. The user cannot see the back button until they scroll up. The whole open is one big layout shift.
confirmed.trigger: Competitions card open, scroll so a game card is mid-screen, tap it. Editor, tally game (axe-throwing). Worse on 360x640.
confirmed.evidence: p5_scroll and p5v_video. 390x844: after open scrollY=1083 and #game-view top=-97, back button rect top=-76..-43 (off-screen). 360x640: back button top=-89. Layout-shift entries on open: [0.304, 0.008, 0.016, 0.016, 0.005] (about 0.35); 0.40 at 360x640. Per-frame: the Competitions card collapses 1156px to 58px over about 200 ms while a smooth scroll runs; docH goes 2276 to 2780 to 2683. Video frames 159-170 in vid_editor/sheet_open.png show the header clipped at rest. Short views are not affected (shields: back button at 357px; viewer watch view: 479px) because the document cannot scroll far enough.
confirmed.rootCause: The click handler calls renderAll() (which starts collapsing every open accordion card via toggle(false), a spring height animation) and immediately does `game-view.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'})`. The target is computed against the mid-collapse layout, so a smooth scroll to a moving target overshoots.
confirmed.location: app.js:5491-5496 (game card click), app.js:5728-5738 (openGame from home), app.js:5520-5528 (accordion fold in renderGameView)
confirmed.proposedFix: Do not animate scrolling against a moving layout. Either (a) collapse the accordion without animation on open (set `open` attribute directly / suppress the spring) and scrollIntoView({behavior:'instant'}), or (b) scroll after the collapse settles (wait for the card's transitionend or about 350 ms) and use block:'start' with a scroll-margin-top. Best, fix it at the root: move #game-view above the accordion (see layout finding) so no scroll is needed.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p5_scroll (editor, axe-throwing, 390x844): after open scrollY=1083, #game-view top=-97, back button rect -76..-43 (off-screen); layout shifts [0.304,0.008,0.016,0.016,0.005]. 360x640: back button top -89, CLS about 0.40. Pictionary (also tall) lands at back top -77. Shields (short) lands fine (back at 357) but still shows CLS 0.29. Viewer's watch view lands fine (back at 479) but CLS 0.30. Root cause verified experimentally (v4_open): the same open performed with the handler's immediate smooth scrollIntoView gives backTop=-76; waiting 450 ms for the accordion collapse before scrollIntoView gives backTop=21, gvTop=0 for both smooth and instant. So it is a smooth scroll computed against a layout that is still collapsing (jelly-collapsible animates grid-template-rows over 0.36 s with an overshooting cubic-bezier). Affects every tall game, which is most editor-scored games (tally, Pictionary).
verdict.refinedFix: Prefer the structural fix in game-view-below-accordion-layout (validated: with a takeover the open has zero layout shifts and the back pill lands at 36 px). Stopgap if that is deferred: in both openers (app.js:5491-5496 and openGame at 5728-5738) replace the immediate `scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'})` with `setTimeout(() => gv.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'}), 420)` (collapse is 0.36 s; verified result gvTop=0), keeping joySlideIn. Do not rely on `data-jelly-motion="reduce"` to skip the collapse: jelly's reduce rules use :host-context, which Firefox/Safari (the iPhones) do not support.
verdict.location: app.js:5491-5496 (game card click), app.js:5728-5738 (openGame from home), app.js:5518-5528 (accordion fold in renderGameView)

confirmed.title: Back from a game whips the page to the top, then drifts down; lands mid-list with the tapped card off-screen
confirmed.symptom: Press "← games": the page jumps to the top of the home screen (footer visible), the Competitions list springs open under the viewport, and the page ends scrolled partway into the list with the card you came from above the screen (or 77 px above it). From the home "Live now" Big Board, Back drops you about 1070-1290 px down inside a list you never opened, with the Big Board 841 px above.
confirmed.trigger: Open a game from the Competitions list (or the home Big Board), then tap Back.
confirmed.evidence: p5_scroll, editor tally, Back from the in-view position: scrollY 987 -> 334 (4 ms) -> 938 -> 1145 (settled); card top after Back = -77 px (off-screen); 10 layout-shift entries ({0.058,0.165,0.138,0.112,0.088,...}, about 0.55 total). From page bottom: lands scrollY 1432, card top -364. Viewer variant ends with card at +299 (ok) but still CLS about 0.37. p18_homeopen (viewer): open from home board then Back: scrollY 1180 -> 355 -> 975 -> 1069, Big Board top = -841, Competitions card forced open; CLS 0.91 on the first frame. Video frames 221-236 in vid_editor/sheet_back.png: the visible page goes game, home top, list springing open.
confirmed.rootCause: Back sets state.ui.gameId=null and renderAll(): #game-view is hidden (the document shrinks so the browser clamps scrollY), then renderGameView forces Competitions open (comp.toggle(true)) so a 1100 px list springs open while scroll anchoring chases it. No scroll position is saved or restored. It also opens Competitions unconditionally even when the user came from the home board.
confirmed.location: app.js:5513-5537 (focus handoff in renderGameView), app.js:5570-5574 (Back click)
confirmed.proposedFix: Remember the opener: store {scrollY, openerCardId} when a game opens and on Back (1) restore Competitions state only if it was open before, (2) re-open without animation and scrollTo the saved scrollY or scrollIntoView the opener card with block:'center', behavior:'instant'. Or restructure so #game-view is a full-screen takeover like #settings-view / #chat-view (body.game-open hides siblings), which makes both open and Back trivial and removes the clamp/spring problem.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p5_scroll Back: scrollY 987 -> 334 (t=6 ms) -> 1081 -> 1145; docH 2683 -> 1178 -> 2276; card top after Back -77 (off-screen); 10 layout-shift entries (about 0.55 total); 360x640: 0.077/0.337/0.274/0.193... and card top -66. Re-ran p18_homeopen (viewer): open from the home Big Board then Back ends at scrollY 1069 with the Big Board at -841 and Competitions forced open (CLS 0.91 first frame). I also viewed the auditor's frame sheet (vid_editor/sheet_back.png, frames 219-236): game -> home top with the footer showing (221-222) -> the Competitions list springing open under the viewport while scroll chases. Short views are less bad (shields lands with the card at +734, CLS 0.14). Root cause is as described: renderAll hides #game-view so the document shrinks and scrollY is clamped, then renderGameView forces Competitions open and the grid-row spring grows the page under scroll anchoring; no scroll is saved or restored, and Competitions opens even when the opener was the home board.
verdict.refinedFix: Structural, and prototyped: make the game a full-screen takeover like chat/builder. v5_takeover prototype (CSS `body.game-open .main-wrap > :not(#game-view), body.game-open #app-footer {display:none}`, toggle the class in renderGameView, `scrollTo(0,0)` on open, remember `window.scrollY` at open and `scrollTo(0, saved)` after Back's renderAll) gave: open CLS 0, back pill at 36 px, and Back returned the opener card to exactly its prior position (366 -> 366) with no layout shifts. Required with it: (1) DELETE the fold/re-open block in renderGameView (app.js:5518-5537). If it stays, the fold happens while hidden and `comp.toggle(true)` still springs open on Back; (2) derive `body.game-open` in renderAll only when `!inBuilder && !inChat`, so it cannot hide chat-view/settings-view when a notification opens chat over an open game; (3) save the scroll in a module variable in both openers (game card click, openGame) and restore in the Back handler; (4) drop the smooth scrollIntoView calls. Risk to confirm with the owner: state.ui.gameId persists, so a reload now shows the game full-screen (that is desirable) and Back lands on the top of home.
verdict.location: app.js:5513-5537 (focus handoff in renderGameView), app.js:5570-5574 (Back click)

confirmed.title: Open game sits below roughly 1100 px of home content, so the first screen shows none of it
confirmed.symptom: Tapping a game from anywhere, or reloading while a game is open, shows the home page with only collapsed accordion headers on screen. The game is the last block, a screen below. It lands only because a scroll is forced; after a reload it is simply not on screen.
confirmed.trigger: Open any game, scroll to the top (or reload the page with a game open).
confirmed.evidence: p12_stack at scrollY 0, viewport 844. Editor: you-strip 156 px, Happening Now 406 px, Chat 127 px, collapsed accordion 350 px; #game-view starts at y=1144 (300 px below the fold). Viewer: starts at y=1038. Full-page shot: shot_stack_full_editor.png. p11_reload: after a reload with state.ui.gameId set, scrollY=580 and the game view top is at y=458, with half the first screen collapsed accordions. state.ui.gameId persists in the localStorage snapshot.
confirmed.rootCause: #game-view is DOM-ordered after the whole home stack (notice, announcements, you-strip, Happening Now, chat, accordion) and is shown in place, rather than replacing the home content like the builder and chat do (body.builder-open / body.chat-open).
confirmed.proposedFix: Make the game a takeover, same pattern as chat and the builder: derive body.game-open from state.ui.gameId in renderAll and hide the other sections via CSS, with scrollTo(0,0) on open and a saved scroll to restore on Back. That also fixes the open overshoot and Back whiplash findings.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p12_stack (editor, scrollY 0): announcements 15, you-strip 156, now-banner 406, chat 127, collapsed accordion 350, then #game-view at y=1144 (h 579); index.html:261 puts section#game-view after jelly-accordion. Re-ran p11_reload: before reload scrollY 1134 / gvTop 10; after reload scrollY 580, gvTop 458, so the game is half off-screen under collapsed headers. state.ui.gameId persists in the cached state, so a device that returns later opens to a home page with the game hidden a screen down. This is the structural cause of findings 4, 5 and 10. Severity is med as its own item: it works after a forced scroll, but it is the design flaw behind the two high-severity scroll glitches.
verdict.refinedFix: Takeover pattern, same as chat/builder (validated in v5_takeover, see game-back-whiplash for the required pieces): derive `body.game-open` in renderAll (only when no other takeover is active), reuse the 4757-4758 CSS pattern, scrollTo(0,0) on open, saved scrollY restored on Back, and remove the accordion fold/re-open code. Existing `dayNav.hidden = true` in renderGameView becomes redundant but harmless.
verdict.location: index.html:261 (section#game-view after jelly-accordion); app.js:5510 (renderGameView); styles.css:4757 (chat-open takeover pattern to copy)

confirmed.title: Clock goes un-red / un-amber for up to half a second on every rebuild in the last minute; heartbeat and zero pulse restart
confirmed.symptom: In the last 60 s (amber) or last 10 s (red heartbeat) of a synced clock, any re-render (a goal, a remote snapshot) flashes the clock back to normal dark text, kills the red board glow, and restarts the heartbeat, until the next 500 ms tick re-applies the classes. At 0:00 the red pulse restarts at full opacity.
confirmed.trigger: Run a game clock with 8 s left on a Big Board (jeb-ball) or standalone clock, then call renderAll() (or a goal arrives from the ref).
confirmed.evidence: p4_clock. Before rebuild: clock class `board-clock clock-final-ten`, board `big-board board-final-ten`, heartbeat animation present. Immediately after renderAll: `board-clock ` and `big-board ` with no animations. Frame sampling: the colour is oklch(0.26) (dark) until the next tick, then the red oklch(0.58 0.2 27). Classes restored after 509 ms (editor) and 166 ms (viewer). Zero pulse phase before 483 ms, after rebuild 0-17 ms (restarts). Goals commonly land in the last seconds, exactly when this shows.
confirmed.rootCause: clockBlockHTML, liveTrackerHTML, liveBoardHTML and tallyBoardHTML emit only `board-clock-zero` at build time. The clock-final-min / clock-final-ten / board-final-ten classes are applied only inside tickBoardClocks on its 500 ms interval, so a freshly built element lacks them until the next tick.
confirmed.proposedFix: Extract the class computation into one helper (e.g. clockUrgencyClasses(clock) returning the clock-final-min/ten classes and a board-final-ten flag) and use it when building the markup in all four builders, and keep tickBoardClocks for in-place updates. Alternatively call tickBoardClocks() at the end of renderAll.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p4_clock (editor): before rebuild `board-clock clock-final-ten` / `big-board board-final-ten` with clock-heartbeat running; right after renderAll the classes are gone and no animations; sampled colour is dark oklch(0.26) until classes return at 446 ms (viewer 202 ms); zero-pulse phase 483 ms -> 0 ms (restart). Code confirms the four builders (app.js:5790, 6504, 6670, 6736) emit only board-clock-zero and the final-min/ten/board-final-ten classes are applied only in tickBoardClocks' 500 ms interval. NEW exposure I measured: the same loss happens on the HOME Big Board, the most common viewer surface, via renderLiveHome (v7_home: viewer, 8 s left, an unrelated bonus triggers renderAll; classes dropped, restored after 329 ms). So any remote change in the last minute (not just goals) flashes the clock back to dark for every viewer watching. Duration is brief (<=500 ms), which keeps it at med. The editor's own goal taps do not trigger it (in-place).
verdict.refinedFix: Extract the body of the `els.forEach` in tickBoardClocks (app.js:3517-3534) into `paintClockClasses()` and call it from tickBoardClocks AND at the end of renderAll (do not call tickBoardClocks from renderAll: settleExpiredClocks can setClock and call renderAll, which would recurse). Validated in-page (v7b_fix): wrapping renderAll with that paint step leaves `clock-final-ten`/`board-final-ten` present immediately after the rebuild (no dark frame). The heartbeat/zero-pulse animation phase still restarts on a rebuilt node; that only goes away once the board nodes survive renders.

confirmed.title: Goal confetti and score pop are cut off mid-flight by the next render
confirmed.symptom: After a goal the emoji cannons and the popped score vanish abruptly if anything re-renders within about 2 s (clock Pause, another goal's snapshot, any remote change).
confirmed.trigger: Editor taps +1 on a team, then taps clock Pause about 350 ms later. Viewer: a remote goal, then any unrelated remote change within 2 s.
confirmed.evidence: p7_board. Editor: cannons 24 right after the tap, 0 right after the Pause re-render; score-pop 0. Viewer: 24 on the goal, 0 after an unrelated renderAll 400 ms later (a bonus on another team); score-pop 0.
confirmed.rootCause: boardCelebrate appends the .board-cannon spans (and the score-pop class) inside the .big-board element, which renderGameView/renderLiveHome replace via innerHTML on the next render.
confirmed.proposedFix: Append the cannons to a persistent overlay (e.g. a fixed `#joy-layer`-style container positioned over the board, or a sibling of #game-view) so they outlive the board rebuild. Also resolved if the board node is preserved across unrelated renders.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p7_board: editor +1 then Pause 350 ms later: cannons 24 -> 0, score-pop 0; viewer remote goal 24 cannons, then an unrelated renderAll 400 ms later: 0 and no score-pop. Cannons live inside the .big-board that the next render replaces. Needs a second render within about 2 s of a goal; that is real at camp (any editor anywhere) but short-lived, and the celebration itself still fires on the goal, so low. Also applies to the home Big Board (renderLiveHome).
verdict.refinedFix: Append the .board-cannon spans to a persistent overlay (a fixed-position container created once, appended in boardCelebrate with coordinates from the board's getBoundingClientRect), so they outlive a board rebuild. Alternatively resolved automatically once the board node survives unrelated renders.

confirmed.title: Score input loses focus (keyboard closes) when the clock hits zero or the members list changes
confirmed.symptom: An editor typing a score in Counselor Hide and Seek when the game clock reaches 0:00 has the field replaced under them: focus goes to the page, and the keyboard dismisses (the typed value survives in the draft).
confirmed.trigger: counselor-hide-seek (timer + tally): focus a score field, let the synced clock expire on that device. Same with any change to the members list (members .on('value') listener).
confirmed.evidence: p27_zero_focus: before expiry the input is focused and editorMidEntry() is true. After expiry the old input node is not in the DOM (sameInputNode false), document.activeElement is BODY, value '12' kept. p6_focus: any unguarded renderAll while a field is focused replaces it (activeTag BODY). By contrast p6b: a real remote snapshot while an input is focused is correctly deferred (clean).
confirmed.rootCause: Two renderAll callers bypass the canAdoptRemote()/editorMidEntry() guard that remote snapshots honour: tickBoardClocks calls renderAll() when settleExpiredClocks changed something, and the members listener calls renderAll() on every members snapshot. Because the whole game view is rebuilt, the focused input is lost.
confirmed.proposedFix: Gate both on !editorMidEntry() (defer through deferRemoteSnapshot/idle tick), or repaint only the clock/board in place instead of renderAll after the settle. Fixing gameview-full-rebuild-every-render (stable input nodes) removes the symptom for all callers.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p27_zero_focus: before expiry the input is focused and editorMidEntry() true; after the synced clock settles at 0:00 the input node was replaced (sameInputNode=false), activeElement is BODY, the value '12' survives in the draft. Code confirms tickBoardClocks calls renderAll() on `settled` (app.js:3516) and the members listener calls renderAll() on every members snapshot (app.js:2742), neither guarded by canAdoptRemote/editorMidEntry; p6b confirms real remote snapshots ARE deferred correctly. Rarity is why it is low: only an editor device with a score field focused at the exact tick the clock expires, or while the member list changes. NOTE for the fix: editorMidEntry() is also true whenever dataEditPending or pushTimer is set, and settleExpiredClocks has just called setClock -> touchData/schedulePush, so gating the settle-render on `!editorMidEntry()` would defer it every time.
verdict.refinedFix: Split the focus clause out of editorMidEntry (app.js:7651) into `fieldFocused()` (the activeElement test only) and use it for these two callers: `if (settled) { if (fieldFocused()) settleRenderPending = true; else renderAll(); }` and in the members listener `if (appStarted) { if (fieldFocused()) membersRenderPending = true; else renderAll(); }`, flushing the pending flags from the existing idleRetryTick/focusout path. Or, better, fix gameview-full-rebuild-every-render so the focused input node survives these renders.
verdict.location: app.js:3516 (if (settled) renderAll()), app.js:2742 (members listener renderAll), app.js:7651 (editorMidEntry)

confirmed.trigger: Open any game, expand "How to play", then any remote change (a score, a goal, a bonus).

confirmed.rootCause: The rules <details> is part of the markup written by `view.innerHTML = html` on every renderAll, so its open state is lost.

confirmed.title: Confetti burst and "Data last updated" stamp on clock Start/Pause/Reset, undoing a goal, innings, Reset tally and the buzzer
confirmed.symptom: Pressing Pause, Reset, a preset chip, goal minus, inning plus or Reset tally throws the same 16-particle celebration as saving a result. When the clock reaches 0:00 the ref's phone also gets a confetti burst (from the last tap position, or screen centre). The footer "Data last updated" time moves for each of these.
confirmed.trigger: As an editor in a tracker game (jeb-ball, ladder-ball): tap clock Start/Pause/Reset, goal minus, inning plus, Reset tally, a ladder rung; or let the clock expire on an editor device.
confirmed.evidence: p20_burst (800 ms throttle bypassed per tap): every action listed produced particles=16 with 4-7 emoji and dataStampBumped=true. p19_zero: at zero, joy-p x16, view rebuilt, alarm-flash and board-zero-pulse start, dataStampBumped=true.
confirmed.rootCause: setClock, setLiveMatch and setLadderMatch each call touchData(), which stamps lastDataChangeAt and fires joyCelebrate() (a big burst). CLAUDE.md says touchData() is only for real scoreboard activity, and settleExpiredClocks routes the buzzer through setClock.
confirmed.proposedFix: Split touchData into stampData() (lastDataChangeAt) and the celebration. Call the celebration only for genuine scoring (goal plus, medals saved, bracket win). Use a quiet save for clock/inning/outs/undo/reset and for the zero-settle.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p20_burst: inning+, goal+, goal-, clock Start/Pause/Reset/preset, Reset tally and ladder rung/round each fire 16 particles (3-8 emoji) and bump lastDataChangeAt. p19_zero: at 0:00 the editor's device gets joy particles and a data-stamp bump from settleExpiredClocks -> setClock -> touchData -> joyCelebrate. joyCelebrate's own comment says it is for 'every action that records real scoreboard data'; CLAUDE.md defines touchData that way, so clock start/pause/reset and the buzzer are misfires; goal+ and ladder rung are legitimately scoring. Partly by design, hence low.
verdict.refinedFix: Do NOT remove the touchData() call from setClock: it also sets `dataEditPending = true`, which editorMidEntry/reloadBlocked rely on to guard an unpushed edit. Instead add an option: `function touchData({ celebrate = true, stamp = true } = {})` and have setClock call `touchData({ celebrate: false, stamp: false })` (still setting dataEditPending). Leave goal+, ladder rungs and saved results as they are; for goal-/inning+ choose celebrate:false. settleExpiredClocks then stops bursting at the buzzer automatically.

confirmed.title: "Live now" card's red pulse ring restarts on every render
confirmed.symptom: The pulsing ring on a Live now card re-fires from full strength each time any update lands, instead of pulsing on its steady 2 s beat.
confirmed.trigger: A bracket game in progress that is not promoted to the home Big Board (e.g. ladder-ball); any renderAll.
confirmed.evidence: p9 and p26 steps show a fresh `button.live-home-card :: live-pulse` animation on every renderAll. Seen only as a running-animation diff, not as a visible-phase measurement. On the home surface (live-home), not the game view; flagged for overlap with the home auditor.
confirmed.rootCause: renderLiveHome sets `wrap.innerHTML = boardHTML + ...` on every render, so each .live-home-card is a new element and its infinite live-pulse animation restarts at phase 0.
confirmed.proposedFix: Write #live-home through setHtmlIfChanged (as v183 did for the other home panels); card markup is unchanged between most renders, so the pulse keeps its phase.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v15_pulse, viewer, ladder-ball bracket in progress): the .live-home-card is a new node after renderAll and the live-pulse animation phase goes from ~400 ms to 0 (a 7 px ring that was mid-expansion restarts from zero). Code confirms `wrap.innerHTML = boardHTML + ...` on every renderLiveHome and v183 did not convert it. The visible effect is a barely noticeable early restart of a 2 s ring, so low and not reliably perceptible. NOTE on the proposed fix: converting the whole #live-home to setHtmlIfChanged does nothing while the promoted Big Board has a running clock, because tickBoardClocks mutates the clock text every 500 ms (measured: #live-home innerHTML changes between renders with no render call), so `__dom !== innerHTML` and it always rebuilds.
verdict.refinedFix: Give the plain `.live-home-card` buttons their own container (e.g. `#live-home-cards`, separate from the board container) and write that one through `if (!setHtmlIfChanged(cards, html)) return;` binding the click handlers only on a fresh write. Cards contain no ticking clock, so the skip works even while the board's clock runs. Keep boardDiffCelebrate running on every render for the board (it diffs internally).

confirmed.title: Schedule sheet day row overflows: Saturday is clipped or unreachable on nearly all phones
confirmed.symptom: Open the full schedule on a phone. The Sat chip is cut off at the sheet edge, and at 360 px wide Fri is half cut and Sat is almost entirely off-screen. The row does not scroll, so Saturday (send-off day) cannot be selected.
confirmed.trigger: Tap the Happening-now banner at any viewport narrower than about 417 px (iPhone 12-16 at 390, SE at 375, most Android at 360-412). Run p3_daysnav.cjs and view daysnav-360-junior.png.
confirmed.evidence: #schedule-days is display:grid with repeat(7,1fr) and overflow-x:visible. Measured navClientW 358 (390 px), 343 (375 px), 328 (360 px) against about 385 px of chip content (scrollWidth 429). Chip rects: Sat spans 353-400 px, so 10 px is clipped at 390 and only a 7 px sliver is visible at 360. The sheet has overflow:hidden. Same in the senior camp. Injected CSS `.schedule-days{grid-template-columns:repeat(7,minmax(0,1fr))} jelly-chip.sched-day-chip::part(main){padding-inline:0;width:100%;justify-content:center}` puts all seven chips inside 16-344 px at 360 and 16-374 px at 390 (p23_fixcheck.cjs, daysfix-360.png).
confirmed.rootCause: `1fr` is minmax(auto,1fr), so each track is floored at the jelly-chip's min-content. A jelly-chip has 13 px of hard-coded shadow padding on each side plus its label, so seven chips plus gaps exceed the 16 px-padded header on narrow phones.
confirmed.proposedFix: Use `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr))` and add `jelly-chip.sched-day-chip::part(main){padding-inline:0;width:100%;justify-content:center}`. Verified by injection. If a scroll row is preferred instead, preserve scrollLeft across renderScheduleDays(), which rebuilds the chips with innerHTML on every tap.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran at 430/412/390/375/360 px, junior and senior (probe v1_days.cjs). Chip rects are identical at every width below about 417 px: Sat spans 353-400. That is 10 px clipped at 390, 25 px at 375, and only a 7 px sliver at 360. #schedule-days is overflow-x:visible inside the overflow:hidden sheet, and navScrollW is 429 against navClientW 358/343/328. Screenshots show Sat cut off. At 430 it fits. A real touch tap on Sat still selects it once it is visible. The root cause (1fr floors at the jelly-chip min-content, 13 px side padding on a small chip) is correct. The auditor's injected CSS is NOT correct as written. All seven chips fit, but with `::part(main){width:100%;justify-content:center}` the label stays left-aligned inside each pill, because `.chip` is a content-width inline-flex inside a block `.jelly-content`. Measured at 360: Sun host 16-59 but label 16-41; the selected Tue label is visibly clipped at the pill's left edge (screenshot daysfix-360c.png). Using text-align:center on the host instead centres the label (host 16-59, label 25-50) and looks right (daysfix-360e.png).
verdict.refinedFix: styles.css .schedule-days: `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr));` plus a new rule `jelly-chip.sched-day-chip { text-align: center; }` and `jelly-chip.sched-day-chip::part(main) { padding-inline: 0; }`. Do NOT use `width:100%; justify-content:center` on the part: it leaves the text left-aligned in the pill. text-align inherits into the shadow tree and centres the inline-flex .chip. Verified at 320/360/390/430: all seven chips sit inside 16..(width-16), and tapping Sat sets scheduleDay 6. Cosmetic follow-up: the 6px `.today-dot` now overlaps the last letter of the label on a 43 px pill at 360, so nudge it to top:-2px/right:-2px or shrink it. No JS change, so no stale-listener risk. The chips are still rebuilt by renderScheduleDays() (see extra finding sched-day-chip-focus-loss).
verdict.location: styles.css:1215 (.schedule-days) and styles.css:4380 (jelly-chip.sched-day-chip host rule); app.js:892 renderScheduleDays

confirmed.title: Swipe-to-dismiss on the schedule sheet snaps back to the top, then slides down
confirmed.symptom: Drag the schedule header down more than 90 px and release. The sheet jumps back up to its resting position in one frame, then animates off-screen from there, instead of continuing down from where the finger let go.
confirmed.trigger: Open the schedule, touch-drag the header down about 200 px, release. Run p4_swipe.cjs.
confirmed.evidence: Sheet top per frame: 284 (while dragged 200 px) then 84, 138, 252, 394, 522, 620, 694, 787, 814, 831, 841. The first frame after release is the 200 px snap-back. Without touch-driven dismiss there is no problem; this affects every swipe dismiss.
confirmed.rootCause: The touchend handler calls closeSchedule(), which sets `sheet.style.transform = ''` before adding .closing. The sched-slide-out keyframes start from translateY(0), discarding the drag offset. The same applies to the 'spring back' branch: no CSS transition is defined on the sheet, so a short drag also snaps instantly.
confirmed.proposedFix: For the swipe path, do not clear the inline transform. Set `sheet.style.transition='transform .2s ease'; sheet.style.transform='translateY(100%)'` and let finish() hide the overlay, or pass the drag offset to the keyframes via a CSS var (`@keyframes sched-slide-out{from{transform:translateY(var(--drag,0px))}}`). For the short-drag spring-back, set `transition:transform .2s` before clearing the transform.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with real CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent (touchStart, 20 touchMoves to +200 px, touchEnd), not synthetic TouchEvents. Sheet top per frame: 284 (dragged), then 84 on the first frame after release, then 138, 251, 394, 522, 694, 748, 787, 814, 831, 841. So the sheet snaps 200 px back to rest and then slides down. The short-drag spring-back also snaps. A 60 px drag gave 144, then 84 on the very next frame, because the sheet has no CSS transition. Root cause confirmed: closeSchedule() clears the inline transform (app.js:871) and the sched-slide-out keyframes start from translateY(0). The touchend handler calls closeSchedule() with no offset.
verdict.refinedFix: app.js touchend (~1074): `if (dy > 90) closeSchedule(dy); else { sheet.style.transition = 'transform .2s ease'; sheet.style.transform = ''; }`. In closeSchedule(fromDy): `if (sheet) { if (typeof fromDy === 'number' && fromDy > 0) sheet.style.setProperty('--drag', fromDy + 'px'); sheet.style.transform = ''; }`, and in finish(): `if (sheet) sheet.style.removeProperty('--drag')`. styles.css: `@keyframes sched-slide-out { from { transform: translateY(var(--drag, 0px)); } to { transform: translateY(100%); } }`. Verified (v2_swipe_fix.cjs): 284, 284, 324, 408, 512, 680, 733, 773 ... continuous, and reopening lands at top 84. Risks: closeSchedule is also a click listener (X button, backdrop), so its first argument is a MouseEvent. The `typeof === 'number'` guard is mandatory. `--drag` must be removed in finish() or a later close inherits a stale offset. touchstart already sets transition:'none', so the spring-back transition does not leak.
verdict.location: app.js:868-884 (closeSchedule, line 871) and app.js:1074-1080 (touchend handler); styles.css:1109 (@keyframes sched-slide-out)

After 4 s there were no reloads and the banner was still up. That is the auditor's point: the banner persists exactly while the composer is in use. elementFromPoint at the centres of Send, input and photo returned #update-banner (banner y 748-828, composer 785-843). Refresh anyway?')) return; doReload(); });` (the codebase already uses confirm()). The same applies to showSdkDownBanner's handler for chat-composer text.
