confirmed.title: Members drawer: every role/team/remove tap rebuilds all rows, freezing the UI for about 1 s and wiping the Add form
confirmed.symptom: After changing one person's role or team, the drawer dims and the page freezes for roughly a second while every row is re-created. Anything typed in the Add someone form (email, name) disappears at the same time.
confirmed.trigger: Settings, Who can sign in, with about 40 members. Change any person's role/team/None switch, or open the drawer. Run p8_members.cjs and p9_members_cost.cjs (Firebase mocked).
confirmed.evidence: 41 members produce 83 jelly-segmented and 42 jelly-select. renderMemberList() took 927 ms synchronously (p9). In isolation, 83 segmented took 703 ms and 42 selects 406 ms, roughly 8.5 ms and 10 ms each from the forced layout in each connectedCallback. In p8 the frame sampler saw frames at t=105 ms and t=1696 ms, a main-thread block of about 1.5 s per refresh, and the first fill after open took 1382 ms with a 120 ms mocked read. A value typed into #member-add-name read 'Typed Name' before and '' after renderMemberList(). Scroll position was preserved (700 to 700) and no new CSS animations fired. Measured on this headless desktop Chromium; phones are likely slower.
confirmed.rootCause: renderMembers() re-reads both camps' member lists and then renderMemberList() replaces the whole body.innerHTML, which includes the Add form, after every single write (and every `.then(renderMembers)` in bindMemberList).
confirmed.proposedFix: Split the body into #members-list and #members-add and only re-render the list. Better, update the affected row in place (or optimistically patch `lists` and re-render just that row) instead of re-fetching and rebuilding all rows. Chunk or lazily create the jelly-select/segmented controls for large lists.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with a mocked firebase (v4_members.cjs). CPU baseline on this machine is fast (a 3e7-iteration loop takes about 60 ms), so phones will be slower. renderMembers() main-thread cost: 15 members gave a 429 ms longtask (rAF gap 481 ms), 25 gave 767 ms (831 ms gap), 40 gave 1093 ms (1187 ms gap), roughly 20-27 ms per member. The roster seeds 15 counselors, so a real list is at least 16 rows. Typed text in #member-add-name read 'Typed Name' before and '' after, because renderMemberList() assigns body.innerHTML including the Add form. Both claims hold. Every role/team/None success handler in bindMemberList calls renderMembers() (app.js ~1597, 1638-1653, 1669, 1689), which re-reads both camps and rebuilds all rows. It is editors-only and setup-time, so med rather than high.
verdict.refinedFix: Cheapest safe change: in bindMemberList, stop calling renderMembers() after a successful role/team write on an EXISTING record. The jelly-segmented/jelly-select already shows the new value and the toast confirms. Keep renderMembers() for failures (to revert the control), removals, grants (a new record changes row state) and the seed/convert paths. Because the closures are not refreshed, patch the captured data in place after each success (`camps[cid].role = value`, `rec.teamId = teamId`, or `delete` it when cleared). convertPendingMember(key, camps[CAMP.id] || rec, lists) reads rec.teamId, and the grant branch decides on `existing`, so stale closures would drop a pending member's team or re-grant over a record. Independently, make the Add form survive any rebuild: before `body.innerHTML = ...` in renderMemberList, capture `#member-add-id/name/role/camps/team` values, and restore them after bindMemberList (jelly-input and jelly-segmented accept `.value`). Do not re-run bindMemberList on a kept shell or the Add button double-binds and a second add fires.

confirmed.title: Lock screen cannot scroll: opening 'Alternative sign in' on a short viewport pushes controls off-screen
confirmed.symptom: On a 360x640 phone, opening 'Alternative sign in' clips the logo at the top and pushes the error text below the fold. In landscape (667x375) the Google button is off-screen at the top and the phone/email forms' lower buttons are off-screen at the bottom, with no way to scroll to them. An Android keyboard shrinking the viewport has the same effect.
confirmed.trigger: Load with no auth hint, tap 'Alternative sign in' at 360x640 or 667x375. Run p13_lock_alt.cjs and view lock-alt-360x640.png.
confirmed.evidence: 360x640 open: logo top -41, box 721 px tall in a 640 px viewport. 667x375 open: logo -166, Google button -88 to -16, box 707 px tall in a 375 px viewport. #lock-screen computed overflow-y is visible, scrollHeight 681 vs clientHeight 640, and #app is display:none so there is no document scroll to fall back on.
confirmed.rootCause: html.locked .lock-screen is position:fixed; inset:0; display:flex; align-items:center with no overflow handling. A flex child taller than the container is centred, so it overflows equally top and bottom, and the fixed container can never scroll.
confirmed.proposedFix: Add `overflow-y:auto` to .lock-screen and use safe centering: remove `align-items:center` and give `.lock-box` `margin:auto`. The box then centres when it fits and scrolls from the top when it does not.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v5_lock.cjs) with a real touch tap on the disclosure. At 360x640 open: logo [-41,-12] is entirely off-screen and the box is [-41,681] (722 px tall) in 640. At 375x667: box [-20,687], logo clipped at the top. At 667x375: logo [-166,-137], Google button [-88,-16] off-screen, email field [349,405] and #email-link-send [414,458] below the fold. #lock-screen has overflow-y:visible, scrollTop stays 0 after a wheel, and #app is display:none, so nothing can scroll. Correction to the claim: in portrait at 360x640 and 375x667 every control is still inside the viewport (only the logo and the bottom error line are clipped), so the 'cannot reach controls' impact is landscape, or a shrunk-by-keyboard viewport. That is why I rate it low, not med. The fix is three lines of CSS.
verdict.refinedFix: styles.css html.locked .lock-screen: replace `align-items:center` with `align-items:flex-start`, add `overflow-y:auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch`, and add `html.locked .lock-screen .lock-box { margin: 0 auto; }`. For the pure overflow fix, `.lock-box{margin:auto}` keeps it vertically centred when it fits. If you also adopt the anchor fix for lock-recenter-jump, add `padding-top:max(1.5rem,14vh)`. Verified at 360x640 and 667x375: scrollTop reaches 195/408, the email Send button ends at 533/268 inside the viewport, and the box keeps 24 px of bottom padding. Risk: `.lock-box.shake` uses transform, which is unaffected. Make sure the new `overflow` does not catch the sign-in error line.

confirmed.title: A Google sign-in error remounts the phone/email forms and wipes what was typed
confirmed.symptom: Typing a phone number or email in the Alternative sign in forms, then getting any Google error (popup blocked, offline), clears both fields because the forms are rebuilt.

confirmed.proposedFix: Mount once: skip when `slot.firstElementChild` already exists, or only call mount() on the first transition into 'signin'.

verdict.reasoning: p29 reproduced: both #phone-number and #email-link-address go from typed values to '', the node identity changes, and the details stays open. showAuthScreen('signin', ...) re-mounts both slots whenever it is called. Callers include showSignInError for Google popup-blocked/offline errors (app.js:8203), the auth-start error (8279) and the signed-out re-emit (8346). Worse than the claim: a phone flow already on the 'enter code' step is reset to the number step, and an email 'Sent!' status is cleared with the Send button re-enabled. confirmed.title: Drawer and dialog backdrop cuts in and out in one frame instead of fading
confirmed.symptom: When a drawer or dialog opens, the dimmed and blurred layer appears at full strength in the first frame while the sheet slides in. On close, the dim stays at full strength until the sheet has finished leaving, then vanishes in a single frame.
confirmed.trigger: Open and close Settings, History, Members, Phone alerts or the pickers (p5_drawers.cjs, p10_picker.cjs).
confirmed.evidence: Settings open: backdrop opacity 1.00 at t=23 ms (sheet still at y=930 off-screen). X-close: backdrop 1.00 through t=319 ms, then display:none at t=350 ms. Team picker X-close: backdrop 1.00 on every frame while the dialog itself fades 1.00 to 0.18, then the host disappears. The Settings to History handoff does not flash (backdrop continuous).
confirmed.rootCause: In vendor/jelly.js the drawer/dialog CSS has `:host{display:none}` and `.backdrop{opacity:0;transition:opacity .3s}`, with `:host([open]){display:block}` and `[open] .backdrop{opacity:1}`. The element goes from display:none to displayed in the same style recalc, so no transition has a before-change style and nothing animates. On close the host is hidden at once when the animated exit ends.
confirmed.location: vendor/jelly.js:5421 (drawer CSS, Wi) and the dialog CSS (Xi); both open/close paths in the Oi (dialog) and Ni (drawer) classes
confirmed.proposedFix: In the vendored copy, animate the backdrop with WAAPI next to the sheet animation (`backdrop.animate([{opacity:0},{opacity:1}],{duration:250,fill:'both'})` in afterOpen, and the reverse in the animated close). Alternatively use `@starting-style` plus visibility instead of display toggling.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v8_drawers.cjs). Settings open: backdrop opacity 1.00 at t=28 ms while the sheet is still at top 930, so there is no fade-in. X-close: backdrop 1.00 on every frame through the sheet exit (t=26-300 ms), then display none at t=341. Team picker X-close: bd1.00 on every frame while the dialog fades 1.00 to 0.18, then gone. The settings to history handoff is continuous, so the auditor's note there is right. Root cause confirmed in vendor/jelly.js: :host{display:none} with .backdrop{opacity:0;transition:opacity .3s}, and `[open]` flips display and opacity in the same style recalc, so no transition runs. It is a subtle one-frame dim snap with a 42% scrim plus blur, hence low.
verdict.refinedFix: Open side needs no vendor edit, because `.backdrop` has `part="backdrop"`. Add to styles.css: `@keyframes jelly-backdrop-in { from { opacity: 0 } to { opacity: 1 } } jelly-drawer[open]::part(backdrop), jelly-dialog[open]::part(backdrop) { animation: jelly-backdrop-in .3s ease both; }`. Verified: opacity goes 0.00, 0.04, 0.11, 0.47, 0.67, 0.95, 1.00 over about 340 ms. The close fade cannot be done from app CSS, because `open` stays set until the exit animation ends and `closing` is only a JS property. It needs a small patch in vendor/jelly.js's close() (animate the backdrop with the sheet), so skip it unless you want to touch the vendored file, which already carries local patches. prefers-reduced-motion: add the animation to the existing reduced-motion block or `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){...{animation:none}}`.
verdict.location: vendor/jelly.js:5319 (dialog CSS Xi) and 5421 (drawer CSS Wi); app-side fix in styles.css

It is a real but brief inconsistency, and only visible on a deliberate Appearance change. The OS dusk flip in Auto mode is CSS-media only (no JS listener) and uses the same body transition, so a JS-only fix would miss it.
verdict.refinedFix: Simplest and covers the OS flip too: delete `transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease;` from `body` (styles.css:230). The remaining thin border fades are barely visible. If you want the whole flip atomic from the Appearance control: in applyTheme(), `document.documentElement.classList.add('theme-switching'); requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => document.documentElement.classList.remove('theme-switching')));` with `html.theme-switching, html.theme-switching *, html.theme-switching *::before, html.theme-switching *::after { transition: none !important; }`. Verified: 0 running transitions and the body already at the dark colour on the next frame. Do not apply the class on the init call (it would suppress nothing useful, but is wasted work). It does not reach Jelly shadow roots, which repaint through jelly-theme-change anyway.

confirmed.title: Schedule sheet stays stuck partly dragged if the touch is cancelled
confirmed.symptom: If the system cancels a header drag (a gesture takeover or an incoming call), the sheet stays offset downward, leaving a gap at the bottom, until the next touch.
confirmed.trigger: Dispatch touchstart, touchmove then touchcancel on .schedule-header. Run p22_swipe_cancel.cjs. The real-world trigger rate is unknown; the state is measured, the trigger is synthetic.
confirmed.evidence: After touchcancel: sheet.style.transform 'translateY(60px)' and transition 'none' persist (top 144 vs 84 at rest).
confirmed.rootCause: wireSchedule() handles touchstart, touchmove and touchend but not touchcancel. touchstart sets `transition='none'` and the reset only lives in touchend.
confirmed.proposedFix: Add `header.addEventListener('touchcancel', reset)`, where reset clears transform, restores the transition and sets startY = null.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v11_cancel.cjs): after touchstart, touchmove, touchcancel the sheet keeps style.transform 'translateY(60px)' and transition 'none' (top 144 vs 84 at rest). wireSchedule registers no touchcancel handler. The state is measured. The real-world trigger (OS gesture takeover, incoming call, iOS edge swipe) is unmeasurable headlessly and likely rare. The sheet recovers when the user closes it (closeSchedule clears the transform) or does another header drag.
verdict.refinedFix: app.js wireSchedule: add `header.addEventListener('touchcancel', () => { if (startY == null) return; startY = null; sheet.style.transition = ''; sheet.style.transform = ''; });`. Combine with the spring-back transition from the swipe-dismiss fix, so it eases back rather than snapping. No stale-closure risk (startY and sheet are in the same closure).

confirmed.title: Schedule sheet changes height per day, so the day chips jump away from the finger

confirmed.title: Every renderAll while the builder is open throws the page back to scrollY 0
confirmed.symptom: In the week builder, any reorder arrow, Add day/team/step, Remove step, notice Post, or any remote update while the builder is open snaps the page to the very top. Move game #14 down and the list jumps to the top. Add a day or team and the new row is off-screen at the bottom.
confirmed.trigger: Open Settings -> Set up the week as an editor. Scroll down on any tab (Games list, Days, Notice, ...). Tap a reorder arrow, Add day/team/step, or Remove step. Or let any renderAll fire: a remote score snapshot from another editor, a members-list change, a clock settling. Reproduced identically in the senior camp.
confirmed.evidence: Measured. renderAll() with scrollY at 1270 (games), 1061 (days), 4927 (notice) gives scrollY 0 synchronously, before any paint. Real touch taps: games reorder 1370->0, days reorder 547->0, notice step move 1948->0, Add day 1161->0 (doc grew 2005->2343), Add team 182->0, Add notice step 3798->0, Remove step 2293->0. Real handleRemoteSnapshot() with a changed result: 900->0 on the Games tab (jelly-tabs element replaced, 223 ms) and 900->0 on the Notice tab (173 ms). Game-editor-internal re-renders (format card, session chip, add/move/remove section) do NOT jump (scrollY 1372->1372), because they replace only card.innerHTML. An in-page patch that keeps the jelly-tabs shell and re-renders only the active card kept scrollY 1500->1500 (p39).
confirmed.rootCause: renderSettings() does `view.innerHTML = ...` on every call (settings.js:60). That inserts five EMPTY .settings-card divs, and the Jelly connectedCallbacks (jelly-tabs, jelly-button, ...) force layout at that moment. The document is then only a few hundred px tall, so the browser clamps scrollY to 0. The cards are filled afterwards by renderSettingsSection (settings.js:96-98), but the scroll offset is already lost. renderAll calls renderSettings unconditionally while builderOpen() (app.js:7850), so every own action and every remote snapshot does this.
confirmed.proposedFix: Make renderSettings build the shell once, the same pattern as renderDayTabs. If jelly-tabs.settings-tabs already exists, patch the 'Last edited' line, set the tabs `value` only if it changed, and re-render only the ACTIVE card in place via renderSettingsSection(tab, card). Re-render the other cards lazily in the tabs `change` handler. Skip the card write entirely when its inputs are unchanged, using a per-card signature of the state slice it reads (games list: config.games/days/sessions + result keys; days: config.days + game counts; teams: state.teams; notice: state.notice + teams; data: nothing). A remote score change then touches nothing but the Games list's result dots. As a cheap safety net, also save window.scrollY before any full rebuild and restore it afterwards.

verdict.location: settings.js:48-99 (renderSettings; innerHTML at line 60) called unconditionally from app.js:7850
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced in my own probes (builder-verify/v1, v2, v7). renderAll() with the builder open sets scrollY to 0 synchronously on every tab (games 822->0, days 696->0, teams 109->0, notice 3016->0, data 42->0). Real touch taps: games reorder 1370->0, days reorder 547->0, Add day 1161->0, Add team 182->0. A real handleRemoteSnapshot() with a changed result (canAdopt=true, midEntry=false) goes 900->0 on both Games and Notice tabs. No paint happens in between, so the user just sees a jump to top. Root cause is right in spirit, but my testing shows it is broader than 'empty cards'. The clamp happens whenever a rebuild briefly shrinks the document while Jelly elements upgrade. Replacing only the Data card's innerHTML (v5, v6) also clamps scrollY 60->0 even though the shell is kept. So the shell-keeping, active-card-only fix on its own is NOT sufficient. In my patch run (v4), games/days/teams/notice kept their offset but Data still went 42->0. Scroll restoration is verified: saving scrollY, running the rebuild and calling scrollTo(0,y) in the same task restores it exactly on every tab (v7), and a real days-reorder tap stays at 547->547 with no visible frame in between.
verdict.refinedFix: Two layers. (1) Immediate 3-line safety net, no rebuild change: in renderSettings, `const y = window.scrollY;` at the top and `if (window.scrollY !== y) window.scrollTo(0, y);` at the end (after the card fill loop). Verified on all five tabs and on real taps. Applying it as a wrapper around the existing renderSettings gave an exact scrollY match everywhere. (2) Structural fix, shared with builder-tabs-pill-respring and builder-rebuild-jank: keep the <jelly-tabs.settings-tabs> shell (back button, h2, tabs, five .settings-card panels) and build it only when view.querySelector('jelly-tabs.settings-tabs') is missing. Patch the 'Last edited' line into a stable slot element and only set the tabs `value` attribute if it differs. Re-render only the active card, mark the other cards data-stale, and render a stale card inside the tabs `change` handler (verified working: v4 'lazy' test). Keep (1) even after (2), because a single-card innerHTML rewrite can still clamp on short tabs such as Data. Risks to guard: wireNoticeTab closes over `const n = noticeBoard()`, so any skip-unchanged logic for the Notice card must key on the full JSON of state.notice (or the object identity), otherwise handlers edit an orphaned object after a remote snapshot replaces state.notice. wireDaysTab, wireTeamsTab and wireGameRows re-read state at click time, so they are safe. Do not skip a card based on state alone. Use the app's own setHtmlIfChanged pattern (compare html AND el.__dom === el.innerHTML), because jelly-checkbox, details and .day-delete-error mutate their own DOM. That means splitting each renderXTab into an xHTML() builder plus a wire step, so the wire step runs only when the markup was actually written.

confirmed.title: Builder tab-bar pill re-springs from the Games tab on every rebuild when another tab is active
confirmed.symptom: Whenever the builder re-renders while Days, Teams, Notice or Data is the active tab, the blue active pill reappears over 'Games' and slides across to the active tab with a squashed, wobbling spring. For roughly half a second the active tab's label is white on grey and unreadable. It happens after every reorder, add or remove in those tabs and on every remote update. It also slides when the builder is first opened with a remembered non-Games tab.
confirmed.trigger: Builder open on Days/Teams/Notice/Data. Tap any reorder arrow, Add, or Remove, or let a remote snapshot arrive. Or set the last-used tab to teams, close, and reopen via openBuilder(). The Games tab is unaffected because it is index 0.
confirmed.evidence: Measured. After renderAll the jelly-segmented pillX starts at -140 (the Games slot) with index = 4, placed = true, pillTarget = +141. The pill then travels and settles in 400-550 ms. Initial distance to target: days 69 px (400 ms), teams 140 px (469 ms), notice 210 px (542 ms), data 281 px (544 ms), games 1 px (80 ms). Opening the builder with remembered tab=teams: 140 px, 462 ms. Screencast strip of the tab bar (f33_tabbar_strip.png in the probe dir) shows the pill jumping to the Days area and sliding to Notice while the 'Notice' label is white on grey for frames 2-10.
confirmed.rootCause: renderSettings always re-creates <jelly-tabs> (the comment at settings.js:56-59 says so deliberately). On connect the inner jelly-segmented places its pill at the first segment, probably because the segments are not upgraded yet when onShape runs. It then springs to the real `value` once they upgrade. The home day tabs avoided this in v183 by updating panels in place; the builder tabs were not converted.
confirmed.location: settings.js:60-70 (jelly-tabs created inside the innerHTML template)
confirmed.proposedFix: Same fix as builder-rebuild-scroll-jump: never re-create the settings jelly-tabs. Create it once, then only set its `value` attribute. Verified in-page: with the shell kept, the pill's max distance to target is 0 and the tabs element is the same node. For the first-open case, create the shell once at app start or first builder open, or wait until the segmented control has measured before un-hiding.

verdict.location: settings.js:60-70 (jelly-tabs created inside the innerHTML template); mechanism in vendor/jelly.js jelly-segmented.sync()/onShape()
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v3). After renderAll on the Notice tab, jelly-segmented pillX starts at -140 (Games slot) with target +70 and index 3, then slides over about 550 ms. A screencast strip (builder-verify/v3_strip.png) shows the blue pill appearing around Days and wobbling across to Notice, while the 'Notice' label is white on grey for roughly 9 frames. First-open with a remembered tab=teams: firstPillX -140, travel 140 px (v8). Root cause confirmed in the vendor code: on first sync the jelly-segment children are not yet upgraded, so `o.value` is undefined, findIndex is -1, index falls back to 0 and the pill is `placed` at segment 0. The segments then upgrade and re-run sync(), which moves pillTarget but not pillX, so the pill springs. Verified in-page that keeping the shell removes the rebuild case (pillMaxDist 0, same tabs node, v4). BUT keeping the shell does NOT fix the first-open case: with the shell patch the first creation with tab=teams still travels 140 px (v8). The proposal's 'create the shell once at app start' is vague and would still spring when the stored tab is not Games.
verdict.refinedFix: Keep the shell (see scroll-jump fix) for the rebuild case. For the first creation, snap the pill right after the shell is written, in the same task (before paint): `const seg = tabs.shadowRoot.querySelector('jelly-segmented'); seg.pillX = seg.pillTarget; seg.pillXVelocity = 0; seg.requestFrame && seg.requestFrame();`. Verified in-page with tab=teams: firstPillX 0, maxDist 0, idx 2 (v9). Put it in one small helper (for example settleTabPill(tabsEl)) so renderDayTabs can reuse it (see extraFindings). Do not edit vendor/jelly.js unless the owner accepts a vendor diff. Risk: only snap on creation, never on a user-driven change, or the spring on real tab taps is lost. Severity is med rather than high because it is cosmetic (about 0.5 s), editor-only, and happens once per builder action, but it does fire on every action while on Days/Teams/Notice/Data.

confirmed.title: 'Back to scoreboard' with a half-edited game leaves a hidden dirty draft that freezes live updates on that phone
confirmed.symptom: An editor opens a game, types anything (even one character), then taps '<- Back to scoreboard'. No confirm appears. The scoreboard looks normal, but from then on that device stops adopting other editors' scores and config changes. A deferred snapshot stays pending forever, auto-reload on deploy is blocked, the 5-minute idle card-collapse never runs, and sign-out or camp switch show a false 'unsynced work' warning. It self-heals only after opening a different game in the editor or reloading.
confirmed.trigger: Settings -> Set up the week -> open any game or + New game -> type in a field (builderDirty() becomes true) -> tap '<- Back to scoreboard' at the top. Then deliver any remote snapshot (another editor saves a score).
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p30). After Back: view='home', editGameId=null, but gameDraft is still set, builderDirty()=true, editorMidEntry()=true, canAdoptRemote()=false. handleRemoteSnapshot() with a new result: remoteApplied=false, remoteRefetchPending=true. 3.5 s of idle ticks later: still remoteRefetchPending=true, editorMidEntry=true, reloadBlocked()=true. No dialog was shown (dialogs=0).
confirmed.rootCause: The settings-back-btn handler (settings.js:72-77) sets state.ui.view='home' and editGameId=null but never clears gameDraft/gameDraftFor and never asks about unsaved edits (leaveGameEditor does both). builderDirty() (settings.js:31-33) only checks the draft against its snapshot, not that the editor is actually open. editorMidEntry() (app.js:7670), reloadBlocked() (app.js:7764-7770), collapseCardsForIdle (app.js:7793) and hasUnsyncedWork (app.js:8528-8530) all consume it.
confirmed.proposedFix: In the back-button handler, route through the same logic as leaveGameEditor: if builderDirty() confirm 'Discard your changes?', then null gameDraft and gameDraftFor. Also harden builderDirty() to return false unless `state.ui.view === 'settings' && state.ui.editGameId` (and likewise clear the draft when renderAll force-closes the builder for a demoted role at app.js:7820), so a stale draft can never block sync.

verdict.location: settings.js:72-77 (back button handler), settings.js:31-33 (builderDirty); consumers app.js:7670 (editorMidEntry), 7764-7770 (reloadBlocked), 7797 (collapseCardsForIdle), 8528-8530 (hasUnsyncedWork)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with real taps and keyboard (v10). Open a game, type 'X' into #gd-name (builderDirty=true), tap '<- Back to scoreboard': no dialog, view='home', editGameId=null, but gameDraft still set, builderDirty=true, editorMidEntry=true, canAdoptRemote=false. handleRemoteSnapshot() with a new result: applied=false, remoteRefetchPending=true, and still true after 3.5 s of idle ticks, with reloadBlocked=true and hasUnsyncedWork=true. Code path matches the claim: the back handler never clears gameDraft/gameDraftFor and never confirms, unlike leaveGameEditor (settings.js:668-676). One extra symptom I measured: reopening the SAME game afterwards silently resurrects the half-edited draft ('ShieldsX'), because ensureGameDraft returns early for the same id; opening a different game rebuilds a clean draft and self-heals the freeze. Severity kept high for impact (a director's phone silently stops adopting other editors' scores and blocks auto-reload on deploy). Frequency is moderate: it needs an edit followed by Back instead of Cancel.
verdict.refinedFix: In the back-button handler, mirror leaveGameEditor: `if (state.ui.editGameId && builderDirty() && !confirm('Discard your changes to this game?')) return; state.ui.editGameId = null; gameDraft = null; gameDraftFor = null;` before saveState()/renderAll(). Harden builderDirty() as well: `return state.ui.view === 'settings' && !!state.ui.editGameId && !!gameDraft && JSON.stringify(gameDraft) !== gameDraftSnapshot;`, so no future path can leave a hidden dirty draft blocking sync. Also null the draft where renderAll force-closes the builder for a demoted role (app.js:7820). Risk: if the builderDirty() guard is added without clearing the draft, reopening the same game still shows the old edits (draft reuse), which is acceptable but should be a deliberate choice. If tab switches keep the draft (see builder-tab-switch-silent-discard), builderDirty() must stay true while on other tabs, i.e. the view/editGameId condition above still holds.

confirmed.title: Each builder rebuild costs a ~1.3 s main-thread freeze on a phone-class CPU, spent mostly on hidden tabs
confirmed.symptom: After tapping a reorder arrow, or whenever a remote score lands while the builder is open, the page freezes for over a second on a mid-range phone. Further taps are swallowed and the keyboard or tab pill stutters.
confirmed.trigger: Builder open (any tab). Tap a reorder arrow, or deliver a remote state change. Measured with 4x CPU throttle on a 22-game junior week.
confirmed.evidence: Measured. renderAll with the builder closed: 18 ms median (4x). Builder open, median/max at 4x: games 1235/1334 ms, days 993/1900, teams 889/906, notice 1050/1218, data 587/642. So even with the cheap Data tab active it costs ~0.6 s, because all five panels are rebuilt. Unthrottled it is 157-230 ms. One reorder tap at 4x produced longtasks [1334, 244, 143, 147, 88] ms. One remote score snapshot produced [1190, 371, 199, 248, 70] ms. Each rebuild re-creates ~230 Jelly elements (junior): 84 jelly-input, 44+ jelly-icon-button, 44 jelly-badge, 24 jelly-textarea, 10 jelly-select, 80 jelly-option, 18 jelly-button.
confirmed.rootCause: renderSettings re-renders all five tab cards, four of them hidden, with fresh Jelly components on every renderAll, including renderAlls that changed nothing the builder shows (a remote score changes only the Games list's result dots).
confirmed.location: settings.js:96-98 (forEach over all SETTINGS_TABS) called from app.js:7850
confirmed.proposedFix: Same root fix as the scroll jump: render only the visible card, only when its signature changed, and the others lazily on tab activation. An idle renderAll then costs ~0 in the builder.

verdict.location: settings.js:96-98 (forEach over all SETTINGS_TABS) called from app.js:7850
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v11). Jelly elements in #settings-view on the Games tab: 230 (jelly-icon-button 94, input 42, option 40, badge 22, textarea 12, button 9, select 5, tabs/panels 6). Their per-type counts (84 jelly-input etc.) are about double what I see, but the total matches. renderAll median: builder closed 2 ms unthrottled and 10 ms at 4x. Builder open unthrottled: games 179, days 200, teams 143, notice 168, data 115 ms. At 4x CPU: games 1068, days 957, teams 831, notice 979, data 552 ms. So even the cheap Data tab costs about 0.55 s because all five cards are rebuilt, which confirms the 'mostly hidden tabs' root cause. Their 4x numbers (1235/993/889/1050/587) are in line with mine. Important nuance from my in-page test (v11): active-card-only rendering alone is not enough. At 4x it still cost games 483, days 782, notice 572 ms (teams 278, data 71). Only skipping an unchanged card removes the cost.
verdict.refinedFix: Do the shell-keeping and active-card-only fix described under builder-rebuild-scroll-jump, then add the unchanged-card skip with the app's setHtmlIfChanged pattern. Refactor renderGamesTab/renderDaysTab/renderTeamsTab/renderNoticeTab/renderDataTab to build markup first, `if (setHtmlIfChanged(card, html)) wireX(card)`. For the Games card, the only thing a remote score changes is the result-dot spans, so an unchanged-markup skip would still rebuild when a result lands. That is acceptable (one card) but could be a targeted DOM patch. Never skip a card whose wire step closes over a state object (Notice's `n`), without re-wiring when that object's identity changes.

confirmed.title: Tapping another builder tab silently throws away an unsaved game draft (no confirm)
confirmed.symptom: While writing a new game (name, rules sections, timer...), one slip on the Days/Teams/Notice/Data tab bar deletes the whole draft and shows the games list. '<- All games' and 'Cancel' ask 'Discard your changes?', but the tab bar does not.
confirmed.trigger: Games tab -> + New game -> type a name and tap '+ Add section' -> tap the 'Days' tab segment -> tap 'Games' again.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p29). Before: builderDirty()=true, draft name 'My brand new game with lots of rules', 1 rule section. After the tab tap: editGameId=null, gameDraft=null, dialogs shown = 0. Back on Games the list is shown.
confirmed.rootCause: The jelly-tabs `change` handler discards the draft without checking builderDirty() ('same semantics as before', settings.js:83-92). The draft already lives in JS memory.
confirmed.proposedFix: Don't discard on tab change: leave state.ui.editGameId and gameDraft alone so the editor is simply still there when the Games tab is revisited. Or, if builderDirty(), confirm first and revert the tab on cancel.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with real taps (v12). + New game, typed 'My brand new game' (builderDirty=true), tapped the Days segment: tab='days', editGameId=null, gameDraft=null, builderDirty=false, dialogs=0. The comment says 'same semantics as before', so it is inherited behaviour rather than a deliberate product decision, while '<- All games' and Cancel (leaveGameEditor) do confirm. Data loss on a one-tap slip.
verdict.refinedFix: Simplest and consistent: delete the discard block from the change handler, so state.ui.editGameId and gameDraft survive a tab switch and the editor is simply still there when Games is revisited. builderDirty() stays true meanwhile, which correctly keeps remote merges and auto-reload from wiping it. This requires the back button to confirm and clear (see builder-dirty-draft-freezes-sync) so a kept draft cannot be abandoned silently. The alternative (confirm, then revert the tab on cancel via tabs.setAttribute('value', previous)) works because the change handler's `key === state.ui.settingsTab` early-return stops re-entry, but it re-plays the 220 ms panel fade (jelly-tabs.activate animates on a programmatic value change) and is more code.

confirmed.title: Returning from the builder replays the 'rise in' animation on every open home card, and the home scroll position is lost
