confirmed.evidence: Measured (p17, p27). Animations started within 2 frames of returning, with three cards open: joy-rise x3 on .settings-row.card-visibility-row, x1 each on #day-tabs, p.standings-hint, p#sync-status, .standings-actions, .table-scroll, p.card-desc, #cleanup-body. Home scrollY 700 before the builder, 0 after returning (doc 2932 tall).
confirmed.rootCause: body.builder-open sets display:none on every .main-wrap child (styles.css:4748-4751). A CSS animation restarts when an element goes from display:none to displayed, and `jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card[open] > *:not([slot=header])` always carries the joy-rise animation (styles.css:5785). openBuilder also calls window.scrollTo({top:0}) (app.js:7873) and nothing remembers the home offset.
confirmed.proposedFix: Run joy-rise only transiently: add a class (for example .card-opening) to the jelly-collapsible when the user toggles it open, remove it after ~500 ms, and scope the CSS rule to that class. That removes every replay source at once (un-hide, re-insert, chat takeover). Also store window.scrollY when entering the builder or chat and restore it on return.

verdict.location: styles.css:5785-5790 (joy-rise on open collapsible children) with styles.css:4748-4751 and 4757-4758 (display:none takeovers); app.js:7865-7874 (openBuilder scrollTo)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced for the builder (v13) and for chat (v14). With a card open, clicking Back from the builder starts joy-rise animations within 2 frames on the open card's children (settings-row, p.card-desc, #cleanup-body in my run; their run had more cards open). Returning from the chat takeover does the same (#cleanup-body). Home scrollY 700 before the builder is 0 after Back, and 400 -> 0 after chat. Root cause is right: the always-on `[open] > *:not([slot=header])` animation restarts when display:none -> shown. Validated the proposed fix in-page (v35): with the rule changed to animation:none and a transient .card-opening class added on the toggle event, a user tap on a card header still plays joy-rise (3 animations), and returning from the builder plays none. Severity is med rather than high: the effect is a 0.38 s fade/rise of content that was already visible, and it needs an open card.
verdict.refinedFix: CSS: change the rule to `jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card[open] > *:not([slot="header"]) { animation: none; }` plus `jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card.card-opening[open] > *:not([slot="header"]) { animation: joy-rise 0.38s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) backwards; }` (keep the nth-child delays scoped to .card-opening). JS: one capture listener, `document.addEventListener('toggle', e => { const c = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card'); if (c && c.hasAttribute('open')) { c.classList.add('card-opening'); setTimeout(() => c.classList.remove('card-opening'), 700); } }, true)`. Verified the toggle event reaches the document. Scroll: store `state.ui`-independent `homeScrollY = window.scrollY` in openBuilder/openChat and `window.scrollTo(0, homeScrollY)` after the renderAll in the Back/closeChat paths. The existing openBuilder scrollTo({top:0}) is intentional and should stay.

confirmed.title: Touching a list row to start a scroll shrinks it to 93% and snaps it back
confirmed.symptom: On the Games list (full-width row buttons), putting a finger down to scroll makes the row visibly shrink and pop back when the scroll starts: a twitch on almost every touch-scroll over the list.
confirmed.trigger: Touch-drag vertically starting on a .game-row-main row in Settings -> Set up the week -> Games. The delegated press handler is app-wide, so any button, link or summary does it, including .format-card and .team-chip.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p25, CDP touch). Timeline of the row: pointerdown -> joy-pressed added at 36 ms, transform animates scale 1 -> 0.93 over ~100 ms, pointercancel when the scroll starts (252 ms) -> class removed and transform jumps straight to none. The transition only exists on .joy-pressed, so release is instant, not animated. A fast flick would show a partial shrink followed by a snap.
confirmed.rootCause: The pointerdown listener adds .joy-pressed immediately to anything matching button, a, summary, jelly-button, jelly-chip, jelly-segment or jelly-icon-button, regardless of size or whether the touch becomes a scroll (app.js:8087-8091). The scale rule lives only on .joy-pressed with its transition (styles.css:5770-5773).
confirmed.proposedFix: Delay adding .joy-pressed ~70-90 ms and cancel the timer on pointermove, pointercancel or touchmove. Skip the scale for wide or row-like targets (for example width > 200 px, or opt out via a class on .game-row-main and .format-card). Optionally put the `transition: transform` on the base state so release animates instead of snapping.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with CDP touch events (v15). On a 228x55 .game-row-main: class added at about 30 ms, transform eases 1 -> 0.93 over about 100 ms, the touch becomes a scroll (pointercancel at about 246 ms) and the transform jumps straight back to none in one frame, because the transition lives only on .joy-pressed. It is app-wide (any button/a/summary/chip), so it affects every user touch-scrolling over buttons, not just the builder. Severity med for frequency, but the visual amplitude is small (7%), so this is a polish issue. Validated the proposed delay fix in-page (v16): with an 80 ms delayed add cleared on pointermove/pointercancel, a quick flick never adds joy-pressed (transform stays none), and a held touch still presses.
verdict.refinedFix: In the pointerdown handler replace the immediate add with a timer: `clearTimeout(joyPressTimer); joyPressTarget = t; joyPressTimer = setTimeout(() => { if (joyPressTarget) joyPressTarget.classList.add('joy-pressed'); }, 80);` and clear it (`clearTimeout; joyPressTarget = null`) in pointermove, pointercancel and pointerup. In the pointerup handler only add joy-pop when joy-pressed was actually applied (a fast tap that never reached 80 ms should still get the existing sparkle but skip the pop, or apply both). Optionally skip scaling on wide row targets (offsetWidth > 200). Risk: the existing global pointerup handler removes .joy-pressed from every element; keep that. Do not move `transition: transform` to the base state of every tappable, because Jelly components run their own canvas physics and the repo's own rule warns against broad transitions.

confirmed.title: Builder layout: long single-column tabs with no sticky navigation or save bar, and no history entry
confirmed.symptom: On a 390 px phone the tab bar and Back link scroll away, so switching tabs or leaving means scrolling back to the top. The game editor is ~2.2-2.8k px tall with Save/Cancel at the very bottom. The Notice tab is ~5.9k px. The system Back gesture leaves the app instead of closing the builder.
confirmed.trigger: Open the builder at 390x844. Games list (22 games), Days, Notice, game editor (tournament game with rules and extras).
confirmed.evidence: Measured. Document heights: games list 2214, days 2005, teams 1026, notice 5871, data 914, game editor 2216 (tally) to 2823 (tournament with tracker + extras open) at 844 px viewport. getComputedStyle position of jelly-tabs and the back button is 'static'. history.length is 2 before and 2 after openBuilder + editor (history.state null): the builder and editor are state-only takeovers with no pushState/popstate anywhere. Home scroll position is lost on a round trip (700 -> 0).
confirmed.rootCause: The builder is one full-page takeover (body.builder-open) with a static header, one long column per tab, and navigation by mutating state.ui.view only.
confirmed.proposedFix: Make the tab bar sticky (position: sticky; top: 0 with a background). Add a sticky bottom action bar (Save / Cancel) in the game editor. Collapse the Notice tab's rows into disclosures, or split Wording / Assignments / Steps / Preview. Push a history entry in openBuilder and close on popstate. Remember and restore the home scroll offset.

verdict.location: styles.css:5062-5080 (settings-view / settings-tabs); settings.js:354-433 (renderGameEditor); app.js:7855-7874; styles.css:222-231 (html/body overflow-x:hidden)
verdict.reasoning: The facts reproduce (v17) at 390x844: document heights games 2214, days 2005, teams 1026, notice 5871, data 914, game editor 2216 (tally) to 2516 (tournament; theirs 2823 with extras open). jelly-tabs and the back button are position:static, so they scroll away. The Save button sits at y 2314 of a 2516 page. history.length stays 2 before and after openBuilder and the editor, and history.state is null. history.back() navigates away from the page, so the Back gesture leaves the app. This is design feedback in answer to the owner's layout question, and the measurements are accurate. IMPORTANT correction to the proposed fix: `position: sticky; top: 0` on the tab bar does not work in this codebase. I tested three variants on the Notice tab at scrollY 1500 (v18, v19, v21): sticky on jelly-tabs::part(tabs) (the bar sits inside the component's shadow `.bar` div, so it has no room to stick), sticky on the jelly-tabs host (the host contains all the panels), and a standalone sticky <jelly-segmented> placed before the tabs. All stayed at top -1384. The standalone bar fails because html and body both have overflow-x:hidden, which makes body a scroll container (overflow-y computes to auto) that never scrolls, so sticky has no scrollport. Changing html,body to overflow-x:clip made the standalone bar stick (top 0) with no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 390).
verdict.refinedFix: For a sticky builder nav: (1) change `html { overflow-x: hidden }` and `body { overflow-x: hidden }` (styles.css:222, 231) to `overflow-x: clip` (same bleed-clipping purpose; Safari 16+, the same floor as vendor/jelly.js's iOS 16.4 requirement), and re-run the 390 px overflow checks; (2) render the five-way switcher as a standalone sticky <jelly-segmented> (opaque background wrapper) above the panels and show/hide the panels yourself, because the bar inside jelly-tabs cannot be made sticky. For the game editor, a sticky bottom action bar for Save/Cancel needs the same overflow fix. History: pushState in openBuilder/openChat plus a popstate handler that closes the takeover is small and self-contained, but applies to chat and game views as well. Store and restore the home scroll offset (see builder-return-joy-rise-replay). Splitting or collapsing the 5.9k px Notice tab is a design decision for the owner.

confirmed.title: A config edit's own echo can register as 'someone else changed it' and trigger a second full builder rebuild ~400-500 ms later
confirmed.symptom: After Add day or saving a new game, the builder flashes and rebuilds a second time half a second after the first (and jumps scroll again if the user already scrolled).
confirmed.trigger: On a synced device whose state.config came from the server (key-sorted): tap '+ Add day' on the Days tab, or Save a new game. 400 ms later pushConfig() fires and RTDB echoes the value back with sorted keys and `dow: null` dropped.
confirmed.evidence: Measured with a STUBBED RTDB echo (fbConfigRef.set fires the listener synchronously with a key-sorted, null-pruned copy; p7). Add day: renderSettings at 12 ms (own) and again at 411 ms (echo). Save new game: rebuild at ~1131 ms and again at 1615 ms (echo at 1610). A plain reorder of existing days produced only one rebuild; renaming a day and blurring produced none. Not run against a live Firebase.
confirmed.rootCause: applyRemoteConfig compares JSON.stringify(state.config) to the adopted remote (app.js:2294 and 2307). RTDB returns children in sorted key order and drops nulls and empties, so any locally created object (new day {id,name,dow:null,note}, new game) stringifies differently from its echo, even though nothing changed.
confirmed.proposedFix: Compare canonical forms using the existing syncCanon() (app.js ~2512) on both sides: `JSON.stringify(syncCanon(before)) !== JSON.stringify(syncCanon(state.config))`.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced only with a stubbed echo (v22: fbConfigRef.set() re-enters the same listener logic with a key-sorted, null/empty-pruned copy), as in the original. Add day: renderSettings fires for the own render and again at the echo (about 390 ms later). Reordering existing days: one rebuild only. This is consistent with how the Firebase SDK behaves (local optimistic value events carry sorted keys with nulls dropped, so JSON.stringify differs for any locally created object like {id,name,dow:null,note}). I could not run a live RTDB or emulator here, so the timing against the real SDK is unverified. The code path (JSON.stringify compare, renderAll on difference) is exact. Impact is a repeat of the rebuild cost and scroll jump, so after the scroll and unchanged-card fixes it becomes nearly harmless.
verdict.refinedFix: In applyRemoteConfig compare canonical forms: `const beforeJson = JSON.stringify(syncCanon(state.config));` and `if (appStarted && JSON.stringify(syncCanon(state.config)) !== beforeJson)`. syncCanon already exists (app.js ~2510) and handles arrays, nulls and key order. Risk: `state.config = remote` is still assigned unconditionally (keep that), so only the re-render is skipped. Also note the echo is held by `editorMidEntry()` into pendingRemoteConfig and then applied on focusout (app.js:7934), where its renderAll would rebuild at the moment the user taps the next field. The canonical compare removes that case too.

confirmed.title: Some renderAll callers ignore editorMidEntry, killing an open dropdown or the keyboard in the builder
confirmed.symptom: If one of the unguarded renderAll paths fires while a builder field or dropdown is in use, the open Day-of-week popup vanishes and the keyboard drops with focus lost.
confirmed.trigger: Builder open with a jelly-select open or a field focused, then the members-list listener fires (any member added, removed or changed by an admin, and once on attach) or a running game clock settles at zero (tickBoardClocks).
confirmed.evidence: Effect measured (p11, p42): with the Day-of-week jelly-select open and editorMidEntry()=true, a renderAll() replaced the select node (isConnected=false); with a field focused, activeElement became BODY. The trigger itself is code-only: app.js:2739-2742 calls renderAll() on every members snapshot with no changed-check and no editorMidEntry check, and app.js:3516-3520 does `if (settled) renderAll()`. Remote state and config paths ARE guarded (canAdoptRemote / editorMidEntry).
confirmed.rootCause: Only handleRemoteSnapshot and the config listener respect editorMidEntry. The members listener and the clock-settle path call renderAll directly.
confirmed.proposedFix: In the members listener, skip renderAll when the directory JSON is unchanged, and defer it with the same pending mechanism when editorMidEntry(). Same guard for the clock-settle renderAll.

verdict.reasoning: Code path verified by reading: the members listener calls renderAll with no changed-check and no editorMidEntry guard, and so does the clock-settle path. Effect measured (v23): with a jelly-input focused in the Days tab (editorMidEntry=true), simulating the members listener's `memberDirectory = ...; renderAll()` replaced the field node (sameNode=false) and dropped focus to BODY (the keyboard closes). The typed text was committed (state.name matched the typed value), so no data is lost, only focus. The trigger is rare: members snapshots fire on attach and when a member record is added, removed or edited, and the clock path needs a running game clock to expire while an editor has the builder open.
verdict.refinedFix: In the members listener: `const next = snap.val() || {}; const changed = JSON.stringify(next) !== JSON.stringify(memberDirectory); memberDirectory = next; memberDirectoryLoaded = true; if (appStarted && changed) { if (editorMidEntry()) { armIdleRetry(); /* or a small pendingRender flag */ } else renderAll(); }`. For tickBoardClocks, defer with the same flag while editorMidEntry(). A tiny `renderAllWhenIdle()` helper (set a flag, have idleRetryTick call renderAll once canAdoptRemote() is true) serves both. Keep the first snapshot (memberDirectoryLoaded false -> true) rendering immediately, because chatAuthorName fails closed until then.

confirmed.title: An open, unmodified game editor ignores a remote edit to that game, and Save overwrites it
confirmed.symptom: Editor B has a game open with no edits. Editor A changes that game's tagline or rules. B's editor keeps showing the old values, and when B edits one field and saves, A's change is silently overwritten.
confirmed.trigger: Two editors. B opens game X in the builder and touches nothing. A saves a change to X. B changes any field and taps Save.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p37). After applyRemoteConfig with the headline changed: state.config.games[0].headline = 'CHANGED BY ANOTHER EDITOR', but the draft headline and the gd-headline input still show the old text, and builderDirty()=false.
confirmed.rootCause: ensureGameDraft returns early when `gameDraftFor === editId && gameDraft` (settings.js:340-343), so the draft built at open time is never refreshed. renderAll does re-render the editor, but from the stale draft.
confirmed.proposedFix: Remember JSON of the source game when the draft is built. In ensureGameDraft, if !builderDirty() and the saved game's JSON now differs, rebuild the draft. If the draft is dirty, show a 'changed elsewhere' note.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced end to end (v24). Game 'shields' open and untouched; applyRemoteConfig with a changed headline: config headline becomes 'CHANGED BY ANOTHER EDITOR', but the draft and #gd-headline still show the old text and builderDirty()=false. Then typing '!' into the name and tapping Save wrote name 'Shields!' with the OLD headline back into state.config, silently reverting the other editor's change. Needs two editors on the same game at the same time, so rare.
verdict.refinedFix: At draft build store `gameDraftSource = JSON.stringify(g)` (null for a new game). In ensureGameDraft: `if (gameDraftFor === editId && gameDraft) { if (builderDirty() || editId === 'new') return; const g = gameById(editId); if (!g || JSON.stringify(g) === gameDraftSource) return; /* fall through and rebuild */ }`, preserving `extrasOpen` across that rebuild instead of resetting it. For a dirty draft, show a 'this game changed elsewhere' note rather than overwriting the user's edits.

confirmed.title: Pasted backup text in Data -> Restore is wiped by any rebuild while it isn't focused
confirmed.symptom: Paste a backup into the Restore box, tap outside to read something, and any renderAll (a remote score, another action) empties the box and clears the 'doesn't look like a backup' error.
confirmed.trigger: Data tab: paste text into #restore-textarea, blur it, then trigger any renderAll.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p35). Textarea length 67 before, 0 after renderAll with nothing focused.
confirmed.rootCause: The whole builder is rebuilt from markup that has no value for this textarea, and the text is not stored anywhere.
confirmed.proposedFix: Largely fixed by the in-place/skip-unchanged render (the Data card has no state inputs and would never re-render). Otherwise stash the value in a module variable and restore it after the card renders.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with a real handleRemoteSnapshot() (v25): 36 characters typed into #restore-textarea, blurred, one remote snapshot later the length is 0. A remote adoption only happens while the field is not focused (editorMidEntry guards the rest), so the paste has to be left unfocused when another editor saves something. A small, occasional annoyance.
verdict.refinedFix: Fixed as a side effect of the unchanged-card skip: the Data card reads nothing from state that a score change touches, so it never re-renders. If that is not done, keep the value in a module variable (`let restoreDraftText = ''`, updated on the textarea's input/change) and refill the textarea after renderDataTab writes.

confirmed.title: Paired inputs misalign by 16 px when one label wraps ('Outs per side (0 = none)')
confirmed.symptom: In the Live match scoreboard fields, the 'Periods' and 'Outs per side' inputs sit at different heights on a phone, because the right label wraps to two lines.
confirmed.trigger: Game editor for a bracket game with the Live match scoreboard on, at 390 px width.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p41 and screenshot s_editor_full.png). gd-tracker-innings top 1069, gd-tracker-outs top 1085 (16 px lower). The right label is 32 px tall and the left one 16 px.
confirmed.rootCause: .form-row is a 2-column grid of .form-field blocks, each label above its input, so unequal label heights push the input down.
confirmed.proposedFix: Shorten the label ('Outs / side') and add `.form-row { align-items: end }` (or give .form-row .form-label a fixed min-height) so inputs line up.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced at 390 px (v26): #gd-tracker-innings top 1069, #gd-tracker-outs top 1085 (16 px lower), label heights 16 vs 32. Static layout only, cosmetic.
verdict.refinedFix: Shorten the label to 'Outs per side' and move '(0 = none)' to the existing field-help line, or give `.form-row { align-items: end; }` (inputs then share a baseline while the taller label grows upward). Check the other .form-row pairs (Name/Day of week, Unit/Period name) afterwards: end-alignment is harmless there because their labels are single-line.

confirmed.title: Team name and counselor inputs are only 160 px wide at 390 px, truncating names while editing
confirmed.symptom: On the Teams tab, long team names such as 'Methodic Mediocre Maples' and 'Particularly Perilous Pumpkins' and the counselor lists are clipped inside narrow inputs, so you cannot see what you are editing.
confirmed.trigger: Teams tab at phone width with the default junior team names.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p41 and screenshot s_teams_days.png). All six .team-name-input hosts are 160 px wide. Two reorder arrows plus a delete button take the rest of the row.
confirmed.rootCause: .team-builder-row puts reorder arrows, the name/counselor stack and the delete button in one flex row; the field column gets whatever is left.
confirmed.proposedFix: Put the name and counselor inputs on full-width lines and move the reorder/delete controls to a compact row above or below them (or into a per-row menu).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v27): all six .team-name-input hosts are 160 px wide in a 316 px row, with three 44 px buttons taking the rest. The inner input's scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth for 'Methodic Mediocre Maples' (248 vs 160), 'Particularly Perilous Pumpkins' (273), 'Patriotic Pilgrims' (169) and 'Runaway John Deersz' (211), so four of six names are clipped while editing. Screenshot at builder-verify/v27_teams.png. Static cosmetic.
verdict.refinedFix: Restructure .team-builder-row into two lines: the full-width name and counselor inputs on top, and the reorder and delete controls in a compact row underneath (or float the delete button into the row header). Use `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto` with the inputs spanning the full width.

confirmed.title: Game-editor validation message pushes Save down and then stays visible after the problem is fixed
confirmed.symptom: Tapping Save with no name inserts 'Give the game a name.' above the Save button, shifting Save/Cancel down ~31 px under the finger. The message stays after the name is typed, until the next Save.
confirmed.trigger: + New game -> scroll to Save -> tap Save with an empty name -> type a name.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p31). Save button top 746 -> 777 when the error appears (doc 1167 -> 1198). After typing a name, #gd-error is still hidden=false with the old text.
confirmed.rootCause: #gd-error is toggled via hidden with no reserved space (settings.js:418, 716-726) and is only cleared by the next Save or a re-render.
confirmed.proposedFix: Reserve a min-height for the error line (or show it in a toast or an inline banner above the fold). Clear it on the next input or format change.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v28): tapping Save with an empty name changes Save's top from 1069 to 1100 (about 31 px) and the document from 1167 to 1198. After typing a name the error is still visible ('Give the game a name.'), cleared only by the next Save or a re-render. The error is also at the bottom of a long form while the offending field is at the top. No animation involved.
verdict.refinedFix: Clear the error on any `input` or `change` inside the editor (in wireGameEditor: `card.addEventListener('input', () => { const e = document.getElementById('gd-error'); if (e && !e.hidden) e.hidden = true; })`). To stop the shift, reserve the line (`#gd-error { min-height: 1.4em; }`, toggled with visibility) or scroll the offending field into view when the error is shown.

confirmed.title: The posted notice card is re-created on every renderAll and every 30 s tick, clearing text selection
confirmed.symptom: A person selecting or copying text from the posted notice (cleanup assignments) loses the selection within 30 s, or the instant any remote update lands.
confirmed.trigger: Post a notice, select text in the card, then wait for the 30 s interval or any renderAll.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (p41). With the notice posted and 22 characters selected, one renderAll left 0 characters selected and the title node was replaced (sameNode=false). No animation is involved (plain text nodes).
confirmed.rootCause: renderNoticeBoard writes `el.innerHTML = html` unconditionally (app.js:686-692); v183's setHtmlIfChanged was not applied to it. It also runs from the 30 s interval (app.js:7971) and from noticeCommit in the builder.
confirmed.proposedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged(el, html || '') as the other home panels now do.

verdict.location: app.js:686-692 (renderNoticeBoard); callers app.js:7835 (renderAll) and 7971 (30 s interval)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v30): posted notice, 22 characters selected in the title, one renderNoticeBoard() (exactly what the 30 s interval runs) leaves 0 characters selected and the title node replaced (sameNode=false). The markup contains only plain nodes (teamEmoji is text, not an , and styles.css has no animation on .notice-card), so there is no blink or animation, only lost text selection. Nothing wires listeners into #notice-board's children (grep), so skipping the write is safe.
verdict.refinedFix: `el.hidden = !html; setHtmlIfChanged(el, html || '');` in renderNoticeBoard. No re-wiring is needed because the card has no listeners.

confirmed.title: Home day-tab pill springs from the first tab to the active day whenever the tab bar is (re)created on a non-Monday day
confirmed.symptom: On a Wednesday-to-Friday the blue pill in the Competitions day tabs starts over 'Mon' and slides across (up to about 250 px, about 0.6 s) with the squash wobble. Usually unseen because the Competitions card is collapsed by default, but visible if the card is open when the tab bar is re-created (day set/label change such as the midnight 'today' dot, or any other shell rewrite).
confirmed.trigger: renderDayTabs() creating a fresh <jelly-tabs> with state.ui.day not equal to the first day. Fresh page load with ?now=4-1330 (Thursday): pill first sample x=-123, target 62, settles in 580 ms, max distance 185 px (builder-verify/v34). Programmatic: creating with day index 3 gave 185 px, index 4 gave 247 px (v33).
confirmed.evidence: Measured. Same root cause as builder-tabs-pill-respring: vendor/jelly.js jelly-segmented.sync() runs before its jelly-segment children upgrade (value undefined -> index 0), onShape() places the pill at segment 0 with placed=true, and later syncs only move pillTarget. Snapping `seg.pillX = seg.pillTarget; seg.pillXVelocity = 0` right after creation removes the spring in the builder (v9).
confirmed.rootCause: jelly-segmented places its pill at index 0 on first shape, before child segments are upgraded; the app creates jelly-tabs with a non-zero active value and never settles the pill.
confirmed.location: app.js:5380-5386 (renderDayTabs shell creation); shared helper could live beside setHtmlIfChanged
confirmed.proposedFix: After the nav.innerHTML shell is written, call the same small helper proposed for the builder: `settleTabPill(tabs)` -> `const seg = tabs.shadowRoot && tabs.shadowRoot.querySelector('jelly-segmented'); if (seg && !seg.reflecting) { seg.pillX = seg.pillTarget; seg.pillXVelocity = 0; seg.requestFrame && seg.requestFrame(); }`. Only on creation, never in the change handler.

verdict.refinedFix: After the nav.innerHTML shell is written, call the same small helper proposed for the builder: `settleTabPill(tabs)` -> `const seg = tabs.shadowRoot && tabs.shadowRoot.querySelector('jelly-segmented'); if (seg && !seg.reflecting) { seg.pillX = seg.pillTarget; seg.pillXVelocity = 0; seg.requestFrame && seg.requestFrame(); }`. Only on creation, never in the change handler.

confirmed.title: Builder 'Last edited' line shows device-local time instead of camp time
confirmed.symptom: The 'Last edited' stamp at the top of Set up the week reads a different clock time on a phone set to another time zone (7/20 6:30 PM camp time shows as 7/21 7:30 AM on a Tokyo-zone device), unlike the footer timestamps which are pinned to America/New_York.
confirmed.trigger: Open the builder on a device whose time zone is not America/New_York.
confirmed.evidence: Measured (builder-verify/v36): same state.config.updatedAt '2026-07-20T22:30:00Z' renders 'Last edited 7/20/2026, 6:30:00 PM' in America/New_York and 'Last edited 7/21/2026, 7:30:00 AM' in Asia/Tokyo. CLAUDE.md says camp timestamps must render in camp time, never device-local.
confirmed.rootCause: settings.js:53 uses `new Date(state.config.updatedAt).toLocaleString()`.
confirmed.proposedFix: Use the existing helper: `Last edited ${esc(formatEasternStamp(state.config.updatedAt) || '')}` (formatEasternStamp is defined at app.js:1839 and already accepts an ISO string).

verdict.refinedFix: Use the existing helper: `Last edited ${esc(formatEasternStamp(state.config.updatedAt) || '')}` (formatEasternStamp is defined at app.js:1839 and already accepts an ISO string).

confirmed.title: Channel tab strip collapses to a sliver in any busy channel
confirmed.symptom: Open a channel with more than ~10 messages and the Announcements/General/Memes/Photos pills shrink to clipped slivers (5px tall at 50 messages); once the history is long there is effectively no way to switch channels or see other channels' unread badges. The tabs visibly shrink as messages load.
confirmed.trigger: Open chat on any channel and let the backlog load (CHAT_WINDOW=50). Or: openChat('general') with 12 / 30 / 50 messages. Worse with photos.
confirmed.evidence: p15_tabs_squash measured .chat-tabs height at 390px: 3 msgs=31px, 12 msgs=21px, 30 msgs=9px, 50 msgs=5px (pill height 15px, tab strip scrollHeight 15), identical for editor. Screenshot hunt/chat/s_tabs_squash_viewer.png shows only clipped pill tops under the header. #chat-view stays 828px, head 35px, composer 58px; only the tab strip shrinks. Injecting `.chat-head,.chat-tabs,.chat-composer{flex-shrink:0}` keeps tabs at 31px with 50 photo messages (p21_verify_fixes).
confirmed.rootCause: .chat-view is a fixed-height flex column. .chat-list is `flex:1 1 auto` with a huge content-based flex-basis, and .chat-tabs has `overflow-x:auto`, which gives it an automatic min-height of 0 and the default flex-shrink:1, so it absorbs a share of the overflow proportional to its basis and gets crushed. Head and composer don't shrink only because they are not scroll containers.
confirmed.proposedFix: Add `flex: 0 0 auto;` to .chat-tabs (and `.chat-head`, `.chat-composer`) so only .chat-list flexes.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran my own probe (hunt/chat-verify/v1_tabs.cjs, real initChatSync via the fake-firebase lib, real styles.css). .chat-tabs height: 3 msgs=31px, 20 msgs=12-13px, 50 msgs=5px at 320/390/430 wide; 6px at 1280x800 desktop. #chat-view stays 828px, head 35, composer 58 — only the strip shrinks (the strip is overflow-x:auto so its automatic min-height is 0, flex-shrink 1, and .chat-list's content-sized flex-basis soaks up the overflow). Injecting `.chat-tabs{flex:0 0 auto}` gave tabs 31 / list 688 / view 828 at every width and message count. Screenshot confirms only clipped pill tops under the header. Root cause as stated is right. (Senior camp not re-tested: my fake emitter hardcodes the junior root, so that run was empty, not a refutation.)
verdict.refinedFix: One line in styles.css: add `flex: 0 0 auto;` to `.chat-tabs` (the strip must not be a flex-shrink participant). Equivalent alternative: `.chat-list { flex: 1 1 0; }` so its basis is 0 and nothing overflows. `.chat-head` and `.chat-composer` do not need it (they are not scroll containers, so min-height:auto already protects them). No JS/listener/state risk. Verified at 320/390/430 with 3/20/50 messages.

confirmed.title: Chat opens (and new photos land) scrolled well above the newest messages when thumbnails are present
confirmed.symptom: Opening a channel that has photos leaves the view in the middle of the history, hundreds or thousands of px above the newest messages; the newest photo is cut off or off-screen. A live photo arriving while you are at the bottom lands half hidden under the composer.
confirmed.trigger: Open Photo Dump (or any channel with thumbnails). Or be at the bottom of a channel when someone posts a photo. Also after a forced rebuild that scrolls to bottom.
confirmed.evidence: p14: 50-photo channel, right after openChat gap=0 and list scrollHeight=2409; ~15ms later images decode and scrollHeight=11184, gap=2625px (last bubble bottom y=3398 vs list bottom 785). Screenshot s_photos_first_open.png shows photos #35-#37 of 50. p2: 12-msg channel with 4 photos: gap 554px after open; live photo appended at bottom: gap 174px (scrollHeight 1379->1554). Verified fix (p22): attaching a one-shot load listener that re-calls chatScrollToBottom() for incomplete .chat-thumb imgs takes the gap from 2625 to 0.
confirmed.rootCause: chatScrollToBottom() runs synchronously right after innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML, while the thumbnail s (no width/height attributes) are still 0px tall; they decode asynchronously and push scrollHeight up afterwards, so the 'pinned to bottom' scroll is stale.
confirmed.proposedFix: In chatScrollToBottom (or right after setting innerHTML/inserting a bubble when pinned), for each `.chat-thumb` with !img.complete add `img.addEventListener('load', () => { list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight; }, {once:true})`, only while the user is still pinned (nearBottom captured before the insert). Optionally also reserve a min-height/aspect-ratio on .chat-thumb-btn.

verdict.location: chat.js:1023 chatScrollToBottom (called from renderChatView :971 and appendChatBubble :1043)
verdict.reasoning: Re-ran their p2/p14 and my own v2_photo_gap.cjs (20 photo thumbs, real JPEG data URLs): gap is 0 synchronously after openChat, then 3291px once the thumbs decode (their 50-photo case: 2625px, last bubble at y=3398 vs list bottom 785). A live photo arriving while pinned grows the gap afterwards too (their p2: 174px; first open of a 4-photo channel: 554px). The tab-away/back case is gap 0 because decoded images are cached, so it is a first-decode problem: has no width/height so it is 0px tall until decoded. Applying a one-shot load listener that re-pins fixed it in my probe (open: 3291 -> 0, live photo: 0). Photos can be sent in any channel, so Photos and Memes both hit this. Not testable here: WebKit's treatment of loading=lazy on data: URLs / no scroll anchoring on iOS (could be worse there).
verdict.refinedFix: Inside chatScrollToBottom(), after `list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight`, do: `list.querySelectorAll('.chat-thumb').forEach((img) => { if (!img.complete) { const pin = () => { list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight; }; img.addEventListener('load', pin, { once: true }); img.addEventListener('error', pin, { once: true }); } });`. Because every pin path (open, rebuild-to-bottom, appendChatBubble when nearBottom) already funnels through chatScrollToBottom, this is the only change needed. Risks: (1) a reader who starts scrolling up while the thumbs are still decoding gets snapped back down - guard with a flag set false by one-time `touchstart`/`wheel` listeners on the list (set it true again in chatScrollToBottom); (2) duplicate once-listeners on repeated calls are harmless. The keepScroll (scrolled-up) rebuild path must NOT pin, which is already the case since it does not call chatScrollToBottom. Optional belt-and-braces: reserve space with `.chat-thumb-btn{min-height:...}` but portrait thumbs make that imperfect.

confirmed.title: The '← Camp' pill (and tab strip, header, composer) re-create and re-run their entrance animation on every channel switch, bell toggle and directory update
confirmed.symptom: Each time you tap a channel tab or the bell, the Camp back pill blinks out and slides in again (0.28s) and the whole header/tabs/list/composer DOM is replaced; same when the member directory changes or the open channel finishes loading.
confirmed.trigger: Tap any channel tab; tap the 🔔/🔕 bell; onMemberDirectoryChanged() (every members-node snapshot, once at startup); backlog-complete flip for the open channel; backfill.
confirmed.evidence: p1_rebuild_anims: getAnimations() two rAFs after each trigger shows `button#chat-back-btn.back-pill :: back-pill-in` x1 running for: openChat, switch tab (memes), switch back, bell toggle, directory changed, directory snapshot. MutationObserver: each forced rebuild adds div.chat-head, div.chat-tabs, div.chat-list, div.chat-composer and removes the old ones. Idle renderAll and live-message append produce 0 animations. p12: the loading jelly-skeleton node is not reused after a rebuild, so its shimmer restarts. (The extra joy-fly sparkle dots on tab/bell taps are the intended tap sparkles.)
confirmed.rootCause: renderChatView(true) replaces the entire view via view.innerHTML even when only the active tab, title, bell state or list changed. .back-pill has `animation: back-pill-in .28s both`, so a re-created pill replays it.
confirmed.location: chat.js:911-972 (renderChatView, forced path), wired from 982 (tab click), 683 (toggleChatSub), 276-279 (onMemberDirectoryChanged), 132-136 (ready flip)
confirmed.proposedFix: Quick: `.chat-view .back-pill { animation: none; }`. Better: build the shell (head/tabs/composer) once per open and, on tab switch/bell/directory change, only update the active-tab class, title, bell icon, composer placeholder and #chat-list contents (the composer node and its focus then never move).

verdict.location: chat.js:911-972 renderChatView forced path; styles.css:1441 (.back-pill animation); callers chat.js:982, 683, 276-279, 132-136
verdict.reasoning: My v3_anims.cjs: getAnimations() two rAFs after each trigger shows exactly one running `button#chat-back-btn.back-pill :: back-pill-in` for tab->memes, tab->general, bell toggle and onMemberDirectoryChanged; MutationObserver shows .chat-head/.chat-tabs/.chat-list/.chat-composer all replaced each time. Per-frame sample after a tab tap: pill opacity 0 -> 0.25 -> 0.48 -> ... -> 1 over ~8 frames with a 10px slide-in, i.e. the Back button visibly blinks out and re-enters on every channel switch. Idle renderAll, a remote state change, and a live message append produce 0 animations and no chat-view DOM churn, so v183's early-return holds. The extra joy-fly dots on tab/bell taps are the intended tap sparkles.
verdict.refinedFix: Cheapest, zero-risk: `.chat-view .back-pill { animation: none; }` in styles.css (the takeover itself appears instantly, so the slide-in adds nothing there). Structural alternative (only if wanted): keep head/tabs/composer nodes and update the active-tab class, title, bell state, placeholder and #chat-list contents in place. RISK of that route: wireChatView closes over `ch` for send/clear/bell/photo handlers, so a kept composer would post to the wrong channel after a switch - handlers must read `state.ui.chatChannel` at call time; also keep chatViewBuiltFor in step because appendChatBubble/onChatMsgAdded/removeChatBubble key off it, and re-run chat-input placeholder + renderChatBadges. If you rebuild the strip anyway, restore/centre its scrollLeft (see chat-tabs-scroll-reset).

confirmed.title: Toasts sit on top of the composer and swallow taps on Send / input / photo
confirmed.symptom: While someone message arrives in another channel (announcement, mention, belled channel) or any app toast fires, the toast pill covers the text box and the send/photo buttons for 4-5.5 s. Tapping ➤ during that time does nothing (the tap dismisses the toast).
confirmed.trigger: Be in the chat view (e.g. General) and have a message land in Announcements or mention you; or any showToast such as 'One moment — sending a little too fast.' or the initial 'Following … Foxes' toast. Then tap Send.
confirmed.evidence: p9: jelly-toaster rect y=766-826 vs send button y=793-835; document.elementFromPoint at send-button centre and at input centre both return `jelly-toaster`. p9b: with 'on my way' typed and the toast showing, a real touchscreen.tap on ➤ -> 0 updates sent and text still in the box; tap after the toast cleared -> 1 update. Screenshots s_toast2_over_composer.png, s_chat_open.png (toast over send button). Verified fix: `body.chat-open jelly-toaster[position="bottom"]{bottom:calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))}` makes elementFromPoint at send/input/photo return the real controls (p21).
confirmed.rootCause: <jelly-toaster position="bottom"> is fixed to the bottom of the viewport and its .toast pills have pointer-events:auto; the chat composer lives in exactly that strip. Nothing offsets the toaster while body.chat-open.
confirmed.location: styles.css (add a body.chat-open rule near 4757); index.html:407 <jelly-toaster position="bottom">
confirmed.proposedFix: Add `body.chat-open jelly-toaster[position="bottom"] { bottom: calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }` (outer-document styles beat the shadow :host rule) — or use position="top" while chat is open.

verdict.location: styles.css near 4757 (add a body.chat-open rule); index.html:407 <jelly-toaster position="bottom">
verdict.reasoning: My v4_toast.cjs (viewer, General open, announcement lands in another channel): toast pill rect x49-372 y780-826 (pointer-events:auto; host is none) vs input x64-326 y795-834 and send x332-374 y793-835. elementFromPoint at send and input centres returns jelly-toaster (photo button at x16-58 is clear). A real touchscreen.tap on the send button with 'on my way' typed sent 0 updates and the tap just dismissed the toast; the toast lasted ~3-5 s. With `body.chat-open jelly-toaster[position="bottom"]{bottom:calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))}` the host moved to y718-764 and elementFromPoint returned the real send/input/photo controls and the tap sent 1 update. Triggers are common in chat: announcement/mention/belled-channel alerts while in another channel, 'sending a little too fast' (which ironically covers the Send button), 'Couldn't send', 'Sending right after the previous one'. Cost is a swallowed tap, not data loss.
verdict.refinedFix: styles.css: `body.chat-open jelly-toaster[position="bottom"] { bottom: calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }` (outer-document rule beats the shadow :host; verified it moves the host). Composer is ~58px tall so 5rem clears it. No JS needed, home page toasts unaffected because it is scoped to body.chat-open. Not verified with the on-screen keyboard up (not testable here).

confirmed.title: The deploy 'New version available — Refresh' bar covers the composer, and tapping it reloads the page and loses the draft
confirmed.symptom: After a deploy, the full-width blue Refresh alert sits over the text box and Send button; a tap meant for the input or ➤ triggers a reload and the half-written message is gone. The banner stays up exactly while a message is being typed, because chatComposerBusy() defers the auto-reload.
confirmed.trigger: Be in chat with a draft in the composer when a new ?v= build is detected (checkForUpdate -> onNewVersion -> showUpdateBanner), then tap the input or Send.
confirmed.evidence: p19: #update-banner rect y=748-828 vs composer y=785-843; elementFromPoint at input centre and send centre = `jelly-alert#update-banner`; a touchscreen.tap on the input fired the banner's click handler (doReload) once. Screenshot s_update_banner_over_composer.png. Raising it with `body.chat-open .update-banner-alert,body.chat-open .update-banner{bottom:calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))}` restores correct hit targets (p21).
confirmed.rootCause: .update-banner-alert / .update-banner are fixed at bottom:1rem, z-index 60, and the whole bar has `addEventListener('click', doReload)`. The chat composer occupies the same strip.
confirmed.proposedFix: Offset both bars while chat is open (rule above), and/or make only the Refresh button (not the whole bar) trigger doReload while chat is open.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran p19: banner y748-828 vs composer y785-843; elementFromPoint at input and send centres = jelly-alert#update-banner; touchscreen.tap on the input fired doReload once (the whole bar has click->doReload). Also read chatComposerBusy(): the reload is deferred only while the composer is FOCUSED with text (or a send is in flight), which is exactly when the banner is up, so the guard that protects the draft invites the tap that destroys it. Fix verified in my v5_banner.cjs: with `body.chat-open .update-banner-alert,body.chat-open .update-banner{bottom:calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))}` the banner sits at y684-764 and input/send/photo hit-test to the real controls. Downgraded to low: it needs a deploy to land during the few seconds someone is typing (otherwise the idle auto-reload clears the banner in ~1.2 s).
verdict.refinedFix: styles.css: `body.chat-open .update-banner-alert, body.chat-open .update-banner { bottom: calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }` (same value as the toaster rule; verified). Optionally make only the Refresh button, not the whole bar, call doReload while chat is open (bar.addEventListener is app.js showUpdateBanner; the jelly-button child would need its own listener and the bar's click would be dropped).

confirmed.title: Tapping the Memes/Photos tab rebuilds the strip so it snaps back to the left and the active tab ends up off-screen
confirmed.symptom: The four tabs are 514px wide, so on every phone width some of them are clipped (Photos is partly or fully hidden); you swipe the strip to reach Photos, tap it, and the strip jumps back to scrollLeft 0 with the now-active Photos pill off-screen (only the title says which channel you are in).
confirmed.trigger: On a 320-430px viewport, swipe the tab strip to the right and tap Photos (or Memes).
confirmed.evidence: p3_tabs: scrollWidth 514 vs clientWidth 288/328/358/398 at viewport 320/360/390/430 (Photos tab right edge 530 > viewport at all four). After scrolling the strip to the end and clicking Photos: scrollLeft 226/186/156/116 -> 0 and a new .chat-tabs node (sameNode false); active pill left/right 417-508 while the viewport is 320-430. Screenshot s_tabs_360_after_photos_tap.png: title says Photo Dump, active pill not visible. (Independent of, and in addition to, the squash bug above.)
confirmed.rootCause: renderChatView(true) re-creates .chat-tabs, resetting its scroll position; nothing scrolls the active tab into view; the strip is wider than any phone.
confirmed.proposedFix: After building, set `strip.scrollLeft` so the active tab is centred (compute from offsetLeft; avoid scrollIntoView so the page doesn't scroll) and/or carry the old scrollLeft across a same-view rebuild; consider a 4-column layout (emoji-only labels on narrow screens) so no horizontal scroll is needed.

verdict.reasoning: My v1_tabs.cjs (unsquashed, 3 msgs): strip scrollWidth is 447 (their 514 likely included badge widths) vs clientWidth 288/328/358/398 at 320/360/390/430; tab rects [16-168],[173-269],[274-367],[373-463]. After scrolling the strip to its end and tapping Photos: scrollLeft 159/119/89/49 -> 0, strip is a new node (sameNode false), and the ACTIVE Photos pill sits at x373-463, i.e. off-screen at every width (strip clips at viewport-16). Bell toggle and directory rebuilds reset it the same way. Root cause as stated is right (renderChatView(true) rebuilds the strip; nothing re-centres the active tab).
verdict.refinedFix: At the end of renderChatView (after view.innerHTML), centre the active tab by rects, not scrollIntoView (which would scroll the page): `const s = view.querySelector('.chat-tabs'), a = s && s.querySelector('.chat-tab-active'); if (a) { const sr = s.getBoundingClientRect(), ar = a.getBoundingClientRect(); s.scrollLeft += (ar.left - sr.left) - (sr.width - ar.width) / 2; }`. Verified in v15_tabfix.cjs: Photos active tab goes from 0px visible to fully visible (x284-374). This also fixes the openChat('photos')/persisted-channel case and the bell/directory rebuilds. Chat tabs are plain <button>s, so there is no selectable-jelly-chip 'selected' state to worry about. Combine with a proper fit (see extra finding chat-photos-tab-hidden-390).

confirmed.title: 'Chat needs live sync, which is off on this device.' flashes on the home card (and in an open chat) while sync is still starting
confirmed.symptom: On every cold start the Chat card on the home page says sync is off, and a device that reloads with the chat takeover persisted open shows that same message as the whole message list until the first backlog completes, then everything pops in. It is false: sync is just not up yet.
confirmed.trigger: Reload/cold-start the app (hint-painted, before initSync sets fbRef); with state.ui.chatOpen persisted true the chat view shows it too.
confirmed.evidence: p11_cold_start_open with fbRef null: chat-list text and #chat-card-preview both = 'Chat needs live sync, which is off on this device.'. After startChat (fbRef set, backlog child_added delivered, once() pending) the list still shows that text (no rebuild until once() resolves); card already shows the real preview. After once() resolves the list builds. Real network duration not measured (depends on SDK/auth/member-read time, plausibly 1-3 s).
confirmed.rootCause: renderChatCard/chatListHTML test `!syncEnabled()` (i.e. fbRef == null) before the 'Loading…'/skeleton branch, but fbRef is only set after approval in initSync; there is no 'sync pending' state, and the open view is only rebuilt when once('value') resolves.
confirmed.proposedFix: Distinguish 'sync not started yet' from 'sync off for good' (e.g. show 'Loading…'/the skeleton until initChatSync has run or the SDK has definitively failed), and call renderChatView(true) when initChatSync attaches if the view is open.

verdict.reasoning: syncEnabled() is just !!fbRef and fbRef is only assigned in initSync after membership approval (app.js:2670), so on every hint-painted cold start the home Chat card reads 'Chat needs live sync, which is off on this device.' until the SDK+auth+member read finish; with state.ui.chatOpen persisted the whole list area says it until once('value') resolves (the open view is not rebuilt when initChatSync attaches, so it stays on the sentence even after sync is up). My v6_cold.cjs confirmed the text pre-sync and the real preview after sync. But it is a plain-text swap: card height is 52px both before and after at 320 and 390 (single-line ellipsis), so no layout shift or animation. Duration in production not measurable here (SDK/auth latency). Downgraded to low: false/alarming wording for 1-3 s, not a visual glitch.
verdict.refinedFix: Add a 'sync pending' state: show the 'Loading…' text/skeleton unless sync is definitively off (`typeof sdkLoadFailed !== 'undefined' && sdkLoadFailed`, `syncDenied`, or no FIREBASE_CONFIG). In chat.js use one helper, e.g. `function chatSyncOff() { return !syncEnabled() && (sdkLoadFailed || syncDenied || !(window.FIREBASE_CONFIG && window.FIREBASE_CONFIG.apiKey)); }`, and use it in both renderChatCard and chatListHTML (falling through to the existing skeleton/'Loading…' branch otherwise). Also call renderChatCard() (and renderChatView(true) if open) from onSdkLoadFailed so a real failure replaces 'Loading…' with the sentence, and from initChatSync right after attaching so the open view swaps the sentence for the skeleton.

confirmed.title: Your own message doesn't scroll into view if you were scrolled up when you sent it
confirmed.symptom: Reply to something older in the history, press send, and nothing visibly happens: the composer clears but the new bubble is appended far below the visible area.
confirmed.trigger: Scroll the message list up (more than 80px from the bottom), type, press Send/Enter.
confirmed.evidence: p4_scroll_reading (a): gap before send 1138px, after 1202px; my new .chat-bubble-mine is not within the list's visible rect (myBubbleVisible=false); input cleared.
confirmed.rootCause: appendChatBubble only calls chatScrollToBottom() when the list was within 80px of the bottom, with no exception for the sender's own message.
confirmed.proposedFix: Pass a `force` flag when msg.byKey === identityKey(authUser) (or after sendChatMessage) so own messages always scroll to bottom.

verdict.reasoning: My v7_misc.cjs: list scrolled 900px above bottom, typed 'my reply', clicked send: gap 900 -> 996, the new .chat-bubble-mine exists but is not within the list's visible rect, input cleared. Control (pinned at bottom): gap 0 after send. So a reader replying from higher up sees the composer clear and nothing happen.
verdict.refinedFix: In appendChatBubble: `const mine = msg.byKey && msg.byKey === identityKey(authUser); ... if (nearBottom || mine) chatScrollToBottom();`. Caveat: the same account signed in on a second device would also force-scroll there; if that matters, track the push id of the local send (sendChatMessage already has `id`) in a small Set and test membership instead of byKey. Pair with the thumb re-pin from chat-photo-scroll-gap since chatScrollToBottom is shared.

confirmed.title: Tapping ➤ moves focus to the button, so the on-screen keyboard drops after every message
confirmed.symptom: After each send the keyboard closes (Android Chrome and anywhere focus leaves the input) and the person has to tap the input again for the next message.
confirmed.trigger: Type a message, tap the ➤ button (not the keyboard Enter/Go key).
confirmed.evidence: p17_send_focus: after a real touchscreen.tap on #chat-send-btn, document.activeElement = button#chat-send-btn (input lost focus). iOS keyboard behaviour not testable here.
confirmed.rootCause: The send handler never returns focus to #chat-input and the button takes focus on tap.
confirmed.proposedFix: On the send (and photo) button add `pointerdown`/`mousedown` handler with `e.preventDefault()` so the input keeps focus, or call `input.focus()` at the end of sendChatMessage.

verdict.reasoning: My v8_blur.cjs (touch emulation, toast waited out first - note an early toast covered the input and swallowed my first attempt, which is finding chat-toast-covers-composer again): input focused and typed, touchscreen.tap on send -> message sent, document.activeElement = chat-send-btn (input lost focus). With `mousedown` preventDefault, with `pointerdown` preventDefault, or with input.focus() in a click handler, activeElement stays chat-input. This is Chromium-with-touch (Android-like) behaviour; the soft keyboard dropping on Android follows from focus leaving the input. iOS Safari (does not focus buttons on tap) not testable here, so impact there is unverified.
verdict.refinedFix: Both belt and braces on the send button: `send.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => e.preventDefault());` (keeps focus on the input - verified) and keep `sendChatMessage` unchanged. Apply the same preventDefault to the photo button only if you want the keyboard to survive opening the picker (usually not wanted). Do not rely on a later input.focus() alone on iOS (programmatic focus outside the gesture won't raise the keyboard), though inside the click handler it is fine and also verified. No stale-listener risk: it is added once per build in wireChatView.

confirmed.title: A half-typed message is thrown away when you leave chat or switch channels
confirmed.symptom: Type a reply, tap '← Camp' to check standings, come back: the box is empty. Same when you tap another channel tab and return.
confirmed.trigger: Type text; press ← Camp then reopen the chat card; or tap another channel tab then back.
confirmed.evidence: p20_draft_close: draft 'a long half-written reply' -> after closeChat()/openChat('general') value = ''; draft 'draft in general' -> after memes tab and back value = ''. (Same-channel rebuilds from directory/bell DO keep text, focus and caret: p4(d).)
confirmed.rootCause: closeChat()/openChat() null chatViewBuiltFor so the next build has no `carry`; channel switches also start clean; no per-channel draft store.
confirmed.proposedFix: Keep a `chatDrafts[ch]` map updated on input events and restore it in renderChatView for the target channel.

verdict.reasoning: My v7_misc.cjs: draft typed, closeChat() then openChat('general') -> input ''. Draft typed, memes tab then back to general -> ''. Same-channel forced rebuilds (onMemberDirectoryChanged, bell) keep the text, so only leave/switch loses it. Note the code comment at 916-918 says 'Switching channels starts clean' on purpose, so the tab-switch half is a design choice; the close/reopen half is the real annoyance (check standings, come back, box empty).
verdict.refinedFix: Per-channel in-memory drafts: `let chatDrafts = {};` updated by an `input` listener in wireChatView (`chatDrafts[ch] = input.value`), restored in renderChatView for the target channel, cleared in sendChatMessage and clearLocalData/sign-out. Keep it in memory only (never localStorage) so it cannot leak across sign-outs, and keep chatComposerBusy() unchanged (it only counts a FOCUSED composer). Low priority.

confirmed.title: Lightbox can show the wrong photo if you close one and open another before the first finishes loading
confirmed.symptom: Tap photo A (slow load), close, tap photo B: B appears, then A's late response replaces it.
confirmed.trigger: Open photo A on a slow connection, close it, open photo B before A's once('value') resolves.
confirmed.evidence: p10 race test (A delay 600ms, B 100ms): width shown when B loaded = 800 (B), after A resolved = 1280 (A's image) while the lightbox for B is open.
confirmed.rootCause: The once('value') callbacks only check `box.hidden`, not which photoId the box is currently showing; the box element is shared and reopened.
confirmed.proposedFix: Set `box.dataset.photoId = photoId` on open and in the then/catch handlers return unless it still equals photoId.

verdict.reasoning: My v9_lightbox.cjs: open A (600 ms), close, open B (100 ms): B (800x800) shows, then A's late response overwrites it with 1280x600 while B's lightbox is still open. Second form (A 200 ms, B 500 ms): frames go Loading -> A (1280x600) for ~300 ms -> B, i.e. a flash of the wrong photo. The then/catch callbacks only test `box.hidden`, but the box element is shared across opens. Needs slow loads plus a quick close-and-reopen, hence low.
verdict.refinedFix: Module-level token: `let chatLightboxSeq = 0;` in openChatLightbox do `const mine = ++chatLightboxSeq;` and in both the .then and .catch callbacks `if (box.hidden || mine !== chatLightboxSeq) return;`. Also remove the stale keydown listener on re-open (each open adds one `onKey` that is only removed by that open's own close(); reopening without closing leaks the previous one - harmless but worth cleaning with the same token). No state/listener risk.

confirmed.title: Closing chat drops you at the top of the home page instead of where the Chat card was
confirmed.symptom: Scroll the home page down, tap Chat, tap ← Camp: you land at the very top of the page.
confirmed.trigger: Open chat from the card while scrolled down, then close it (viewer or editor).
confirmed.evidence: p5: viewer scrollY 228 before open -> 0 while open -> 0 after close (chat card top 379px before, 607px after); editor 334 -> 0 -> 0.
confirmed.rootCause: body.chat-open display:none's the rest of .main-wrap so the document collapses to the chat view height and the browser clamps scrollY to 0; closeChat() doesn't restore it.
confirmed.proposedFix: Record `window.scrollY` in openChat and `window.scrollTo(0, saved)` after the renderAll() in closeChat.

verdict.reasoning: My v10_scroll.cjs: viewer scrollY 228 (chat card at top=379) -> 0 while open (document collapses to 844px) -> 0 after close, chat card now at 607; editor 334 -> 0 -> 0. Home page order is you-strip, now-banner, chat-card@607, accordion, so the card is usually still on screen after the jump, which keeps this low.
verdict.refinedFix: In openChat record `chatSavedScrollY = window.scrollY` before renderAll(); in closeChat after renderAll(): `window.scrollTo(0, chatSavedScrollY || 0); chatSavedScrollY = 0;`. Skip when chat was restored open on a cold load (no saved value). Layout is synchronous after renderAll so the scroll lands correctly (home panels use setHtmlIfChanged, so heights are intact).

confirmed.title: Chat announcement banner briefly shows the sender's raw email address instead of their name

confirmed.title: An unread badge appearing widens its tab and shifts the other tabs under the finger

confirmed.title: Phone Back gesture/button leaves the site instead of closing the chat

confirmed.proposedFix: history.pushState({chat:1}) in openChat and a popstate listener that calls closeChat().

verdict.location: chat.js:768-784 openChat/closeChat (and app-wide: no history API use anywhere)
verdict.reasoning: Was code-only in the report; I measured it. v12_back.cjs: about:blank -> app, open chat (body.chat-open true, history.length 2), page.goBack() -> URL becomes about:blank, i.e. system Back leaves Camp instead of closing the takeover. grep shows no history.pushState/popstate/hashchange in app.js, chat.js or settings.js (the pushState hits are the Firebase pushState() function). Matters mainly for Android Back / iOS edge-swipe in a browser tab; an installed PWA just exits.

Cold start with chatOpen persisted has no entry to pop, so push one on init or accept it. Risks: sign-out/reload flows (location.reload keeps state fine), and doing it for chat only gives inconsistent Back behaviour vs settings/game detail - better done for all takeovers at once.

confirmed.title: Same-channel forced rebuilds re-create the input and refocus it outside a user gesture (iOS keyboard likely drops)
confirmed.symptom: If the member directory updates (an editor renames/changes someone), a window backfill happens, or the open channel's ready flip lands while a person is typing, the composer text and caret are restored but on iOS the soft keyboard probably closes and has to be re-opened with a tap.
confirmed.trigger: Typing in the composer on an iPhone while onMemberDirectoryChanged() / backfill / chatReady flip calls renderChatView(true) for the same channel.
confirmed.evidence: Suspected from code only (not measured; iOS not testable here). renderChatView(true) replaces view.innerHTML (the focused input is detached), then calls input.focus() from a Promise/snapshot callback, which iOS Safari does not honour for opening the keyboard. Chromium keeps focus and caret (my v7 draft test: directory/bell rebuilds keep value). The CLAUDE.md/code comments claim the keyboard is carried across.
confirmed.rootCause: Rebuild via innerHTML instead of updating head/tabs/list in place; programmatic focus() without a gesture.
confirmed.proposedFix: For same-channel rebuilds (sameCh true), replace only #chat-list's innerHTML (and refresh the title/bell/tab classes) and leave .chat-composer's nodes untouched so focus never moves; reserve the full innerHTML rebuild for first open and channel switch. Because the composer node is kept only within the same channel, the closures over `ch` in wireChatView stay correct.

Because the composer node is kept only within the same channel, the closures over `ch` in wireChatView stay correct.

confirmed.title: Every open paints a half-built shell, then the real content pops in above it (CLS 0.43)
confirmed.symptom: For roughly 0.2 s on a fast phone and 0.75-0.85 s at 4x CPU, the page shows only five floating card headers (Competitions, Current Standings, ...) at the top of an empty page. Then the follow card, Happening-now banner, chat card and day tabs all appear at once above them and shove the cards down about 620 px.
confirmed.trigger: Open index.html with campScoreboardAuthHint set to viewer or editor (a returning device), warm cache, Firebase blocked. `node p3_return.cjs viewer 1` and `node p3_return.cjs viewer 4`; cold cache: `node p1_boot.cjs fast`.
confirmed.evidence: Layout-shift entry 'jelly-accordion.home-accordion 46->670 h350->174' = 0.433 on every one of 3 reloads at both 1x and 4x CPU (cold cache: 46->556, 0.4308). First paint at 44-148 ms; first content frame at 201-237 ms (1x) and 740-841 ms (4x CPU). Frame log: html class '' with 35 undefined elements and page height 844, then 'view-only' with 0 undefined and height 1072. p26_dcl.cjs: delaying vendor/jelly.js by 1500 ms moved DOMContentLoaded 236 -> 1576 ms and first content 538 -> 1777 ms while first paint stayed at 56 ms.
confirmed.rootCause: boot() is bound to DOMContentLoaded, and that event cannot fire until the deferred module vendor/jelly.js (320 KB) has downloaded and evaluated. In the meantime styles.css deliberately paints the pre-upgrade accordion as a stack of headers, and every section above it is hidden or empty until init() runs. The boot-guard comment says approved devices 'paint the app immediately', but the module gate delays the real paint.
confirmed.location: app.js:8735 (document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', boot)); styles.css:573-590 (jelly-accordion/collapsible :not(:defined) shell rules); boot-guard.js (no hold-back class)
confirmed.proposedFix: Do not paint the shell. Have boot-guard.js add html.booting when a hint exists, add `html.booting #app { visibility: hidden }`, and remove the class at the end of startApp() after the first renderAll (plus a 4 s safety timeout). Alternative: stop gating boot on the module by running boot() as soon as the classic scripts finish (readyState check) and letting Jelly upgrade late, which needs typeof-guards on jelly method calls. At minimum drop the pre-upgrade accordion header stack so nothing paints until content exists.

verdict.location: styles.css:573-590 (jelly-accordion/jelly-collapsible :not(:defined) shell rules); root cause is app.js:8735 DOMContentLoaded gating behind the deferred vendor/jelly.js module
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with my own sampler (hunt/boot-theme-pages-verify/v1_boot.cjs), warm-cache reloads, viewer: first paint 56-72 ms, DCL 121-146 ms, then CLS 0.4308 on every reload ('jelly-accordion 46->556 h350->288'). Html class goes '' (35 undefined elements, scrollHeight 844) to 'view-only' (0 undefined, 958) at ~220-290 ms. At 4x CPU: first paint 144-184 ms, content at ~955-1127 ms (viewer) and ~1.8-2.0 s (editor), same 0.431 CLS. A CDP screencast (v1b_screencast.cjs, 4x CPU) shows the actual composited frames: frame 1 at +169 ms is five floating card headers (Competitions, Current Standings, Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse, Quick Points) on an otherwise empty gray page; frame 2 at +1160 ms is the full page (follow card, Happening-now, Chat card) shoved in above them. Root cause is right: DOMContentLoaded cannot fire until the deferred module has run (jelly.js delayed 5 s moved view-only from ~0.2 s to 5.3 s in v5_backstop.cjs). In this harness Firebase is aborted instantly; with the real SDK (three parser-blocking scripts from gstatic) DCL is later still, so the shell window is at least as long in production. Editors see it longer than viewers (~320 ms vs ~190 ms at 1x). v183 did not touch this.
verdict.refinedFix: Smallest correct fix is CSS-only and I verified it by patching styles.css in flight: restrict the pre-upgrade header-stack shell to the failed-module case, so on a normal load the global :where(html:not(.jelly-failed)) :not(:defined){visibility:hidden} (styles.css:145) keeps it invisible while layout space is preserved. e.g. change the selectors at styles.css:573 and :579 to `html.jelly-failed jelly-accordion:not(:defined)` and `html.jelly-failed jelly-collapsible:not(:defined)` (keep their declarations), leave the :where() body-hide rule at ~:590 as is. Measured result (v1c_fixtest.cjs, variant B, 4x CPU): CLS 0.431 -> 0.002; the pre-module frame is a blank page background, then everything appears at once. With the jelly.js request aborted the fallback still shows the cards (v1d_failedcheck.cjs: accordion visibility visible, class jelly-failed). Equivalent alternative: html.booting + `#app{visibility:hidden}` set in boot-guard.js and cleared at the end of startApp(), but that needs a safety timeout so a boot() exception cannot leave a blank page; the CSS route needs none. Risks/notes: (1) it trades a half-built shell for a blank gray frame for the pre-DCL window, a deliberate reversal of the 'no blank screen' comment at styles.css:567-572 (update that comment); (2) tests/shell.test.js pins the :where() wrappers and the body-hide gating but not these header rules, so it should still pass, run node tests/run.js shell to confirm; (3) combine with the wrong-theme and bg-fade fixes so the blank frame is in the right colour; (4) no JS, no listener or state-object implications. Not recommended: running boot() before the module (needs typeof-guards on every Jelly call).

confirmed.title: Users who override the OS theme get a flash of the wrong theme on every load
confirmed.symptom: If Appearance is set explicitly to Dark while the phone is in light mode, every open starts with a light-gray shell for 0.2-0.9 s and then flips to dark. The reverse (Light chosen while the phone is dark) flashes a dark shell first. Auto users are unaffected.
confirmed.trigger: Set Appearance to Dark with OS light (or Light with OS dark), then reload. `node p4_themeboot.cjs`; `node p30_wrongtheme_cpu.cjs` for the CPU-throttled timing.
confirmed.evidence: OS light + theme dark: body background is rgb(244,246,249) from 25 ms until 238 ms, then body.dark-theme + data-jelly-mode=dark appear. With 4x CPU the dark class lands at 863 ms. OS dark + theme light: rgb(16,20,28) until about 225 ms, then light-theme. Auto matches the OS from the first frame.
confirmed.rootCause: The chosen theme lives only inside the big state JSON (state.theme in campScoreboardV2). applyTheme() runs from boot(), which waits for DOMContentLoaded and therefore for jelly.js (see boot-shell-popin). boot-guard.js, the only pre-paint script, never reads the theme, and styles.css can only pre-paint the OS scheme through its prefers-color-scheme media block.
confirmed.location: boot-guard.js (add a pre-paint theme read); app.js:7233 applyTheme / saveState (mirror the choice); styles.css:50 and :77 token blocks
confirmed.proposedFix: Mirror the choice into a tiny key (for example localStorage.campScoreboardTheme = 'light'|'dark'), written from applyTheme. In boot-guard.js read it and set document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-jelly-mode', t). Add `:root[data-jelly-mode="dark"] body` / `[data-jelly-mode="light"] body` to the token blocks in styles.css so the pre-module shell paints in the right palette. Holding the shell back (boot-shell-popin fix) also hides most of it.

verdict.location: boot-guard.js (no theme read); app.js:7233 applyTheme / app.js:7270 setTheme; styles.css:50 body.dark-theme and :77 media block
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v2_wrongtheme.cjs, warm reloads, theme persisted via setTheme). OS light + stored dark: body background rgb(244,246,249) from 61 ms until ~252 ms, then body.dark-theme + data-jelly-mode=dark appear and the bg fades to oklch(0.2198...) by ~345 ms. OS dark + stored light: rgb(16,20,28) until ~247 ms, then light-theme and a fade to white. At 4x CPU the light shell holds from 118 ms to 958 ms before the dark flip (1066 ms settled). The screencast frame (v2_light_dark_cpu4_f1.png) shows the bright shell on a user who chose Dark. Auto users get the OS palette from frame 1 (OS dark/auto: rgb(16,20,28) from 42 ms), so they are unaffected. Root cause is right: the choice lives only in state.theme inside the big state JSON and applyTheme() runs from boot() after DCL; boot-guard never reads it. Population is limited to people whose explicit choice differs from the OS (hence med, not high), but for them it is a full-screen colour inversion on every open, harshest as a bright flash on a dark-mode phone.
verdict.refinedFix: Mirror the choice and apply it pre-paint. (1) app.js applyTheme(): after the data-jelly-mode block, `try { if (state.theme === 'dark' || state.theme === 'light') localStorage.setItem('campScoreboardTheme', state.theme); else localStorage.removeItem('campScoreboardTheme'); } catch (e) {}`. (2) boot-guard.js, in the first IIFE next to the hint read: `var t = localStorage.getItem('campScoreboardTheme'); if (t === 'dark' || t === 'light') document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-jelly-mode', t);`. (3) styles.css: extend the dark token block selector to `body.dark-theme, :root[data-jelly-mode="dark"] body {` (:50) and scope the OS media block to `:root:not([data-jelly-mode]) body:not(.light-theme):not(.dark-theme) {` (:77) so OS-dark + explicit-light does not paint dark first. Verified in flight (v2b_fixtest.cjs, boot-guard + css patched, key pre-seeded): OS light + stored dark now paints rgb(16,20,28) from the first frame, OS dark + stored light paints rgb(244,246,249), at 1x and 4x. Risks: the new key must be added to clearLocalData's wipe list (app.js ~8661-8665) or theme survives sign-out, contradicting CLAUDE.md, and tests/auth.test.js pins that wipe list so update it; the key is device-wide while state.theme is per-camp, so a dual-camp device with different themes could flash once on camp switch (boot corrects it); Jelly reads data-jelly-mode when it injects tokens, so pre-setting it is consistent with what applyTheme does. Combine with the boot-shell-popin fix, which also hides most of the wrong-coloured shell.

confirmed.title: Theme Auto + phone flips dark->light while Camp is open: podium rows and gold text stay dark and become unreadable
confirmed.symptom: After the OS switches from dark to light with the tab still open, the Current Standings podium rows keep their dark-tinted gold/silver/bronze backgrounds while the text turns dark. Team names in the top three rows become near-illegible. The status-bar colour also stays dark.
confirmed.trigger: Appearance = Auto, OS dark at load, then flip the OS to light without reloading. `node p8_osflip.cjs`, `node p9_osflip_shots.cjs` (sheet_p9.png shows flipped vs fresh-boot).
confirmed.evidence: After the flip: body.className is still 'dark-theme', computed color-scheme is 'dark', --color-on-primary #181b1d, --color-gold #e8c15a, --color-danger-text #ff8a8a, --shadow-card dark, #dynamic-theme-color #181b1d. A fresh light boot has no class, #fff, #96690a and so on. Light->dark works fine because the media block handles it. No matchMedia change listener exists in app.js.
confirmed.rootCause: applyTheme() adds body.dark-theme in Auto mode when the OS is dark at that moment (`dark = state.theme === 'dark' || (state.theme === null && prefersDark)`). It only runs at boot and in setTheme, never on an OS change. body.dark-theme outranks the media block, so the non-Jelly tokens (gold/silver/bronze backgrounds, on-primary, shadows) stay dark while Jelly's own tokens follow the OS to light. Nothing in JS reads the class; it is used only by the two CSS blocks.
confirmed.proposedFix: Only set the class for an explicit choice: `document.body.classList.toggle('dark-theme', state.theme === 'dark')`. Auto is already handled by the `body:not(.light-theme):not(.dark-theme)` media block. Also add `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener('change', applyTheme)` so the theme-color meta tracks the OS.

verdict.location: app.js:7236 (document.body.classList.toggle('dark-theme', dark)) in applyTheme; styles.css:50 and :77
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v3_osflip.cjs, Auto theme, viewer, standings seeded with 9 results). OS dark at load -> body.dark-theme; then page.emulateMedia({colorScheme:'light'}): body class stays 'dark-theme', --color-gold #e8c15a and --color-gold-bg #3a3116 stay dark, while --color-text flips to Jelly's light-mode dark text. Computed contrast of the podium-1 row text vs its background: 11.61 before, 1.21:1 after the flip (fresh light boot: 14.39:1, bg #fff6dd). Screenshot v3_flip_dark_to_light.png shows the three podium rows with dark-brown/navy tints and near-illegible team names while rows 4-6 are fine. #dynamic-theme-color also stays #181b1d. No matchMedia change listener exists (grep: only reduced-motion and the one prefersDark read at app.js:7234). Needs the page to be resident across an OS flip (scheduled dark mode at sunrise, installed PWA kept in memory), hence med rather than high, but it garbles the core Current Standings content.
verdict.refinedFix: One-line fix, verified by patching app.js in flight (v3b_osflip_patched.cjs): in applyTheme change line 7236 to `document.body.classList.toggle('dark-theme', state.theme === 'dark');`. Auto + dark OS is already fully handled by the `body:not(.light-theme):not(.dark-theme)` media block at styles.css:77. Result: flipped state is identical to a fresh boot in both directions (contrast 14.39 after dark->light, 11.61 after light->dark; body class ''). Nothing else reads the class (grep: only styles.css:50/:77 and app.js:7236-7237; no tests reference it). For the status-bar colour also add, once in wireSettings or init: `const mq = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'); if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener('change', () => { if (state.theme === null) applyTheme(); });` so #dynamic-theme-color (a no-media meta that beats the media metas) tracks the OS. applyTheme only toggles classes/attributes, so no DOM rebuild or state-object risk.
