At the 40 ms freeze, inherited text is oklab L 0.47 on a dark card (about 2.3:1; 1:1 in the first frames), and the screenshot shows near-invisible 'Elective 1', 'Swimming', and names. Transitions running at frame 3: body color and background-color 200 ms, plus now-banner border/box-shadow, game-card.done borders and verse-day-chip color (150 ms). Jelly canvas settle: chip 561 ms, button 535-611 ms, switch about 535 ms. The Settings drawer flips in one frame with no dip.
confirmed.rootCause: `body { transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease }` animates the root text colour and page background, but surfaces, tokens and explicit colours flip instantly because the --jelly-*/--color-* variables change in one style recalc. Anything that inherits colour from body is mid-fade against an already-flipped background.
confirmed.location: styles.css:225-231 (body transition); also the 150 ms border/box-shadow/color transitions on .game-card, .now-banner and .verse-day-chip
confirmed.proposedFix: Remove the transition from body, or suppress transitions for the flip frame: in applyTheme add `document.documentElement.classList.add('theme-switching')` with `.theme-switching *, .theme-switching *::before, .theme-switching *::after { transition: none !important }`, then remove the class two animation frames later. Jelly canvases may keep their own easing.

verdict.location: styles.css:225-231 (body transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v4_flip.cjs, standings card open, 60 sampled text elements, per-frame contrast against the nearest opaque ancestor background). setTheme('dark'): first sampled frame t=29 ms has 24 elements below 3:1 (min 1.03), by t=91 ms none below 3:1. setTheme('light'): still 24 elements below 3:1 at t=73 ms (min 1.82), clean by ~115 ms. CDP screencast frame 2 after the flip (v4_dark_f2.png) shows cards already dark while 'Elective 1', Swimming, Nerf War and every name chip are nearly invisible; frame 4 (~100 ms later) has them back. Cause is as stated: body color/background transition 0.2 s while surfaces and var tokens flip in one style recalc. It lasts roughly 3-6 frames and follows a user tap, so it reads as a blink, not a persistent artifact (low).
verdict.refinedFix: Delete `transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease;` from the body rule (styles.css:230). Verified by patching in flight (v4_flip.cjs patched): 0 elements below 3:1 in every sampled frame in both directions, steady-state minimum unchanged (3.94 / 4.35 which are real design values, not the dip). No JS impact; this also removes the page-background fade that boot-bg-fade describes. Do not add `transition:all` anywhere (CLAUDE.md). The 150 ms border/box-shadow/color transitions on .game-card/.now-banner/.verse-day-chip were not seen to cause a dip in the contrast sampling, leave them.

confirmed.title: A slow (not failed) jelly.js load trips the 4 s 'jelly-failed' fallback: raw card bodies and editor-only rows flash, then collapse again
confirmed.symptom: On a slow connection, after 4 s the page suddenly expands all five cards into unstyled content, including the editors' 'Hide from viewers' rows even for viewers. When jelly.js finally arrives everything re-collapses and re-lays out (two big jumps).
confirmed.trigger: Delay vendor/jelly.js by 5 s: `node p2_slowshots.cjs 5000 1`. Also reproduced with 1.6 Mbps + 4x CPU on the uncompressed local server: `node p1_boot.cjs slow`.
confirmed.evidence: html.jelly-failed appears at about 4.0 s, page height 844 -> 1070; at about 5.5 s jelly arrives (cls 'view-only', height 958, picker open). Two layout shifts: 0.5733 (accordion 46->70, h350->774) and 0.4976 (70->556, h774->288), total 1.07. Screenshots in sheet_p2_boot_slow.png show 'Hide from viewers' rows before the view-only class exists. Real GitHub Pages gzip is about 540 KB for all scripts including the Firebase SDK, so it takes roughly <1 Mbps effective to reach 4 s; the guard's own comment names congested camp wifi right after a deploy as the likely case.
confirmed.rootCause: boot-guard.js starts a 4000 ms timer at head-parse, but a type=module script only executes after the whole document and all parser-blocking body scripts (3 Firebase SDKs, app.js, settings.js, chat.js, push.js ...) have loaded and run. On a slow link the module is therefore late through no fault of its own. The real failure signals (script error event, window error with jelly.js filename) already cover request and parse failures, so the timer only guards a hang. view-only is also not applied until boot() runs, which is why editor rows show.
confirmed.proposedFix: Raise the backstop to about 15-20 s (or arm it only after window 'load'), since failures are caught immediately by the error listeners. Optionally keep html.view-only decisions out of the fallback by applying the hint role class in boot-guard.js pre-paint.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced two ways. (1) jelly.js delayed 5 s (v5_backstop.cjs, viewer): html.jelly-failed at 4042 ms, scrollHeight 844->1070, five .card-visibility-row 'Hide from viewers' rows become visible to a VIEWER (view-only class does not exist until boot() runs), module arrives 5305 ms and everything re-collapses; layout shifts 0.5733 + 0.4976 = 1.071. Screenshot v5_5000_viewer_4500.png shows the unstyled expanded cards with the editor rows. (2) Whole-link throttle, no per-resource delay (v5b_throttle.cjs, cache disabled, 150 ms latency): at 250 KB/s (about 1 Mbps effective once Pages gzip is considered; total gz of the app scripts is ~305 KB plus ~180 KB Firebase SDK) jelly-failed appears at 5480 ms, module at 6104 ms, CLS 1.071; at 500 KB/s the module lands at 4.0 s, before the guard timer (~4.9 s) fires, so no misfire. So it needs sustained roughly under 2 Mbps (rural camp wifi or cell right after a deploy when every phone reloads), which is why it is low. Root cause correct: the module executes only after the parser and all body scripts, so 'late' is not 'failed'.
verdict.refinedFix: Raise the backstop: `setTimeout(check, 15000);` (the request-error and window-error listeners already catch real failures immediately; the timer only guards a hung request, where 15 s of a blank/shell page is acceptable). Must update tests/shell.test.js line ~35 (`GUARD.includes('setTimeout(check, 4000)')`) in the same commit or the suite fails. Optional hardening: have boot-guard.js also add the hint role class (html.view-only when hint === 'viewer') pre-paint so a viewer never sees editor rows even in a real failure; keep it inside the first IIFE, mirror what setMemberRole does. Do not arm the timer on window 'load' (a hung module never fires load). No state or listener implications.

confirmed.title: The Google Fonts stylesheet is render-blocking: a stalled fonts.googleapis.com leaves a blank white page
confirmed.symptom: On a network where fonts.googleapis.com is slow or hangs (filtered or captive wifi), nothing paints, not even the lock screen, until that request resolves or times out.
confirmed.trigger: Delay the fonts.googleapis.com request 3 s: `node p20_fontblock.cjs`.
confirmed.evidence: first-paint and first-contentful-paint at 68 ms with no delay, and at 3040 ms with a 3000 ms delay. The font swap itself is harmless (see checkedClean).
confirmed.rootCause: `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">` in <head> is a render-blocking stylesheet. display=swap only affects the font files, not the CSS fetch.
confirmed.proposedFix: Load the font CSS without blocking paint: inject the <link> from boot-guard.js (CSP forbids inline onload handlers) or use rel=preload as=style plus a script-applied swap. Alternatively self-host an Inter subset under font-src 'self'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v6_fontblock.cjs): first-paint/FCP 68 ms with no delay, 3052 ms when fonts.googleapis.com stalls 3 s then fails, identical with or without the auth hint (so even the lock screen waits). The stylesheet is render-blocking as claimed. Real-world reach is small: it needs fonts.googleapis.com to hang rather than fail fast (filtered hosts normally reject quickly), and Google serves that CSS with a one-day max-age plus stale-while-revalidate so returning devices rarely wait on it. Not visible in normal use, so low and not worth a risky change.
verdict.refinedFix: Optional. Cheapest safe form under the CSP (no inline onload allowed): change the tag to `<link id="gfonts" rel="stylesheet" media="print" href="...">` and add to a separate IIFE in boot-guard.js `var l=document.getElementById('gfonts'); if(l){ var on=function(){ l.media='all'; }; l.addEventListener('load',on); if(l.sheet) on(); }` (media=print links do not block render). Expect a font-swap reflow (Inter vs system-ui) on first visit; p19 showed it is minor but it would add a small CLS, so apply the shell fix first. Or self-host an Inter subset under font-src 'self'. Remember tests/shell.test.js reads index.html.

confirmed.title: current-standings.html cold load flashes white -> near-black 'Checking sign-in...' -> white before the intro
confirmed.symptom: On the TV/presenter machine every load (and every auto-reload after a TV_BUILD bump) goes: white page with 'Loading standings...', then a full-screen 96% black overlay saying 'Camp - Current Standings / Checking sign-in...', then back to white, then the intro.
confirmed.trigger: Open current-standings.html on a machine that is already signed in. Reproduced with a stubbed Firebase (SRI removed, auth resolves after 450 ms): `node p25_tvsignin.cjs` (sheet_p25_tv.png).
confirmed.evidence: Timeline of [overlay, loading, screen.hidden]: 7 ms [none, flex, true]; 521 ms [flex, flex, true] (black overlay); 1117 ms [none, flex, true]; 1368 ms [none, none, false] (intro). The black overlay stays up for about 600 ms with the stub timings; with the real SDK it lasts as long as auth restore plus the member read. Stub timings are artificial but the order is deterministic.
confirmed.rootCause: startData() calls setAuthOverlay('checking') synchronously before auth has answered, and the overlay is rgba(6,8,12,0.96) on a white page. For an already-approved machine that state is a hard cut with no transition.
confirmed.proposedFix: Show the overlay only for the 'signin' and 'denied' modes, or delay 'checking' by about 1.5 s so a quick approval never shows it. Use the existing 'Loading standings...' state for the check.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced with my own stubbed Firebase (v7_tv.cjs; SDK script replaced inline, auth resolves 300 ms, member read 200 ms). Timeline: 7 ms white page with 'Loading standings...'; 52 ms #auth-overlay flex (rgba(6,8,12,0.96) full screen, 'Checking sign-in...'); 567 ms overlay none, white again; 668 ms intro shown. Screenshot v7_tv_1.png shows the near-black card over the white page. The order is deterministic from the code: startData() calls setAuthOverlay('checking') synchronously, and again at :740 when a user object arrives; with the real SDK the black phase lasts auth restore plus member read. It is a one-time hard cut at load on the presenter machine, so low.
verdict.refinedFix: Don't show the 'checking' state immediately. In startData replace both setAuthOverlay('checking') calls with a delayed one: `var checkTimer = setTimeout(function () { setAuthOverlay('checking'); }, 1500);` and clear it (clearTimeout(checkTimer)) inside setAuthOverlay for every other mode (add at the top of setAuthOverlay), so a normal sub-second approval never shows it but a slow/offline check still does. The existing 'Loading standings...' state already covers the wait. The keydown/click guards at :1068 and :1079 read the overlay display only to block input once data exists, so skipping the overlay during checking changes nothing there. 'signin' and 'denied' stay immediate.

confirmed.title: Zero-clock 'alarm-flash' (infinite background strobe) is not covered by prefers-reduced-motion
confirmed.symptom: When a game clock reaches 0:00 the clock box flashes between its background and a red tint twice a second, forever, on every device that has that game open, even with reduce-motion on. The other zero-clock effect (pulsing digits) is correctly disabled.
confirmed.trigger: Emulate reduced motion, open a clock game (for example counselor-hide-seek) with remaining 0. `node p12_alarm.cjs`.
confirmed.evidence: reduce=true still runs '#clock-area div.tool-box.game-clock-box :: alarm-flash iter=Infinity dur=500'; reduce=false also runs board-zero-pulse, which is gone under reduce. Of all @keyframes in styles.css only alarm-flash lacks a guard (lock-shake is also unguarded but dead: no JS adds .shake).
confirmed.rootCause: The reduce block at styles.css:5751 lists the board clock classes but not .tool-box.alarming; the rule at :2813 has no media guard.
confirmed.proposedFix: Add `.tool-box.alarming { animation: none; }` to a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block (keep the border-color change as the static cue). Optionally delete the dead .lock-box.shake rule.

verdict.location: styles.css:2813-2822 (.tool-box.alarming / @keyframes alarm-flash); reduce block at styles.css:5751
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v8_alarm.cjs, counselor-hide-seek with remaining 0, editor): with reducedMotion 'reduce' (matchMedia true) the computed animation-name is still alarm-flash, iteration infinite, one running alarm-flash animation, background cycling between oklab L 0.88 and 0.999 across 6 samples 120 ms apart; identical to no-preference. Only the board-clock classes are covered at :5751. Confirmed lock-shake is dead: no JS references 'shake' (grep of *.js finds only an unrelated 'handshake' comment). Low because it affects reduce-motion users only and only while a clock sits at 0:00; the effect is a slow background pulse (about 1 Hz), not a hard strobe.
verdict.refinedFix: Add `.tool-box.alarming { animation: none; }` inside the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block at styles.css:5751; the red border-color on the same rule stays as the static cue. Optionally delete the dead `.lock-box.shake`/@keyframes lock-shake (styles.css:394-402). No JS involved.

confirmed.title: Opening a game still smooth-scrolls under prefers-reduced-motion
confirmed.symptom: With reduce-motion on, tapping a game card (or a Live-now card) still performs the animated eased scroll to the game view.
confirmed.trigger: Emulate reduced motion, expand Competitions, tap a game card. `node p11_reduced2.cjs`.
confirmed.evidence: scrollY samples across frames: reduce=false 17 distinct values (0,0,2,10,27,56,105,190 ...) ending at 759; reduce=true 28 distinct values with the same curve (0,0,2,11,27,58,113,206 ...). Explicit behavior:'smooth' is not suppressed by the media query.
confirmed.rootCause: Two scrollIntoView calls hard-code behavior:'smooth' with no reduced-motion check, unlike celebrate() and joyBurst().
confirmed.proposedFix: Use `behavior: JOY_REDUCED.matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth'` (JOY_REDUCED is already defined at app.js:8005, so hoist it or re-query matchMedia).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v9_scroll.cjs, editor, tap a game card): scrollY samples reduce=false 17 distinct values (0,0,2,10,27,56,105,190,310,423 ... 759); reduce=true 28 distinct values on the same curve ending at 759 (matchMedia reduce confirmed true). An explicit behavior:'smooth' is not suppressed by the media query. Code confirmed at both call sites; JOY_REDUCED (app.js:8005) is a top-level const initialised at script load, and both call sites are click handlers, so referencing it there has no TDZ problem. Accessibility inconsistency only: low.
verdict.refinedFix: Replace `{ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' }` at app.js:5495 and :5737 with `{ behavior: JOY_REDUCED.matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth', block: 'start' }`. confirmed.title: jelly-failed fallback: Settings/picker sheets can only be closed with the Escape key, and the Appearance control is inert
confirmed.symptom: On a phone where jelly.js cannot load (iOS < 16.4 is the documented case), opening Settings shows a plain bottom sheet with no close button or backdrop. Tapping outside does nothing, and the Light/Auto/Dark control is plain text that does nothing when tapped.
confirmed.trigger: Block vendor/jelly.js and call openSettings(): `node p15_failed_settings.cjs`.
confirmed.evidence: Sheet open at top 213 px, height 631; no close/aria-label button in it; after tapping outside open is still true; clicking the 'dark' segment left state.theme null. Screenshot p15_failed_settings.png (the identity picker stacked on top is from the test sequence). The jelly-failed path otherwise works: no page errors, lock screen and Google button visible, both for a request abort and a parse error.
confirmed.rootCause: The pre-upgrade jelly-drawer/jelly-dialog fallback CSS has no dismiss affordance, and wireSettings() only adds an Escape keydown handler, which touch phones have no key for.
confirmed.proposedFix: In the :not(:defined)[open] fallback add a visible close affordance (for example a ::before 'Close' bar) and have the same degraded-mode handler close on a tap of the sheet's top bar or outside. Optionally render native <select> or radios for Appearance when jelly-failed.

verdict.location: styles.css:176-198 (jelly-drawer/jelly-dialog:not(:defined)[open] fallback); app.js:1110-1121 (Escape-only handler in wireSettings)
verdict.reasoning: Reproduced for both a request abort and a SyntaxError module (v11_failed.cjs, real touch taps, class 'jelly-failed view-only'): page.tap('#settings-btn') opens the sheet (top 395, height 449) which has no close button (hasClose false); a touch tap on the page outside it leaves open=true; tapping the Dark segment leaves state.theme null (jelly-segmented never upgrades, so no change event). Screenshot v11_syntax_settings.png shows the plain sheet with Appearance as inert text. No page errors. The sheet is not a trap (the page behind still scrolls and a reload clears it; sign-out is reachable) and only devices that cannot load jelly.js are affected (iOS < 16.4 is the documented case), hence low.
verdict.refinedFix: In wireSettings' degraded-mode block (app.js:1114-1120), add, guarded at event time by `!customElements.get('jelly-drawer')` so a late-arriving module takes over cleanly: (a) a capture-phase `document.addEventListener('click', e => { const open = [...document.querySelectorAll('jelly-drawer[open], jelly-dialog[open]')]; if (open.length && !open.some(el => el.contains(e.target))) { open.forEach(el => el.removeAttribute('open')); e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); } }, true)` (the settings-btn click that opens the sheet runs when nothing is open, so it is unaffected; nested sheets such as alerts-overlay are covered because the target is inside an open sheet); (b) for Appearance, a delegated click on `#theme-toggle jelly-segment` calling setTheme(seg.getAttribute('value')) only when !customElements.get('jelly-segmented') (otherwise it would double-fire with the component's own change event), or simply hide the Appearance row under html.jelly-failed. Optionally add a `::before` 'Close' bar in the :not(:defined)[open] rule for discoverability. These are plain document listeners on elements that are not rebuilt, so no stale-listener or typed-value risk.

confirmed.title: Light and dark boots both fade the page background when Jelly's tokens land
confirmed.symptom: At load the page background is #f4f6f9 (light) or #10141c (dark) and then fades to Jelly's #ffffff / #181b1d a moment later, in the same window as the content pop-in. In light mode cards (white) go from sitting on gray to sitting on pure white.
confirmed.trigger: Reload in either OS scheme with Auto. `node p4_themeboot.cjs` (rows for OS=light/auto and OS=dark/auto).
confirmed.evidence: OS light auto: rgb(244,246,249) at 37 ms -> oklch(1 0 0) at 354 ms via an oklab fade. OS dark auto: rgb(16,20,28) at 35 ms -> oklch(0.2198 0.006 236.84) by 321 ms; card surfaces keep the same value.
confirmed.rootCause: The var() fallbacks in styles.css (#f4f6f9, #10141c) differ from Jelly's injected token values, and `body { transition: background 0.2s }` turns the swap into a visible fade.
confirmed.proposedFix: Align the fallbacks with Jelly's actual defaults (#ffffff / #181b1d) and drop the body transition (see theme-flip-text-dip).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v14_bgfade.cjs, per-frame body and card colour, cold load). OS light: body rgb(244,246,249) at 73 ms, starts fading at ~487 ms, reaches oklch(1 0 0) at ~781 ms; cards are white throughout, so cards go from sitting on gray to white on white. OS dark: rgb(16,20,28) at 49 ms -> oklch(0.2198 0.006 236.84) (#181b1d) by ~623 ms; card surface rgb(26,32,48) = oklch(0.2514 0.0163 264.22) is unchanged. So the claim is exact, but the magnitude is about 3% lightness, in the same window as the shell pop-in, so it is a subtle secondary artifact (low).
verdict.refinedFix: Align the three --color-bg fallbacks with Jelly's real defaults: `#ffffff` at styles.css:16 and `#181b1d` at :52 and :79 (and drop the body transition, see theme-flip-text-dip). Verified by patching in flight (v14b_bgfade_patched.cjs): body background is rgb(255,255,255) / rgb(24,27,29) from the first frame and the Jelly token landing changes it by < 1e-5 in oklab, i.e. no visible fade; card colours unchanged. confirmed.title: Auto theme: OS flip light->dark leaves the browser-chrome theme-color meta stuck on white
confirmed.symptom: With Appearance = Auto, if the phone switches from light to dark while Camp is open, the page itself goes dark (media block) but the status bar / URL bar colour meta stays #ffffff, so a white bar sits above a dark page. findings.title: Happening-now progress bar still refills from empty whenever the rain hint changes
findings.symptom: On days with a rain forecast of 40% or more in the next 3 hours, the 'Happening now' bar blanks and refills from 0 mid-block. This is the same 'progress bar keeps reloading' glitch the owner reported. It happens at each hour rollover and after each weather refresh that changes the percentage. It also happens when the hint appears or disappears, and once at page load when the weather arrives after the first paint.
findings.trigger: Senior: ?now=1-1950 (Evening worship 7:15-8:30). Inject weatherData with precip 60 at hours 20 and 21 and step the minute 19:50 to 20:10: at 20:00 the hint text changes 'near 8pm' to 'this hour' and the bar is a new element. In the same setup, calling repaintWeather() with a changed % or with the rain cleared also swaps the bar. Junior: Sunday 'Registration 2:00-4:00pm' at 3:00 behaves the same. Repro: node p15_rain.cjs senior.
findings.evidence: p15_rain.cjs senior: 'BAR RE-CREATED (refills from 0)' with hint '60% chance of rain near 8pm -> 60% chance of rain this hour' at minute 1200. 'weather refresh changed rain % 50->70' gave barRecreated:true, and 'rain hint disappears' gave barRecreated:true. A fresh jelly-progress keeps changing pixels for more than 40 frames (p9_connect.cjs, 40 distinct canvas states), so every re-creation shows a fill animation of about 0.7 s or longer. Junior reproduced the hour-rollover case (minute 900, 'Registration').
findings.rootCause: renderNowBanner's shape check (app.js:825) strips only the bar's value attribute. nowBannerHtml (app.js:755-760) places upcomingRainHint() inside the same markup string, so any change to the hint text changes the shape. The early return is skipped and setHtmlIfChanged rebuilds the whole banner, including a new jelly-progress. The same path also fires when mealCleanupNote text changes, for example a remote team rename. The bar is also absent while a live Big Board hides the banner (app.js:813-817 clears innerHTML), so it fills from 0 again after every live game or game-view toggle.
findings.proposedFix:
Make the bar a persistent node that is never part of the replaced markup. Either (a) strip the `
...
` from `shape` and patch `.now-wx` in place on the early-return path, or (b) split the banner into stable children (eyebrow, body, bar) and update only the changed pieces. For the live-board case, set `el.hidden = true` and keep the children instead of `innerHTML = ''`, so the bar does not refill from 0 when a live game ends.

findings.title: Big Board loses its final-minute and final-ten red clock, heartbeat and glow on every renderAll
findings.symptom: In the last 10 seconds of a live game, any incoming snapshot (a goal, another editor's save, an announcement) turns the red heartbeat clock back to normal text colour and switches the board glow off. It stays that way for up to 500 ms, then jumps back with the heartbeat and glow restarted from phase 0. The last-minute amber pulse is restarted the same way. Visible on the home Big Board for viewers and editors.
findings.trigger: Junior: a live-tracker game (jeb-ball) or a tally game with a clock (counselor-hide-seek) with a running clock inside its last 10 s. Call renderAll() with any real change. Repro: node p22_final10.cjs light (and dark), or p2_live.cjs.
findings.evidence: p22_final10.cjs: steady state has clock colour oklch(0.577 0.215 27) (red), animation clock-heartbeat, board animation board-glow. Right after renderAll: colour oklch(0.26 ...) (default text), clock animation none, board animation none. This is unchanged at +250 ms and restored at +650 ms. Dark scheme is the same (colour flips to oklch(0.96 ...)). p2_live.cjs C and D show clsImmediately = 'board-clock | big-board viewer' with no clock-final-ten or board-final-ten classes, and sameBoard:false.
findings.rootCause: renderLiveHome rewrites the whole board with innerHTML (app.js:5688). liveTrackerHTML and tallyBoardHTML emit only `board-clock-zero` in markup. `clock-final-min`, `clock-final-ten` and `board-final-ten` are applied only by tickBoardClocks (app.js:3529-3533), which runs every 500 ms. So a freshly rebuilt board is missing them until the next tick. The new nodes also restart their CSS animations from 0.
findings.location: app.js:5664-5751 (renderLiveHome), app.js:5776 (tallyBoardHTML), app.js:6635 (liveTrackerHTML), app.js:3511-3535 (tickBoardClocks); same pattern wherever the board is rebuilt in the game view
findings.proposedFix: Factor the class logic out of tickBoardClocks into one helper, for example `clockStateClasses(clock, rem)`, and call it both when building the markup and in the tick. A rebuilt board is then born in its final state. Better still, avoid rebuilding the board when only unrelated state changed: wrap the innerHTML in setHtmlIfChanged keyed on the markup with the clock text and state classes excluded, so the animation phase survives.

findings.title: Live-now card's red pulse ring restarts on every renderAll
findings.symptom: The 2 s ring around a 'LIVE' card is cut off and restarts each time any snapshot lands. During active scoring (an editor tapping every few seconds) the ring never completes its cycle and looks like it is twitching.
findings.trigger: Junior: start a bracket on a game without liveTracker (ladder-ball), or have a second live game. Call renderAll(). A live-tracker game on its own is shown as a Big Board, not a card. Repro: node p2_live.cjs viewer junior light (A and B) and p20_ring.cjs.
findings.evidence: p2_live A: sameNode:false, pulse currentTime 2000 ms before and 17 ms after. B: sampled 0-16 ms after each renderAll, 400 ms apart, the phase is [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] where a steady ring would read 400, 800, 1200 and so on. p20_ring.cjs: box-shadow spread 5.26 px at alpha 0.11 just before, then 0 px at alpha 0.45 in the same frame after renderAll, so the ring snaps away.
findings.rootCause: renderLiveHome does `wrap.innerHTML = boardHTML + games.map(...)` unconditionally (app.js:5688). Each .live-home-card button is re-created, which restarts its `animation: live-pulse 2s infinite`. setHtmlIfChanged (v183) is not used here.
findings.proposedFix: Build the markup string first and write it with setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html), wiring listeners only when it returns true. For the board, exclude the ticking clock text from the compared string (or patch it in place) so a clock tick does not count as a change. Shares one fix with the lost-tap and cannon findings.

findings.title: Tapping a Live-now card or home Big Board does nothing if a snapshot lands during the press
findings.symptom: A spectator taps the live card or board to open the game. If any renderAll runs between pointerdown and pointerup, nothing opens. The tap is silently dropped.
findings.trigger: Junior with a live ladder-ball card (or a kickball Big Board). Hold the pointer down, call renderAll() (any remote snapshot), release. Repro: node p14_press.cjs.
findings.evidence: p14_press.cjs: card: control tap opens game 'ladder-ball'; tap with renderAll between down and up leaves state.ui.gameId = null. Board: control opens 'kangaroo-kickball'; with a snapshot between down and up, null. The tap fails because the pressed element is replaced.
findings.rootCause: Same unconditional innerHTML rebuild in renderLiveHome (app.js:5688). The element that received pointerdown is detached before pointerup, so no click is dispatched. A press lasts about 100 ms and snapshots arrive every few seconds during live scoring, so only a small share of taps are lost.
findings.proposedFix: Same fix as the pulse-restart finding: setHtmlIfChanged or in-place patching so unchanged live cards keep their nodes. Alternatively use one delegated click handler on the stable #live-home wrapper instead of per-node listeners.

findings.title: Goal emoji cannons and the score pop are wiped by the next renderAll
findings.symptom: On the home Big Board, the 24-emoji cannon volley (1-1.8 s) and the score-pop vanish instantly if any other snapshot or tick-driven render arrives within about 2 s of the goal.
findings.trigger: Junior kickball board on the home screen. Raise a team's hr in state.live and call renderAll(), then call renderAll() again 0.4 s later. Repro: node p10_cannon.cjs.
findings.evidence: p10_cannon.cjs: cannonsAtGoal 24 and scorePopAtGoal 1. After 400 ms, still 24. After the next renderAll, cannonsAfterNextRender 0 and scorePopAfterNextRender 0.
findings.rootCause: boardCelebrate appends the cannon spans to the .big-board element itself and removes them with a 2100 ms timer (app.js:6587-6620). renderLiveHome replaces that element on every render, taking the particles and the .score-pop class with it.
findings.proposedFix: Stop rebuilding the board when nothing about it changed (same fix as the pulse finding). Also host the cannons in a persistent overlay (a sibling of the board inside #live-home, or #joy-layer positioned from the board's rect) so a rebuild cannot erase them.

findings.title: Sparkle burst fires on editor devices when a game clock hits zero, with no user action
findings.symptom: When a synced game clock expires (the alarm sounds), every editor device throws a 16-particle 'big' sparkle burst from wherever the last tap was, or from screen centre if there was none. It is a celebration with no save behind it. Viewers see nothing.
findings.trigger: Editor device with a running synced clock reaching 0:00. In no-sync mode set window.FIREBASE_CONFIG = {} so settleExpiredClocks may write. Repro: node p6_joy.cjs.
findings.evidence: p6_joy.cjs: editor: particles before expiry 0, peak 16 within about 2.6 s, lastTap {x:null,y:null} (centre of screen), clock.running false afterwards. Viewer: peak 0.
findings.rootCause: tickBoardClocks calls settleExpiredClocks (app.js:3482), which runs setClock (app.js:6425). setClock calls touchData (app.js:2075), which calls joyCelebrate (app.js:2079 and 8078). joyCelebrate has no check that the write came from a user gesture. Every editor device settles the clock, so each one bursts.
findings.proposedFix: Let joyCelebrate fire only when a pointer or keyboard event happened in the last ~1.5 s. Record the time in the existing pointerdown handler, which already tracks joyLastTap. That also protects any future automated writes. Alternatively give settleExpiredClocks a quiet write path that skips touchData's celebration.

findings.title: Toasts stack without limit and can cover most of the screen
findings.symptom: One remote snapshot that moves several teams' points produces one toast per team, all at once, for 4-5.5 s each. Nine toasts filled a 598 px column of an 844 px phone. The toasts take taps (pointer-events:auto), and the first one sits directly over the 'tap to refresh' update bar.
findings.trigger: Any phone with notifications on. Following a team turns that on automatically (enableNotify in the team picker). Then receive a remote snapshot that changes several teams: a placement save moves 3 teams, a new-week reset or restore moves all 6, and waking a phone after a long sleep replays the catch-up. Repro: node p7_toast.cjs light, and node p19_overlap.cjs for the update banner.
findings.evidence: p7_toast.cjs: n = 9 toasts, rail top 228 to bottom 826 (598 px of an 844 px viewport), 2 still visible at about 4.6 s. p19_overlap.cjs: with the update banner at y 748-828, the bottom toast at y 747-826 spans the same x range, so toastOverlapsUpdateBanner is true for that toast.
findings.rootCause: notifyPointChanges (app.js:3272-3285) calls showToast once per changed team with no coalescing. jelly-toaster has no cap (vendor/jelly.js:1262 push appends). The toaster and the update bar share the same bottom-right corner (toaster z-index 10002, update bar z-index 60).
findings.location: app.js:3272-3296 (notifyPointChanges, notifyMatchupChanges), app.js:3198 (showToast), vendor/jelly.js ~1262 (jelly-toaster push), styles.css:4258 (.update-banner)
findings.proposedFix: Coalesce each snapshot's point alerts into one toast, for example '+5 Maples, +4 Turkey, +3 Foxes', and keep the 'Your team' toast separate. Cap visible toasts at about 3 by removing the oldest in showToast. Lift the toaster above the update bar, or hide the bar while toasts show.

findings.title: Toasts and OS notifications show ''' and '&' for names with apostrophes or ampersands
findings.symptom: A team or game name with an apostrophe or ampersand reads wrongly in point and 'up next' toasts and OS notifications, for example "Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts".
findings.trigger: Rename a team to "Pete's Pandas & Co" or have a game named "Let's Go". Fire notifyPointChanges or notifyMatchupChanges. Repro: node p13_esc.cjs.
findings.evidence: p13_esc.cjs toast texts: "🦃 Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts (now 12)" and "Up next: 🦃 Pete's Pandas & Co vs 🍁 Methodic Mediocre Maples — Let's Go <Ball>". Current default junior team names have no special characters, so it appears only after a rename or a game name that contains an apostrophe or ampersand.
findings.rootCause: msg is built with esc(team.name) and esc(game.name) (app.js:3277 and 3292), but it is passed to showToast and maybeNativeNotification. Both are text sinks (jellyToast uses textContent; showNotification takes plain text), so the HTML escaping is displayed literally.
findings.proposedFix: Drop esc() when building toast and notification text. Escape only where markup is actually generated.

findings.title: Notice board, My electives, standings rows and catch-up hint are rebuilt on every renderAll and 30 s tick, dropping selection
findings.symptom: Text a counselor has selected in the notice board (for example the cleanup assignments) is deselected within 30 s or on the next snapshot. The same holds for text selected in the My electives card and the standings rows. No animation or scroll jump results; scroll position was stable in tests.
findings.trigger: Posted notice, then select text and call renderAll() or the tick set. Repro: node p18_scroll.cjs (selection) and node p1_census.cjs (mutation census).
findings.evidence: p18_scroll.cjs: selection 'Where your team cleans' before, '' after renderAll. Scroll Y was unchanged (135 to 135 and 2157 to 2157). p1_census.cjs: #notice-board adds and removes a div.notice-card on every renderAll and every tick. #my-electives-card is rebuilt on every renderAll and tick. #standings-tbody is fully rebuilt on every renderAll. No new animations were created in any idle scenario. Rebuilds of the standings table, #catchup-hint and My electives under idle renderAll with a card open created no animations (p4_cards.cjs).
findings.rootCause: renderNoticeBoard (app.js:690-691) and renderMyElectives (app.js:4618-4630) assign innerHTML unconditionally. renderStandings (app.js:4296-4333) clears tbody and re-creates every row each time. These were not moved to setHtmlIfChanged in v183.
findings.proposedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged for the notice board and My electives. For standings, rebuild a row only when its row HTML or its pulse flag changed, or skip the whole tbody write when nothing changed (the points-pulse logic needs the fresh rows only when a pulse is due).

findings.title: Happening-now banner changes height at nearly every block boundary, pushing the page by up to 300 px
findings.symptom: At a block boundary the banner height jumps between 49 px (competitions one-liner) and 131-206 px (rising bell, meals with a dish and cleanup note), and up to 406-448 px for an elective (the full station roster). Everything below it (live card, Chat, all five cards) jumps by that amount. If the user is scrolled below the banner, Chrome shifts scrollY to compensate; if the banner is on screen, the cards jump off-screen.
findings.trigger: Junior Monday at 1:15pm (Elective 1), 3:00 and 4:00pm (Elective 2 and 3). Every one of the 144 junior boundaries and 106 senior boundaries changes content. Repro: node p3_boundaries.cjs viewer junior, node p3b_shift.cjs viewer junior.
findings.evidence: p3_boundaries.cjs: dow1 13:15 Prepare for Elective 1 (109 px) to Elective 1 (406 px); 14:00 back to 125 px; 15:00 to 422 px; 16:00 to 448 px; 10:00 competitions 131 to 49 px. No hidden gaps (the banner never disappears) and the bar is never reused across blocks. p3b_shift.cjs: at scrollY 0 the Standings card moves from y=600 to y=897; layout-shift entries 0.1506 and 0.1736. With the page scrolled down, scrollY auto-adjusted from 378 to 97 and the card stayed at y=519.
findings.rootCause: The banner renders the full per-station roster inline for elective blocks (app.js:784-796), and every block has its own height from label wrapping, the 'Up next' line, the cleanup note and the rain hint. There is no reserved or capped height, no collapse or expand control, and no transition.
findings.proposedFix: Cap the elective roster behind a 'Your station / see everyone' toggle, or show only the viewer's station (state.identity) with the full roster in the Full-schedule sheet. Give the banner a stable min-height for the common timed case. This overlaps with the owner's request to rethink the page layout.

findings.title: Team picker briefly opens, then closes itself, on a brand-new device for a counselor with an assigned team
findings.symptom: On a first launch (no stored follow-team), the 'Which team are you rooting for?' dialog opens, then closes once the member snapshot arrives and assigns the team. The delay is the member snapshot latency, probably 0.3-1 s on a phone (suspected, not timed on a real device).
findings.trigger: Fresh device (state.followTeam undefined, no cache) signing in as a member whose record has a teamId; the hint paints the app before the member snapshot arrives. Simulated with maybeShowTeamPicker() then setMemberTeam('t2'). Repro: node p24_picker.cjs.
findings.evidence: p24_picker.cjs: picker open at t0 and at +500 ms, then open:false after setMemberTeam('t2'), with followTeam 't2'. Only the sequence was simulated, not real latency.
findings.rootCause: startApp() calls maybeShowTeamPicker() (app.js:8137, 4684) before memberTeamId is known. adoptMemberTeam (app.js:4662-4682) later closes the already-open dialog.
findings.proposedFix: When an authHint exists but the member record has not resolved, defer maybeShowTeamPicker until the first member snapshot (approved branch), or hold it for about 1 s. Do not open the dialog and then close it.

findings.title: A remote announcement moves the caret to the end of the editor's half-typed announcement
findings.symptom: An editor typing in the announcement composer, with the caret mid-text, has the caret jump to the end when another announcement arrives. The text and focus are kept.
findings.trigger: Editor opens the composer, types text and places the caret at position 7, then a remote announcement arrives (renderAnnouncements with new content). Repro: node p12_misc.cjs editor junior.
findings.evidence: p12_misc.cjs: input was re-created (sameInput:false), focusAfter:true, value preserved, caret [19,19] after being [7,7] before.
findings.rootCause: renderAnnouncements rebuilds the markup and restores value and focus, but not selectionStart or selectionEnd (app.js:7546-7556). It also calls focus(), which on iOS can reopen the keyboard or scroll.
findings.proposedFix: Save and restore selectionStart and selectionEnd. Better, insert the new banner nodes before the composer and leave the composer element untouched when only the banners changed.

findings.title: Schedule sheet rows re-run their rise-in if a snapshot or tick lands within 0.9 s of a day-chip tap
findings.symptom: After tapping a day chip in the open Full-schedule sheet, a renderAll or 30 s tick that lands during the 900 ms stagger window makes the heading, timeline and calendar button re-run joy-rise from invisible. Rare and brief.
findings.trigger: Open the schedule sheet, tap a day chip, then call renderAll() 350 ms later. Repro: node p12_misc.cjs (schedule-sheet section).
findings.evidence: p12_misc.cjs: joyRiseRunningAt350ms 3, joyRiseREPLAYEDbySyncInWindow 3. In the same run, an idle renderAll with no tap created no animations, and scroll position stayed correct. p12b_sched.cjs and p12c_sched.cjs: scrollTop stayed at 400 or 500 through renderAll, refreshOpenSchedule and the real 30 s interval.
findings.rootCause: refreshOpenSchedule (app.js:7879-7882) rebuilds `wrap.innerHTML` (app.js:969) every render and tick while `.joy-stagger` is still on #schedule-body (set for 900 ms by joyStagger, app.js:8057-8063). The new children replay `.joy-stagger > *` animations.
findings.proposedFix: Skip renderScheduleBody while the stagger class is present, or use setHtmlIfChanged on #schedule-body so an unchanged timeline is not rewritten.

findings.title: Follow-card crest area is blank until the new team's shield image loads
findings.symptom: After switching the followed team, the left crest area is empty while the new shield downloads. Shields are 68-179 KB each; on a slow camp connection that is roughly 0.5-1.5 s (not timed on a real network). On localhost it was under 120 ms. The card height also changes by 20-40 px depending on the new team's next-matchup and cleanup lines.
findings.trigger: Set state.followTeam to a different team and renderAll(). Repro: node p5_follow.cjs.
findings.evidence: p5_follow.cjs: img state 'LOADING 0px' at t0 and at the next frame, 'complete' by 120 ms. Card height 140 to 140 to 160 to 181 across three switches. Layout-shift entries of 0.018-0.024 (now-banner, my-electives, chat-card and accordion moved 20 px). The image node is kept across idle and points re-renders (sameImg:true).
findings.rootCause: renderFollowCard emits `` for the new team's shield (app.js:4562-4566), and nothing preloads the other teams' shields.
findings.proposedFix: Preload the shield (`new Image().src = ...`) for each team when the picker opens, or call the new img's decode() and swap it in once ready. Use loading="eager".

checkedClean: Idle renderAll and the 30 s tick set create zero new animations in every scenario tried (base, notice, announcement, live card, tally board with clock, tracker plus card, chat). Roles/camps/themes run: viewer/junior/light and editor/senior/dark; senior has no live games by default. Only plain-text nodes in #standings-tbody, #catchup-hint, #my-electives-card and the chat badge/preview change, as reported.

Accordion cards: opening each of the 5 cards then calling renderAll at +120 ms and +260 ms creates no new animations; joy-rise on the direct children continues its phase (100 ms to 133 ms) instead of replaying. Idle renderAll with a card fully open is also clean. Tested viewer/junior/light, editor/junior/dark and editor/senior/dark.

Happening-now banner at all 1440 minutes of all 7 days, junior and senior: the banner never hides in a gap, and the progress bar is always a new element at a block change (it starts empty, which is correct). Within a block, the 30 s tick only nudges the value attribute and the same bar glides. Early-morning 'Lights out', no-time blocks and slim competition blocks all behave.

Fresh Jelly components paint their final state on the first frame and do not animate on connect, so rebuilding them is visually harmless: jelly-chip (selected or not), jelly-badge, jelly-button, jelly-switch and jelly-icon-button each had 1 distinct pixel state over 40 frames. Only jelly-progress (fill) and jelly-segmented (about 25-frame settle) animate.

Real remote snapshots (applyRemoteState) while cards are open: clock started elsewhere, announcement, notice posted, hiddenCards change, team rename and a result saved all re-create no unexpected canvas Jelly components. The follow-card crest node is re-used on points changes, and the crest also persists across idle renders (sameImg:true).

points-pulse is not misfiring: it fires only on genuine remote points changes, with the right rows and cell count. Its background keyframe ends at transparent, and the podium and following tint lives on the tr, so there is no tint flash when the 0.6 s animation ends (p16_pulse.cjs).

Announcements strip: the __lastHtml guard prevents rebuilds on the 30 s tick, and typed text and focus survive. Chat card: stable 52 px height with the badge hidden, shown, or at 99+. [hidden] is !important so the badge hides correctly.

Notice board, My electives and the standings tbody rebuilds cause no scroll jump (scrollY unchanged) and no animation. Scroll position in the schedule sheet survives refreshOpenSchedule, renderAll and a real 30 s interval wait.

Runtime theme flips repaint canvas Jelly components correctly: an OS flip to dark and setTheme(light/dark) produce the same canvas colours as a fresh dark load, for the button, chips, switch and progress bar.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce leaves no running animations on the home screen with live cards, a final-ten board, pulses and toasts present.

A late-day weather response with no rain leaves the banner untouched. Only hint text changes (hour rollover, percentage change, appear or disappear) rebuild the bar, as reported in the rain-hint finding.

Chat card, unread badge, follow-card switch (other than image latency and a 20-40 px layout shift) and the idle auto-collapse after 5 minutes of no interaction: no glitch found beyond what is listed. Not measured: the banner-yields-to-live-board flip, the live card position (below the fold at y=798), and the long scroll to the game view.

verdicts.location: app.js:808-834 (renderNowBanner, shape at 825); app.js:743-760 (nowBannerHtml main()); app.js:515-529 (upcomingRainHint)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced twice. (1) Their p15_rain.cjs senior prints BAR RE-CREATED at minute 1200 ('near 8pm' -> 'this hour'), and again for a weather refresh that changes the percentage and for the hint disappearing. (2) My own probe (hunt/home-live-verify/v1_rain.cjs): bar settled at shownFrac 0.59, then renderAll() at 20:00 made a new element whose shownFrac was 0.024, 0.109, 0.183 ... 0.59 over about 25 frames (~0.4 s). So a visible empty-to-full sweep, the exact glitch the owner reported. The control (idle renderAll, same hint) kept the bar. v1b_rain_cases.cjs on the live build: rain appears, % changes, rain moves later and rain clears all gave barKept:false for the senior-worship layout and the junior elective layout. The slim competitions layout has no bar, so it is unaffected. Root cause is right: the shape check strips only value=, and the hint lives inside the same markup string. It only fires on days with a forecast of 40% or more (WEATHER_RAIN_MIN) within three hours, at hour rollovers and 30-min weather refreshes that change the %, so rain days only. The claim that the bar refills after a live Big Board hides the banner is a banner re-appearing, which is natural and not worth fixing.

verdicts.location: app.js:3511-3535 (tickBoardClocks), app.js:5688 (renderLiveHome), liveTrackerHTML ~6670, tallyBoardHTML ~5790, game-view clock box app.js:6504 and 6736
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. p22_final10.cjs light: steady state is colour oklch(0.577 0.215 27) with clock-heartbeat and board-glow. Right after renderAll it is the default text colour with animation none, still unchanged at +250 ms, and restored by +650 ms. My own v2_final10.cjs gave the same for viewer and editor on the home Big Board. It also reproduces in the game view's clock box (gv_after_sync cls 'board-clock' with anim none, restored at +250 ms). Cause is as stated: markup carries only board-clock-zero, and clock-final-min, clock-final-ten and board-final-ten are added only by the 500 ms tick. renderAll runs only on real synced changes, because echo snapshots are skipped in applyRemoteState, so a score tap inside the last 10 s of a clocked game is needed. That is why I rate it low, not med: a brief flicker (0 to 500 ms, mean 250 ms) at a high-attention moment but a rare coincidence.

Reproduced. p2_live.cjs A: sameNode:false, pulse currentTime 2017 ms before and 17 ms after. B: phase [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] sampled after each renderAll, where a steady ring would read 400, 800, 1200 and so on. p20_ring.cjs: box-shadow spread 5.4 px at alpha 0.10 before, 0 px at alpha 0.45 in the same frame after the render. The keyframe is a 2 s infinite ring that is invisible from 70% to 100%, so the effect is an irregular ring that restarts on every real change, not a flash. Subtle but real, and it shares one root cause with the cannon, press and final-ten findings.

Reproduced for a mouse, and NOT for touch, so this is overstated for a phone app. My v3_press_touch.cjs (stable card position, scrolled into view) on the live build: mouse with renderAll between down and up gives null for both the card and the board, while the control opens the game. Touch via CDP touchStart, renderAll, touchEnd opens the game for both, because Chromium hit-tests the tap gesture at tap time and hits the new node. WebKit also synthesizes the click from the tap point at tap time. So phones are not affected, only desktop or laptop mouse users with a roughly 100 ms press window. Their p14 harness is unreliable: on the patched build it still prints null because the card has drifted after the earlier smooth scrollIntoView. My probe, with a stable layout, passes on the patched build. The proposed alternative fix, a delegated listener on #live-home, does not work: with the mousedown node detached, Chromium dispatches no click at all (a document-level capture listener saw nothing).
verdicts.refinedFix: The only working fix is not replacing unchanged nodes, which is the same renderLiveHome change as livehome-card-pulse-restart (liveKey skip). Verified in a scratch copy: with that change the mouse tap with a snapshot between down and up opens the game for both the card and the board. Drop the delegated-listener alternative. A real score change mid-press will still replace the node, which is inherent and negligible.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with p10_cannon.cjs on the live build: cannonsAtGoal 24 and scorePopAtGoal 1, 24 still at +400 ms, then cannonsAfterNextRender 0 and scorePopAfterNextRender 0 after an unrelated renderAll. The cannons are children of the .big-board that renderLiveHome replaces. It needs another real change within about 2 s of a goal, for example the next tap, an inning change or an announcement. Rare, so low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Same renderLiveHome liveKey skip as livehome-card-pulse-restart. Tested: cannonsAfterNextRender 24 and scorePopAfterNextRender 1 on the patched build. Do not move the cannons into an overlay: they live inside .big-board, which is overflow:hidden, so an overlay would change how they are clipped. A real score change in the markup still rebuilds the board and clears in-flight cannons, which is acceptable.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with p6_joy.cjs on the live build: the editor peaks at 16 joy particles within about 2.6 s of expiry with no tap, and the viewer sees 0. The chain is as stated: settleExpiredClocks, setClock, touchData, joyCelebrate, joyBurst(joyLastTap). In production the burst starts at the last pointer position (likely the Start button), not the screen centre as in the headless run. Every editor device with the app open does the same. Cosmetic, editors only. It also stamps 'Data last updated', but that is out of scope here.

Mechanism confirmed, but the headline is overstated. p7_toast.cjs reproduces 9 toasts and 598 px of an 844 px viewport, but that needs all 6 teams changing (new-week reset or restore) plus the 'Following' toast and two manual toasts. My v6_toast.cjs with a realistic placement-style save moving 3 teams gives 3 toasts at 172 px (20% of the viewport), each lasting 4 to 5.5 s. p19_overlap.cjs confirms that the bottom toast (y 747-826) sits over the update bar (y 748-828), but both being up at once is rare. Stacking is uncapped and uncoalesced, so it is worth a small fix, at low severity.
verdicts.refinedFix: In notifyPointChanges, show one toast for all non-mine changes and keep 'Your team scored!' separate, for example `📈 🍁 Maples +5 · 🦃 Turkey +4 · 🦊 Foxes +3`. Keep the per-team maybeNativeNotification for mine. Cap visible toasts at about 3 in showToast. Raise the toaster clear of the update bar, or hide the bar while toasts are up. Do this together with the esc() removal in toast-double-escaped-text, so the coalesced text is not double-escaped. Risk: joining team names makes one long toast, so check the wrapping on a 320 px phone.

verdicts.location: app.js:3279 and app.js:3293 (esc() inside toast and notification text)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with p13_esc.cjs on the live build: toast text reads "Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts" and "Let's Go <Ball>". jellyToast sets textContent, the legacy #toast-container fallback also uses textContent, and showNotification takes plain text, so every sink is a text sink and esc() is wrong. None of the current default names contain ' or &. The only default with an apostrophe is senior 'Let's Make a Deal', a placement game that never reaches notifyMatchupChanges. So it only shows after an editor renames a team or game. Hence visibleToUsers false for the default data.
verdicts.refinedFix: Remove the three esc() calls: `${team.name}` at 3279, and `${teamName(aId)}`, `${teamName(bId)}` and `${game.name}` at 3293. Tested in a scratch copy: toast text is "Pete's Pandas & Co +5 pts" and "Let's Go <Ball>". No markup is generated from those strings, so nothing becomes an injection path. grep showed these are the only two esc() uses feeding showToast or maybeNativeNotification.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. p18_scroll.cjs: selecting the notice-card text and calling renderAll leaves an empty selection. p1_census.cjs editor: #notice-board, #my-electives-card, #standings-tbody and #catchup-hint are rebuilt on every renderAll, and notice-board and my-electives also on the 30 s tick. No new animations are created and no jelly nodes are involved (notice-card has no entrance animation; chips and buttons paint on frame 0 in p9). Scroll is stable. So the only effect is that text a counselor has selected or is long-pressing is dropped. Plain-text nodes, as the task brief already judged, but the selection loss is real. Low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged in renderNoticeBoard (`setHtmlIfChanged(el, html || '')`) and renderMyElectives (build the template string, then `setHtmlIfChanged(card, ...)`). Tested in a scratch copy: all 436 tests pass, the selection survives renderAll, and idle renders create no nodes. Neither container holds inputs or jelly components, so there is no typed-value or toggled-attribute risk. For standings, build each row as a string (the className and pulse logic is already per-row), `setHtmlIfChanged(tbody, rowsHtml)`, and keep the changedTeams and lastPointsByTeam bookkeeping outside it. See the extra finding about points-pulse: a pulse row's markup differs from the next idle render, so that render still rewrites it.

verdicts.reasoning: Numbers reproduced with p3b_shift.cjs: banner 109 to 406 px at Monday 1:15pm; at scrollY 0 the Standings card moves from y=600 to y=897 (layout-shift 0.15); when scrolled, Chrome's scroll anchoring moves scrollY 378 to 97 and the card stays at y=519. Nothing animates and nothing is an artifact: the content swap is by design, because the roster is deliberately shown inline. When the user is scrolled the page does not visibly jump. This is a layout-density question (a 400-450 px roster in the banner on elective blocks), not a graphical glitch, and belongs to the layout rethink.
verdicts.refinedFix: No bug fix. For the layout rethink: show only the viewer's own station (state.identity) in the banner with a 'see everyone' link to the Full-schedule sheet, which already lists every station. That caps the banner at about 130 px and removes the 300 px swing. Alternatively give the timed banner a stable min-height.

verdicts.location: app.js:8386-8396 (onMemberSnapshot approved branch), app.js:8724-8727 (hint path), app.js:4662-4693
verdicts.reasoning: The probe is not measured (measured:false) and simulates an unreachable start. A brand-new device has no auth hint, so it goes through onMemberSnapshot's approved branch, which calls setMemberTeam(rec.teamId) at line 8387 BEFORE startApp() at 8396. adoptMemberTeam then answers the picker before it can open, so there is no flash. The hint-painted path (8724-8727) calls startApp() with memberTeamId null, but a returning device normally has followTeam already set by the first approval. The flash needs a device that never answered the picker and whose member record later gained a teamId, or the first launch of a dual-camp account into the other camp's fresh namespace. Both are rare, once per device, and bounded by the member-snapshot latency. The code comment at 4676-4679 documents and handles it ('take it back down'). I did not time it on a real device.
verdicts.refinedFix: No change needed for the claimed scenario. If the narrow dual-camp first-launch path is ever worth closing: in the hint path (8724-8727) skip maybeShowTeamPicker and let the approved branch's startApp raise it, now that the team is known.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v12_caret.cjs, live build). Caret at 7 in 'Dinner is at six pm tonight' goes to 27 after a remote announcement arrives; value and focus are kept. I also measured a second, related case: with the composer focused but EMPTY, focus is dropped after a remote announcement (`if (newInput && draft)` gates the focus() call too), which on a phone dismisses the keyboard. Editors only, and only while the composer is open when someone else posts.

Reproduced (p12_misc.cjs live build): joyRiseRunningAt350ms 3, joyRiseREPLAYEDbySyncInWindow 3, and the schedule body is fully rebuilt by every renderAll and 30 s tick while the sheet is open (rowsRecreatedOnRenderAll true). The idle rebuild creates no animations outside the 900 ms stagger window, and scroll is unaffected. The scrollKept [400,0] in their output is the chip tap resetting scrollTop, not a sync effect. Needs a real snapshot inside the sub-second window after a day-chip tap, so low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Build the markup into a string and use setHtmlIfChanged: `const bodyHtml = `...`; if (!setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, bodyHtml)) return;` before wiring #sched-ics-btn. Tested in a scratch copy: rows are not recreated on renderAll, replays during the stagger drop from 3 to 0, and all tests pass. The ICS button listener is wired only on a write, and its closure over dow and day is safe because the day title is in the markup, so a day change always rewrites. The NOW pill still updates because it is in the markup.

verdicts.reasoning: p5_follow.cjs reproduces the img as LOADING at t0 and at the next frame, then complete by 120 ms on localhost, with the card height changing 20 px because the next-matchup and cleanup lines differ. That is an ordinary image load on a rare action: following a team is set once per device, or once by adoptMemberTeam. The shields are 68-179 KB webp. The img already carries width and height attributes, and the height change comes from text content, not the image. The same img node is kept across idle and points renders (sameImg:true). Not an animation glitch or artifact.
verdicts.refinedFix: None needed. Optional polish: drop loading="lazy" on this one above-the-fold img.

extraFindings.title: Standings points-pulse is cut off mid-flight by the next renderAll
extraFindings.symptom: A row that just gained points flashes a blue tint fading out over 0.6 s. If any other real snapshot lands inside that window, the tint vanishes instantly (a faint flicker) instead of finishing its fade.
extraFindings.trigger: Viewer with Standings open. Remote change gives a team points, then another renderAll() about 200 ms later (the next editor tap or an announcement).
extraFindings.evidence: hunt/home-live-verify/v_pulse_cut.cjs: right after the first render the row has class 'points-pulse' and td background oklab(... / 0.105) at +200 ms. In the same frame after the second renderAll the row has no 'points-pulse' class and the background is rgba(0,0,0,0). Measured in Chromium, 390x844.
extraFindings.rootCause: renderStandings rebuilds every tr and applies points-pulse only when pulseFromRemote and the points changed in THIS render, so the next render recreates the rows without the class and kills the running animation.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Remember when each team's pulse started (for example a module-level `pulseAt[team.id] = Date.now()` set where the class is added) and keep adding 'points-pulse' to that row for 600 ms. Or skip the tbody write when the row markup is unchanged. Note the animation will still restart on a re-created row, so prefer the skip.

extraFindings.title: Announcement composer loses focus (keyboard dismisses) when a remote announcement arrives while it is empty
extraFindings.symptom: An editor who has tapped the announcement box but not typed yet has the keyboard dismissed when another announcement lands.
extraFindings.trigger: Editor opens the composer, focuses the empty input, then renderAnnouncements runs with a changed banner list.
extraFindings.evidence: hunt/home-live-verify/v12_caret.cjs case B on the live build: focusedBefore true, focusedAfter false.
extraFindings.rootCause: renderAnnouncements restores focus only inside `if (newInput && draft)`, so an empty draft never regains focus after the rebuild.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Restore focus whenever hadFocus is true, independent of the draft, and restore the caret as in announce-composer-caret-jump. Verified in a scratch copy: focusedAfter true.

findings.title: Every renderAll re-creates the whole open game view (all Jelly controls, back pill, rules)
findings.symptom: While any game is open, every remote snapshot, clock action or tap tears down and rebuilds the entire game card. The "← games" back pill slides in again, "How to play" snaps shut, and all Jelly buttons and selects are re-created. Players see the pill blink on every goal and every editor tap.
findings.trigger: Open any game, then call renderAll() or deliver a remote snapshot that changes anything (a Quick Points bonus on another team is enough). Editor taps do it too: team chip, clock Start/Pause/Reset, ladder score-round. Viewer watching a Big Board: any remote goal.
findings.evidence: p1_census, editor, idle renderAll. Nodes added and Jelly elements added: tally axe-throwing 242 / 102 (38 jelly-button, 9 jelly-select, 54 jelly-option); counselor-hide-seek 283 / 102; pictionary 220 / 72; placement shields 92 / 45; bracket 31-37 / 3. Back button, input and Save button are never the same node (sameBack/sameInput/sameSave false). Every run shows a fresh running animation `button#back-btn.back-pill :: back-pill-in`. p6b with a real handleRemoteSnapshot (a bonus on t3 only): game view rebuilt, rules <details> closed, back-pill-in replayed. p9 shows the same on every chip tap and clock tap. p26 viewer remote goal: back-pill-in plus 135 nodes. p2/p15: Jelly canvases paint synchronously (no blank frames), so the cost is replay and CPU, not a blank flash. Scroll jump on rebuild is 0.
findings.rootCause: renderGameView does `view.innerHTML = html` and then re-renders #clock-area, #tools-area and #entry-area unconditionally. The setHtmlIfChanged treatment from v183 was never applied here, and the whole game view re-renders on every renderAll. `.back-pill` has `animation: back-pill-in ... both`, so each re-creation replays the slide-in.
findings.proposedFix: Make renderGameView incremental. (1) Rebuild the header, back button and rules <details> only when g.id changes (track lastGameViewId) and leave them alone otherwise. (2) Write #clock-area, #tools-area and #entry-area through setHtmlIfChanged and bind listeners only when it returns true. Pass `entry.__dom`-style state so a focused input or open select is not lost. (3) As a stopgap, play back-pill-in only on first show: add the animation via a class that joySlideIn-style code adds and removes on open, not as a permanent rule.

findings.title: Each renderAll with a game open costs 50-130 ms of main-thread work
findings.symptom: On a real phone every remote update or tap re-render during a game is a visible hitch (several hundred ms). Scoring a rapid sequence feels laggy.
findings.trigger: Open a tally or placement game and call renderAll() (any remote snapshot).
findings.evidence: p3_cost, median over 15 renders (max). No game open: 1.2 ms (2.1). Placement shields: 56 ms (98). Tally axe-throwing: 88 ms (130). counselor-hide-seek: 75 ms (152). pictionary: 47 ms (74). Bracket kangaroo: 5.4 ms. That is desktop headless Chromium; phones are typically 4-6x slower. The cost tracks the number of jelly-select and jelly-option elements: a placement view has 6 jelly-selects and costs about 56 ms.
findings.rootCause: Same unconditional rebuild as gameview-full-rebuild-every-render. The expensive parts are the medal pickers (3 jelly-select, 18 jelly-option) and the counter jelly-buttons, re-created on every render.
findings.proposedFix: Fixed by the same incremental render. Additionally keep the medal pickers out of the rebuild: update the existing selects' value attributes in place when draft.medals changes.

findings.title: Every tally keystroke or +N tap rebuilds the medal pickers (about 50 ms, 21 Jelly elements)
findings.symptom: Typing a score or tapping +1/+5 is laggy on a phone (50-65 ms desktop, so 200-300 ms on a phone). The medal selects are torn down and re-created each time even though nothing in them changed.
findings.trigger: Axe Throwing / Counselor Hide and Seek: tap a +1/+5 counter or type in a score field.
findings.evidence: p8_tally: counter tap handler 65 ms, with 31 nodes added and 21 of them jelly (3 jelly-select + 18 jelly-option). Three taps 148 ms. Keystrokes 64, 45, 43, 41 ms. The input stays focused (clean).
findings.rootCause: updateTallyMedals always does `wrap.innerHTML = ...` including medalPickerHTML and re-binds the selects, even when ranking and picks are unchanged.
findings.proposedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html) and bind the select listeners only when it returns true. Better, skip the call when the ranked order and picks are the same as last time.

findings.title: Opening a game scrolls too far: back pill and title end up clipped above the screen
findings.symptom: Tap a tall game (tally, Pictionary) in the Competitions list: the page whips down and settles with the "← games" pill and the top of the title cut off. The user cannot see the back button until they scroll up. The whole open is one big layout shift.
findings.trigger: Competitions card open, scroll so a game card is mid-screen, tap it. Editor, tally game (axe-throwing). Worse on 360x640.
findings.evidence: p5_scroll and p5v_video. 390x844: after open scrollY=1083 and #game-view top=-97, back button rect top=-76..-43 (off-screen). 360x640: back button top=-89. Layout-shift entries on open: [0.304, 0.008, 0.016, 0.016, 0.005] (about 0.35); 0.40 at 360x640. Per-frame: the Competitions card collapses 1156px to 58px over about 200 ms while a smooth scroll runs; docH goes 2276 to 2780 to 2683. Video frames 159-170 in vid_editor/sheet_open.png show the header clipped at rest. Short views are not affected (shields: back button at 357px; viewer watch view: 479px) because the document cannot scroll far enough.
findings.rootCause: The click handler calls renderAll() (which starts collapsing every open accordion card via toggle(false), a spring height animation) and immediately does `game-view.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'})`. The target is computed against the mid-collapse layout, so a smooth scroll to a moving target overshoots.
findings.location: app.js:5491-5496 (game card click), app.js:5728-5738 (openGame from home), app.js:5520-5528 (accordion fold in renderGameView)
findings.proposedFix: Do not animate scrolling against a moving layout. Either (a) collapse the accordion without animation on open (set `open` attribute directly / suppress the spring) and scrollIntoView({behavior:'instant'}), or (b) scroll after the collapse settles (wait for the card's transitionend or about 350 ms) and use block:'start' with a scroll-margin-top. Best, fix it at the root: move #game-view above the accordion (see layout finding) so no scroll is needed.

findings.title: Back from a game whips the page to the top, then drifts down; lands mid-list with the tapped card off-screen
findings.symptom: Press "← games": the page jumps to the top of the home screen (footer visible), the Competitions list springs open under the viewport, and the page ends scrolled partway into the list with the card you came from above the screen (or 77 px above it). From the home "Live now" Big Board, Back drops you about 1070-1290 px down inside a list you never opened, with the Big Board 841 px above.
findings.trigger: Open a game from the Competitions list (or the home Big Board), then tap Back.
findings.evidence: p5_scroll, editor tally, Back from the in-view position: scrollY 987 -> 334 (4 ms) -> 938 -> 1145 (settled); card top after Back = -77 px (off-screen); 10 layout-shift entries ({0.058,0.165,0.138,0.112,0.088,...}, about 0.55 total). From page bottom: lands scrollY 1432, card top -364. Viewer variant ends with card at +299 (ok) but still CLS about 0.37. p18_homeopen (viewer): open from home board then Back: scrollY 1180 -> 355 -> 975 -> 1069, Big Board top = -841, Competitions card forced open; CLS 0.91 on the first frame. Video frames 221-236 in vid_editor/sheet_back.png: the visible page goes game, home top, list springing open.
findings.rootCause: Back sets state.ui.gameId=null and renderAll(): #game-view is hidden (the document shrinks so the browser clamps scrollY), then renderGameView forces Competitions open (comp.toggle(true)) so a 1100 px list springs open while scroll anchoring chases it. No scroll position is saved or restored. It also opens Competitions unconditionally even when the user came from the home board.
findings.location: app.js:5513-5537 (focus handoff in renderGameView), app.js:5570-5574 (Back click)
findings.proposedFix: Remember the opener: store {scrollY, openerCardId} when a game opens and on Back (1) restore Competitions state only if it was open before, (2) re-open without animation and scrollTo the saved scrollY or scrollIntoView the opener card with block:'center', behavior:'instant'. Or restructure so #game-view is a full-screen takeover like #settings-view / #chat-view (body.game-open hides siblings), which makes both open and Back trivial and removes the clamp/spring problem.

findings.title: Open game sits below roughly 1100 px of home content, so the first screen shows none of it
findings.symptom: Tapping a game from anywhere, or reloading while a game is open, shows the home page with only collapsed accordion headers on screen. The game is the last block, a screen below. It lands only because a scroll is forced; after a reload it is simply not on screen.
findings.trigger: Open any game, scroll to the top (or reload the page with a game open).
findings.evidence: p12_stack at scrollY 0, viewport 844. Editor: you-strip 156 px, Happening Now 406 px, Chat 127 px, collapsed accordion 350 px; #game-view starts at y=1144 (300 px below the fold). Viewer: starts at y=1038. Full-page shot: shot_stack_full_editor.png. p11_reload: after a reload with state.ui.gameId set, scrollY=580 and the game view top is at y=458, with half the first screen collapsed accordions. state.ui.gameId persists in the localStorage snapshot.
findings.rootCause: #game-view is DOM-ordered after the whole home stack (notice, announcements, you-strip, Happening Now, chat, accordion) and is shown in place, rather than replacing the home content like the builder and chat do (body.builder-open / body.chat-open).
findings.proposedFix: Make the game a takeover, same pattern as chat and the builder: derive body.game-open from state.ui.gameId in renderAll and hide the other sections via CSS, with scrollTo(0,0) on open and a saved scroll to restore on Back. That also fixes the open overshoot and Back whiplash findings.

findings.title: Clock goes un-red / un-amber for up to half a second on every rebuild in the last minute; heartbeat and zero pulse restart
findings.symptom: In the last 60 s (amber) or last 10 s (red heartbeat) of a synced clock, any re-render (a goal, a remote snapshot) flashes the clock back to normal dark text, kills the red board glow, and restarts the heartbeat, until the next 500 ms tick re-applies the classes. At 0:00 the red pulse restarts at full opacity.
findings.trigger: Run a game clock with 8 s left on a Big Board (jeb-ball) or standalone clock, then call renderAll() (or a goal arrives from the ref).
findings.evidence: p4_clock. Before rebuild: clock class `board-clock clock-final-ten`, board `big-board board-final-ten`, heartbeat animation present. Immediately after renderAll: `board-clock ` and `big-board ` with no animations. Frame sampling: the colour is oklch(0.26) (dark) until the next tick, then the red oklch(0.58 0.2 27). Classes restored after 509 ms (editor) and 166 ms (viewer). Zero pulse phase before 483 ms, after rebuild 0-17 ms (restarts). Goals commonly land in the last seconds, exactly when this shows.
findings.rootCause: clockBlockHTML, liveTrackerHTML, liveBoardHTML and tallyBoardHTML emit only `board-clock-zero` at build time. The clock-final-min / clock-final-ten / board-final-ten classes are applied only inside tickBoardClocks on its 500 ms interval, so a freshly built element lacks them until the next tick.
findings.proposedFix: Extract the class computation into one helper (e.g. clockUrgencyClasses(clock) returning the clock-final-min/ten classes and a board-final-ten flag) and use it when building the markup in all four builders, and keep tickBoardClocks for in-place updates. Alternatively call tickBoardClocks() at the end of renderAll.

findings.title: Goal confetti and score pop are cut off mid-flight by the next render
findings.symptom: After a goal the emoji cannons and the popped score vanish abruptly if anything re-renders within about 2 s (clock Pause, another goal's snapshot, any remote change).
findings.trigger: Editor taps +1 on a team, then taps clock Pause about 350 ms later. Viewer: a remote goal, then any unrelated remote change within 2 s.
findings.evidence: p7_board. Editor: cannons 24 right after the tap, 0 right after the Pause re-render; score-pop 0. Viewer: 24 on the goal, 0 after an unrelated renderAll 400 ms later (a bonus on another team); score-pop 0.
findings.rootCause: boardCelebrate appends the .board-cannon spans (and the score-pop class) inside the .big-board element, which renderGameView/renderLiveHome replace via innerHTML on the next render.
findings.proposedFix: Append the cannons to a persistent overlay (e.g. a fixed `#joy-layer`-style container positioned over the board, or a sibling of #game-view) so they outlive the board rebuild. Also resolved if the board node is preserved across unrelated renders.

findings.title: Score input loses focus (keyboard closes) when the clock hits zero or the members list changes
findings.symptom: An editor typing a score in Counselor Hide and Seek when the game clock reaches 0:00 has the field replaced under them: focus goes to the page, and the keyboard dismisses (the typed value survives in the draft).
findings.trigger: counselor-hide-seek (timer + tally): focus a score field, let the synced clock expire on that device. Same with any change to the members list (members .on('value') listener).
findings.evidence: p27_zero_focus: before expiry the input is focused and editorMidEntry() is true. After expiry the old input node is not in the DOM (sameInputNode false), document.activeElement is BODY, value '12' kept. p6_focus: any unguarded renderAll while a field is focused replaces it (activeTag BODY). By contrast p6b: a real remote snapshot while an input is focused is correctly deferred (clean).
findings.rootCause: Two renderAll callers bypass the canAdoptRemote()/editorMidEntry() guard that remote snapshots honour: tickBoardClocks calls renderAll() when settleExpiredClocks changed something, and the members listener calls renderAll() on every members snapshot. Because the whole game view is rebuilt, the focused input is lost.
findings.proposedFix: Gate both on !editorMidEntry() (defer through deferRemoteSnapshot/idle tick), or repaint only the clock/board in place instead of renderAll after the settle. Fixing gameview-full-rebuild-every-render (stable input nodes) removes the symptom for all callers.

findings.title: "How to play" slams shut and the page jumps while someone is reading it
findings.symptom: A counselor reading the rules in an open game has the section collapse whenever any score changes anywhere. Everything below it jumps up by hundreds of pixels.
findings.trigger: Open any game, expand "How to play", then any remote change (a score, a goal, a bonus).
findings.evidence: p25_rules (viewer, ladder-ball): before: details height 573 px, summary at y=73, board at y=649. After a remote score change: details.open=false, summary at y=155 (scroll corrected 82 px), board at y=203 (moved 446 px); layout shift 0.036. p1_census: detailsStillOpen false for every game. p6b: rulesStillOpen false after a Quick Points bonus.
findings.rootCause: The rules <details> is part of the markup written by `view.innerHTML = html` on every renderAll, so its open state is lost.
findings.proposedFix: Build the header and rules once per game (only when g.id changes), or capture `details.open` before the rebuild and restore it after.

findings.title: On Back, the game list rises in twice (parent and every card both fade/translate)
findings.symptom: After Back the Competitions list fades and slides up in a sluggish, compounded way instead of one clean rise.
findings.trigger: Open a game, then tap Back with Competitions previously open.
findings.evidence: p13_back_anims (editor). New animations after Back: `div#day-tabs :: joy-rise` 1, `div.settings-row.card-visibility-row :: joy-rise` 1, `button.game-card :: joy-rise` 6, `h2.session-heading :: joy-rise` 2.
