findings.title: Standalone game clock strobes forever at 0:00, even for viewers and with reduced motion on
findings.symptom: When a Hide-and-Seek / Plunder clock reaches 0:00 the whole clock box flashes red/neutral twice a second until an editor presses Reset, Restart or Next round. That can be minutes. Viewers cannot stop it and phones set to reduced motion still get it.
findings.trigger: counselor-hide-seek or pumpkin-patch-plunder: let the clock reach 0:00 (or load state with remaining 0), open the game.
findings.evidence: p14_alarm (viewer): the clock box has `alarm-flash` with duration 500 ms, iterations Infinity, playState running; with prefers-reduced-motion=reduce it is still running, while board-zero-pulse on the digits is correctly removed.
findings.rootCause: clockBlockHTML adds `alarming` whenever remaining === 0, and `.tool-box.alarming` has `animation: alarm-flash 0.5s infinite alternate` with no stop and no prefers-reduced-motion override.
findings.proposedFix: Limit it: `animation: alarm-flash 0.5s ease-in-out 6 alternate` (a few seconds) then settle on the danger border. Add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .tool-box.alarming { animation: none; } }` block.

findings.title: Pale square block behind every +N counter button on tally games
findings.symptom: In Axe Throwing, Inflatable Bowling, Color Call Chaos, Counselor Hide and Seek and Pumpkin Patch Plunder, each blue +1/+5 pill sits on a visible lavender (light mode) or slate (dark mode) rectangle that extends past the rounded pill.
findings.trigger: Open any tally game with counterSteps as an editor (light or dark).
findings.evidence: Screenshots halo_light.png and halo_dark.png. p16_halo / p17_hostbg: jelly-button.counter-btn.plus host has computed background-color color(srgb 0.936 0.947 1) and border-radius 0px. It is the only leaking jelly-button class across tally, placement, Pictionary, bracket, ladder and kickball views (12 instances in axe-throwing).
findings.rootCause: The host-reset rule `jelly-button.counter-btn { background: none; ... }` (specificity 0,1,1) loses to the legacy `.counter-btn.plus { background: color-mix(...) }` (0,2,0), so the old chrome lands on the host behind the canvas pill. (`.counter-btn.minus` sets color/max-width similarly but shows nothing.)
findings.location: styles.css:2956-2960 (.counter-btn.plus legacy background) vs styles.css:4287-4300 (jelly-button host reset)
findings.proposedFix: Delete the legacy `.counter-btn.plus` background/border-color rule, or raise the host reset to `jelly-button.counter-btn.plus, jelly-button.counter-btn.minus { background: none; border: none; }`.

findings.title: Confetti burst and "Data last updated" stamp on clock Start/Pause/Reset, undoing a goal, innings, Reset tally and the buzzer
findings.symptom: Pressing Pause, Reset, a preset chip, goal minus, inning plus or Reset tally throws the same 16-particle celebration as saving a result. When the clock reaches 0:00 the ref's phone also gets a confetti burst (from the last tap position, or screen centre). The footer "Data last updated" time moves for each of these.
findings.trigger: As an editor in a tracker game (jeb-ball, ladder-ball): tap clock Start/Pause/Reset, goal minus, inning plus, Reset tally, a ladder rung; or let the clock expire on an editor device.
findings.evidence: p20_burst (800 ms throttle bypassed per tap): every action listed produced particles=16 with 4-7 emoji and dataStampBumped=true. p19_zero: at zero, joy-p x16, view rebuilt, alarm-flash and board-zero-pulse start, dataStampBumped=true.
findings.rootCause: setClock, setLiveMatch and setLadderMatch each call touchData(), which stamps lastDataChangeAt and fires joyCelebrate() (a big burst). CLAUDE.md says touchData() is only for real scoreboard activity, and settleExpiredClocks routes the buzzer through setClock.
findings.proposedFix: Split touchData into stampData() (lastDataChangeAt) and the celebration. Call the celebration only for genuine scoring (goal plus, medals saved, bracket win). Use a quiet save for clock/inning/outs/undo/reset and for the zero-settle.

findings.title: Viewers are told to tap "View only" and enter a score PIN, neither of which exists
findings.symptom: A counselor opening any unscored placement or bracket game reads: "Tap View only at the top and enter the score PIN to run it."
findings.trigger: Sign in as a viewer, open a game with no result and no bracket (e.g. Shields, Kangaroo Kickball).
findings.evidence: p21_viewer: entry-area text for shields and kangaroo-kickball is "👀 View-only. This game hasn't been scored yet. Tap 🔒 View only at the top and enter the score PIN to run it." CLAUDE.md: the PIN gate was removed 2026-07-25.
findings.rootCause: Leftover copy in renderLiveWatch from the PIN era.
findings.proposedFix: Replace with "This game hasn't been scored yet. Scores show here as soon as a director enters them."

findings.title: "Live now" card's red pulse ring restarts on every render
findings.symptom: The pulsing ring on a Live now card re-fires from full strength each time any update lands, instead of pulsing on its steady 2 s beat.
findings.trigger: A bracket game in progress that is not promoted to the home Big Board (e.g. ladder-ball); any renderAll.
findings.evidence: p9 and p26 steps show a fresh `button.live-home-card :: live-pulse` animation on every renderAll. Seen only as a running-animation diff, not as a visible-phase measurement. On the home surface (live-home), not the game view; flagged for overlap with the home auditor.
findings.rootCause: renderLiveHome sets `wrap.innerHTML = boardHTML + ...` on every render, so each .live-home-card is a new element and its infinite live-pulse animation restarts at phase 0.
findings.proposedFix: Write #live-home through setHtmlIfChanged (as v183 did for the other home panels); card markup is unchanged between most renders, so the pulse keeps its phase.

checkedClean: Clocks do not re-create DOM per tick. tickBoardClocks only swaps the text node (about 2 text-node writes per second per clock element, no new elements, 0 attribute changes), and the Pictionary stopwatch tick does the same (about 20 text-node swaps per second across both displays, no elements). Harmless churn.
Pictionary stopwatch is continuous across a rebuild: it read 0:02.3 right after renderAll mid-lap and 0:02.6 250 ms later, with no reset to 0:00. Only the back-pill replays.
Jelly canvases do not blink on re-creation: jelly-button and jelly-select paint synchronously (non-transparent pixel counts equal on the first frame and steady after; selected value kept).

A real remote snapshot while an input is focused is deferred correctly: handleRemoteSnapshot with remoteReady=true leaves the same node, focus kept, remoteRefetchPending true. A typed score also survives rebuilds via the draft.

In-place updates are smooth: goal +, ladder rung and round-clear, inning and out steppers refresh numbers without rebuilding (0 nodes added on the inning tap; the goal tap only adds the intended cannons and score-pop). The bracket flow scrollDelta is 0 on every step.
No scroll reset or jump on a rebuild while a game is open (scrollDelta 0 in all census runs). The one jump is the collapse of an open "How to play" (reported separately).

Stale celebration on reopening a game: the home board and the game view share the lastBoardScores memo, so goals scored while away celebrate once on the home board and reopening does not re-fire (0 cannons on reopen and second reopen).
Save Result at the bottom of a tall tally view lands correctly after the page shrinks (Final results heading at y=375; layout shift 0.058).
Day-tab strip is unaffected by the hidden container: after open, a render while hidden, and Back, the jelly-tabs value and width are identical (316 px, d3).

Confetti canvas (celebrate()) removes itself after 1.6 s; no lingering elements. Under prefers-reduced-motion it returns early, and board-cannon, board-zero-pulse, heartbeat and score-pop are all disabled (only alarm-flash is missed, reported above).
winner-ready highlight has no animation (just a transform and drop-shadow), and highlightWinner re-applies it after each rebuild.
Opening from the home Big Board lands within 33 px of the top (editor -22 px). The long 1180-1340 px smooth scroll is acceptable. Only Back is bad (reported above).
After the v183 work, an idle renderAll with NO game open costs 1.2 ms median. Game views are the only expensive path.
Placement and bracket tools (Start Bracket, chips, winner, undo, cancel) work with no console errors; no pageerror was logged in any probe.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran p1_census (editor): every idle renderAll with a game open re-creates the whole view (shields 92 nodes/45 jelly, axe-throwing 242/102, pictionary 220/72, kickball 34/3). Back button, input and Save are never the same node, rules <details> closes, and a fresh back-pill-in runs. My own probe (v1_pill, jeb-ball, scrolled to the game) sampled the pill's opacity per frame after renderAll: 0,0,0,0.26,0.49,...,1 for editor, and 0,0,0.26,... for viewer. That is a real fade-from-invisible blink. p6b with a real handleRemoteSnapshot (a bonus on t3 only) rebuilds the view (the snapshot is a genuine signature change, so applyRemoteState calls renderAll). p9 shows the same on team-chip taps and clock Start/Pause/Reset (222-234 nodes and back-pill-in each). p26 shows the viewer remote goal rebuilding 135 nodes. Jelly canvases paint synchronously (p2/p15: pixel counts never drop to 0), so no blank flash on the controls, only replay and CPU. Two corrections to the claim: (1) the editor's own goal tap is NOT a rebuild (p9 'goal +1 (in-place)' adds only the 24 cannons, and inning+ adds 0 nodes), so 'every goal' is true only for viewers receiving it remotely; (2) v183 never touched renderGameView or renderLiveHome (git show 554fbe1; setHtmlIfChanged is used only by the footer, follow card, bonuses, verse, cleanup and day panels). Root cause as stated is right: `view.innerHTML = html` at app.js:5567 plus unconditional re-render of clock/tools/entry areas. This is the same class of bug the owner reported with the progress bar, and it is the common root of findings 2, 3, 9 and 10.
verdicts.refinedFix: Do it in stages, cheapest and safest first. (A) styles.css:1441: delete the permanent `animation: back-pill-in ...` from `.back-pill` (and its reduced-motion override). The open already plays joySlideIn(#game-view). Verified: with `.back-pill{animation:none}` the opacity stays 1 across a rebuild. (B) In renderGameView split the markup into a stable head (back pill, title, messtival tag, rules <details>) and the three areas (#clock-area/#tools-area/#entry-area, created once). Rebuild the head only when a key changes, e.g. `headKey = [g.id,g.name,g.emoji,g.location,g.session,g.messtival,backDay&&backDay.name,JSON.stringify(g.rules)].join('|')`, stored on the view; capture `lastGameViewId` before it is overwritten at app.js:5538 to detect the id change. Do NOT use setHtmlIfChanged for the head: a user-opened <details> gains an `open` attribute, so `el.__dom !== el.innerHTML` reads as 'DOM altered' and the rules would still be rebuilt shut. (C) Only then make the three areas skip identical markup, and be careful: (i) renderTally/renderPlacement/renderTournament/renderLiveWatch/renderTools bind handlers that close over `draft = state.drafts[g.id]`, `state.brackets[g.id]`, etc. applyRemoteState replaces `state[k]` with fresh objects on every non-echo snapshot, so if markup is identical and the rebuild is skipped, the old handlers keep writing into orphaned objects and saveState() pushes a state that lacks the edit, which silently loses scores (the CLAUDE.md 'closures over replaced state objects' invariant). Re-resolve at event time (`const draft = () => state.drafts[g.id]`) or keep rebuilding those areas. (ii) setHtmlIfChanged never skips for any area containing a ticking clock (tickBoardClocks rewrites textContent every 500 ms, verified: #live-home innerHTML changes with no render), so tracker games' boards won't benefit; compare against the last html string only (drop the __dom check) for those, or split the clock out. (iii) Focus/typed values survive because renderAll is already deferred while a field is focused. Re-run tests/render-stability.test.js and add a game-view case.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran p3_cost: no game 1.3 ms; shields 45 ms; axe-throwing 69 ms (max 105); counselor-hide-seek 68 ms; pictionary 52 ms; kangaroo-kickball 6 ms. That is a main-thread freeze of roughly a quarter to half a second whenever a remote update lands while an editor has a tally/placement game open (CPU throttling only approximates a phone). Viewers' watch views are cheap (kickball 6 ms, p26 viewer goal 8 ms), so the pain is editor-side. Same root cause as finding 1, not an independent defect; fixing 1 plus the tally split (finding 3) removes it. Kept at med only because the audience is the handful of editors.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran p5_scroll Back: scrollY 987 -> 334 (t=6 ms) -> 1081 -> 1145; docH 2683 -> 1178 -> 2276; card top after Back -77 (off-screen); 10 layout-shift entries (about 0.55 total); 360x640: 0.077/0.337/0.274/0.193... and card top -66. Re-ran p18_homeopen (viewer): open from the home Big Board then Back ends at scrollY 1069 with the Big Board at -841 and Competitions forced open (CLS 0.91 first frame). I also viewed the auditor's frame sheet (vid_editor/sheet_back.png, frames 219-236): game -> home top with the footer showing (221-222) -> the Competitions list springing open under the viewport while scroll chases. Short views are less bad (shields lands with the card at +734, CLS 0.14). Root cause is as described: renderAll hides #game-view so the document shrinks and scrollY is clamped, then renderGameView forces Competitions open and the grid-row spring grows the page under scroll anchoring; no scroll is saved or restored, and Competitions opens even when the opener was the home board.
verdicts.refinedFix: Structural, and prototyped: make the game a full-screen takeover like chat/builder. v5_takeover prototype (CSS `body.game-open .main-wrap > :not(#game-view), body.game-open #app-footer {display:none}`, toggle the class in renderGameView, `scrollTo(0,0)` on open, remember `window.scrollY` at open and `scrollTo(0, saved)` after Back's renderAll) gave: open CLS 0, back pill at 36 px, and Back returned the opener card to exactly its prior position (366 -> 366) with no layout shifts. Required with it: (1) DELETE the fold/re-open block in renderGameView (app.js:5518-5537). If it stays, the fold happens while hidden and `comp.toggle(true)` still springs open on Back; (2) derive `body.game-open` in renderAll only when `!inBuilder && !inChat`, so it cannot hide chat-view/settings-view when a notification opens chat over an open game; (3) save the scroll in a module variable in both openers (game card click, openGame) and restore in the Back handler; (4) drop the smooth scrollIntoView calls. Risk to confirm with the owner: state.ui.gameId persists, so a reload now shows the game full-screen (that is desirable) and Back lands on the top of home.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran (v12_halo): jelly-button.counter-btn.plus host computed background color(srgb 0.936 0.947 1), border-radius 0px; the .minus host is transparent. Screenshots: faint lavender rectangle behind the pill in light mode, clearly visible dark-slate square corners behind +1/+5 in dark mode (halo_dark.png). Cascade confirmed: `.counter-btn.plus` (0,2,0, styles.css:2956) beats `jelly-button.counter-btn {background:none}` (0,1,1, styles.css:4285). The only .counter-btn elements in the code are jelly-buttons (app.js:6013-6016), so the legacy rule is dead chrome. Validated the fix in-page in dark mode (v12b): background becomes rgba(0,0,0,0) and the halo disappears (halo_dark_after.png).
verdicts.refinedFix: Delete the legacy `.counter-btn.plus` rule (styles.css:2956-2960) and the border-color on `.counter-btn.minus`; or minimally add `jelly-button.counter-btn.plus, jelly-button.counter-btn.minus { background: none; border: none; }` next to the host reset at 4285. No behavioural risk: the pill is canvas-drawn.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran p20_burst: inning+, goal+, goal-, clock Start/Pause/Reset/preset, Reset tally and ladder rung/round each fire 16 particles (3-8 emoji) and bump lastDataChangeAt. p19_zero: at 0:00 the editor's device gets joy particles and a data-stamp bump from settleExpiredClocks -> setClock -> touchData -> joyCelebrate. joyCelebrate's own comment says it is for 'every action that records real scoreboard data'; CLAUDE.md defines touchData that way, so clock start/pause/reset and the buzzer are misfires; goal+ and ladder rung are legitimately scoring. Partly by design, hence low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Do NOT remove the touchData() call from setClock: it also sets `dataEditPending = true`, which editorMidEntry/reloadBlocked rely on to guard an unpushed edit. Instead add an option: `function touchData({ celebrate = true, stamp = true } = {})` and have setClock call `touchData({ celebrate: false, stamp: false })` (still setting dataEditPending). Leave goal+, ladder rungs and saved results as they are; for goal-/inning+ choose celebrate:false. settleExpiredClocks then stops bursting at the buzzer automatically.

verdicts.reasoning: Code check at app.js:5872: renderLiveWatch renders 'Tap 🔒 View only at the top and enter the score PIN to run it.' for a viewer on any game with no bracket and no result (placement games before they are scored are the common case). No such control exists (grep of index.html/app.js/settings.js finds no 'View only' button) and CLAUDE.md says the PIN gate was removed 2026-07-25. Copy bug rather than a graphical glitch, but a common viewer flow.
verdicts.refinedFix:
app.js:5872: `

👀 This game hasn't been scored yet. Scores show here as soon as a director enters them.

`. Also the stale 'no score PIN' comment at 5829 can stay as is.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v15_pulse, viewer, ladder-ball bracket in progress): the .live-home-card is a new node after renderAll and the live-pulse animation phase goes from ~400 ms to 0 (a 7 px ring that was mid-expansion restarts from zero). Code confirms `wrap.innerHTML = boardHTML + ...` on every renderLiveHome and v183 did not convert it. The visible effect is a barely noticeable early restart of a 2 s ring, so low and not reliably perceptible. NOTE on the proposed fix: converting the whole #live-home to setHtmlIfChanged does nothing while the promoted Big Board has a running clock, because tickBoardClocks mutates the clock text every 500 ms (measured: #live-home innerHTML changes between renders with no render call), so `__dom !== innerHTML` and it always rebuilds.
verdicts.refinedFix: Give the plain `.live-home-card` buttons their own container (e.g. `#live-home-cards`, separate from the board container) and write that one through `if (!setHtmlIfChanged(cards, html)) return;` binding the click handlers only on a fresh write. Cards contain no ticking clock, so the skip works even while the board's clock runs. Keep boardDiffCelebrate running on every render for the board (it diffs internally).

extraFindings.title: Home Big Board clock loses its red heartbeat/glow on any remote change in the last 10 s
extraFindings.symptom: A viewer watching the home screen Big Board sees the clock's red heartbeat and the board's red glow switch off for about a third of a second whenever any remote update lands (any score, bonus or clock action by anyone), then come back.
extraFindings.trigger: Viewer on the home page with a live timed tracker game (jeb-ball) promoted to the Big Board and its clock at 8 s running. Any change in state that makes renderAll run (e.g. a bonus on another team).
extraFindings.evidence: v7_home.cjs (viewer, 390x844): before renderAll clock class `board-clock clock-final-ten`, board `big-board viewer board-final-ten`; immediately after renderAll `board-clock ` and `big-board viewer` (no urgency classes); classes return after 329 ms (next 500 ms tick). The same loss for the amber final-min state is implied by the same code. In-page validation (v7b_fix): calling the tick's class-painting step at the end of renderAll leaves both classes present on the first frame.
extraFindings.rootCause: renderLiveHome re-creates the home Big Board on every renderAll via liveTrackerHTML/tallyBoardHTML, which emit only board-clock-zero; clock-final-min/ten and board-final-ten are applied solely in tickBoardClocks' interval.
extraFindings.location: app.js:5664 (renderLiveHome) and app.js:3517-3534 (tickBoardClocks); same fix as clock-urgency-styling-lost-on-rebuild
extraFindings.proposedFix: Extract the els.forEach body of tickBoardClocks into paintClockClasses() and call it from both tickBoardClocks and at the end of renderAll (not tickBoardClocks itself, to avoid settle/renderAll recursion).

extraFindings.title: setHtmlIfChanged can never skip a panel that contains a running clock (fix-risk, not a user-visible glitch)
extraFindings.symptom: Any attempt to extend the v183 setHtmlIfChanged pattern to #live-home, the Big Board or the game view's clock area will silently never skip while a game clock is running, so it will look like the fix did nothing for exactly the games that matter.
extraFindings.trigger: Promote a timed tracker game to the home Big Board with a running clock, wait one tick, compare the container's innerHTML with its last written html.
extraFindings.evidence: v15b.cjs: with a running jeb-ball clock on the home board, #live-home innerHTML changes between two reads 1.3 s apart with no renderAll call (tickBoardClocks rewrites textContent and toggles classes); setHtmlIfChanged requires `el.__dom === el.innerHTML`, so it always rebuilds. Similarly a user-opened <details> or a jelly-select/chip that reflects its own attribute counts as 'DOM altered'.
extraFindings.rootCause: setHtmlIfChanged (app.js:3092) treats any post-render DOM mutation as 'someone changed the panel', which includes the 500 ms clock tick and Jelly components reflecting their own attributes.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Keep clock text out of the compared container (separate container for cards vs board), or give setHtmlIfChanged an opt-out of the __dom check (`setHtmlIfChanged(el, html, { trustHtml: true })`) for panels whose only DOM mutations come from tickBoardClocks, and key the rules <details> on game id instead.

Run any of them with `node <file>`. Firebase is mocked only where noted (window.firebase + fbRef + authUser for p8/p9/p26).

Screenshots (daysnav-*.png, lock-alt-*.png, banner-*.png, daysfix-*.png) are in the same folder.

findings.title: Schedule sheet day row overflows: Saturday is clipped or unreachable on nearly all phones
findings.symptom: Open the full schedule on a phone. The Sat chip is cut off at the sheet edge, and at 360 px wide Fri is half cut and Sat is almost entirely off-screen. The row does not scroll, so Saturday (send-off day) cannot be selected.
findings.trigger: Tap the Happening-now banner at any viewport narrower than about 417 px (iPhone 12-16 at 390, SE at 375, most Android at 360-412). Run p3_daysnav.cjs and view daysnav-360-junior.png.
findings.evidence: #schedule-days is display:grid with repeat(7,1fr) and overflow-x:visible. Measured navClientW 358 (390 px), 343 (375 px), 328 (360 px) against about 385 px of chip content (scrollWidth 429). Chip rects: Sat spans 353-400 px, so 10 px is clipped at 390 and only a 7 px sliver is visible at 360. The sheet has overflow:hidden. Same in the senior camp. Injected CSS `.schedule-days{grid-template-columns:repeat(7,minmax(0,1fr))} jelly-chip.sched-day-chip::part(main){padding-inline:0;width:100%;justify-content:center}` puts all seven chips inside 16-344 px at 360 and 16-374 px at 390 (p23_fixcheck.cjs, daysfix-360.png).
findings.rootCause: `1fr` is minmax(auto,1fr), so each track is floored at the jelly-chip's min-content. A jelly-chip has 13 px of hard-coded shadow padding on each side plus its label, so seven chips plus gaps exceed the 16 px-padded header on narrow phones.
findings.proposedFix: Use `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr))` and add `jelly-chip.sched-day-chip::part(main){padding-inline:0;width:100%;justify-content:center}`. Verified by injection. If a scroll row is preferred instead, preserve scrollLeft across renderScheduleDays(), which rebuilds the chips with innerHTML on every tap.

findings.title: Swipe-to-dismiss on the schedule sheet snaps back to the top, then slides down
findings.symptom: Drag the schedule header down more than 90 px and release. The sheet jumps back up to its resting position in one frame, then animates off-screen from there, instead of continuing down from where the finger let go.
findings.trigger: Open the schedule, touch-drag the header down about 200 px, release. Run p4_swipe.cjs.
findings.evidence: Sheet top per frame: 284 (while dragged 200 px) then 84, 138, 252, 394, 522, 620, 694, 787, 814, 831, 841. The first frame after release is the 200 px snap-back. Without touch-driven dismiss there is no problem; this affects every swipe dismiss.
findings.rootCause: The touchend handler calls closeSchedule(), which sets `sheet.style.transform = ''` before adding .closing. The sched-slide-out keyframes start from translateY(0), discarding the drag offset. The same applies to the 'spring back' branch: no CSS transition is defined on the sheet, so a short drag also snaps instantly.
findings.proposedFix: For the swipe path, do not clear the inline transform. Set `sheet.style.transition='transform .2s ease'; sheet.style.transform='translateY(100%)'` and let finish() hide the overlay, or pass the drag offset to the keyframes via a CSS var (`@keyframes sched-slide-out{from{transform:translateY(var(--drag,0px))}}`). For the short-drag spring-back, set `transition:transform .2s` before clearing the transform.

findings.title: New-version banner covers the chat composer, Bonus card and footer, and tapping it reloads and discards unsent chat
findings.symptom: When a new version is detected the banner sits over the bottom 80 px of the screen. In chat it covers the message box, photo button and Send button. On the home page at full scroll it covers the Bonus card and the footer's Settings link. Tapping where Send is reloads the page and the typed message is lost.
findings.trigger: Open chat (or scroll home to the bottom) while onNewVersion()/showUpdateBanner() has run. The reload is deliberately deferred while a chat message is being typed or an editor is mid-entry, so the banner stays up exactly while the composer is in use. Run p14_banner.cjs and p16_banner2.cjs and view banner-chat.png and banner-home-bottom.png.
findings.evidence: With 390x844: banner rect y 748-828 (16-374 px wide). Chat composer is y 785-843, and elementFromPoint at the Send, input and photo buttons all returned #update-banner. A touchscreen tap at the Send button position called doReload once while the typed text was still unsent. At home scrollMax (228) the footer is y 795-844 and the banner y 748-828, so the Settings link and Bonus card are under it. The jelly-alert banner is not dismissible (no `dismissible` attribute) although CLAUDE.md calls it dismissible. The SDK-down pill (#sdk-banner) sits in the same bottom slot (p25_sdk.cjs) and is fully hidden under the update banner when both show.
findings.rootCause: The banner is position:fixed at the bottom with z-index 60 and no space reserved in the page or chat view. The whole alert is a click-to-reload target (`bar.addEventListener('click', doReload)`) that bypasses reloadBlocked(), so the safety logic that protects an unsent message is skipped.
findings.proposedFix: Anchor the banner at the top (below the safe-area inset), or add `body.has-update-banner #app, .chat-view{padding-bottom: 6rem}` and lift it above the sticky composer. Attach doReload to the Refresh button only and have it confirm (or check reloadBlocked()) when chatComposerBusy() or editorMidEntry() is true. Give the alert `dismissible` or hide it while chat is open. Stack the SDK banner above or below rather than at the same position.

findings.title: Members drawer: every role/team/remove tap rebuilds all rows, freezing the UI for about 1 s and wiping the Add form
findings.symptom: After changing one person's role or team, the drawer dims and the page freezes for roughly a second while every row is re-created. Anything typed in the Add someone form (email, name) disappears at the same time.
findings.trigger: Settings, Who can sign in, with about 40 members. Change any person's role/team/None switch, or open the drawer. Run p8_members.cjs and p9_members_cost.cjs (Firebase mocked).
findings.evidence: 41 members produce 83 jelly-segmented and 42 jelly-select. renderMemberList() took 927 ms synchronously (p9). In isolation, 83 segmented took 703 ms and 42 selects 406 ms, roughly 8.5 ms and 10 ms each from the forced layout in each connectedCallback. In p8 the frame sampler saw frames at t=105 ms and t=1696 ms, a main-thread block of about 1.5 s per refresh, and the first fill after open took 1382 ms with a 120 ms mocked read. A value typed into #member-add-name read 'Typed Name' before and '' after renderMemberList(). Scroll position was preserved (700 to 700) and no new CSS animations fired. Measured on this headless desktop Chromium; phones are likely slower.
findings.rootCause: renderMembers() re-reads both camps' member lists and then renderMemberList() replaces the whole body.innerHTML, which includes the Add form, after every single write (and every `.then(renderMembers)` in bindMemberList).
findings.proposedFix: Split the body into #members-list and #members-add and only re-render the list. Better, update the affected row in place (or optimistically patch `lists` and re-render just that row) instead of re-fetching and rebuilding all rows. Chunk or lazily create the jelly-select/segmented controls for large lists.

findings.title: Lock screen cannot scroll: opening 'Alternative sign in' on a short viewport pushes controls off-screen
findings.symptom: On a 360x640 phone, opening 'Alternative sign in' clips the logo at the top and pushes the error text below the fold. In landscape (667x375) the Google button is off-screen at the top and the phone/email forms' lower buttons are off-screen at the bottom, with no way to scroll to them. An Android keyboard shrinking the viewport has the same effect.
findings.trigger: Load with no auth hint, tap 'Alternative sign in' at 360x640 or 667x375. Run p13_lock_alt.cjs and view lock-alt-360x640.png.
findings.evidence: 360x640 open: logo top -41, box 721 px tall in a 640 px viewport. 667x375 open: logo -166, Google button -88 to -16, box 707 px tall in a 375 px viewport. #lock-screen computed overflow-y is visible, scrollHeight 681 vs clientHeight 640, and #app is display:none so there is no document scroll to fall back on.
findings.rootCause: html.locked .lock-screen is position:fixed; inset:0; display:flex; align-items:center with no overflow handling. A flex child taller than the container is centred, so it overflows equally top and bottom, and the fixed container can never scroll.
findings.proposedFix: Add `overflow-y:auto` to .lock-screen and use safe centering: remove `align-items:center` and give `.lock-box` `margin:auto`. The box then centres when it fits and scrolls from the top when it does not.

findings.title: Lock screen content jumps vertically when its state changes (checking, sign-in, Alternative sign in)
findings.symptom: The logo drops into view, then jumps up about 80 px when 'Checking sign-in' becomes the sign-in panel. Tapping 'Alternative sign in' makes the whole stack leap up about 235 px, so the control you just tapped moves out from under your finger.
findings.trigger: Load with no auth hint (jelly.js delayed 1.5 s in p12_lock.cjs to make it easy to see), then tap the disclosure (p13_lock_alt.cjs).
findings.evidence: p12: .lock-logo top 383 (box 78 px) at 63 ms, then 303 (box 239 px) at 1631 ms, layout-shift 0.022. p13 at 390x844: summary at y 463-491 before and 228-257 after opening; logo 303 before, 69 after.
findings.rootCause: The lock box is vertically centred in the viewport and its content height changes between states, so every height change re-centres everything.
findings.proposedFix: Anchor to a fixed top offset (e.g. `align-items:flex-start; padding-top:max(1.5rem,18vh)`), combined with the safe-centering fix above.

findings.title: A Google sign-in error remounts the phone/email forms and wipes what was typed
findings.symptom: Typing a phone number or email in the Alternative sign in forms, then getting any Google error (popup blocked, offline), clears both fields because the forms are rebuilt.
findings.trigger: Fill #phone-number and #email-link-address, then showSignInError({code:'auth/popup-blocked'}). Run p29_remount.cjs.
findings.evidence: Before: phone '555-123-4567', email 'me@example.com'. After: both '' and the input node is a different element (sameNode false). The details element stays open.
findings.rootCause: showAuthScreen('signin', ...) calls CampPhone.mount() and CampEmailLink.mount() every time, and each mount() replaces the slot's innerHTML.
findings.proposedFix: Mount once: skip when `slot.firstElementChild` already exists, or only call mount() on the first transition into 'signin'.

findings.title: Drawer and dialog backdrop cuts in and out in one frame instead of fading
findings.symptom: When a drawer or dialog opens, the dimmed and blurred layer appears at full strength in the first frame while the sheet slides in. On close, the dim stays at full strength until the sheet has finished leaving, then vanishes in a single frame.
findings.trigger: Open and close Settings, History, Members, Phone alerts or the pickers (p5_drawers.cjs, p10_picker.cjs).
findings.evidence: Settings open: backdrop opacity 1.00 at t=23 ms (sheet still at y=930 off-screen). X-close: backdrop 1.00 through t=319 ms, then display:none at t=350 ms. Team picker X-close: backdrop 1.00 on every frame while the dialog itself fades 1.00 to 0.18, then the host disappears. The Settings to History handoff does not flash (backdrop continuous).
findings.rootCause: In vendor/jelly.js the drawer/dialog CSS has `:host{display:none}` and `.backdrop{opacity:0;transition:opacity .3s}`, with `:host([open]){display:block}` and `[open] .backdrop{opacity:1}`. The element goes from display:none to displayed in the same style recalc, so no transition has a before-change style and nothing animates. On close the host is hidden at once when the animated exit ends.
findings.location: vendor/jelly.js:5421 (drawer CSS, Wi) and the dialog CSS (Xi); both open/close paths in the Oi (dialog) and Ni (drawer) classes
findings.proposedFix: In the vendored copy, animate the backdrop with WAAPI next to the sheet animation (`backdrop.animate([{opacity:0},{opacity:1}],{duration:250,fill:'both'})` in afterOpen, and the reverse in the animated close). Alternatively use `@starting-style` plus visibility instead of display toggling.

findings.title: Pickers and Settings vanish instantly when closed by choice; only the X/backdrop path animates
findings.symptom: Picking a team or identity, or the 'stay here' camp option, makes the dialog disappear in one frame, while closing the same dialog with X or the backdrop fades and shrinks over about 150 ms. During first-run camp discovery the team picker also cuts straight to the camp picker and back.
findings.trigger: Pick 'just cheering' in the identity step (p10_picker.cjs). For the cut, call maybeShowCampPicker() while the team picker is open (p11_camp.cjs).
findings.evidence: Close by choice: display is none on the first sampled frame. Close by X: dialog opacity 1.00, 0.92, 0.84, 0.74, 0.62, 0.49, 0.34, 0.18, then gone (about 150 ms). closeSettings() via removeAttribute also hides the Settings sheet in one frame (p5). Team picker 'x' to camp 'open' on the same frame, then team picker re-opens about 160 ms after the camp picker closes.
findings.rootCause: closeTeamPicker(), closeSettings() and the camp picker's stay-put branch use overlay.removeAttribute('open'). That path runs afterClose() synchronously and skips the component's animated `open = false` setter.
findings.proposedFix: For user-initiated closes (a choice, stay put) use `overlay.open = false`. Keep removeAttribute for programmatic handoffs such as adoptMemberTeam, openCampPicker and openBuilder.

findings.title: Open schedule sheet is rebuilt every 30 s and on every remote snapshot even when nothing changed
findings.symptom: While the full schedule is open, every 30 s tick and every score anyone saves recreates the whole timeline and the 'Add to calendar' jelly-button. Nothing visibly animates and scroll is kept, but text selection is lost and a press or momentum fling on the list can be interrupted.
findings.trigger: Open the schedule, select some text or scroll, then wait 30 s or call renderAll(). Run p1_schedule.cjs and p20_sched_rebuild.cjs.
findings.evidence: refreshOpenSchedule() recreated 268 nodes (27 .sched-block plus #sched-ics-btn, which is a new element: sameIcs false) with no change. Selection text before refresh was the sched label, after was ''. Cost 6.3-7.9 ms each. Scroll stayed at 2231 to 2231, new CSS animations 0, layout shifts 0. renderScheduleBody is called once per renderAll plus once per 30 s tick.
findings.rootCause: renderScheduleBody() assigns wrap.innerHTML unconditionally. It was not converted to setHtmlIfChanged in v183 like the other renderAll panels.
findings.proposedFix: Build the markup into a string and use `if (!setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html)) return;`, then attach the ics click handler only when it changed. Keep the now-pill and dimming updating because the markup differs when a block boundary passes.

findings.title: History and Members sheets jump taller in one frame when their content arrives
findings.symptom: The drawer opens as a short sheet with skeleton bars, then after the fetch it jumps to nearly full height in a single frame, moving the top edge up several hundred pixels.
findings.trigger: Settings, Change history or Who can sign in with sync on. Run p26_grow.cjs (fetch mocked at 450 ms).
findings.evidence: History sheet [top,height]: 559, 335 at t=117 ms then 136, 692 at t=501 ms. Members: 561, 277 at t=173 ms then 136, 692 at t=1308 ms. Real fetch latency is 200 ms to seconds.
findings.rootCause: The sheet is auto-height with max-height 82dvh, and the skeleton placeholder is much shorter than the loaded content. There is no min-height on #history-body or #members-body, and no height transition.
findings.proposedFix: Reserve height while loading: `#history-body, #members-body {min-height: 55dvh}`, or size the skeleton to fill the sheet. Optionally animate max-height.

findings.title: Theme flip is a mixed fade: body cross-fades while cards and the drawer snap
findings.symptom: Switching Appearance (or the OS flipping to dark at dusk while on Auto) briefly shows a mid-grey page behind surfaces that have already changed colour. About 57 borders and labels fade on their own timers.
findings.trigger: Settings, Appearance, choose Dark/Light, or an OS prefers-color-scheme change. Run p28_theme2.cjs.
findings.evidence: setTheme('dark') started 57 running transitions: body background-color/color, #now-banner border-*-color and box-shadow, 5 game-card.done borders, 10 verse-day-chip colors, six .settings-link rows' border-color. Sampling after setTheme('light'): at t=52 ms body bg was oklab(0.83 ...) (mid-grey) while the card and drawer sheet were already oklch(1 0 0); fully switched by about 200 ms.
findings.rootCause: Only some elements have colour transitions (body 0.2 s, borders 0.15 s) while most surfaces switch instantly, so the change is not atomic.
findings.location: styles.css:230 (body transition), 4643 (.settings-link border-color), plus the game-card and verse chip transitions
findings.proposedFix: Add a transient `html.theme-switching *{transition:none !important}` class removed after two rAFs in applyTheme(), or drop the body colour transition.

findings.title: Schedule sheet stays stuck partly dragged if the touch is cancelled
findings.symptom: If the system cancels a header drag (a gesture takeover or an incoming call), the sheet stays offset downward, leaving a gap at the bottom, until the next touch.
findings.trigger: Dispatch touchstart, touchmove then touchcancel on .schedule-header. Run p22_swipe_cancel.cjs. The real-world trigger rate is unknown; the state is measured, the trigger is synthetic.
findings.evidence: After touchcancel: sheet.style.transform 'translateY(60px)' and transition 'none' persist (top 144 vs 84 at rest).
findings.rootCause: wireSchedule() handles touchstart, touchmove and touchend but not touchcancel. touchstart sets `transition='none'` and the reset only lives in touchend.
findings.proposedFix: Add `header.addEventListener('touchcancel', reset)`, where reset clears transform, restores the transition and sets startY = null.

findings.title: No history or overscroll handling for overlays (suspected, not measured)
findings.symptom: Suspected: on Android, system Back with the schedule, a drawer, chat, the builder or a game detail open leaves the page or exits the PWA instead of closing the overlay. A downward drag on the schedule header at page top may trigger Chrome pull-to-refresh and reload mid-dismiss.
findings.trigger: Android Chrome or an installed PWA: open an overlay and press Back; or open the schedule at scrollY 0 and drag down on the header. Not reproducible in headless desktop Chromium.
findings.evidence: Code only: grep finds no popstate/pushState/hashchange for overlays in app.js, chat.js, settings.js or push.js (the only pushState hits are the unrelated database push). styles.css has no overscroll-behavior rule anywhere, and the sheet only has touch-action:pan-y.
findings.rootCause: Overlays are purely attribute- or class-driven with no history entries. There is no overscroll-behavior:contain on the sheet or body.
findings.location: app.js (openSchedule, openChat, openBuilder, drawer open helpers) and styles.css:1084 (.schedule-sheet)
findings.proposedFix: Add `overscroll-behavior: contain` to .schedule-sheet/.schedule-body (and `jelly-drawer::part(sheet)`), plus `html:has(.no-scroll){overscroll-behavior:none}`. Optionally push a history entry on open and close the overlay on popstate.

checkedClean: Schedule sheet open animation plays once: sheet top 844 to 84 over about 300 ms, backdrop 0 to 1, no extra sched-fade/sched-slide replays and no CSS animations after open (p17_sched_anim.cjs). Close fade/slide-out is clean via X, backdrop and Escape.

Schedule 30 s tick and renderAll while open: scrollTop preserved (2231 to 2231), 0 new running animations, 0 layout shifts (p1_schedule.cjs). Day chips are not rebuilt by the refresh. Day-chip click replays joy-rise stagger on the body only, which is intended; scroll resets to top on a day change on purpose.

renderAll() plus the full 30 s tick with Settings, History, Members (sync-off message) and Phone alerts drawers open: zero mutations inside any drawer container and zero new animations (p7_open_rerender.cjs).
Phone alerts drawer: re-renders only from push events (enable, disable, reconnect), never from a timer or renderAll. Dormant here, so the live drawer was not exercised.

Body scroll lock: scrollY preserved across drawer and schedule open/close (334 to 334) on 390 px mobile and 1100 px desktop viewports, with no horizontal shift in the main content (p6_scrolllock.cjs). Headless Chromium uses overlay scrollbars, so classic-scrollbar padding compensation was not tested. The schedule uses body.no-scroll without padding compensation, which is a possible 15 px content shift on desktop browsers with classic scrollbars; unmeasured.

Focus ring: with a real touch tap, neither the settings drawer sheet nor the schedule close button matches :focus-visible, so no outline (p19_ring.cjs, p24_ring2.cjs). The thick black ring seen in synthetic screenshots comes only from programmatic open without input. Closing the drawer by tap restores focus to #settings-btn with no page scroll jump.
Settings to History/Members/Alerts handoff: the first drawer vanishes instantly and the next slides in, with a continuous backdrop (no flash) and one slide-in play (p5_drawers.cjs).
Drawer slide-in plays once (about 560 ms with a slight overshoot). Close via X slides out in about 300 ms.
Pre-upgrade case: with jelly.js delayed 2.5 s the team picker does not open until jelly-dialog is defined, and then inert, scroll lock and focus activate correctly (p21_preupgrade.cjs).
maybeShowTeamPicker() re-entry while the identity step is open does not rebuild options (same node, step stays 'identity'). The camp picker to team picker deferral works functionally (p10, p11).

Members drawer refresh: scrollTop preserved (700 to 700) across the rebuild, and the re-created jelly-segmented/select controls start no CSS animations; the dim only applies after a 0.15 s delay, so fast reloads do not flicker (p8_members.cjs).
Update banner (jelly-alert) has no entrance animation or position jitter: geometry and opacity constant over 600 ms (p14_banner.cjs).

Lock screen: custom elements are hidden with visibility:hidden, not display:none, so jelly upgrade itself causes no layout shift. The only shifts are the content-state swaps listed in findings. Lock-screen error text and the Google button render correctly at 390x844.
jelly components re-created by innerHTML paint synchronously (applyShape runs frame(0) in connectedCallback, per vendor/jelly.js), so schedule or members rebuilds produce no blank-canvas frame.

v183 claims confirmed: idle renderAll created 0 new animations with any overlay open. Out-of-surface things seen in passing, all harmless and not re-reported: #my-electives-card innerHTML is rewritten on each renderAll/30 s tick, and #chat-card-badge and #chat-card-preview text are rewritten each render (plain text only).

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran at 430/412/390/375/360 px, junior and senior (probe v1_days.cjs). Chip rects are identical at every width below about 417 px: Sat spans 353-400. That is 10 px clipped at 390, 25 px at 375, and only a 7 px sliver at 360. #schedule-days is overflow-x:visible inside the overflow:hidden sheet, and navScrollW is 429 against navClientW 358/343/328. Screenshots show Sat cut off. At 430 it fits. A real touch tap on Sat still selects it once it is visible. The root cause (1fr floors at the jelly-chip min-content, 13 px side padding on a small chip) is correct. The auditor's injected CSS is NOT correct as written. All seven chips fit, but with `::part(main){width:100%;justify-content:center}` the label stays left-aligned inside each pill, because `.chip` is a content-width inline-flex inside a block `.jelly-content`. Measured at 360: Sun host 16-59 but label 16-41; the selected Tue label is visibly clipped at the pill's left edge (screenshot daysfix-360c.png). Using text-align:center on the host instead centres the label (host 16-59, label 25-50) and looks right (daysfix-360e.png).
verdicts.refinedFix: styles.css .schedule-days: `grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr));` plus a new rule `jelly-chip.sched-day-chip { text-align: center; }` and `jelly-chip.sched-day-chip::part(main) { padding-inline: 0; }`. Do NOT use `width:100%; justify-content:center` on the part: it leaves the text left-aligned in the pill. text-align inherits into the shadow tree and centres the inline-flex .chip. Verified at 320/360/390/430: all seven chips sit inside 16..(width-16), and tapping Sat sets scheduleDay 6. Cosmetic follow-up: the 6px `.today-dot` now overlaps the last letter of the label on a 43 px pill at 360, so nudge it to top:-2px/right:-2px or shrink it. No JS change, so no stale-listener risk. The chips are still rebuilt by renderScheduleDays() (see extra finding sched-day-chip-focus-loss).
verdicts.location: styles.css:1215 (.schedule-days) and styles.css:4380 (jelly-chip.sched-day-chip host rule); app.js:892 renderScheduleDays

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with real CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent (touchStart, 20 touchMoves to +200 px, touchEnd), not synthetic TouchEvents. Sheet top per frame: 284 (dragged), then 84 on the first frame after release, then 138, 251, 394, 522, 694, 748, 787, 814, 831, 841. So the sheet snaps 200 px back to rest and then slides down. The short-drag spring-back also snaps. A 60 px drag gave 144, then 84 on the very next frame, because the sheet has no CSS transition. Root cause confirmed: closeSchedule() clears the inline transform (app.js:871) and the sched-slide-out keyframes start from translateY(0). The touchend handler calls closeSchedule() with no offset.
verdicts.refinedFix: app.js touchend (~1074): `if (dy > 90) closeSchedule(dy); else { sheet.style.transition = 'transform .2s ease'; sheet.style.transform = ''; }`. In closeSchedule(fromDy): `if (sheet) { if (typeof fromDy === 'number' && fromDy > 0) sheet.style.setProperty('--drag', fromDy + 'px'); sheet.style.transform = ''; }`, and in finish(): `if (sheet) sheet.style.removeProperty('--drag')`. styles.css: `@keyframes sched-slide-out { from { transform: translateY(var(--drag, 0px)); } to { transform: translateY(100%); } }`. Verified (v2_swipe_fix.cjs): 284, 284, 324, 408, 512, 680, 733, 773 ... continuous, and reopening lands at top 84. Risks: closeSchedule is also a click listener (X button, backdrop), so its first argument is a MouseEvent. The `typeof === 'number'` guard is mandatory. `--drag` must be removed in finish() or a later close inherits a stale offset. touchstart already sets transition:'none', so the spring-back transition does not leak.
verdicts.location: app.js:868-884 (closeSchedule, line 871) and app.js:1074-1080 (touchend handler); styles.css:1109 (@keyframes sched-slide-out)

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced through the REAL path, not just showUpdateBanner(). I typed into #chat-input with the keyboard (so chatComposerBusy() is true), then called onNewVersion(). After 4 s there were no reloads and the banner was still up. That is the auditor's point: the banner persists exactly while the composer is in use. elementFromPoint at the centres of Send, input and photo returned #update-banner (banner y 748-828, composer 785-843). A real touchscreen tap at the Send position called doReload once while the typed text was still unsent. The bar click handler is `addEventListener('click', doReload)`, so it bypasses reloadBlocked(). The SDK pill (#sdk-banner, same .update-banner class and bottom slot) sits fully inside the update banner's rect when both show (v3_sdk.cjs: 90-270x551-624 inside 16-344x544-624). That combination is rare, because it needs the SDK down AND a new deploy. At home scrollMax the footer (795-844) is under the banner (748-828), but only while a reload is blocked; otherwise the page reloads about 1.2 s later. So the real harm is chat only. It needs a deploy to land while someone has unsent text, hence a narrow trigger. The alert has no `dismissible` attribute, which contradicts CLAUDE.md's wording.
verdicts.refinedFix: styles.css: `body.chat-open .update-banner-alert, body.chat-open .update-banner { bottom: calc(5.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }`. Verified (v3_banner_fix.cjs): banner 676-756, and Send, input and photo hit-test to their own elements. This also covers the SDK pill, which shares the class. In app.js showUpdateBanner(), make the click handler respect the safety logic: `bar.addEventListener('click', () => { if (typeof reloadBlocked === 'function' && reloadBlocked() && !confirm('You have an unsent message or unsaved score. Refresh anyway?')) return; doReload(); });` (the codebase already uses confirm()). The same applies to showSdkDownBanner's handler for chat-composer text. Optional: stack #sdk-banner above the update banner (bottom: 6rem) so both stay visible. Risk: the chat composer height varies (multi-line, photo preview), so keep the offset generous or measure `.chat-composer` height.
verdicts.location: app.js:7726-7750 (showUpdateBanner click handler) and app.js:8324 (showSdkDownBanner); styles.css:4258 (.update-banner) and 4408 (.update-banner-alert)

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with a mocked firebase (v4_members.cjs). CPU baseline on this machine is fast (a 3e7-iteration loop takes about 60 ms), so phones will be slower. renderMembers() main-thread cost: 15 members gave a 429 ms longtask (rAF gap 481 ms), 25 gave 767 ms (831 ms gap), 40 gave 1093 ms (1187 ms gap), roughly 20-27 ms per member. The roster seeds 15 counselors, so a real list is at least 16 rows. Typed text in #member-add-name read 'Typed Name' before and '' after, because renderMemberList() assigns body.innerHTML including the Add form. Both claims hold. Every role/team/None success handler in bindMemberList calls renderMembers() (app.js ~1597, 1638-1653, 1669, 1689), which re-reads both camps and rebuilds all rows. It is editors-only and setup-time, so med rather than high.
verdicts.refinedFix: Cheapest safe change: in bindMemberList, stop calling renderMembers() after a successful role/team write on an EXISTING record. The jelly-segmented/jelly-select already shows the new value and the toast confirms. Keep renderMembers() for failures (to revert the control), removals, grants (a new record changes row state) and the seed/convert paths. Because the closures are not refreshed, patch the captured data in place after each success (`camps[cid].role = value`, `rec.teamId = teamId`, or `delete` it when cleared). convertPendingMember(key, camps[CAMP.id] || rec, lists) reads rec.teamId, and the grant branch decides on `existing`, so stale closures would drop a pending member's team or re-grant over a record. Independently, make the Add form survive any rebuild: before `body.innerHTML = ...` in renderMemberList, capture `#member-add-id/name/role/camps/team` values, and restore them after bindMemberList (jelly-input and jelly-segmented accept `.value`). Do not re-run bindMemberList on a kept shell or the Add button double-binds and a second add fires.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v5_lock.cjs) with a real touch tap on the disclosure. At 360x640 open: logo [-41,-12] is entirely off-screen and the box is [-41,681] (722 px tall) in 640. At 375x667: box [-20,687], logo clipped at the top. At 667x375: logo [-166,-137], Google button [-88,-16] off-screen, email field [349,405] and #email-link-send [414,458] below the fold. #lock-screen has overflow-y:visible, scrollTop stays 0 after a wheel, and #app is display:none, so nothing can scroll. Correction to the claim: in portrait at 360x640 and 375x667 every control is still inside the viewport (only the logo and the bottom error line are clipped), so the 'cannot reach controls' impact is landscape, or a shrunk-by-keyboard viewport. That is why I rate it low, not med. The fix is three lines of CSS.
verdicts.refinedFix: styles.css html.locked .lock-screen: replace `align-items:center` with `align-items:flex-start`, add `overflow-y:auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch`, and add `html.locked .lock-screen .lock-box { margin: 0 auto; }`. For the pure overflow fix, `.lock-box{margin:auto}` keeps it vertically centred when it fits. If you also adopt the anchor fix for lock-recenter-jump, add `padding-top:max(1.5rem,14vh)`. Verified at 360x640 and 667x375: scrollTop reaches 195/408, the email Send button ends at 533/268 inside the viewport, and the box keeps 24 px of bottom padding. Risk: `.lock-box.shake` uses transform, which is unaffected. Make sure the new `overflow` does not catch the sign-in error line.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. With jelly.js delayed 1.2 s, the .lock-logo top goes 383 (checking) to 303 (signin) in one frame. At 390x844, tapping the real 'Alternative sign in' summary moved the logo 303 to 69 and the summary 463 to 228, a 235 px leap under the finger (v5_lock.cjs). The root cause, a vertically centred box whose height changes with state, is correct. It only affects signed-out devices (a returning approved device never paints the lock), so low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Same CSS block as lock-overflow-unreachable: top-anchor the box with `align-items:flex-start; padding-top:max(1.5rem,14vh); overflow-y:auto` and `.lock-box{margin:0 auto}`. Verified with the 1.2 s jelly delay plus a real tap at 390x844: the logo stays at 118 through checking, signin and open; the summary stays at 277-278 (1 px rounding) before and after opening. Same at 360x640 (logo 90) and 667x375 (logo 53).

verdicts.reasoning: p29 reproduced: both #phone-number and #email-link-address go from typed values to '', the node identity changes, and the details stays open. showAuthScreen('signin', ...) re-mounts both slots whenever it is called. Callers include showSignInError for Google popup-blocked/offline errors (app.js:8203), the auth-start error (8279) and the signed-out re-emit (8346). Worse than the claim: a phone flow already on the 'enter code' step is reset to the number step, and an email 'Sent!' status is cleared with the Send button re-enabled. That risks burning another of the shared daily 10 texts / 5 emails. The trigger is rare (a Google error mid-way through typing in the alternative forms), so low.
verdicts.refinedFix: app.js showAuthScreen: mount only when the slot is empty, e.g. `const ph = document.getElementById('alt-phone-slot'); if (window.CampPhone && ph && !ph.firstElementChild) window.CampPhone.mount(ph);` and likewise for alt-email-slot. Both mount() functions fully rebuild the slot and wire their own listeners, so skipping a second call is safe. Nothing reads state across mounts, and the iOS-standalone variant of the email slot is also non-empty. Do not add the guard inside mount() unless you also keep the first-mount wiring.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v8_drawers.cjs). Settings open: backdrop opacity 1.00 at t=28 ms while the sheet is still at top 930, so there is no fade-in. X-close: backdrop 1.00 on every frame through the sheet exit (t=26-300 ms), then display none at t=341. Team picker X-close: bd1.00 on every frame while the dialog fades 1.00 to 0.18, then gone. The settings to history handoff is continuous, so the auditor's note there is right. Root cause confirmed in vendor/jelly.js: :host{display:none} with .backdrop{opacity:0;transition:opacity .3s}, and `[open]` flips display and opacity in the same style recalc, so no transition runs. It is a subtle one-frame dim snap with a 42% scrim plus blur, hence low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Open side needs no vendor edit, because `.backdrop` has `part="backdrop"`. Add to styles.css: `@keyframes jelly-backdrop-in { from { opacity: 0 } to { opacity: 1 } } jelly-drawer[open]::part(backdrop), jelly-dialog[open]::part(backdrop) { animation: jelly-backdrop-in .3s ease both; }`. Verified: opacity goes 0.00, 0.04, 0.11, 0.47, 0.67, 0.95, 1.00 over about 340 ms. The close fade cannot be done from app CSS, because `open` stays set until the exit animation ends and `closing` is only a JS property. It needs a small patch in vendor/jelly.js's close() (animate the backdrop with the sheet), so skip it unless you want to touch the vendored file, which already carries local patches. prefers-reduced-motion: add the animation to the existing reduced-motion block or `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){...{animation:none}}`.
verdicts.location: vendor/jelly.js:5319 (dialog CSS Xi) and 5421 (drawer CSS Wi); app-side fix in styles.css

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v9_picker.cjs). Close by choice ('just cheering'): display is none on the first sampled frame. Close by X: dialog opacity 1.00, 0.98, 0.92, 0.84, 0.74, 0.62, 0.34, 0.18, then gone (about 150 ms). Root cause is correct: removeAttribute('open') skips the animated `open=false` setter. Two of the three cited locations are intentional programmatic hand-offs, not defects. closeSettings() is only called from openBuilder() (the builder takes over the screen), and openCampPicker() closes the team picker so one dialog shows at a time. The user-visible cases are only closeTeamPicker() via closePickerAndRender() after the final pick/skip (app.js ~4812, which then runs renderAll()) and the camp picker's stay-put branch (~8635). It is a first-run, one-time-per-device inconsistency, so low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Only change user-initiated closes: in closePickerAndRender() and the camp picker's `cid === CAMP.id` branch use `overlay.open = false` (the animated setter) instead of removeAttribute. Leave removeAttribute in closeSettings() and in adoptMemberTeam/openCampPicker/openBuilder, which are hand-offs. Risks: the dialog `close` event now fires about 150-300 ms later, so the pending-notify toast and the 'camp question first, then team question' re-ask timing shift slightly. renderAll() runs while the dialog is still animating, so do the renderAll in the close listener or accept one busy frame. Don't call .open=false on an already-closed dialog.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v10_sched.cjs). Each refreshOpenSchedule() takes 5-8 ms and re-creates the whole body, 268 elements including #sched-ics-btn. A text selection inside .sched-label is lost (selAfter ''), and renderScheduleBody runs exactly once per renderAll while the sheet is open (plus once per 30 s tick). It is gated on the sheet being open and nothing animates, so in practice a user only notices lost text selection, or a tap landing in the ~7 ms window on the calendar button. That is effectively invisible, so visibleToUsers is false and the severity is low.
verdicts.refinedFix: app.js renderScheduleBody: build the markup into `const html = ...` and replace `wrap.innerHTML = ...` with `if (!setHtmlIfChanged(wrap, html)) return;`, leaving the #sched-ics-btn listener wiring after it (it only needs to run when the markup was actually written). Day changes, the block-boundary 'Now' pill and past-dimming all change the markup, so they still update. Risk: joyStagger(body) and the day-chip click handler mutate the DOM after the write, so setHtmlIfChanged's `__dom === innerHTML` check correctly forces a rewrite after them.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with the mocked-fetch probe (v11_grow.cjs): History [top,height] 878,335 sliding up to 530,335 then 136,692 at t=509 ms. Members 870,277 up to 561,277 then 136,692 at t=1313 ms. The loaded sheet jumps about 360-420 px taller in one frame. Real Firebase once() latency is hundreds of ms to seconds, so it is visible every time the drawers are opened (editors only).
verdicts.refinedFix: styles.css: `#history-overlay::part(sheet), #members-overlay::part(sheet) { min-height: 70dvh; }`. Verified: the loading sheet starts at 591 px instead of 335/277, and the post-load jump shrinks from about 357 px to about 101 px. Use 80-82dvh (the jelly max-height) to remove the jump entirely. Risk: a near-empty list shows blank space, which is acceptable for admin drawers. Do not size #history-body/#members-body directly (the sheet, not the body, is what auto-sizes).

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v12_theme.cjs): setTheme('dark') starts 57 running transitions (body background-color/color, #now-banner borders and box-shadow, 5 .game-card.done borders, 10 .verse-day-chip colours, six .settings-link borders). Sampling after setTheme('light'): at t=63 ms body bg was oklab(0.83...) (mid-grey) while the card and drawer sheet were already oklch(1 0 0). It is fully switched by about 240 ms. It is a real but brief inconsistency, and only visible on a deliberate Appearance change. The OS dusk flip in Auto mode is CSS-media only (no JS listener) and uses the same body transition, so a JS-only fix would miss it.
verdicts.refinedFix: Simplest and covers the OS flip too: delete `transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease;` from `body` (styles.css:230). The remaining thin border fades are barely visible. If you want the whole flip atomic from the Appearance control: in applyTheme(), `document.documentElement.classList.add('theme-switching'); requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => document.documentElement.classList.remove('theme-switching')));` with `html.theme-switching, html.theme-switching *, html.theme-switching *::before, html.theme-switching *::after { transition: none !important; }`. Verified: 0 running transitions and the body already at the dark colour on the next frame. Do not apply the class on the init call (it would suppress nothing useful, but is wasted work). It does not reach Jelly shadow roots, which repaint through jelly-theme-change anyway.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v11_cancel.cjs): after touchstart, touchmove, touchcancel the sheet keeps style.transform 'translateY(60px)' and transition 'none' (top 144 vs 84 at rest). wireSchedule registers no touchcancel handler. The state is measured. The real-world trigger (OS gesture takeover, incoming call, iOS edge swipe) is unmeasurable headlessly and likely rare. The sheet recovers when the user closes it (closeSchedule clears the transform) or does another header drag.
verdicts.refinedFix: app.js wireSchedule: add `header.addEventListener('touchcancel', () => { if (startY == null) return; startY = null; sheet.style.transition = ''; sheet.style.transform = ''; });`. Combine with the spring-back transition from the swipe-dismiss fix, so it eases back rather than snapping. No stale-closure risk (startY and sheet are in the same closure).

verdicts.reasoning: The auditor flags this as suspected, and I cannot measure it. Pull-to-refresh and Android system Back cannot be exercised in headless desktop Chromium. The code facts are accurate: grep finds no popstate/pushState/hashchange for overlays (only the unrelated database pushState() and two replaceState URL cleanups in push.js and auth-email-link.js), and styles.css and vendor/jelly.js contain no overscroll-behavior at all. body.no-scroll is just overflow:hidden, and the sheet has touch-action:pan-y. Android Chrome pull-to-refresh on scroll-chaining out of .schedule-body at scrollTop 0 is a known pattern but is unmeasured here. Back-button handling is a missing feature, not a visual glitch.
verdicts.refinedFix: The zero-risk, unmeasured part is worth adding anyway: `.schedule-body { overscroll-behavior: contain; }` and `html:has(body.no-scroll) { overscroll-behavior: none; }` in styles.css. Jelly's drawer scrolls inside its shadow `.sheet`, so use `jelly-drawer::part(sheet) { overscroll-behavior: contain; }`. Treat history/Back support as a separate feature decision (it needs one pushState per overlay and a popstate closer, interacting with the lock/auth reloads). Do not bundle it with the glitch fixes.

extraFindings.title: Schedule sheet changes height per day, so the day chips jump away from the finger
extraFindings.symptom: Tap Sat in the junior schedule and the whole sheet drops about 96 px and the chip row moves with it. In the senior camp, tapping Sun shrinks the sheet to about 400 px and drops the chip row about 357 px, and tapping Sat does similar. Tapping back to a long day moves it all back up. There is no animation, so the chip you were aiming for moves right after the tap.
extraFindings.trigger: Open the schedule (tap Happening now), then tap the Sat chip (junior) or the Sun or Sat chip (senior), then tap another day. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/hunt/overlays-verify/v15_dayjump.cjs
extraFindings.evidence: 430x844. Junior: Sun to Fri sheetTop 84 / h 760 / chip row y 169; Sat sheetTop 180 / h 664 / chip y 265 (5 blocks). Senior: Sun sheetTop 441 / h 403 / chip y 526 (2 blocks); Mon to Fri 84/760/169; Sat sheetTop 294 / h 550 / chip y 379 (4 blocks). Adding `.schedule-sheet{height:90dvh}` gave sheetTop 84, h 760 and chip y 169 for all seven days in both camps.
extraFindings.rootCause: .schedule-sheet is bottom-aligned with only max-height:90dvh, so its height is the content height. Days with few blocks make the sheet shorter, and because the overlay is align-items:flex-end the top edge (and the header and chip row in it) moves.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Give the sheet a fixed height: `.schedule-sheet { height: 90vh; height: 90dvh; max-height: 90dvh; }` (the .schedule-body already has flex:1 1 auto; overflow-y:auto, so it fills). Verified as above. Trade-off: short days (Sat, senior Sun) show blank space under the timeline, which is better than a moving target. Optionally put the Add-to-calendar row at the bottom with margin-top:auto.

extraFindings.title: Tapping a schedule day chip destroys the chip and drops keyboard focus to the page body
extraFindings.symptom: Keyboard, switch and screen-reader users lose their place after selecting a day. Focus goes to body, so the next Tab starts from the top, and the chip's own selection animation never plays because a fresh pre-selected chip appears.
extraFindings.trigger: Open the schedule, focus a day chip button, press Enter or Space (or click it). Probe: .../overlays-verify/v14_chipfocus.cjs
extraFindings.evidence: Before the click document.activeElement was the chip (true). After: sameNode false, the old chip isConnected false, activeElement BODY#, and the new chip has `selected`.
extraFindings.rootCause: The chip click handler calls renderSchedule(), and renderScheduleDays() rebuilds all seven jelly-chips via wrap.innerHTML on every tap, re-running each chip's connectedCallback.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Build the chips once per open and update selection in place: in the click handler set `scheduleDay` then `wrap.querySelectorAll('.sched-day-chip').forEach((c) => c.toggleAttribute('selected', +c.dataset.dow === scheduleDay))` and only call renderScheduleBody(). Risk: selectable jelly-chips toggle their own `selected` on click, so re-assert it for the tapped chip (a tap on the already-selected day would otherwise deselect it). Bind the click listeners once, not on every render.

extraFindings.title: Team picker dialog snaps from tall to short and re-centres when moving to the identity step
extraFindings.symptom: After picking a team on first run, the dialog instantly shrinks and re-centres. The old content is swapped with no transition, and the 7-option dialog becomes a 4-option one.
extraFindings.trigger: First launch on a junior-camp device, tap a team in the team picker. Probe: .../overlays-verify/v16_picker_steps.cjs
extraFindings.evidence: Team step: dialog top 140, height 565, 7 options. After the pick: top 242, height 359, 4 options, and it holds that value from the first sampled frame (28 ms) onward, so there is no animation.
extraFindings.rootCause: renderPickerStep() rewrites the title, hint and option list in place and the jelly-dialog is vertically centred, so the height change re-centres in one frame.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Give the dialog a stable height for both steps, e.g. `#team-picker-options { min-height: 22rem; }`, or top-anchor the dialog with `jelly-dialog#team-picker-overlay::part(wrap){align-items:flex-start;padding-top:12vh}` so only the bottom edge moves. It appears once per device, so this is cosmetic and low priority.

found.probesRun:
All probes are Playwright scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/hunt/builder/ (390x844 mobile emulation, Firebase blocked, editor hint, ?now=2-1330, team picker dismissed; boot.cjs is the shared bootstrap, frames.cjs is a CDP screencast + pixel-diff helper). Each probe is run as `node <file>`.

- p29/p30: unsaved game draft versus tab switch and versus "Back to scoreboard".
- p8/p9/p13/p14/p24/p38: open, close and tab-switch transitions, details open, and checkbox re-render, via screencast.
