findings.title: Every renderAll while the builder is open throws the page back to scrollY 0
findings.symptom: In the week builder, any reorder arrow, Add day/team/step, Remove step, notice Post, or any remote update while the builder is open snaps the page to the very top. Move game #14 down and the list jumps to the top. Add a day or team and the new row is off-screen at the bottom.
findings.trigger: Open Settings -> Set up the week as an editor. Scroll down on any tab (Games list, Days, Notice, ...). Tap a reorder arrow, Add day/team/step, or Remove step. Or let any renderAll fire: a remote score snapshot from another editor, a members-list change, a clock settling. Reproduced identically in the senior camp.
findings.evidence: Measured. renderAll() with scrollY at 1270 (games), 1061 (days), 4927 (notice) gives scrollY 0 synchronously, before any paint. Real touch taps: games reorder 1370->0, days reorder 547->0, notice step move 1948->0, Add day 1161->0 (doc grew 2005->2343), Add team 182->0, Add notice step 3798->0, Remove step 2293->0. Real handleRemoteSnapshot() with a changed result: 900->0 on the Games tab (jelly-tabs element replaced, 223 ms) and 900->0 on the Notice tab (173 ms). Game-editor-internal re-renders (format card, session chip, add/move/remove section) do NOT jump (scrollY 1372->1372), because they replace only card.innerHTML. An in-page patch that keeps the jelly-tabs shell and re-renders only the active card kept scrollY 1500->1500 (p39).
findings.rootCause: renderSettings() does `view.innerHTML = ...` on every call (settings.js:60). That inserts five EMPTY .settings-card divs, and the Jelly connectedCallbacks (jelly-tabs, jelly-button, ...) force layout at that moment. The document is then only a few hundred px tall, so the browser clamps scrollY to 0. The cards are filled afterwards by renderSettingsSection (settings.js:96-98), but the scroll offset is already lost. renderAll calls renderSettings unconditionally while builderOpen() (app.js:7850), so every own action and every remote snapshot does this.
findings.proposedFix: Make renderSettings build the shell once, the same pattern as renderDayTabs. If jelly-tabs.settings-tabs already exists, patch the 'Last edited' line, set the tabs `value` only if it changed, and re-render only the ACTIVE card in place via renderSettingsSection(tab, card). Re-render the other cards lazily in the tabs `change` handler. Skip the card write entirely when its inputs are unchanged, using a per-card signature of the state slice it reads (games list: config.games/days/sessions + result keys; days: config.days + game counts; teams: state.teams; notice: state.notice + teams; data: nothing). A remote score change then touches nothing but the Games list's result dots. As a cheap safety net, also save window.scrollY before any full rebuild and restore it afterwards.

findings.title: Builder tab-bar pill re-springs from the Games tab on every rebuild when another tab is active
findings.symptom: Whenever the builder re-renders while Days, Teams, Notice or Data is the active tab, the blue active pill reappears over 'Games' and slides across to the active tab with a squashed, wobbling spring. For roughly half a second the active tab's label is white on grey and unreadable. It happens after every reorder, add or remove in those tabs and on every remote update. It also slides when the builder is first opened with a remembered non-Games tab.
findings.trigger: Builder open on Days/Teams/Notice/Data. Tap any reorder arrow, Add, or Remove, or let a remote snapshot arrive. Or set the last-used tab to teams, close, and reopen via openBuilder(). The Games tab is unaffected because it is index 0.
findings.evidence: Measured. After renderAll the jelly-segmented pillX starts at -140 (the Games slot) with index = 4, placed = true, pillTarget = +141. The pill then travels and settles in 400-550 ms. Initial distance to target: days 69 px (400 ms), teams 140 px (469 ms), notice 210 px (542 ms), data 281 px (544 ms), games 1 px (80 ms). Opening the builder with remembered tab=teams: 140 px, 462 ms. Screencast strip of the tab bar (f33_tabbar_strip.png in the probe dir) shows the pill jumping to the Days area and sliding to Notice while the 'Notice' label is white on grey for frames 2-10.
findings.rootCause: renderSettings always re-creates <jelly-tabs> (the comment at settings.js:56-59 says so deliberately). On connect the inner jelly-segmented places its pill at the first segment, probably because the segments are not upgraded yet when onShape runs. It then springs to the real `value` once they upgrade. The home day tabs avoided this in v183 by updating panels in place; the builder tabs were not converted.
findings.location: settings.js:60-70 (jelly-tabs created inside the innerHTML template)
findings.proposedFix: Same fix as builder-rebuild-scroll-jump: never re-create the settings jelly-tabs. Create it once, then only set its `value` attribute. Verified in-page: with the shell kept, the pill's max distance to target is 0 and the tabs element is the same node. For the first-open case, create the shell once at app start or first builder open, or wait until the segmented control has measured before un-hiding.

findings.title: 'Back to scoreboard' with a half-edited game leaves a hidden dirty draft that freezes live updates on that phone
findings.symptom: An editor opens a game, types anything (even one character), then taps '<- Back to scoreboard'. No confirm appears. The scoreboard looks normal, but from then on that device stops adopting other editors' scores and config changes. A deferred snapshot stays pending forever, auto-reload on deploy is blocked, the 5-minute idle card-collapse never runs, and sign-out or camp switch show a false 'unsynced work' warning. It self-heals only after opening a different game in the editor or reloading.
findings.trigger: Settings -> Set up the week -> open any game or + New game -> type in a field (builderDirty() becomes true) -> tap '<- Back to scoreboard' at the top. Then deliver any remote snapshot (another editor saves a score).
findings.evidence: Measured (p30). After Back: view='home', editGameId=null, but gameDraft is still set, builderDirty()=true, editorMidEntry()=true, canAdoptRemote()=false. handleRemoteSnapshot() with a new result: remoteApplied=false, remoteRefetchPending=true. 3.5 s of idle ticks later: still remoteRefetchPending=true, editorMidEntry=true, reloadBlocked()=true. No dialog was shown (dialogs=0).
findings.rootCause: The settings-back-btn handler (settings.js:72-77) sets state.ui.view='home' and editGameId=null but never clears gameDraft/gameDraftFor and never asks about unsaved edits (leaveGameEditor does both). builderDirty() (settings.js:31-33) only checks the draft against its snapshot, not that the editor is actually open. editorMidEntry() (app.js:7670), reloadBlocked() (app.js:7764-7770), collapseCardsForIdle (app.js:7793) and hasUnsyncedWork (app.js:8528-8530) all consume it.
findings.proposedFix: In the back-button handler, route through the same logic as leaveGameEditor: if builderDirty() confirm 'Discard your changes?', then null gameDraft and gameDraftFor. Also harden builderDirty() to return false unless `state.ui.view === 'settings' && state.ui.editGameId` (and likewise clear the draft when renderAll force-closes the builder for a demoted role at app.js:7820), so a stale draft can never block sync.

findings.title: Each builder rebuild costs a ~1.3 s main-thread freeze on a phone-class CPU, spent mostly on hidden tabs
findings.symptom: After tapping a reorder arrow, or whenever a remote score lands while the builder is open, the page freezes for over a second on a mid-range phone. Further taps are swallowed and the keyboard or tab pill stutters.
findings.trigger: Builder open (any tab). Tap a reorder arrow, or deliver a remote state change. Measured with 4x CPU throttle on a 22-game junior week.
findings.evidence: Measured. renderAll with the builder closed: 18 ms median (4x). Builder open, median/max at 4x: games 1235/1334 ms, days 993/1900, teams 889/906, notice 1050/1218, data 587/642. So even with the cheap Data tab active it costs ~0.6 s, because all five panels are rebuilt. Unthrottled it is 157-230 ms. One reorder tap at 4x produced longtasks [1334, 244, 143, 147, 88] ms. One remote score snapshot produced [1190, 371, 199, 248, 70] ms. Each rebuild re-creates ~230 Jelly elements (junior): 84 jelly-input, 44+ jelly-icon-button, 44 jelly-badge, 24 jelly-textarea, 10 jelly-select, 80 jelly-option, 18 jelly-button.
findings.rootCause: renderSettings re-renders all five tab cards, four of them hidden, with fresh Jelly components on every renderAll, including renderAlls that changed nothing the builder shows (a remote score changes only the Games list's result dots).
findings.location: settings.js:96-98 (forEach over all SETTINGS_TABS) called from app.js:7850
findings.proposedFix: Same root fix as the scroll jump: render only the visible card, only when its signature changed, and the others lazily on tab activation. An idle renderAll then costs ~0 in the builder.

findings.title: Tapping another builder tab silently throws away an unsaved game draft (no confirm)
findings.symptom: While writing a new game (name, rules sections, timer...), one slip on the Days/Teams/Notice/Data tab bar deletes the whole draft and shows the games list. '<- All games' and 'Cancel' ask 'Discard your changes?', but the tab bar does not.
findings.trigger: Games tab -> + New game -> type a name and tap '+ Add section' -> tap the 'Days' tab segment -> tap 'Games' again.
findings.evidence: Measured (p29). Before: builderDirty()=true, draft name 'My brand new game with lots of rules', 1 rule section. After the tab tap: editGameId=null, gameDraft=null, dialogs shown = 0. Back on Games the list is shown.
findings.rootCause: The jelly-tabs `change` handler discards the draft without checking builderDirty() ('same semantics as before', settings.js:83-92). The draft already lives in JS memory.
findings.proposedFix: Don't discard on tab change: leave state.ui.editGameId and gameDraft alone so the editor is simply still there when the Games tab is revisited. Or, if builderDirty(), confirm first and revert the tab on cancel.

findings.title: Returning from the builder replays the 'rise in' animation on every open home card, and the home scroll position is lost
findings.symptom: An editor with Competitions, Standings or Cleanup expanded opens the builder and taps '<- Back to scoreboard'. The contents of every open card fade and rise in again (as if each had just been opened), and the page is back at the top instead of where they were. Chat's full-screen takeover uses the same hide method.
findings.trigger: Expand a home card, open Settings -> Set up the week, then tap '<- Back to scoreboard'. Cards stay open until the 5-minute idle collapse.
findings.evidence: Measured (p17, p27). Animations started within 2 frames of returning, with three cards open: joy-rise x3 on .settings-row.card-visibility-row, x1 each on #day-tabs, p.standings-hint, p#sync-status, .standings-actions, .table-scroll, p.card-desc, #cleanup-body. Home scrollY 700 before the builder, 0 after returning (doc 2932 tall).
findings.rootCause: body.builder-open sets display:none on every .main-wrap child (styles.css:4748-4751). A CSS animation restarts when an element goes from display:none to displayed, and `jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card[open] > *:not([slot=header])` always carries the joy-rise animation (styles.css:5785). openBuilder also calls window.scrollTo({top:0}) (app.js:7873) and nothing remembers the home offset.
findings.proposedFix: Run joy-rise only transiently: add a class (for example .card-opening) to the jelly-collapsible when the user toggles it open, remove it after ~500 ms, and scope the CSS rule to that class. That removes every replay source at once (un-hide, re-insert, chat takeover). Also store window.scrollY when entering the builder or chat and restore it on return.

findings.title: Touching a list row to start a scroll shrinks it to 93% and snaps it back
findings.symptom: On the Games list (full-width row buttons), putting a finger down to scroll makes the row visibly shrink and pop back when the scroll starts: a twitch on almost every touch-scroll over the list.
findings.trigger: Touch-drag vertically starting on a .game-row-main row in Settings -> Set up the week -> Games. The delegated press handler is app-wide, so any button, link or summary does it, including .format-card and .team-chip.
findings.evidence: Measured (p25, CDP touch). Timeline of the row: pointerdown -> joy-pressed added at 36 ms, transform animates scale 1 -> 0.93 over ~100 ms, pointercancel when the scroll starts (252 ms) -> class removed and transform jumps straight to none. The transition only exists on .joy-pressed, so release is instant, not animated. A fast flick would show a partial shrink followed by a snap.
findings.rootCause: The pointerdown listener adds .joy-pressed immediately to anything matching button, a, summary, jelly-button, jelly-chip, jelly-segment or jelly-icon-button, regardless of size or whether the touch becomes a scroll (app.js:8087-8091). The scale rule lives only on .joy-pressed with its transition (styles.css:5770-5773).
findings.proposedFix: Delay adding .joy-pressed ~70-90 ms and cancel the timer on pointermove, pointercancel or touchmove. Skip the scale for wide or row-like targets (for example width > 200 px, or opt out via a class on .game-row-main and .format-card). Optionally put the `transition: transform` on the base state so release animates instead of snapping.

findings.title: Builder layout: long single-column tabs with no sticky navigation or save bar, and no history entry
findings.symptom: On a 390 px phone the tab bar and Back link scroll away, so switching tabs or leaving means scrolling back to the top. The game editor is ~2.2-2.8k px tall with Save/Cancel at the very bottom. The Notice tab is ~5.9k px. The system Back gesture leaves the app instead of closing the builder.
findings.trigger: Open the builder at 390x844. Games list (22 games), Days, Notice, game editor (tournament game with rules and extras).
findings.evidence: Measured. Document heights: games list 2214, days 2005, teams 1026, notice 5871, data 914, game editor 2216 (tally) to 2823 (tournament with tracker + extras open) at 844 px viewport. getComputedStyle position of jelly-tabs and the back button is 'static'. history.length is 2 before and 2 after openBuilder + editor (history.state null): the builder and editor are state-only takeovers with no pushState/popstate anywhere. Home scroll position is lost on a round trip (700 -> 0).
findings.rootCause: The builder is one full-page takeover (body.builder-open) with a static header, one long column per tab, and navigation by mutating state.ui.view only.
findings.proposedFix: Make the tab bar sticky (position: sticky; top: 0 with a background). Add a sticky bottom action bar (Save / Cancel) in the game editor. Collapse the Notice tab's rows into disclosures, or split Wording / Assignments / Steps / Preview. Push a history entry in openBuilder and close on popstate. Remember and restore the home scroll offset.

findings.title: A config edit's own echo can register as 'someone else changed it' and trigger a second full builder rebuild ~400-500 ms later
findings.symptom: After Add day or saving a new game, the builder flashes and rebuilds a second time half a second after the first (and jumps scroll again if the user already scrolled).
findings.trigger: On a synced device whose state.config came from the server (key-sorted): tap '+ Add day' on the Days tab, or Save a new game. 400 ms later pushConfig() fires and RTDB echoes the value back with sorted keys and `dow: null` dropped.
findings.evidence: Measured with a STUBBED RTDB echo (fbConfigRef.set fires the listener synchronously with a key-sorted, null-pruned copy; p7). Add day: renderSettings at 12 ms (own) and again at 411 ms (echo). Save new game: rebuild at ~1131 ms and again at 1615 ms (echo at 1610). A plain reorder of existing days produced only one rebuild; renaming a day and blurring produced none. Not run against a live Firebase.
findings.rootCause: applyRemoteConfig compares JSON.stringify(state.config) to the adopted remote (app.js:2294 and 2307). RTDB returns children in sorted key order and drops nulls and empties, so any locally created object (new day {id,name,dow:null,note}, new game) stringifies differently from its echo, even though nothing changed.
findings.proposedFix: Compare canonical forms using the existing syncCanon() (app.js ~2512) on both sides: `JSON.stringify(syncCanon(before)) !== JSON.stringify(syncCanon(state.config))`.

findings.title: Some renderAll callers ignore editorMidEntry, killing an open dropdown or the keyboard in the builder
findings.symptom: If one of the unguarded renderAll paths fires while a builder field or dropdown is in use, the open Day-of-week popup vanishes and the keyboard drops with focus lost.
findings.trigger: Builder open with a jelly-select open or a field focused, then the members-list listener fires (any member added, removed or changed by an admin, and once on attach) or a running game clock settles at zero (tickBoardClocks).
findings.evidence: Effect measured (p11, p42): with the Day-of-week jelly-select open and editorMidEntry()=true, a renderAll() replaced the select node (isConnected=false); with a field focused, activeElement became BODY. The trigger itself is code-only: app.js:2739-2742 calls renderAll() on every members snapshot with no changed-check and no editorMidEntry check, and app.js:3516-3520 does `if (settled) renderAll()`. Remote state and config paths ARE guarded (canAdoptRemote / editorMidEntry).
findings.rootCause: Only handleRemoteSnapshot and the config listener respect editorMidEntry. The members listener and the clock-settle path call renderAll directly.
findings.proposedFix: In the members listener, skip renderAll when the directory JSON is unchanged, and defer it with the same pending mechanism when editorMidEntry(). Same guard for the clock-settle renderAll.

findings.title: An open, unmodified game editor ignores a remote edit to that game, and Save overwrites it
findings.symptom: Editor B has a game open with no edits. Editor A changes that game's tagline or rules. B's editor keeps showing the old values, and when B edits one field and saves, A's change is silently overwritten.
findings.trigger: Two editors. B opens game X in the builder and touches nothing. A saves a change to X. B changes any field and taps Save.
findings.evidence: Measured (p37). After applyRemoteConfig with the headline changed: state.config.games[0].headline = 'CHANGED BY ANOTHER EDITOR', but the draft headline and the gd-headline input still show the old text, and builderDirty()=false.
findings.rootCause: ensureGameDraft returns early when `gameDraftFor === editId && gameDraft` (settings.js:340-343), so the draft built at open time is never refreshed. renderAll does re-render the editor, but from the stale draft.
findings.proposedFix: Remember JSON of the source game when the draft is built. In ensureGameDraft, if !builderDirty() and the saved game's JSON now differs, rebuild the draft. If the draft is dirty, show a 'changed elsewhere' note.

findings.title: Pasted backup text in Data -> Restore is wiped by any rebuild while it isn't focused
findings.symptom: Paste a backup into the Restore box, tap outside to read something, and any renderAll (a remote score, another action) empties the box and clears the 'doesn't look like a backup' error.
findings.trigger: Data tab: paste text into #restore-textarea, blur it, then trigger any renderAll.
findings.evidence: Measured (p35). Textarea length 67 before, 0 after renderAll with nothing focused.
findings.rootCause: The whole builder is rebuilt from markup that has no value for this textarea, and the text is not stored anywhere.
findings.proposedFix: Largely fixed by the in-place/skip-unchanged render (the Data card has no state inputs and would never re-render). Otherwise stash the value in a module variable and restore it after the card renders.

findings.title: Paired inputs misalign by 16 px when one label wraps ('Outs per side (0 = none)')
findings.symptom: In the Live match scoreboard fields, the 'Periods' and 'Outs per side' inputs sit at different heights on a phone, because the right label wraps to two lines.
findings.trigger: Game editor for a bracket game with the Live match scoreboard on, at 390 px width.
findings.evidence: Measured (p41 and screenshot s_editor_full.png). gd-tracker-innings top 1069, gd-tracker-outs top 1085 (16 px lower). The right label is 32 px tall and the left one 16 px.
findings.rootCause: .form-row is a 2-column grid of .form-field blocks, each label above its input, so unequal label heights push the input down.
findings.proposedFix: Shorten the label ('Outs / side') and add `.form-row { align-items: end }` (or give .form-row .form-label a fixed min-height) so inputs line up.

findings.title: Team name and counselor inputs are only 160 px wide at 390 px, truncating names while editing
findings.symptom: On the Teams tab, long team names such as 'Methodic Mediocre Maples' and 'Particularly Perilous Pumpkins' and the counselor lists are clipped inside narrow inputs, so you cannot see what you are editing.
findings.trigger: Teams tab at phone width with the default junior team names.
findings.evidence: Measured (p41 and screenshot s_teams_days.png). All six .team-name-input hosts are 160 px wide. Two reorder arrows plus a delete button take the rest of the row.
findings.rootCause: .team-builder-row puts reorder arrows, the name/counselor stack and the delete button in one flex row; the field column gets whatever is left.
findings.proposedFix: Put the name and counselor inputs on full-width lines and move the reorder/delete controls to a compact row above or below them (or into a per-row menu).

findings.title: Game-editor validation message pushes Save down and then stays visible after the problem is fixed
findings.symptom: Tapping Save with no name inserts 'Give the game a name.' above the Save button, shifting Save/Cancel down ~31 px under the finger. The message stays after the name is typed, until the next Save.
findings.trigger: + New game -> scroll to Save -> tap Save with an empty name -> type a name.
findings.evidence: Measured (p31). Save button top 746 -> 777 when the error appears (doc 1167 -> 1198). After typing a name, #gd-error is still hidden=false with the old text.
findings.rootCause: #gd-error is toggled via hidden with no reserved space (settings.js:418, 716-726) and is only cleared by the next Save or a re-render.
findings.proposedFix: Reserve a min-height for the error line (or show it in a toast or an inline banner above the fold). Clear it on the next input or format change.

findings.title: Senior camp always shows an amber 'bracket wizard designed for 6 teams' warning on a normal 4-team roster
findings.symptom: Every visit to Settings -> Teams in the senior camp shows an alarm-coloured warning, even though 4 teams is exactly what that camp runs.
findings.trigger: Senior camp, builder, Teams tab.
findings.evidence: Measured (p16). Text: '⚠️ The bracket wizard is designed for 6 teams — you have 4 (this camp normally runs 4). Bracket games may need improvising.'
findings.rootCause: The warn condition is `teams.length !== 6` (settings.js:999) and ignores CAMP.teamCount.
findings.proposedFix: Only warn when teams.length !== CAMP.teamCount, or soften it to a neutral note for the senior camp.

findings.title: The posted notice card is re-created on every renderAll and every 30 s tick, clearing text selection
findings.symptom: A person selecting or copying text from the posted notice (cleanup assignments) loses the selection within 30 s, or the instant any remote update lands.
findings.trigger: Post a notice, select text in the card, then wait for the 30 s interval or any renderAll.
findings.evidence: Measured (p41). With the notice posted and 22 characters selected, one renderAll left 0 characters selected and the title node was replaced (sameNode=false). No animation is involved (plain text nodes).
findings.rootCause: renderNoticeBoard writes `el.innerHTML = html` unconditionally (app.js:686-692); v183's setHtmlIfChanged was not applied to it. It also runs from the 30 s interval (app.js:7971) and from noticeCommit in the builder.
findings.proposedFix: Use setHtmlIfChanged(el, html || '') as the other home panels now do.

checkedClean: Rebuild blink at scroll 0: screencast diffs across 3 renderAlls on the Games tab were 0.00-0.01 (p4). Jelly canvases paint before the first frame, so there is no visible blank flash. The visible rebuild symptoms are the scroll jump and the pill slide.
Opening the builder from the Settings sheet: lands at scrollY 0 from home scroll 0/334 (p38); no flash or glitch frames (p9). The sparkle dots are the intended joy burst.
Return to home: the Happening-now jelly-progress keeps its fill from the first frame, no refill (p8; region diff constant at 55.77 from frame 1).

Tab switching: only the intended 220 ms panel fade and pill spring. Controls inside previously hidden panels are sized and painted by the first visible frames (canvas 300x150 -> 134x134 etc., p13). 'Tools & extras' details opens with everything painted on frame 1 (p14).

Game-editor internal re-renders (format card, session chip, tracker toggle, add/move/remove section, timer toggle): scrollY preserved (1372->1372, 40->40), ~29-33 Jelly elements re-created, no visible blink; the checkbox toggle shows no intermediate frames (p10, p24).
Idle timers: over 32 s with a focused gd-name field, the 30 s interval, the 500 ms clock tick and idleRetry produced 0 DOM mutations in #settings-view; same input node, focus and value kept (p28).

Per-keystroke work: typing in the game editor only assigns to the draft. Days/Teams/Notice commit on `change` (natural blur works, p42); an unguarded rebuild while typing still committed the text (Tuesday-lost), so only focus/keyboard is lost. The Notice preview is plain HTML (no Jelly) and refreshes on blur only, so there is no per-keystroke rebuild of Jelly components.

Remote snapshots and config while a field, jelly-select or dirty draft is active are deferred by editorMidEntry/canAdoptRemote (p11: midEntry=true while select open). The only issue is the dirty-draft leak (builder-dirty-draft-freezes-sync).
Two-editor config race (p26): B's blur-commit push overwrites A's concurrent edit (documented last-write-wins), with no flicker and no stale-state flash.
Reload while the builder is open: ui.view resets to home at first render, so the builder is not re-opened (p15).
Senior camp builder (25 games, 4 teams): same behaviour as junior for the scroll jump (500->0) and a 157 ms rebuild with 201 Jelly elements (p16).

Horizontal overflow: body.scrollWidth is 419 vs 390 in the builder only, from Jelly canvas overhang (jelly-segmented canvas L=-29..R=419, jelly-button -7..397). html and body are overflow-x:hidden, so there is no scroll in Chromium. Not verified on iOS Safari.

verdicts.location: settings.js:48-99 (renderSettings; innerHTML at line 60) called unconditionally from app.js:7850
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced in my own probes (builder-verify/v1, v2, v7). renderAll() with the builder open sets scrollY to 0 synchronously on every tab (games 822->0, days 696->0, teams 109->0, notice 3016->0, data 42->0). Real touch taps: games reorder 1370->0, days reorder 547->0, Add day 1161->0, Add team 182->0. A real handleRemoteSnapshot() with a changed result (canAdopt=true, midEntry=false) goes 900->0 on both Games and Notice tabs. No paint happens in between, so the user just sees a jump to top. Root cause is right in spirit, but my testing shows it is broader than 'empty cards'. The clamp happens whenever a rebuild briefly shrinks the document while Jelly elements upgrade. Replacing only the Data card's innerHTML (v5, v6) also clamps scrollY 60->0 even though the shell is kept. So the shell-keeping, active-card-only fix on its own is NOT sufficient. In my patch run (v4), games/days/teams/notice kept their offset but Data still went 42->0. Scroll restoration is verified: saving scrollY, running the rebuild and calling scrollTo(0,y) in the same task restores it exactly on every tab (v7), and a real days-reorder tap stays at 547->547 with no visible frame in between.
verdicts.refinedFix: Two layers. (1) Immediate 3-line safety net, no rebuild change: in renderSettings, `const y = window.scrollY;` at the top and `if (window.scrollY !== y) window.scrollTo(0, y);` at the end (after the card fill loop). Verified on all five tabs and on real taps. Applying it as a wrapper around the existing renderSettings gave an exact scrollY match everywhere. (2) Structural fix, shared with builder-tabs-pill-respring and builder-rebuild-jank: keep the <jelly-tabs.settings-tabs> shell (back button, h2, tabs, five .settings-card panels) and build it only when view.querySelector('jelly-tabs.settings-tabs') is missing. Patch the 'Last edited' line into a stable slot element and only set the tabs `value` attribute if it differs. Re-render only the active card, mark the other cards data-stale, and render a stale card inside the tabs `change` handler (verified working: v4 'lazy' test). Keep (1) even after (2), because a single-card innerHTML rewrite can still clamp on short tabs such as Data. Risks to guard: wireNoticeTab closes over `const n = noticeBoard()`, so any skip-unchanged logic for the Notice card must key on the full JSON of state.notice (or the object identity), otherwise handlers edit an orphaned object after a remote snapshot replaces state.notice. wireDaysTab, wireTeamsTab and wireGameRows re-read state at click time, so they are safe. Do not skip a card based on state alone. Use the app's own setHtmlIfChanged pattern (compare html AND el.__dom === el.innerHTML), because jelly-checkbox, details and .day-delete-error mutate their own DOM. That means splitting each renderXTab into an xHTML() builder plus a wire step, so the wire step runs only when the markup was actually written.

verdicts.location: settings.js:60-70 (jelly-tabs created inside the innerHTML template); mechanism in vendor/jelly.js jelly-segmented.sync()/onShape()
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v3). After renderAll on the Notice tab, jelly-segmented pillX starts at -140 (Games slot) with target +70 and index 3, then slides over about 550 ms. A screencast strip (builder-verify/v3_strip.png) shows the blue pill appearing around Days and wobbling across to Notice, while the 'Notice' label is white on grey for roughly 9 frames. First-open with a remembered tab=teams: firstPillX -140, travel 140 px (v8). Root cause confirmed in the vendor code: on first sync the jelly-segment children are not yet upgraded, so `o.value` is undefined, findIndex is -1, index falls back to 0 and the pill is `placed` at segment 0. The segments then upgrade and re-run sync(), which moves pillTarget but not pillX, so the pill springs. Verified in-page that keeping the shell removes the rebuild case (pillMaxDist 0, same tabs node, v4). BUT keeping the shell does NOT fix the first-open case: with the shell patch the first creation with tab=teams still travels 140 px (v8). The proposal's 'create the shell once at app start' is vague and would still spring when the stored tab is not Games.
verdicts.refinedFix: Keep the shell (see scroll-jump fix) for the rebuild case. For the first creation, snap the pill right after the shell is written, in the same task (before paint): `const seg = tabs.shadowRoot.querySelector('jelly-segmented'); seg.pillX = seg.pillTarget; seg.pillXVelocity = 0; seg.requestFrame && seg.requestFrame();`. Verified in-page with tab=teams: firstPillX 0, maxDist 0, idx 2 (v9). Put it in one small helper (for example settleTabPill(tabsEl)) so renderDayTabs can reuse it (see extraFindings). Do not edit vendor/jelly.js unless the owner accepts a vendor diff. Risk: only snap on creation, never on a user-driven change, or the spring on real tab taps is lost. Severity is med rather than high because it is cosmetic (about 0.5 s), editor-only, and happens once per builder action, but it does fire on every action while on Days/Teams/Notice/Data.

verdicts.location: settings.js:72-77 (back button handler), settings.js:31-33 (builderDirty); consumers app.js:7670 (editorMidEntry), 7764-7770 (reloadBlocked), 7797 (collapseCardsForIdle), 8528-8530 (hasUnsyncedWork)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with real taps and keyboard (v10). Open a game, type 'X' into #gd-name (builderDirty=true), tap '<- Back to scoreboard': no dialog, view='home', editGameId=null, but gameDraft still set, builderDirty=true, editorMidEntry=true, canAdoptRemote=false. handleRemoteSnapshot() with a new result: applied=false, remoteRefetchPending=true, and still true after 3.5 s of idle ticks, with reloadBlocked=true and hasUnsyncedWork=true. Code path matches the claim: the back handler never clears gameDraft/gameDraftFor and never confirms, unlike leaveGameEditor (settings.js:668-676). One extra symptom I measured: reopening the SAME game afterwards silently resurrects the half-edited draft ('ShieldsX'), because ensureGameDraft returns early for the same id; opening a different game rebuilds a clean draft and self-heals the freeze. verdicts.refinedFix: In the back-button handler, mirror leaveGameEditor: `if (state.ui.editGameId && builderDirty() && !confirm('Discard your changes to this game?')) return; state.ui.editGameId = null; gameDraft = null; gameDraftFor = null;` before saveState()/renderAll(). Harden builderDirty() as well: `return state.ui.view === 'settings' && !!state.ui.editGameId && !!gameDraft && JSON.stringify(gameDraft) !== gameDraftSnapshot;`, so no future path can leave a hidden dirty draft blocking sync. Also null the draft where renderAll force-closes the builder for a demoted role (app.js:7820). Risk: if the builderDirty() guard is added without clearing the draft, reopening the same game still shows the old edits (draft reuse), which is acceptable but should be a deliberate choice. If tab switches keep the draft (see builder-tab-switch-silent-discard), builderDirty() must stay true while on other tabs, i.e. the view/editGameId condition above still holds.

verdicts.location: styles.css:5785-5790 (joy-rise on open collapsible children) with styles.css:4748-4751 and 4757-4758 (display:none takeovers); app.js:7865-7874 (openBuilder scrollTo)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced for the builder (v13) and for chat (v14). With a card open, clicking Back from the builder starts joy-rise animations within 2 frames on the open card's children (settings-row, p.card-desc, #cleanup-body in my run; their run had more cards open). Returning from the chat takeover does the same (#cleanup-body). Home scrollY 700 before the builder is 0 after Back, and 400 -> 0 after chat. Root cause is right: the always-on `[open] > *:not([slot=header])` animation restarts when display:none -> shown. Validated the proposed fix in-page (v35): with the rule changed to animation:none and a transient .card-opening class added on the toggle event, a user tap on a card header still plays joy-rise (3 animations), and returning from the builder plays none. verdicts.refinedFix: CSS: change the rule to `jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card[open] > *:not([slot="header"]) { animation: none; }` plus `jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card.card-opening[open] > *:not([slot="header"]) { animation: joy-rise 0.38s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) backwards; }` (keep the nth-child delays scoped to .card-opening). JS: one capture listener, `document.addEventListener('toggle', e => { const c = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('jelly-collapsible.collapsible-card'); if (c && c.hasAttribute('open')) { c.classList.add('card-opening'); setTimeout(() => c.classList.remove('card-opening'), 700); } }, true)`. Verified the toggle event reaches the document. Scroll: store `state.ui`-independent `homeScrollY = window.scrollY` in openBuilder/openChat and `window.scrollTo(0, homeScrollY)` after the renderAll in the Back/closeChat paths. The existing openBuilder scrollTo({top:0}) is intentional and should stay.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with CDP touch events (v15). On a 228x55 .game-row-main: class added at about 30 ms, transform eases 1 -> 0.93 over about 100 ms, the touch becomes a scroll (pointercancel at about 246 ms) and the transform jumps straight back to none in one frame, because the transition lives only on .joy-pressed. It is app-wide (any button/a/summary/chip), so it affects every user touch-scrolling over buttons, not just the builder. Severity med for frequency, but the visual amplitude is small (7%), so this is a polish issue. Validated the proposed delay fix in-page (v16): with an 80 ms delayed add cleared on pointermove/pointercancel, a quick flick never adds joy-pressed (transform stays none), and a held touch still presses.
verdicts.refinedFix: In the pointerdown handler replace the immediate add with a timer: `clearTimeout(joyPressTimer); joyPressTarget = t; joyPressTimer = setTimeout(() => { if (joyPressTarget) joyPressTarget.classList.add('joy-pressed'); }, 80);` and clear it (`clearTimeout; joyPressTarget = null`) in pointermove, pointercancel and pointerup. In the pointerup handler only add joy-pop when joy-pressed was actually applied (a fast tap that never reached 80 ms should still get the existing sparkle but skip the pop, or apply both). Optionally skip scaling on wide row targets (offsetWidth > 200). Risk: the existing global pointerup handler removes .joy-pressed from every element; keep that. Do not move `transition: transform` to the base state of every tappable, because Jelly components run their own canvas physics and the repo's own rule warns against broad transitions.

verdicts.location: styles.css:5062-5080 (settings-view / settings-tabs); settings.js:354-433 (renderGameEditor); app.js:7855-7874; styles.css:222-231 (html/body overflow-x:hidden)
verdicts.reasoning: The facts reproduce (v17) at 390x844: document heights games 2214, days 2005, teams 1026, notice 5871, data 914, game editor 2216 (tally) to 2516 (tournament; theirs 2823 with extras open). jelly-tabs and the back button are position:static, so they scroll away. I tested three variants on the Notice tab at scrollY 1500 (v18, v19, v21): sticky on jelly-tabs::part(tabs) (the bar sits inside the component's shadow `.bar` div, so it has no room to stick), sticky on the jelly-tabs host (the host contains all the panels), and a standalone sticky <jelly-segmented> placed before the tabs. All stayed at top -1384. The standalone bar fails because html and body both have overflow-x:hidden, which makes body a scroll container (overflow-y computes to auto) that never scrolls, so sticky has no scrollport. Changing html,body to overflow-x:clip made the standalone bar stick (top 0) with no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 390).
verdicts.refinedFix: For a sticky builder nav: (1) change `html { overflow-x: hidden }` and `body { overflow-x: hidden }` (styles.css:222, 231) to `overflow-x: clip` (same bleed-clipping purpose; Safari 16+, the same floor as vendor/jelly.js's iOS 16.4 requirement), and re-run the 390 px overflow checks; (2) render the five-way switcher as a standalone sticky <jelly-segmented> (opaque background wrapper) above the panels and show/hide the panels yourself, because the bar inside jelly-tabs cannot be made sticky. For the game editor, a sticky bottom action bar for Save/Cancel needs the same overflow fix. History: pushState in openBuilder/openChat plus a popstate handler that closes the takeover is small and self-contained, but applies to chat and game views as well. Store and restore the home scroll offset (see builder-return-joy-rise-replay). Splitting or collapsing the 5.9k px Notice tab is a design decision for the owner.

I could not run a live RTDB or emulator here, so the timing against the real SDK is unverified. The code path (JSON.stringify compare, renderAll on difference) is exact. verdicts.refinedFix: In the members listener: `const next = snap.val() || {}; const changed = JSON.stringify(next) !== JSON.stringify(memberDirectory); memberDirectory = next; memberDirectoryLoaded = true; if (appStarted && changed) { if (editorMidEntry()) { armIdleRetry(); /* or a small pendingRender flag */ } else renderAll(); }`. extraFindings.title: Home day-tab pill springs from the first tab to the active day whenever the tab bar is (re)created on a non-Monday day

extraFindings.evidence: Measured. Same root cause as builder-tabs-pill-respring: vendor/jelly.js jelly-segmented.sync() runs before its jelly-segment children upgrade (value undefined -> index 0), onShape() places the pill at segment 0 with placed=true, and later syncs only move pillTarget. extraFindings.rootCause: jelly-segmented places its pill at index 0 on first shape, before child segments are upgraded; the app creates jelly-tabs with a non-zero active value and never settles the pill.

found.probesRun: All probes are Playwright/Chromium (390x844 mobile emulation unless noted; also 320/360/430/1280 widths, light + dark, viewer + editor), under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/hunt/chat/. Nothing under /home/user/Camp was touched. lib.cjs installs a fake `firebase` (captures chat child_added/child_removed listeners, echoes update() locally, delayed chatPhotos once()) plus authUser/memberDirectory/fbRef, calls the real initChatSync(), and emits fake snapshots in SDK order. Probes: p1_rebuild_anims (getAnimations + MutationObserver per trigger: open, tab switch, bell, directory change, idle renderAll, live msg, live photo); p2_scroll_photos + p14_first_open_photo_gap (gap between scrollTop and bottom over time with real JPEG thumbs; 50-photo channel); p3_tabs (tab strip overflow + scrollLeft after tapping 4th tab at 320/360/390/430); p15_tabs_squash (tab strip height vs message count 3/12/30/50, viewer + editor); p4_scroll_reading (own send while scrolled up, window-slide removal with and without overflow-anchor to emulate Safari, backfill, composer carry across directory/bell/tab switch); p5/p6 (scrollY across open/close, now-banner transition investigated = test mouse hover artifact); p7_hidden_render (state changes while chat open, canvases after close, persisted chatOpen reload); p8_announce_strip (chat announcements into #announcements, by-line before/after directory, composer churn, age-out, layout-shift observer); p9/p9b (toast vs composer, elementFromPoint, real touch tap on send); p10_lightbox (frame-by-frame spinner/img states, anims, open/close race, keydown listener balance); p11_cold_start_open (persisted chatOpen, pre-sync/ready states); p12_skeleton; p13 (50 photo thumbs rebuild cost + blank-frame sampling); p17_send_focus; p18_badge_shift; p19_update_banner_over_composer (showUpdateBanner + tap on input); p20_draft_close; p21/p22 verify proposed fixes by runtime injection (CSS flex-shrink, toaster/banner offset, load-listener re-pin) without editing the repo. Run any with `node <file>`; the app server is http://localhost:8932. Not testable here: real iOS Safari (scroll anchoring, keyboard/dvh behaviour), real Firebase latency.

findings.title: Channel tab strip collapses to a sliver in any busy channel
findings.symptom: Open a channel with more than ~10 messages and the Announcements/General/Memes/Photos pills shrink to clipped slivers (5px tall at 50 messages); once the history is long there is effectively no way to switch channels or see other channels' unread badges. The tabs visibly shrink as messages load.
findings.trigger: Open chat on any channel and let the backlog load (CHAT_WINDOW=50). Or: openChat('general') with 12 / 30 / 50 messages. Worse with photos.
findings.evidence: p15_tabs_squash measured .chat-tabs height at 390px: 3 msgs=31px, 12 msgs=21px, 30 msgs=9px, 50 msgs=5px (pill height 15px, tab strip scrollHeight 15), identical for editor. Screenshot hunt/chat/s_tabs_squash_viewer.png shows only clipped pill tops under the header. #chat-view stays 828px, head 35px, composer 58px; only the tab strip shrinks. Injecting `.chat-head,.chat-tabs,.chat-composer{flex-shrink:0}` keeps tabs at 31px with 50 photo messages (p21_verify_fixes).
findings.rootCause: .chat-view is a fixed-height flex column. .chat-list is `flex:1 1 auto` with a huge content-based flex-basis, and .chat-tabs has `overflow-x:auto`, which gives it an automatic min-height of 0 and the default flex-shrink:1, so it absorbs a share of the overflow proportional to its basis and gets crushed. Head and composer don't shrink only because they are not scroll containers.
findings.proposedFix: Add `flex: 0 0 auto;` to .chat-tabs (and `.chat-head`, `.chat-composer`) so only .chat-list flexes.

findings.title: Chat opens (and new photos land) scrolled well above the newest messages when thumbnails are present
findings.symptom: Opening a channel that has photos leaves the view in the middle of the history, hundreds or thousands of px above the newest messages; the newest photo is cut off or off-screen. A live photo arriving while you are at the bottom lands half hidden under the composer.
findings.trigger: Open Photo Dump (or any channel with thumbnails). Or be at the bottom of a channel when someone posts a photo. Also after a forced rebuild that scrolls to bottom.
findings.evidence: p14: 50-photo channel, right after openChat gap=0 and list scrollHeight=2409; ~15ms later images decode and scrollHeight=11184, gap=2625px (last bubble bottom y=3398 vs list bottom 785). Screenshot s_photos_first_open.png shows photos #35-#37 of 50. p2: 12-msg channel with 4 photos: gap 554px after open; live photo appended at bottom: gap 174px (scrollHeight 1379->1554). Verified fix (p22): attaching a one-shot load listener that re-calls chatScrollToBottom() for incomplete .chat-thumb imgs takes the gap from 2625 to 0.
findings.rootCause: chatScrollToBottom() runs synchronously right after innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML, while the thumbnail s (no width/height attributes) are still 0px tall; they decode asynchronously and push scrollHeight up afterwards, so the 'pinned to bottom' scroll is stale.
findings.proposedFix: In chatScrollToBottom (or right after setting innerHTML/inserting a bubble when pinned), for each `.chat-thumb` with !img.complete add `img.addEventListener('load', () => { list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight; }, {once:true})`, only while the user is still pinned (nearBottom captured before the insert). Optionally also reserve a min-height/aspect-ratio on .chat-thumb-btn.

findings.title: The '← Camp' pill (and tab strip, header, composer) re-create and re-run their entrance animation on every channel switch, bell toggle and directory update
findings.symptom: Each time you tap a channel tab or the bell, the Camp back pill blinks out and slides in again (0.28s) and the whole header/tabs/list/composer DOM is replaced; same when the member directory changes or the open channel finishes loading.
findings.trigger: Tap any channel tab; tap the 🔔/🔕 bell; onMemberDirectoryChanged() (every members-node snapshot, once at startup); backlog-complete flip for the open channel; backfill.
findings.evidence: p1_rebuild_anims: getAnimations() two rAFs after each trigger shows `button#chat-back-btn.back-pill :: back-pill-in` x1 running for: openChat, switch tab (memes), switch back, bell toggle, directory changed, directory snapshot. MutationObserver: each forced rebuild adds div.chat-head, div.chat-tabs, div.chat-list, div.chat-composer and removes the old ones. Idle renderAll and live-message append produce 0 animations. p12: the loading jelly-skeleton node is not reused after a rebuild, so its shimmer restarts. (The extra joy-fly sparkle dots on tab/bell taps are the intended tap sparkles.)
findings.rootCause: renderChatView(true) replaces the entire view via view.innerHTML even when only the active tab, title, bell state or list changed. .back-pill has `animation: back-pill-in .28s both`, so a re-created pill replays it.
findings.location: chat.js:911-972 (renderChatView, forced path), wired from 982 (tab click), 683 (toggleChatSub), 276-279 (onMemberDirectoryChanged), 132-136 (ready flip)
findings.proposedFix: Quick: `.chat-view .back-pill { animation: none; }`. Better: build the shell (head/tabs/composer) once per open and, on tab switch/bell/directory change, only update the active-tab class, title, bell icon, composer placeholder and #chat-list contents (the composer node and its focus then never move).

findings.title: Toasts sit on top of the composer and swallow taps on Send / input / photo
findings.symptom: While someone message arrives in another channel (announcement, mention, belled channel) or any app toast fires, the toast pill covers the text box and the send/photo buttons for 4-5.5 s. Tapping ➤ during that time does nothing (the tap dismisses the toast).
findings.trigger: Be in the chat view (e.g. General) and have a message land in Announcements or mention you; or any showToast such as 'One moment — sending a little too fast.' or the initial 'Following … Foxes' toast. Then tap Send.
findings.evidence: p9: jelly-toaster rect y=766-826 vs send button y=793-835; document.elementFromPoint at send-button centre and at input centre both return `jelly-toaster`. p9b: with 'on my way' typed and the toast showing, a real touchscreen.tap on ➤ -> 0 updates sent and text still in the box; tap after the toast cleared -> 1 update. Screenshots s_toast2_over_composer.png, s_chat_open.png (toast over send button). Verified fix: `body.chat-open jelly-toaster[position="bottom"]{bottom:calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))}` makes elementFromPoint at send/input/photo return the real controls (p21).
findings.rootCause: <jelly-toaster position="bottom"> is fixed to the bottom of the viewport and its .toast pills have pointer-events:auto; the chat composer lives in exactly that strip. Nothing offsets the toaster while body.chat-open.
findings.location: styles.css (add a body.chat-open rule near 4757); index.html:407 <jelly-toaster position="bottom">
findings.proposedFix: Add `body.chat-open jelly-toaster[position="bottom"] { bottom: calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }` (outer-document styles beat the shadow :host rule) — or use position="top" while chat is open.

findings.title: The deploy 'New version available — Refresh' bar covers the composer, and tapping it reloads the page and loses the draft
findings.symptom: After a deploy, the full-width blue Refresh alert sits over the text box and Send button; a tap meant for the input or ➤ triggers a reload and the half-written message is gone. The banner stays up exactly while a message is being typed, because chatComposerBusy() defers the auto-reload.
findings.trigger: Be in chat with a draft in the composer when a new ?v= build is detected (checkForUpdate -> onNewVersion -> showUpdateBanner), then tap the input or Send.
findings.evidence: p19: #update-banner rect y=748-828 vs composer y=785-843; elementFromPoint at input centre and send centre = `jelly-alert#update-banner`; a touchscreen.tap on the input fired the banner's click handler (doReload) once. Screenshot s_update_banner_over_composer.png. Raising it with `body.chat-open .update-banner-alert,body.chat-open .update-banner{bottom:calc(5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))}` restores correct hit targets (p21).
findings.rootCause: .update-banner-alert / .update-banner are fixed at bottom:1rem, z-index 60, and the whole bar has `addEventListener('click', doReload)`. The chat composer occupies the same strip.
findings.proposedFix: Offset both bars while chat is open (rule above), and/or make only the Refresh button (not the whole bar) trigger doReload while chat is open.

findings.title: Tapping the Memes/Photos tab rebuilds the strip so it snaps back to the left and the active tab ends up off-screen
findings.symptom: The four tabs are 514px wide, so on every phone width some of them are clipped (Photos is partly or fully hidden); you swipe the strip to reach Photos, tap it, and the strip jumps back to scrollLeft 0 with the now-active Photos pill off-screen (only the title says which channel you are in).
findings.trigger: On a 320-430px viewport, swipe the tab strip to the right and tap Photos (or Memes).
findings.evidence: p3_tabs: scrollWidth 514 vs clientWidth 288/328/358/398 at viewport 320/360/390/430 (Photos tab right edge 530 > viewport at all four). After scrolling the strip to the end and clicking Photos: scrollLeft 226/186/156/116 -> 0 and a new .chat-tabs node (sameNode false); active pill left/right 417-508 while the viewport is 320-430. Screenshot s_tabs_360_after_photos_tap.png: title says Photo Dump, active pill not visible. (Independent of, and in addition to, the squash bug above.)
findings.rootCause: renderChatView(true) re-creates .chat-tabs, resetting its scroll position; nothing scrolls the active tab into view; the strip is wider than any phone.
findings.proposedFix: After building, set `strip.scrollLeft` so the active tab is centred (compute from offsetLeft; avoid scrollIntoView so the page doesn't scroll) and/or carry the old scrollLeft across a same-view rebuild; consider a 4-column layout (emoji-only labels on narrow screens) so no horizontal scroll is needed.

findings.title: 'Chat needs live sync, which is off on this device.' flashes on the home card (and in an open chat) while sync is still starting
findings.symptom: On every cold start the Chat card on the home page says sync is off, and a device that reloads with the chat takeover persisted open shows that same message as the whole message list until the first backlog completes, then everything pops in. It is false: sync is just not up yet.
findings.trigger: Reload/cold-start the app (hint-painted, before initSync sets fbRef); with state.ui.chatOpen persisted true the chat view shows it too.
findings.evidence: p11_cold_start_open with fbRef null: chat-list text and #chat-card-preview both = 'Chat needs live sync, which is off on this device.'. After startChat (fbRef set, backlog child_added delivered, once() pending) the list still shows that text (no rebuild until once() resolves); card already shows the real preview. After once() resolves the list builds. Real network duration not measured (depends on SDK/auth/member-read time, plausibly 1-3 s).
findings.rootCause: renderChatCard/chatListHTML test `!syncEnabled()` (i.e. fbRef == null) before the 'Loading…'/skeleton branch, but fbRef is only set after approval in initSync; there is no 'sync pending' state, and the open view is only rebuilt when once('value') resolves.
findings.proposedFix: Distinguish 'sync not started yet' from 'sync off for good' (e.g. show 'Loading…'/the skeleton until initChatSync has run or the SDK has definitively failed), and call renderChatView(true) when initChatSync attaches if the view is open.

findings.title: Your own message doesn't scroll into view if you were scrolled up when you sent it
findings.symptom: Reply to something older in the history, press send, and nothing visibly happens: the composer clears but the new bubble is appended far below the visible area.
findings.trigger: Scroll the message list up (more than 80px from the bottom), type, press Send/Enter.
findings.evidence: p4_scroll_reading (a): gap before send 1138px, after 1202px; my new .chat-bubble-mine is not within the list's visible rect (myBubbleVisible=false); input cleared.
findings.rootCause: appendChatBubble only calls chatScrollToBottom() when the list was within 80px of the bottom, with no exception for the sender's own message.
findings.proposedFix: Pass a `force` flag when msg.byKey === identityKey(authUser) (or after sendChatMessage) so own messages always scroll to bottom.

findings.title: Tapping ➤ moves focus to the button, so the on-screen keyboard drops after every message
findings.symptom: After each send the keyboard closes (Android Chrome and anywhere focus leaves the input) and the person has to tap the input again for the next message.
findings.trigger: Type a message, tap the ➤ button (not the keyboard Enter/Go key).
findings.evidence: p17_send_focus: after a real touchscreen.tap on #chat-send-btn, document.activeElement = button#chat-send-btn (input lost focus). iOS keyboard behaviour not testable here.
findings.rootCause: The send handler never returns focus to #chat-input and the button takes focus on tap.
findings.proposedFix: On the send (and photo) button add `pointerdown`/`mousedown` handler with `e.preventDefault()` so the input keeps focus, or call `input.focus()` at the end of sendChatMessage.

findings.title: A half-typed message is thrown away when you leave chat or switch channels
findings.symptom: Type a reply, tap '← Camp' to check standings, come back: the box is empty. Same when you tap another channel tab and return.
findings.trigger: Type text; press ← Camp then reopen the chat card; or tap another channel tab then back.
findings.evidence: p20_draft_close: draft 'a long half-written reply' -> after closeChat()/openChat('general') value = ''; draft 'draft in general' -> after memes tab and back value = ''. (Same-channel rebuilds from directory/bell DO keep text, focus and caret: p4(d).)
findings.rootCause: closeChat()/openChat() null chatViewBuiltFor so the next build has no `carry`; channel switches also start clean; no per-channel draft store.
findings.proposedFix: Keep a `chatDrafts[ch]` map updated on input events and restore it in renderChatView for the target channel.

findings.title: In a full channel, every new message makes the history you are reading jump up (without scroll anchoring)
findings.symptom: When a channel already holds 50 messages, each arriving message first removes the oldest bubble at the top; a reader scrolled up in the middle sees the content shift up by a bubble height each time (~65px in the probe).
findings.trigger: Channel at CHAT_WINDOW (50) messages, user scrolled up, someone posts. In Chromium scroll anchoring hides it; WebKit/iOS Safari lacks overflow-anchor (my belief, not verified on a device).
findings.evidence: p4_scroll_reading (b): with default Chromium anchoring, bubble position unchanged and scrollTop adjusted 1884->1819 (jump 0). With `.chat-list{overflow-anchor:none}` (Safari emulation) the probe bubble moved from y=-17 to y=-82 (-65px) on child_removed of the oldest message, scrollTop unchanged at 1884.
findings.rootCause: removeChatBubble() deletes the oldest bubble from the top of the scroller without compensating scrollTop; relies on browser scroll anchoring.
findings.proposedFix: In removeChatBubble, if the bubble is above the viewport and the reader is not pinned to the bottom, subtract its height (plus gap) from list.scrollTop in the same frame as the removal.

findings.title: Lightbox can show the wrong photo if you close one and open another before the first finishes loading
findings.symptom: Tap photo A (slow load), close, tap photo B: B appears, then A's late response replaces it.
findings.trigger: Open photo A on a slow connection, close it, open photo B before A's once('value') resolves.
findings.evidence: p10 race test (A delay 600ms, B 100ms): width shown when B loaded = 800 (B), after A resolved = 1280 (A's image) while the lightbox for B is open.
findings.rootCause: The once('value') callbacks only check `box.hidden`, not which photoId the box is currently showing; the box element is shared and reopened.
findings.proposedFix: Set `box.dataset.photoId = photoId` on open and in the then/catch handlers return unless it still equals photoId.

findings.title: Closing chat drops you at the top of the home page instead of where the Chat card was
findings.symptom: Scroll the home page down, tap Chat, tap ← Camp: you land at the very top of the page.
findings.trigger: Open chat from the card while scrolled down, then close it (viewer or editor).
findings.evidence: p5: viewer scrollY 228 before open -> 0 while open -> 0 after close (chat card top 379px before, 607px after); editor 334 -> 0 -> 0.
findings.rootCause: body.chat-open display:none's the rest of .main-wrap so the document collapses to the chat view height and the browser clamps scrollY to 0; closeChat() doesn't restore it.
findings.proposedFix: Record `window.scrollY` in openChat and `window.scrollTo(0, saved)` after the renderAll() in closeChat.

findings.title: Chat announcement banner briefly shows the sender's raw email address instead of their name
findings.symptom: A chat announcement on the top banner strip shows 'Oct 26, 11:43pm ET · sam@camp.test' until the member directory arrives, then flips to 'Sam Director'.
findings.trigger: A chat announcement from the last 15 minutes exists while memberDirectory hasn't loaded yet (cold start).
findings.evidence: p8_announce_strip: by-line before directory = 'sam@camp.test'; after memberDirectory loaded + renderAll() = 'Sam Director' (viewer and editor).
findings.rootCause: chatAuthorName() fails closed to identityFromKey(key) when !memberDirectoryLoaded, and chatAnnouncementBanners() uses it directly for the banner by-line.
findings.proposedFix: While !memberDirectoryLoaded return `by: ''` (or hold chat-sourced banners until it loads); the existing renderAll() on directory load re-renders.

findings.title: Each chat announcement (and each 15-min age-out) re-creates the editor composer/chips and shifts the whole page without any transition
findings.symptom: The announcements strip replaces its entire innerHTML on any change, so an editor with the composer open gets the form, TTL chips and Post button re-created every time a chat announcement arrives or expires; every device gets an abrupt full-page jump (banner insertion/removal).
findings.trigger: Editor opens '📣 Post an announcement' and someone posts in the Announcements channel; or any viewer when a chat announcement arrives/ages out.
findings.evidence: p8: editor MutationObserver on #announcements shows `rm form`, `rm div (ttl row)`, `add form.announce-form`, `add div.announce-ttl-row`, `add div.announce-banner` per new announcement (draft text and focus are preserved). layout-shift entries during the sequence: viewer 0.115/0.094/0.216, editor 0.074/0.095/0.083/0.184; age-out collapsed #announcements height 184->0 (viewer) / 277->84 (editor) with no animation. Idle renderAnnouncements() produces 0 churn.
findings.rootCause: renderAnnouncements builds one HTML string (banners + composer) and replaces wrap.innerHTML whenever it differs.
findings.proposedFix: Render banners and composer into separate children and only replace the banner list (setHtmlIfChanged on its own container), leaving the composer nodes alone.

findings.title: An unread badge appearing widens its tab and shifts the other tabs under the finger
findings.symptom: When a message lands in another channel the badge pops in, that tab grows ~22px and every tab to its right jumps.
findings.trigger: Chat open; a message arrives in a different channel.
findings.evidence: p18_badge_shift: tab lefts before [16,173,274,373], widths [152,96,93,90]; after one unread in Memes: Memes width 93->115 and Photos left 373->395. Badge saturates at '50' because CHAT_WINDOW caps the in-memory list (120 emitted).
findings.rootCause: .chat-tab-badge toggles `hidden` (display) inside an auto-width tab.
findings.proposedFix: Reserve badge space (visibility:hidden instead of hidden) or position the badge absolutely on the tab corner.

findings.title: Chat header title is ellipsized on phones ('Announcements & I…')
findings.symptom: With the Camp pill, bell and (for editors) broom button, the channel title is cut off at 390px.
findings.trigger: Open the Announcements channel at 390px (editors have even less room).
findings.evidence: Screenshots s_skeleton_light.png and s_view_mobile-dark-editor.png: title reads '📣 Announcements & I…' / 'Announcements …'; desktop shows the full 'Announcements & Important Info' (s_view_desktop-light.png).
findings.rootCause: .chat-title is `flex:1 1 auto; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap` between three fixed controls; the long label is not shortened.
findings.proposedFix: Use the channel's `short` label (or allow two lines / smaller font) in the header; the active tab already shows the name.

findings.title: Phone Back gesture/button leaves the site instead of closing the chat
findings.symptom: On Android or with an iOS back-swipe, Back while the chat takeover is open navigates away from Camp rather than returning to the home page.
findings.trigger: Open chat, press the system Back.
findings.evidence: Suspected from code only: grep finds no history.pushState/popstate/hashchange anywhere in app.js/chat.js/settings.js; openChat() only flips state.ui.chatOpen.
findings.rootCause: The takeover is in-page state with no history entry.
findings.proposedFix: history.pushState({chat:1}) in openChat and a popstate listener that calls closeChat().

checkedClean: Idle renderAll() with chat open: 0 new animations; only text-node churn in #chat-card-badge, #chat-card-preview and .chat-tab-badge (no visual change, no flicker). renderChatView() non-forced is a no-op as designed.
30 s tick (renderChatCard): badge/preview text only; no attribute toggling, no layout change. Unread badges on the card and tabs do not flicker.
Live message append: exactly one .chat-bubble added, no rebuild, no animation, composer untouched; scrolls only when within 80px of the bottom (apart from the photo-height issue above).

Same-channel forced rebuild (directory change, bell toggle, backfill) preserves composer text, focus and caret, and the reader's scroll position (p4 d: value kept, focused, caret 5; backfill jump 0px).

Rebuilding bubbles with already-decoded thumbnails: no blank frames, no scroll jump in Chromium (50 photo bubbles, thumbs complete on frame 0); rebuild cost 22-36 ms for 50 photo bubbles, openChat() incl. full renderAll 36 ms.
Home components created/updated while the chat takeover hid them (display:none) look correct after closing chat (screenshot comparison; no blank Jelly canvases).
Lightbox: spinner->image swap has no blank frame (spinner x10 frames then img-ready), no animations beyond tap sparkles; keydown listener leak is only 1 handler after a double-open (negligible).
Announcements strip: idle renderAnnouncements() is a no-op (no churn); editor's half-typed draft and focus are preserved across a rebuild; chat banners age out at 15 min.
Page does not double-scroll while chat is open (document scrollHeight == innerHeight == 844); composer pinned at the bottom of the chat view.
back-pill-in respects reduced-motion; the now-banner border/box-shadow transitions seen on close in p5 were a hover artifact of the test mouse position (not reproduced with no pointer, p6).
Day separators and removeChatBubble() separator cleanup behave correctly in tests; own-message echo is deduped and not counted as unread.
After v183 the idle-renderAll conclusion for plain-text nodes holds for the chat card (no animation attached to those nodes).

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran my own probe (hunt/chat-verify/v1_tabs.cjs, real initChatSync via the fake-firebase lib, real styles.css). .chat-tabs height: 3 msgs=31px, 20 msgs=12-13px, 50 msgs=5px at 320/390/430 wide; 6px at 1280x800 desktop. #chat-view stays 828px, head 35, composer 58 — only the strip shrinks (the strip is overflow-x:auto so its automatic min-height is 0, flex-shrink 1, and .chat-list's content-sized flex-basis soaks up the overflow). Injecting `.chat-tabs{flex:0 0 auto}` gave tabs 31 / list 688 / view 828 at every width and message count. Screenshot confirms only clipped pill tops under the header. Root cause as stated is right. (Senior camp not re-tested: my fake emitter hardcodes the junior root, so that run was empty, not a refutation.)
verdicts.refinedFix: One line in styles.css: add `flex: 0 0 auto;` to `.chat-tabs` (the strip must not be a flex-shrink participant). Equivalent alternative: `.chat-list { flex: 1 1 0; }` so its basis is 0 and nothing overflows. `.chat-head` and `.chat-composer` do not need it (they are not scroll containers, so min-height:auto already protects them). No JS/listener/state risk. Verified at 320/390/430 with 3/20/50 messages.

verdicts.location: chat.js:1023 chatScrollToBottom (called from renderChatView :971 and appendChatBubble :1043)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran their p2/p14 and my own v2_photo_gap.cjs (20 photo thumbs, real JPEG data URLs): gap is 0 synchronously after openChat, then 3291px once the thumbs decode (their 50-photo case: 2625px, last bubble at y=3398 vs list bottom 785). A live photo arriving while pinned grows the gap afterwards too (their p2: 174px; first open of a 4-photo channel: 554px). The tab-away/back case is gap 0 because decoded images are cached, so it is a first-decode problem: has no width/height so it is 0px tall until decoded. Applying a one-shot load listener that re-pins fixed it in my probe (open: 3291 -> 0, live photo: 0). Photos can be sent in any channel, so Photos and Memes both hit this. Not testable here: WebKit's treatment of loading=lazy on data: URLs / no scroll anchoring on iOS (could be worse there).
verdicts.refinedFix: Inside chatScrollToBottom(), after `list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight`, do: `list.querySelectorAll('.chat-thumb').forEach((img) => { if (!img.complete) { const pin = () => { list.scrollTop = list.scrollHeight; }; img.addEventListener('load', pin, { once: true }); img.addEventListener('error', pin, { once: true }); } });`. Because every pin path (open, rebuild-to-bottom, appendChatBubble when nearBottom) already funnels through chatScrollToBottom, this is the only change needed. Risks: (1) a reader who starts scrolling up while the thumbs are still decoding gets snapped back down - guard with a flag set false by one-time `touchstart`/`wheel` listeners on the list (set it true again in chatScrollToBottom); (2) duplicate once-listeners on repeated calls are harmless. The keepScroll (scrolled-up) rebuild path must NOT pin, which is already the case since it does not call chatScrollToBottom. Optional belt-and-braces: reserve space with `.chat-thumb-btn{min-height:...}` but portrait thumbs make that imperfect.

verdicts.location: chat.js:911-972 renderChatView forced path; styles.css:1441 (.back-pill animation); callers chat.js:982, 683, 276-279, 132-136

extraFindings.title: On a 390px phone the Photos tab is entirely off-screen (0px visible) with no scroll cue
extraFindings.symptom: The Photo Dump tab cannot be seen at all on a standard 390px phone, and Memes is clipped; the strip scrolls sideways but its scrollbar is hidden and nothing hints at it. When Photos is the open channel, the active tab is invisible and only the header title says where you are.
extraFindings.trigger: Open chat at 390px (and similarly 320-430) - no taps needed. Worst when the last/persisted channel is Photos.
extraFindings.evidence: Measured (hunt/chat-verify/v15_tabfix.cjs, no squash): openChat('photos') at 390 -> tab visibility: Announcements 152/152px, General 118/118, Memes 77/93, Photos 0/90 px visible (ACTIVE). Strip scrollWidth 447 vs clientWidth 358 (320: 288, 360: 328, 430: 398); tabs end at x463, so even 430 clips Photos by ~33px. It only fits at >= ~480px. Centering the active tab via scrollLeft (+= (ar.left-sr.left)-(sr.width-ar.width)/2) brings it to x284-374 fully visible.
extraFindings.rootCause: Four fixed-padding pills (0.4rem 0.7rem, 0.82rem font, full short labels + emoji + badge slot) total ~447px, wider than any phone's usable width, in a horizontally scrolling strip with scrollbar-width:none and no edge fade or snap; the active tab is never scrolled into view.
extraFindings.proposedFix: Make the strip fit without scrolling: `.chat-tab{flex:1 1 0; min-width:0; padding:0.4rem 0.4rem; justify-content:center}` and hide the text label under ~480px (`@media (max-width:480px){.chat-tab-label{display:none}}` after wrapping the short name in a span; emoji + badge are enough since the header names the channel), or keep scrolling but add `scroll-snap-type:x proximity` + a right-edge fade and always centre the active tab after each build (see chat-tabs-scroll-reset fix). Combine with `flex:0 0 auto` on .chat-tabs (chat-tabs-squashed) and an absolute-corner badge (chat-tab-badge-shift).

extraFindings.title: Same-channel forced rebuilds re-create the input and refocus it outside a user gesture (iOS keyboard likely drops)
extraFindings.symptom: If the member directory updates (an editor renames/changes someone), a window backfill happens, or the open channel's ready flip lands while a person is typing, the composer text and caret are restored but on iOS the soft keyboard probably closes and has to be re-opened with a tap.
extraFindings.trigger: Typing in the composer on an iPhone while onMemberDirectoryChanged() / backfill / chatReady flip calls renderChatView(true) for the same channel.
extraFindings.evidence: Suspected from code only (not measured; iOS not testable here). renderChatView(true) replaces view.innerHTML (the focused input is detached), then calls input.focus() from a Promise/snapshot callback, which iOS Safari does not honour for opening the keyboard. Chromium keeps focus and caret (my v7 draft test: directory/bell rebuilds keep value). The CLAUDE.md/code comments claim the keyboard is carried across.
extraFindings.rootCause: Rebuild via innerHTML instead of updating head/tabs/list in place; programmatic focus() without a gesture.
extraFindings.proposedFix: For same-channel rebuilds (sameCh true), replace only #chat-list's innerHTML (and refresh the title/bell/tab classes) and leave .chat-composer's nodes untouched so focus never moves; reserve the full innerHTML rebuild for first open and channel switch. Because the composer node is kept only within the same channel, the closures over `ch` in wireChatView stay correct.

findings.title: Every open paints a half-built shell, then the real content pops in above it (CLS 0.43)
findings.symptom: For roughly 0.2 s on a fast phone and 0.75-0.85 s at 4x CPU, the page shows only five floating card headers (Competitions, Current Standings, ...) at the top of an empty page. Then the follow card, Happening-now banner, chat card and day tabs all appear at once above them and shove the cards down about 620 px.
findings.trigger: Open index.html with campScoreboardAuthHint set to viewer or editor (a returning device), warm cache, Firebase blocked. `node p3_return.cjs viewer 1` and `node p3_return.cjs viewer 4`; cold cache: `node p1_boot.cjs fast`.
findings.evidence: Layout-shift entry 'jelly-accordion.home-accordion 46->670 h350->174' = 0.433 on every one of 3 reloads at both 1x and 4x CPU (cold cache: 46->556, 0.4308). First paint at 44-148 ms; first content frame at 201-237 ms (1x) and 740-841 ms (4x CPU). Frame log: html class '' with 35 undefined elements and page height 844, then 'view-only' with 0 undefined and height 1072. p26_dcl.cjs: delaying vendor/jelly.js by 1500 ms moved DOMContentLoaded 236 -> 1576 ms and first content 538 -> 1777 ms while first paint stayed at 56 ms.
findings.rootCause: boot() is bound to DOMContentLoaded, and that event cannot fire until the deferred module vendor/jelly.js (320 KB) has downloaded and evaluated. In the meantime styles.css deliberately paints the pre-upgrade accordion as a stack of headers, and every section above it is hidden or empty until init() runs. The boot-guard comment says approved devices 'paint the app immediately', but the module gate delays the real paint.
findings.location: app.js:8735 (document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', boot)); styles.css:573-590 (jelly-accordion/collapsible :not(:defined) shell rules); boot-guard.js (no hold-back class)
findings.proposedFix: Do not paint the shell. Have boot-guard.js add html.booting when a hint exists, add `html.booting #app { visibility: hidden }`, and remove the class at the end of startApp() after the first renderAll (plus a 4 s safety timeout). Alternative: stop gating boot on the module by running boot() as soon as the classic scripts finish (readyState check) and letting Jelly upgrade late, which needs typeof-guards on jelly method calls. At minimum drop the pre-upgrade accordion header stack so nothing paints until content exists.

findings.title: Users who override the OS theme get a flash of the wrong theme on every load
findings.symptom: If Appearance is set explicitly to Dark while the phone is in light mode, every open starts with a light-gray shell for 0.2-0.9 s and then flips to dark. The reverse (Light chosen while the phone is dark) flashes a dark shell first. Auto users are unaffected.
findings.trigger: Set Appearance to Dark with OS light (or Light with OS dark), then reload. `node p4_themeboot.cjs`; `node p30_wrongtheme_cpu.cjs` for the CPU-throttled timing.
findings.evidence: OS light + theme dark: body background is rgb(244,246,249) from 25 ms until 238 ms, then body.dark-theme + data-jelly-mode=dark appear. With 4x CPU the dark class lands at 863 ms. OS dark + theme light: rgb(16,20,28) until about 225 ms, then light-theme. Auto matches the OS from the first frame.
findings.rootCause: The chosen theme lives only inside the big state JSON (state.theme in campScoreboardV2). applyTheme() runs from boot(), which waits for DOMContentLoaded and therefore for jelly.js (see boot-shell-popin). boot-guard.js, the only pre-paint script, never reads the theme, and styles.css can only pre-paint the OS scheme through its prefers-color-scheme media block.
findings.location: boot-guard.js (add a pre-paint theme read); app.js:7233 applyTheme / saveState (mirror the choice); styles.css:50 and :77 token blocks
findings.proposedFix: Mirror the choice into a tiny key (for example localStorage.campScoreboardTheme = 'light'|'dark'), written from applyTheme. In boot-guard.js read it and set document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-jelly-mode', t). Add `:root[data-jelly-mode="dark"] body` / `[data-jelly-mode="light"] body` to the token blocks in styles.css so the pre-module shell paints in the right palette. Holding the shell back (boot-shell-popin fix) also hides most of it.

findings.title: Theme Auto + phone flips dark->light while Camp is open: podium rows and gold text stay dark and become unreadable
findings.symptom: After the OS switches from dark to light with the tab still open, the Current Standings podium rows keep their dark-tinted gold/silver/bronze backgrounds while the text turns dark. Team names in the top three rows become near-illegible. The status-bar colour also stays dark.
findings.trigger: Appearance = Auto, OS dark at load, then flip the OS to light without reloading. `node p8_osflip.cjs`, `node p9_osflip_shots.cjs` (sheet_p9.png shows flipped vs fresh-boot).
findings.evidence: After the flip: body.className is still 'dark-theme', computed color-scheme is 'dark', --color-on-primary #181b1d, --color-gold #e8c15a, --color-danger-text #ff8a8a, --shadow-card dark, #dynamic-theme-color #181b1d. A fresh light boot has no class, #fff, #96690a and so on. Light->dark works fine because the media block handles it. No matchMedia change listener exists in app.js.
findings.rootCause: applyTheme() adds body.dark-theme in Auto mode when the OS is dark at that moment (`dark = state.theme === 'dark' || (state.theme === null && prefersDark)`). It only runs at boot and in setTheme, never on an OS change. body.dark-theme outranks the media block, so the non-Jelly tokens (gold/silver/bronze backgrounds, on-primary, shadows) stay dark while Jelly's own tokens follow the OS to light.
