Nothing in JS reads the class; it is used only by the two CSS blocks.
findings.proposedFix: Only set the class for an explicit choice: `document.body.classList.toggle('dark-theme', state.theme === 'dark')`. Auto is already handled by the `body:not(.light-theme):not(.dark-theme)` media block. Also add `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener('change', applyTheme)` so the theme-color meta tracks the OS.

findings.title: Theme flip: card surfaces change instantly but inherited text fades over 0.2 s, so text blinks out for about 100 ms
findings.symptom: On a Light<->Dark switch (Settings, or an OS flip in Auto) the cards snap to the new colour in one frame while most body text is still the old colour. White text on a white card, or dark on dark, then fades in. Card titles, names and lists visibly vanish for about 0.1 s and the page background fades behind them. Jelly chips and buttons then ease over about 0.55 s.
findings.trigger: Home screen with cards open, call setTheme('dark') or tap Dark in the Appearance control. `node p7_themeshot.cjs` freezes the body transition at 40 ms (sheet_p7_flip.png). `node p5_themeflip.cjs`, `node p6_themecontrast.cjs` for numbers.
findings.evidence: At 17 ms the card is already oklch(0.2514 ...) while body color is still oklab(0.26 ...) and body background oklab(1 0 0); the body color transition finishes at about 280 ms. At the 40 ms freeze, inherited text is oklab L 0.47 on a dark card (about 2.3:1; 1:1 in the first frames), and the screenshot shows near-invisible 'Elective 1', 'Swimming', and names. Transitions running at frame 3: body color and background-color 200 ms, plus now-banner border/box-shadow, game-card.done borders and verse-day-chip color (150 ms). Jelly canvas settle: chip 561 ms, button 535-611 ms, switch about 535 ms. The Settings drawer flips in one frame with no dip.
findings.rootCause: `body { transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease }` animates the root text colour and page background, but surfaces, tokens and explicit colours flip instantly because the --jelly-*/--color-* variables change in one style recalc. Anything that inherits colour from body is mid-fade against an already-flipped background.
findings.location: styles.css:225-231 (body transition); also the 150 ms border/box-shadow/color transitions on .game-card, .now-banner and .verse-day-chip
findings.proposedFix: Remove the transition from body, or suppress transitions for the flip frame: in applyTheme add `document.documentElement.classList.add('theme-switching')` with `.theme-switching *, .theme-switching *::before, .theme-switching *::after { transition: none !important }`, then remove the class two animation frames later. Jelly canvases may keep their own easing.

findings.title: A slow (not failed) jelly.js load trips the 4 s 'jelly-failed' fallback: raw card bodies and editor-only rows flash, then collapse again
findings.symptom: On a slow connection, after 4 s the page suddenly expands all five cards into unstyled content, including the editors' 'Hide from viewers' rows even for viewers. When jelly.js finally arrives everything re-collapses and re-lays out (two big jumps).
findings.trigger: Delay vendor/jelly.js by 5 s: `node p2_slowshots.cjs 5000 1`. Also reproduced with 1.6 Mbps + 4x CPU on the uncompressed local server: `node p1_boot.cjs slow`.
findings.evidence: html.jelly-failed appears at about 4.0 s, page height 844 -> 1070; at about 5.5 s jelly arrives (cls 'view-only', height 958, picker open). Two layout shifts: 0.5733 (accordion 46->70, h350->774) and 0.4976 (70->556, h774->288), total 1.07. Screenshots in sheet_p2_boot_slow.png show 'Hide from viewers' rows before the view-only class exists. Real GitHub Pages gzip is about 540 KB for all scripts including the Firebase SDK, so it takes roughly <1 Mbps effective to reach 4 s; the guard's own comment names congested camp wifi right after a deploy as the likely case.
findings.rootCause: boot-guard.js starts a 4000 ms timer at head-parse, but a type=module script only executes after the whole document and all parser-blocking body scripts (3 Firebase SDKs, app.js, settings.js, chat.js, push.js ...) have loaded and run. On a slow link the module is therefore late through no fault of its own. The real failure signals (script error event, window error with jelly.js filename) already cover request and parse failures, so the timer only guards a hang. view-only is also not applied until boot() runs, which is why editor rows show.
findings.proposedFix: Raise the backstop to about 15-20 s (or arm it only after window 'load'), since failures are caught immediately by the error listeners. Optionally keep html.view-only decisions out of the fallback by applying the hint role class in boot-guard.js pre-paint.

findings.title: The Google Fonts stylesheet is render-blocking: a stalled fonts.googleapis.com leaves a blank white page
findings.symptom: On a network where fonts.googleapis.com is slow or hangs (filtered or captive wifi), nothing paints, not even the lock screen, until that request resolves or times out.
findings.trigger: Delay the fonts.googleapis.com request 3 s: `node p20_fontblock.cjs`.
findings.evidence: first-paint and first-contentful-paint at 68 ms with no delay, and at 3040 ms with a 3000 ms delay. The font swap itself is harmless (see checkedClean).
findings.rootCause: `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">` in <head> is a render-blocking stylesheet. display=swap only affects the font files, not the CSS fetch.
findings.proposedFix: Load the font CSS without blocking paint: inject the <link> from boot-guard.js (CSP forbids inline onload handlers) or use rel=preload as=style plus a script-applied swap. Alternatively self-host an Inter subset under font-src 'self'.

findings.title: current-standings.html cold load flashes white -> near-black 'Checking sign-in...' -> white before the intro
findings.symptom: On the TV/presenter machine every load (and every auto-reload after a TV_BUILD bump) goes: white page with 'Loading standings...', then a full-screen 96% black overlay saying 'Camp - Current Standings / Checking sign-in...', then back to white, then the intro.
findings.trigger: Open current-standings.html on a machine that is already signed in. Reproduced with a stubbed Firebase (SRI removed, auth resolves after 450 ms): `node p25_tvsignin.cjs` (sheet_p25_tv.png).
findings.evidence: Timeline of [overlay, loading, screen.hidden]: 7 ms [none, flex, true]; 521 ms [flex, flex, true] (black overlay); 1117 ms [none, flex, true]; 1368 ms [none, none, false] (intro). The black overlay stays up for about 600 ms with the stub timings; with the real SDK it lasts as long as auth restore plus the member read. Stub timings are artificial but the order is deterministic.
findings.rootCause: startData() calls setAuthOverlay('checking') synchronously before auth has answered, and the overlay is rgba(6,8,12,0.96) on a white page. For an already-approved machine that state is a hard cut with no transition.
findings.proposedFix: Show the overlay only for the 'signin' and 'denied' modes, or delay 'checking' by about 1.5 s so a quick approval never shows it. Use the existing 'Loading standings...' state for the check.

findings.title: Zero-clock 'alarm-flash' (infinite background strobe) is not covered by prefers-reduced-motion
findings.symptom: When a game clock reaches 0:00 the clock box flashes between its background and a red tint twice a second, forever, on every device that has that game open, even with reduce-motion on. The other zero-clock effect (pulsing digits) is correctly disabled.
findings.trigger: Emulate reduced motion, open a clock game (for example counselor-hide-seek) with remaining 0. `node p12_alarm.cjs`.
findings.evidence: reduce=true still runs '#clock-area div.tool-box.game-clock-box :: alarm-flash iter=Infinity dur=500'; reduce=false also runs board-zero-pulse, which is gone under reduce. Of all @keyframes in styles.css only alarm-flash lacks a guard (lock-shake is also unguarded but dead: no JS adds .shake).
findings.rootCause: The reduce block at styles.css:5751 lists the board clock classes but not .tool-box.alarming; the rule at :2813 has no media guard.
findings.proposedFix: Add `.tool-box.alarming { animation: none; }` to a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block (keep the border-color change as the static cue). Optionally delete the dead .lock-box.shake rule.

findings.title: Opening a game still smooth-scrolls under prefers-reduced-motion
findings.symptom: With reduce-motion on, tapping a game card (or a Live-now card) still performs the animated eased scroll to the game view.
findings.trigger: Emulate reduced motion, expand Competitions, tap a game card. `node p11_reduced2.cjs`.
findings.evidence: scrollY samples across frames: reduce=false 17 distinct values (0,0,2,10,27,56,105,190 ...) ending at 759; reduce=true 28 distinct values with the same curve (0,0,2,11,27,58,113,206 ...). Explicit behavior:'smooth' is not suppressed by the media query.
findings.rootCause: Two scrollIntoView calls hard-code behavior:'smooth' with no reduced-motion check, unlike celebrate() and joyBurst().
findings.proposedFix: Use `behavior: JOY_REDUCED.matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth'` (JOY_REDUCED is already defined at app.js:8005, so hoist it or re-query matchMedia).

findings.title: jelly-progress still animates value changes under reduced motion (vendor)
findings.symptom: The Happening-now progress bar still sweeps smoothly to its new value when reduce-motion is on, while the switch, segmented control, drawers, tabs and collapsibles are instant.
findings.trigger: Emulate reduced motion and change a jelly-progress value attribute. `node p13_jellyreduce.cjs`.
findings.evidence: Canvas changed on 33 frames (reduce) vs 41 (no preference) for one value change; jelly-switch 0 vs 38, jelly-segmented 0 vs 32, drawer open 1 vs 15 distinct positions.
findings.rootCause: vendor/jelly.js progress component does not consult its F() reduced-motion helper (the helper is used by drawer, dialog, tabs, switch and others).
findings.proposedFix: Vendor patch: snap the displayed value when F() is true. Treating a progress fill as essential motion is also defensible, so this is cosmetic.

findings.title: current-standings.html ignores prefers-reduced-motion for everything except the tie 'fight'
findings.symptom: With reduce-motion on, the TV page still runs the infinite shield bobbing, 'Press to begin' pulse, hero/row pop-ins and the emoji confetti cannons.
findings.trigger: Emulate reduced motion, open current-standings.html?demo=1, press right arrow. `node p29_tv_reduce.cjs`.
findings.evidence: reduce=true shows the same running set as reduce=false: img bob [infinite] x6, p.intro-go pulse [infinite], floatIn, popIn; hero shield bob [infinite]; confetti canvas pixels drawn (102 and 804 sampled vs 88 and 793). The only guard is the .hero.fight block at line 218.
findings.rootCause: Only one @media (prefers-reduced-motion) rule exists and cannon() has no reduced-motion check. This is a presenter spectacle page, so it may be intentional.
findings.proposedFix: Add a reduce block disabling bob/pulse/rowPop/heroIn and an early return in cannon() when matchMedia reduce matches; keep it a static reveal.

findings.title: jelly-failed fallback: Settings/picker sheets can only be closed with the Escape key, and the Appearance control is inert
findings.symptom: On a phone where jelly.js cannot load (iOS < 16.4 is the documented case), opening Settings shows a plain bottom sheet with no close button or backdrop. Tapping outside does nothing, and the Light/Auto/Dark control is plain text that does nothing when tapped.
findings.trigger: Block vendor/jelly.js and call openSettings(): `node p15_failed_settings.cjs`.
findings.evidence: Sheet open at top 213 px, height 631; no close/aria-label button in it; after tapping outside open is still true; clicking the 'dark' segment left state.theme null. Screenshot p15_failed_settings.png (the identity picker stacked on top is from the test sequence). The jelly-failed path otherwise works: no page errors, lock screen and Google button visible, both for a request abort and a parse error.
findings.rootCause: The pre-upgrade jelly-drawer/jelly-dialog fallback CSS has no dismiss affordance, and wireSettings() only adds an Escape keydown handler, which touch phones have no key for.
findings.proposedFix: In the :not(:defined)[open] fallback add a visible close affordance (for example a ::before 'Close' bar) and have the same degraded-mode handler close on a tap of the sheet's top bar or outside. Optionally render native <select> or radios for Appearance when jelly-failed.

findings.title: TV reveal: every dock rebuilds the whole board, so already-docked rows replay their entry animation
findings.symptom: When a team docks into the standings table (auto-dock after 8 s, or the back step), all rows pop in again together instead of only the new row. At the final dock the table briefly re-pops.
findings.trigger: current-standings.html?demo=1, press right arrow, wait 8 s for the auto-dock. `node p16_tv.cjs`, `node p17_tv_autodock.cjs`.
findings.evidence: After each advance, rows == rowPop animations running (1/1, 2/2, 3/3, 5/5, 6/6). At the auto-dock the board fades 0->1 over about 450 ms with both rows at the same rowPop time (popT [33,33] ... [433,433]). On 'back from done' 5 rows replay while the board is at opacity 0.94 and about to drop away. Mostly masked because the board is dropped/transparent during hero spotlights.
findings.rootCause: renderBoardRows() replaces boardEl.innerHTML with all docked rows, and every .row carries `animation: rowPop 0.45s` on creation.
findings.proposedFix: Keep existing row nodes and append or insert only the new row(s), or add the rowPop class only to rows not previously rendered (track a rendered count). Rebuild with animation:none for back().

findings.title: Light and dark boots both fade the page background when Jelly's tokens land
findings.symptom: At load the page background is #f4f6f9 (light) or #10141c (dark) and then fades to Jelly's #ffffff / #181b1d a moment later, in the same window as the content pop-in. In light mode cards (white) go from sitting on gray to sitting on pure white.
findings.trigger: Reload in either OS scheme with Auto. `node p4_themeboot.cjs` (rows for OS=light/auto and OS=dark/auto).
findings.evidence: OS light auto: rgb(244,246,249) at 37 ms -> oklch(1 0 0) at 354 ms via an oklab fade. OS dark auto: rgb(16,20,28) at 35 ms -> oklch(0.2198 0.006 236.84) by 321 ms; card surfaces keep the same value.
findings.rootCause: The var() fallbacks in styles.css (#f4f6f9, #10141c) differ from Jelly's injected token values, and `body { transition: background 0.2s }` turns the swap into a visible fade.
findings.proposedFix: Align the fallbacks with Jelly's actual defaults (#ffffff / #181b1d) and drop the body transition (see theme-flip-text-dip).

checkedClean: Font swap magnitude: laying out the populated home in stand-in fonts (Liberation, DejaVu, Noto) vs Inter changes total page height by only -9 to +20 px on a 1700 px page and the now-banner by 1 px, so a webfont swap is negligible.
Lock screen (signed out, Firebase blocked): CLS 0.022 (the lock box recentres from h78 to h239); themed at boot in both schemes; Google button visible.

jelly-failed fallback path: the class is set immediately on a request abort and on a parse error; the app boots without page errors; viewer sees no editor-only rows; all cards expand; the lock screen offers the Google button. (Closing sheets is a finding above.)
Off-screen Jelly canvases (switch, button, chip) already hold the new theme colours when scrolled into view after a flip, so there is no frame in old colours.
Settings drawer in the real control path (click the Dark segment): sheet and label colours flip in one frame, with no old-colour frame; Jelly canvas controls ease over about 0.55 s by design.

Explicit theme choices set html/body color-scheme and the theme-color meta correctly in all OS x theme combinations; Auto with OS light->dark flipping while open works (only the dark->light direction is broken).

prefers-reduced-motion, CSS: every @keyframes in styles.css is guarded (live-pulse, sched-*, back-pill-in, points-pulse, toast-in/out, score-pop, board-cannon, board-zero-pulse, clock-min-pulse, clock-heartbeat, board-glow), the joy layer is wrapped in no-preference and joyBurst/celebrate check matchMedia, except alarm-flash (finding) and the dead lock-shake. A runtime battery (open each card, switch day tab, schedule overlay, chat, joyBurst) shows 0 running CSS animations under reduce vs 2-6 each with no preference; only the 150-200 ms colour transitions of a theme flip remain.
Jelly components respect reduce for drawers (1 vs 15 positions), switch (0 vs 38 changed frames), segmented (0 vs 32), tabs/dialog/collapsible CSS. Only jelly-progress does not (finding).
Micro press transforms (0.05-0.15 s scale 0.95-0.99 on counter, reorder and delete buttons, .game-card, back-pill) are not reduced-motion guarded but are immaterial.
No `transition: all` remains in styles.css, current-standings.html or stalling.html; the only will-change is on joy particles.

stalling.html: reduced-motion block is complete (0 running animations in both stages under reduce vs keyBreathe plus 16 dust, and floatJunk plus spin plus wobble normally); load CLS 0.0009; no re-render loops (stages are built once).

current-standings.html data path: after the first snapshot ingest() only updates liveGroups, so the table is frozen at reveal start by design and there is no polling rebuild or bar refill; checkForUpdate fetches only its own HTML every 90 s and auto-reloads only on the intro screen, otherwise shows a chip. Board rebuilds are masked by the dropped board in the mid-reveal docks (only auto-dock and back show them).

Team and identity picker on a fresh install opens in the same frame as the content, with no extra layout shift; the CLS entries during boot are only the accordion shift in boot-shell-popin and a 0.0019 follow-card entry.
Lock-screen to app handoff (no hint) is a hard cut with no flash of the app.
Standings-table last column (the cleanup sponge) is clipped inside .table-scroll in all modes; this is a home-layout item, not boot/theme, so it is only noted here.

verdicts.location: styles.css:573-590 (jelly-accordion/jelly-collapsible :not(:defined) shell rules); root cause is app.js:8735 DOMContentLoaded gating behind the deferred vendor/jelly.js module
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with my own sampler (hunt/boot-theme-pages-verify/v1_boot.cjs), warm-cache reloads, viewer: first paint 56-72 ms, DCL 121-146 ms, then CLS 0.4308 on every reload ('jelly-accordion 46->556 h350->288'). Html class goes '' (35 undefined elements, scrollHeight 844) to 'view-only' (0 undefined, 958) at ~220-290 ms. At 4x CPU: first paint 144-184 ms, content at ~955-1127 ms (viewer) and ~1.8-2.0 s (editor), same 0.431 CLS. A CDP screencast (v1b_screencast.cjs, 4x CPU) shows the actual composited frames: frame 1 at +169 ms is five floating card headers (Competitions, Current Standings, Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse, Quick Points) on an otherwise empty gray page; frame 2 at +1160 ms is the full page (follow card, Happening-now, Chat card) shoved in above them. Root cause is right: DOMContentLoaded cannot fire until the deferred module has run (jelly.js delayed 5 s moved view-only from ~0.2 s to 5.3 s in v5_backstop.cjs). In this harness Firebase is aborted instantly; with the real SDK (three parser-blocking scripts from gstatic) DCL is later still, so the shell window is at least as long in production. Editors see it longer than viewers (~320 ms vs ~190 ms at 1x). v183 did not touch this.
verdicts.refinedFix: Smallest correct fix is CSS-only and I verified it by patching styles.css in flight: restrict the pre-upgrade header-stack shell to the failed-module case, so on a normal load the global :where(html:not(.jelly-failed)) :not(:defined){visibility:hidden} (styles.css:145) keeps it invisible while layout space is preserved. e.g. change the selectors at styles.css:573 and :579 to `html.jelly-failed jelly-accordion:not(:defined)` and `html.jelly-failed jelly-collapsible:not(:defined)` (keep their declarations), leave the :where() body-hide rule at ~:590 as is. Measured result (v1c_fixtest.cjs, variant B, 4x CPU): CLS 0.431 -> 0.002; the pre-module frame is a blank page background, then everything appears at once. With the jelly.js request aborted the fallback still shows the cards (v1d_failedcheck.cjs: accordion visibility visible, class jelly-failed). Equivalent alternative: html.booting + `#app{visibility:hidden}` set in boot-guard.js and cleared at the end of startApp(), but that needs a safety timeout so a boot() exception cannot leave a blank page; the CSS route needs none. Risks/notes: (1) it trades a half-built shell for a blank gray frame for the pre-DCL window, a deliberate reversal of the 'no blank screen' comment at styles.css:567-572 (update that comment); (2) tests/shell.test.js pins the :where() wrappers and the body-hide gating but not these header rules, so it should still pass, run node tests/run.js shell to confirm; (3) combine with the wrong-theme and bg-fade fixes so the blank frame is in the right colour; (4) no JS, no listener or state-object implications. Not recommended: running boot() before the module (needs typeof-guards on every Jelly call).

verdicts.location: boot-guard.js (no theme read); app.js:7233 applyTheme / app.js:7270 setTheme; styles.css:50 body.dark-theme and :77 media block
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v2_wrongtheme.cjs, warm reloads, theme persisted via setTheme). OS light + stored dark: body background rgb(244,246,249) from 61 ms until ~252 ms, then body.dark-theme + data-jelly-mode=dark appear and the bg fades to oklch(0.2198...) by ~345 ms. OS dark + stored light: rgb(16,20,28) until ~247 ms, then light-theme and a fade to white. At 4x CPU the light shell holds from 118 ms to 958 ms before the dark flip (1066 ms settled). The screencast frame (v2_light_dark_cpu4_f1.png) shows the bright shell on a user who chose Dark. Auto users get the OS palette from frame 1 (OS dark/auto: rgb(16,20,28) from 42 ms), so they are unaffected. Root cause is right: the choice lives only in state.theme inside the big state JSON and applyTheme() runs from boot() after DCL; boot-guard never reads it. Population is limited to people whose explicit choice differs from the OS (hence med, not high), but for them it is a full-screen colour inversion on every open, harshest as a bright flash on a dark-mode phone.
verdicts.refinedFix: Mirror the choice and apply it pre-paint. (1) app.js applyTheme(): after the data-jelly-mode block, `try { if (state.theme === 'dark' || state.theme === 'light') localStorage.setItem('campScoreboardTheme', state.theme); else localStorage.removeItem('campScoreboardTheme'); } catch (e) {}`. (2) boot-guard.js, in the first IIFE next to the hint read: `var t = localStorage.getItem('campScoreboardTheme'); if (t === 'dark' || t === 'light') document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-jelly-mode', t);`. (3) styles.css: extend the dark token block selector to `body.dark-theme, :root[data-jelly-mode="dark"] body {` (:50) and scope the OS media block to `:root:not([data-jelly-mode]) body:not(.light-theme):not(.dark-theme) {` (:77) so OS-dark + explicit-light does not paint dark first. Verified in flight (v2b_fixtest.cjs, boot-guard + css patched, key pre-seeded): OS light + stored dark now paints rgb(16,20,28) from the first frame, OS dark + stored light paints rgb(244,246,249), at 1x and 4x. Risks: the new key must be added to clearLocalData's wipe list (app.js ~8661-8665) or theme survives sign-out, contradicting CLAUDE.md, and tests/auth.test.js pins that wipe list so update it; the key is device-wide while state.theme is per-camp, so a dual-camp device with different themes could flash once on camp switch (boot corrects it); Jelly reads data-jelly-mode when it injects tokens, so pre-setting it is consistent with what applyTheme does. Combine with the boot-shell-popin fix, which also hides most of the wrong-coloured shell.

verdicts.location: app.js:7236 (document.body.classList.toggle('dark-theme', dark)) in applyTheme; styles.css:50 and :77
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v3_osflip.cjs, Auto theme, viewer, standings seeded with 9 results). OS dark at load -> body.dark-theme; then page.emulateMedia({colorScheme:'light'}): body class stays 'dark-theme', --color-gold #e8c15a and --color-gold-bg #3a3116 stay dark, while --color-text flips to Jelly's light-mode dark text. Computed contrast of the podium-1 row text vs its background: 11.61 before, 1.21:1 after the flip (fresh light boot: 14.39:1, bg #fff6dd). Screenshot v3_flip_dark_to_light.png shows the three podium rows with dark-brown/navy tints and near-illegible team names while rows 4-6 are fine. #dynamic-theme-color also stays #181b1d. No matchMedia change listener exists (grep: only reduced-motion and the one prefersDark read at app.js:7234). Needs the page to be resident across an OS flip (scheduled dark mode at sunrise, installed PWA kept in memory), hence med rather than high, but it garbles the core Current Standings content.
verdicts.refinedFix: One-line fix, verified by patching app.js in flight (v3b_osflip_patched.cjs): in applyTheme change line 7236 to `document.body.classList.toggle('dark-theme', state.theme === 'dark');`. Auto + dark OS is already fully handled by the `body:not(.light-theme):not(.dark-theme)` media block at styles.css:77. Result: flipped state is identical to a fresh boot in both directions (contrast 14.39 after dark->light, 11.61 after light->dark; body class ''). Nothing else reads the class (grep: only styles.css:50/:77 and app.js:7236-7237; no tests reference it). For the status-bar colour also add, once in wireSettings or init: `const mq = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'); if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener('change', () => { if (state.theme === null) applyTheme(); });` so #dynamic-theme-color (a no-media meta that beats the media metas) tracks the OS. applyTheme only toggles classes/attributes, so no DOM rebuild or state-object risk.

verdicts.location: styles.css:225-231 (body transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v4_flip.cjs, standings card open, 60 sampled text elements, per-frame contrast against the nearest opaque ancestor background). setTheme('dark'): first sampled frame t=29 ms has 24 elements below 3:1 (min 1.03), by t=91 ms none below 3:1. setTheme('light'): still 24 elements below 3:1 at t=73 ms (min 1.82), clean by ~115 ms. CDP screencast frame 2 after the flip (v4_dark_f2.png) shows cards already dark while 'Elective 1', Swimming, Nerf War and every name chip are nearly invisible; frame 4 (~100 ms later) has them back. Cause is as stated: body color/background transition 0.2 s while surfaces and var tokens flip in one style recalc. It lasts roughly 3-6 frames and follows a user tap, so it reads as a blink, not a persistent artifact (low).
verdicts.refinedFix: Delete `transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease;` from the body rule (styles.css:230). Verified by patching in flight (v4_flip.cjs patched): 0 elements below 3:1 in every sampled frame in both directions, steady-state minimum unchanged (3.94 / 4.35 which are real design values, not the dip). No JS impact; this also removes the page-background fade that boot-bg-fade describes. Do not add `transition:all` anywhere (CLAUDE.md). The 150 ms border/box-shadow/color transitions on .game-card/.now-banner/.verse-day-chip were not seen to cause a dip in the contrast sampling, leave them.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced two ways. (1) jelly.js delayed 5 s (v5_backstop.cjs, viewer): html.jelly-failed at 4042 ms, scrollHeight 844->1070, five .card-visibility-row 'Hide from viewers' rows become visible to a VIEWER (view-only class does not exist until boot() runs), module arrives 5305 ms and everything re-collapses; layout shifts 0.5733 + 0.4976 = 1.071. Screenshot v5_5000_viewer_4500.png shows the unstyled expanded cards with the editor rows. (2) Whole-link throttle, no per-resource delay (v5b_throttle.cjs, cache disabled, 150 ms latency): at 250 KB/s (about 1 Mbps effective once Pages gzip is considered; total gz of the app scripts is ~305 KB plus ~180 KB Firebase SDK) jelly-failed appears at 5480 ms, module at 6104 ms, CLS 1.071; at 500 KB/s the module lands at 4.0 s, before the guard timer (~4.9 s) fires, so no misfire. So it needs sustained roughly under 2 Mbps (rural camp wifi or cell right after a deploy when every phone reloads), which is why it is low. Root cause correct: the module executes only after the parser and all body scripts, so 'late' is not 'failed'.
verdicts.refinedFix: Raise the backstop: `setTimeout(check, 15000);` (the request-error and window-error listeners already catch real failures immediately; the timer only guards a hung request, where 15 s of a blank/shell page is acceptable). Must update tests/shell.test.js line ~35 (`GUARD.includes('setTimeout(check, 4000)')`) in the same commit or the suite fails. Optional hardening: have boot-guard.js also add the hint role class (html.view-only when hint === 'viewer') pre-paint so a viewer never sees editor rows even in a real failure; keep it inside the first IIFE, mirror what setMemberRole does. Do not arm the timer on window 'load' (a hung module never fires load). No state or listener implications.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v6_fontblock.cjs): first-paint/FCP 68 ms with no delay, 3052 ms when fonts.googleapis.com stalls 3 s then fails, identical with or without the auth hint (so even the lock screen waits). The stylesheet is render-blocking as claimed. Real-world reach is small: it needs fonts.googleapis.com to hang rather than fail fast (filtered hosts normally reject quickly), and Google serves that CSS with a one-day max-age plus stale-while-revalidate so returning devices rarely wait on it. Not visible in normal use, so low and not worth a risky change.
verdicts.refinedFix: Optional. Cheapest safe form under the CSP (no inline onload allowed): change the tag to `<link id="gfonts" rel="stylesheet" media="print" href="...">` and add to a separate IIFE in boot-guard.js `var l=document.getElementById('gfonts'); if(l){ var on=function(){ l.media='all'; }; l.addEventListener('load',on); if(l.sheet) on(); }` (media=print links do not block render). Expect a font-swap reflow (Inter vs system-ui) on first visit; p19 showed it is minor but it would add a small CLS, so apply the shell fix first. Or self-host an Inter subset under font-src 'self'. Remember tests/shell.test.js reads index.html.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with my own stubbed Firebase (v7_tv.cjs; SDK script replaced inline, auth resolves 300 ms, member read 200 ms). Timeline: 7 ms white page with 'Loading standings...'; 52 ms #auth-overlay flex (rgba(6,8,12,0.96) full screen, 'Checking sign-in...'); 567 ms overlay none, white again; 668 ms intro shown. Screenshot v7_tv_1.png shows the near-black card over the white page. The order is deterministic from the code: startData() calls setAuthOverlay('checking') synchronously, and again at :740 when a user object arrives; with the real SDK the black phase lasts auth restore plus member read. It is a one-time hard cut at load on the presenter machine, so low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Don't show the 'checking' state immediately. In startData replace both setAuthOverlay('checking') calls with a delayed one: `var checkTimer = setTimeout(function () { setAuthOverlay('checking'); }, 1500);` and clear it (clearTimeout(checkTimer)) inside setAuthOverlay for every other mode (add at the top of setAuthOverlay), so a normal sub-second approval never shows it but a slow/offline check still does. The existing 'Loading standings...' state already covers the wait. The keydown/click guards at :1068 and :1079 read the overlay display only to block input once data exists, so skipping the overlay during checking changes nothing there. 'signin' and 'denied' stay immediate.

verdicts.location: styles.css:2813-2822 (.tool-box.alarming / @keyframes alarm-flash); reduce block at styles.css:5751
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v8_alarm.cjs, counselor-hide-seek with remaining 0, editor): with reducedMotion 'reduce' (matchMedia true) the computed animation-name is still alarm-flash, iteration infinite, one running alarm-flash animation, background cycling between oklab L 0.88 and 0.999 across 6 samples 120 ms apart; identical to no-preference. Only the board-clock classes are covered at :5751. Confirmed lock-shake is dead: no JS references 'shake' (grep of *.js finds only an unrelated 'handshake' comment). Low because it affects reduce-motion users only and only while a clock sits at 0:00; the effect is a slow background pulse (about 1 Hz), not a hard strobe.
verdicts.refinedFix: Add `.tool-box.alarming { animation: none; }` inside the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block at styles.css:5751; the red border-color on the same rule stays as the static cue. Optionally delete the dead `.lock-box.shake`/@keyframes lock-shake (styles.css:394-402). No JS involved.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v9_scroll.cjs, editor, tap a game card): scrollY samples reduce=false 17 distinct values (0,0,2,10,27,56,105,190,310,423 ... 759); reduce=true 28 distinct values on the same curve ending at 759 (matchMedia reduce confirmed true). An explicit behavior:'smooth' is not suppressed by the media query. Code confirmed at both call sites; JOY_REDUCED (app.js:8005) is a top-level const initialised at script load, and both call sites are click handlers, so referencing it there has no TDZ problem. Accessibility inconsistency only: low.
verdicts.refinedFix: Replace `{ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' }` at app.js:5495 and :5737 with `{ behavior: JOY_REDUCED.matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth', block: 'start' }`. JOY_REDUCED is declared later in the file but only read inside event handlers, so no hoisting is needed. No state or listener risk.

verdicts.location: vendor/jelly.js jelly-progress frame() (value ease: shownFrac += (fraction - shownFrac) * min(1, t*9))
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism is real (v10_progress.cjs: value 10->90, shownFrac eases over ~500 ms under both reduce and no-preference, with the component's reducedMotion flag true under reduce) but it is the component's value interpolation, not a decorative effect; the vendor only suppresses the ripple pulses and the indeterminate blob under reduce, a defensible reading of 'essential motion'. In this app the Happening-now bar moves about 1% per 30 s tick, so the ease is imperceptible, and the earlier whole-bar refill glitch is already fixed in v183. Patching a vendored file to snap a progress fill buys nothing.
verdicts.refinedFix: No change. If ever wanted, patch vendor/jelly.js frame() so `this.shownFrac = this.fraction` when this.reducedMotion, but that diverges from upstream and is not worth it.

verdicts.location: current-standings.html:218-220 (the only reduced-motion rule) and :858 (fight guard)
verdicts.reasoning: Factually correct (the page has one @media (prefers-reduced-motion) rule and one matchMedia check, both for the tie 'fight'; shield bob, 'Press to begin' pulse, hero pop-ins and confetti cannons run regardless). But this is a projector/TV showpiece whose whole point is spectacle; the intended feedback here is the confetti and bounce, the presenter machine rarely sets reduce-motion, and the owner's report is about glitches in the phone app. Not a glitch.
verdicts.refinedFix: No change needed. If the owner ever wants it: a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { img, .intro-go, .row, .hero { animation: none !important; } }` block plus an early return in the confetti cannon() function.

verdicts.location: styles.css:176-198 (jelly-drawer/jelly-dialog:not(:defined)[open] fallback); app.js:1110-1121 (Escape-only handler in wireSettings)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced for both a request abort and a SyntaxError module (v11_failed.cjs, real touch taps, class 'jelly-failed view-only'): page.tap('#settings-btn') opens the sheet (top 395, height 449) which has no close button (hasClose false); a touch tap on the page outside it leaves open=true; tapping the Dark segment leaves state.theme null (jelly-segmented never upgrades, so no change event). Screenshot v11_syntax_settings.png shows the plain sheet with Appearance as inert text. No page errors. The sheet is not a trap (the page behind still scrolls and a reload clears it; sign-out is reachable) and only devices that cannot load jelly.js are affected (iOS < 16.4 is the documented case), hence low.
verdicts.refinedFix: In wireSettings' degraded-mode block (app.js:1114-1120), add, guarded at event time by `!customElements.get('jelly-drawer')` so a late-arriving module takes over cleanly: (a) a capture-phase `document.addEventListener('click', e => { const open = [...document.querySelectorAll('jelly-drawer[open], jelly-dialog[open]')]; if (open.length && !open.some(el => el.contains(e.target))) { open.forEach(el => el.removeAttribute('open')); e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); } }, true)` (the settings-btn click that opens the sheet runs when nothing is open, so it is unaffected; nested sheets such as alerts-overlay are covered because the target is inside an open sheet); (b) for Appearance, a delegated click on `#theme-toggle jelly-segment` calling setTheme(seg.getAttribute('value')) only when !customElements.get('jelly-segmented') (otherwise it would double-fire with the component's own change event), or simply hide the Appearance row under html.jelly-failed. Optionally add a `::before` 'Close' bar in the :not(:defined)[open] rule for discoverability. These are plain document listeners on elements that are not rebuilt, so no stale-listener or typed-value risk.

verdicts.reasoning: Measured with a MutationObserver on #board across a full demo reveal (v13b_tvfull.cjs, v13_tvrows.cjs): every rebuild happens while the board is hidden. Rebuild log: t=1360 rows 1, 2687 rows 2, 4003 rows 3, 5325 rows 5 (all opacity 0, class dropped), t=6648 rows 6 (final, opacity 0 and just un-dropped). The old row nodes are replaced (sameNodes 0) and rowPop runs on all of them, but the previously docked rows were not on screen, because the board is dropped for every hero spotlight, so the all-rows pop is simply the table's entrance animation, not a replay of something visible. Only the Left-arrow 'back from the finale' rebuild happens at opacity 1 while the board fades out (t=11877, rows 5), a rare presenter undo lasting ~0.35 s. Not a glitch.
verdicts.refinedFix: No change. If the back-step ever matters, rebuild with an `.instant` class (animation:none) in back().

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (v14_bgfade.cjs, per-frame body and card colour, cold load). OS light: body rgb(244,246,249) at 73 ms, starts fading at ~487 ms, reaches oklch(1 0 0) at ~781 ms; cards are white throughout, so cards go from sitting on gray to white on white. OS dark: rgb(16,20,28) at 49 ms -> oklch(0.2198 0.006 236.84) (#181b1d) by ~623 ms; card surface rgb(26,32,48) = oklch(0.2514 0.0163 264.22) is unchanged. So the claim is exact, but the magnitude is about 3% lightness, in the same window as the shell pop-in, so it is a subtle secondary artifact (low).
verdicts.refinedFix: Align the three --color-bg fallbacks with Jelly's real defaults: `#ffffff` at styles.css:16 and `#181b1d` at :52 and :79 (and drop the body transition, see theme-flip-text-dip). Verified by patching in flight (v14b_bgfade_patched.cjs): body background is rgb(255,255,255) / rgb(24,27,29) from the first frame and the Jelly token landing changes it by < 1e-5 in oklab, i.e. no visible fade; card colours unchanged. Side effect: the pre-module lock screen sits on white (light) / #181b1d (dark), which is exactly the post-module look. Do not rely on removing only the body transition: that would turn the fade into a snap at DCL.

extraFindings.title: Auto theme: OS flip light->dark leaves the browser-chrome theme-color meta stuck on white
extraFindings.symptom: With Appearance = Auto, if the phone switches from light to dark while Camp is open, the page itself goes dark (media block) but the status bar / URL bar colour meta stays #ffffff, so a white bar sits above a dark page. The reverse flip (dark->light) leaves it #181b1d. It only corrects on the next reload.
extraFindings.trigger: Appearance Auto, OS light at load, emulateMedia colorScheme dark without reloading, read document.getElementById('dynamic-theme-color').content.
extraFindings.evidence: v3_osflip.cjs: after the OS light->dark flip the body is dark (bg oklch(0.2198 ...), color-scheme dark) but #dynamic-theme-color content is still '#ffffff'; after dark->light it is still '#181b1d'. The auditor's boot-theme-pages report said light->dark 'works fine'; that is true for page colours only. Only the meta value was measured (headless has no browser chrome), so the visual is inferred from the documented rule that a no-media meta appended last beats the media-specific metas (comment at app.js:7255).
extraFindings.rootCause: applyTheme() writes the no-media #dynamic-theme-color meta only at boot and in setTheme(); nothing re-runs it on a prefers-color-scheme change, and that meta overrides the pre-paint media metas in index.html.
extraFindings.location: app.js:7233-7264 (applyTheme) - add a matchMedia change listener
extraFindings.proposedFix: Same listener as the os-flip-stale-dark-class fix: `const mq = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'); if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener('change', () => { if (state.theme === null) applyTheme(); });` (applyTheme only toggles classes/attributes/meta, so it is safe to call at any time).

lenses.lens: Counselor (viewer) mid-day: standing in sun, one hand, kids around, 5–10 second glances. Needs: where do I need to be, what's next, how is my team doing, who is winning, messages.
lenses.summary: The order is roughly right: messages, then my team, then what's happening now, then details. The pieces are good too: the team card, the "My electives today" list, the Happening Now card that opens the full schedule, and a standings table that shows who moved up and how far behind you are. What fails is the 5-second glance. The answers a counselor looks for are the smallest, greyest text on the screen, while the largest type is the titles of five boxes that are always closed. Tap counts at 390×844 for a counselor who has said who they are (Alysa, Ferocious Foxes): where am I now = 0 taps during electives (shown twice), but during the games block the screen never says which game or where. What's next = 0 taps in ordinary blocks, but a tap into Full schedule during electives and games, exactly when it matters. My team = 0 taps for rank and points (11.5px pill), but seeing the gap to the leader takes a scroll, a tap and another scroll. Who's winning = a scroll plus a tap on every glance, because Standings starts closed on each load and closes again after 5 minutes idle. Chat = 1 tap, and its row moves anywhere from y≈457 to y≈1022 depending on the time of day. The layout makes sense as a list of everything, but not as a tool you glance at.

problems.problem: Who's winning is never on the home screen, and it closes itself again.
problems.evidence: Standings is a closed accordion row. applyCardDefaults (app.js:8139) removes [open] from every card on each load, and collapseCardsForIdle closes them again after IDLE_COLLAPSE_MS = 5 min (app.js:7790). During Elective 1 the Standings header sits at y=954 on an 844px screen (layout/counselor/elective-id-full.png), and at y=1162 when a live game and an announcement are up (announce-live-full.png). The team card shows only your own rank. It never names the leader or the gap. The useful line 'Ferocious Foxes needs 2 golds (8 pts) to catch Methodic Mediocre Maples' sits under the 6-row table (viewer-card-standings.png).
problems.impact: A counselor who checks every 20–30 minutes pays a scroll and a tap every time for the most common camp question ('are we winning?'). With kids around, they won't bother. They'll ask a director instead.

problems.problem: The hierarchy is upside down: the answers are small and grey, and the labels of closed boxes are the biggest text on the page.
problems.evidence: Rank pill .follow-rank-pill is 0.72rem (styles.css:1814). Points .follow-points are 0.85rem muted #5b6472 (styles.css:1826). 'Up next' .now-next is 0.85rem muted (styles.css:937). Elective times .my-el-time are 0.82rem muted. Meanwhile 'Quick Points', 'Memory Verse' and 'Meal Cleanup' render as ~20px bold headings on full-width 58px rows. Five of them take ~360px (home-viewer-light.png). For a viewer, Quick Points opens to the single line 'No bonus points yet.' (viewer-card-bonus.png).
problems.impact: In sunlight, 13px mid-grey text is the first thing to wash out. The eye lands on navigation labels instead of facts. Everything has the same visual weight, so nothing tells you 'look here first'.

problems.problem: The first screen goes to content that doesn't change, and the live content gets pushed down.
problems.evidence: At 1:30pm, the team card (140px), My electives (151px) and a full-width grey '🔕 Notify me' bar (42px) come before Happening Now, which starts at y=393 (elective-id-full.png). The My electives card stays up all morning: at 10:30, during team competitions, it still takes 151px for electives three hours away (games-first.png). During an elective, the Happening Now card spends 406px on all six stations' rosters (renderNowBanner, app.js:796). That repeats what My electives already said three inches higher.
problems.impact: Half of the first screen is spent before it says what's happening now. The counselor's own station shows up twice. Standings and Chat get pushed below the fold.

problems.problem: 'What's next' disappears in exactly the two blocks where it's needed.
problems.evidence: nowBannerHtml passes next=null for elective blocks (app.js:796), so there's no 'Up next' during Elective 1/2/3. During games blocks it shrinks to a one-line '🏅 Team competitions' with no game, place or opponent (app.js:778; games-first.png). Tapping through to the Full schedule sheet lists game names only, with no locations or matchups (tap-schedule.png). The Competitions card lists the day's games under 'MORNING' with no 'now' marker, plus scoring-format jargon badges ('Bracket', 'Podium pick') (tap-competitions.png). The team card's 'Up next: vs X' line only appears when a tournament bracket is already queued (findNextMatchupFor, app.js:3001).
problems.impact: During competitions, the busiest time of day, a counselor can't tell from the home screen where their team should be or who they play next. It takes 1–2 taps plus scanning, so they ask someone instead.

problems.problem: The live game board is placed low and padded with empty space.
problems.evidence: When a game is live, it takes over the Happening Now slot, but that slot is still below the announcement, team card, electives and Notify bar, so it starts at y=517. .big-board.viewer { min-height: 55vh; justify-content: center } (styles.css:5650) is spectator sizing reused on the home screen. It makes a 491px box with ~120px of blank space above the rows, so the first score row lands at y≈710 (announce-live-first.png). Only two of the three teams are visible without scrolling. Related, not verified on device: renderLiveHome rewrites wrap.innerHTML on every render, unlike the other home panels, which use setHtmlIfChanged. That would restart the board's pulse/heartbeat CSS animations on each synced score.
problems.impact: The most time-sensitive thing in the app is the fifth block down, and it starts with a white gap that looks like a loading failure.

problems.problem: There are four different ways to go deeper, so 'back' means something different each time.
problems.evidence: There are five accordion cards that open in place, one at a time (index.html jelly-accordion single). The schedule is a bottom sheet. Chat is a full-screen takeover (body.chat-open). A game opens as an inline section appended below all five closed cards, with a smooth scroll down to it (editor-game-open.png, wireDayPanels). Settings is another bottom drawer.
problems.impact: A one-handed user can't build a mental map. Opening a game jumps the page, and getting back to the list depends on remembering which kind of view you're in.

problems.problem: Every box looks the same, with no grouping by how often it changes.
problems.evidence: There are 10 rounded boxes on the 1:30pm screen, each a slightly different tint: a peach team card, a lavender electives card, a grey Notify pill, a white Happening Now card with a blue left rule, a white Chat row and five white accordion rows (elective-id-full.png). 'Today' is marked three different ways: 'Tue •' in the Competitions tabs, an orange dot hanging off the chip corner in the Cleanup/Verse/Schedule chips, and a 'NOW' pill in the schedule sheet. The team card has two adjacent 'Change' links (team and identity).
problems.impact: Nothing separates now, today and this week from reference material. Low-use cards (Verse, Quick Points) look as important as Standings.

keep: The team card leads the page: shield crest, rank, points and 'Next meal cleanup: Wednesday Breakfast'. That last line answers a real counselor question with 0 taps. The hand-drawn shields are real team identity, not decoration.
'My electives today' (time · station · break). This is exactly 'where do I need to be' for a junior counselor. Keep the content, just show it at the right time.
Your own name highlighted in the station roster (kid-chip-you).

Happening Now with an 'Up next' line that includes the meal's dish and cleanup team. Tapping it opens a full-week sheet that lands on NOW and lists that block's actual games. This is the best piece of the app.
Announcements at the very top, dismissible and expiring on their own. The posted notice board as the one big message.
The Live board taking the top slot automatically while a game runs. The idea is right, only its sizing and position aren't.
Standings content: movement arrows (↑2, ↓3), counselor names under each team, and the 'needs 2 golds (8 pts) to catch' hint. It's the most motivating sentence in the app.
Game list cards that show the medal result inline, so finished games need no tap.
Editor-only copy and controls hidden for viewers (card-desc, standings hint, hide switches), and the no-flicker re-render work (setHtmlIfChanged).
lenses.direction:
Make the first screen a fixed 'glance' area with three plain bands, not a stack of boxes. Make the answers the biggest type (18–22px, full-contrast), and keep labels small.

1) Messages: only when present. A posted notice or an unexpired announcement on one line, plus the chat unread count as a small marker in the page header instead of a full row.

2) 'You, now': one block that merges Happening Now with My electives for an identified counselor. 'NOW 1:15–2:00 · Crafts with Eileen (you + Josh)' and on the next line 'NEXT 2:00 Snack Shack · 3:00 Break'. Always show a next line, including during electives and games. During a games block, show the current game, its location and your team's next opponent. The six-station roster goes behind 'See who's where' (open by default for editors only). My electives only appears from lunch until Elective 3 ends.

3) 'Scoreboard': always open, never auto-collapsed. One line per team (rank, team mark, short name, points), your team highlighted, and the catch-up sentence under it. Six rows at ~36px each is about 230px. When a game is live, this band becomes a compact live board without the 55vh spectator padding, and the season table moves one step down. The team card shrinks to a header strip (crest, name, rank, points). The Notify control becomes a bell icon in that strip.

Below the fold, as a flat list rather than equal cards: Today's games with now/next markers and location (open one as a bottom sheet, like the schedule, not as a section appended at the page bottom), then Meal cleanup, Verse and Quick points as plain rows.

Navigation: one detail pattern only, bottom sheets, for schedule, game, verse and cleanup. Chat stays the only full-screen takeover. If the owner wants tabs instead, use a 3-item bottom bar (Now · Scores · Chat) within thumb reach. Either way, drop the idle auto-collapse.

Senior uses the same frame with no electives line. It already fits one screen, so the scoreboard band would just appear above the fold.
aiHabitsSpotted: Identical rounded cards stacked vertically: 10 boxes on the 1:30pm phone screen, each with a slightly different tint (peach, lavender, grey, white with a blue rule).
Everything is a collapsible: 5 accordion rows closed by default, closed again on every load and after 5 minutes idle.
Emoji as the main icon system on nearly every line (🧽 🙋 ⭐ 🔕 📅 🌟 🏊 🎯 🎨 🥏 🎲 ☕ 💬), including table column headers (🥇🥈🥉📖🧽) and the footer (📋 🛠️ ⚙️).
Pills everywhere: the '4TH PLACE' rank pill, 'Bracket'/'Podium pick' format pills, a pill around every counselor name, '🔴 LIVE', '📣 ANNOUNCEMENT', 'NOW'.
Uppercase letter-spaced eyebrows: 'HAPPENING NOW', 'THEME VERSE · HARVEST OF THE HEART', 'TEAM TOTALS · 3/6 IN', 'MORNING', 'TUESDAY'.
A colored left-border accent rule as the 'important' signal (Happening Now, the verse day card, highlighted standings rows).
Generic hierarchy: section titles are the largest type, data is small and muted grey.
Vertical centering in a fixed-height box (the 55vh live board) that leaves a large blank band.
A full-width grey secondary button ('🔕 Notify me') that reads as disabled.
Light-tint gradient card with a soft shadow for the hero (team card).

ownerQuestions.question: When a counselor pulls their phone out mid-day for a few seconds, what is the ONE thing the first screen must answer?
ownerQuestions.why: Right now the first screen tries to answer everything equally. The answer decides what gets the biggest type and the top spot.
options: Where I need to be now and next (personal schedule first)
How the competition stands: who's winning and how far my team is behind
It changes with the time of day: schedule during electives and meals, live scores during competition blocks
Messages from directors first, everything else after

ownerQuestions.question: Should counselors see the standings without tapping?
ownerQuestions.why: Standings is currently closed on every load and closes itself after 5 minutes. There is also a 'Hide Current Standings from viewers' switch, which suggests you sometimes want suspense. The answer changes the layout a lot.
options: Yes, a compact leaderboard is always open on the home screen
Only my team's rank and the gap to the leader on the home screen, with the full table one tap away
Keep it one tap away, but remember that I opened it (no auto-closing)
Keep as is: hidden behind a tap is deliberate (suspense or fairness)

ownerQuestions.question: During an elective, who is the full 'who's at which station' roster for?
ownerQuestions.why: It's the biggest block on the screen (≈400px). An identified counselor already has their own station in 'My electives' just above it.
options: Counselors only need their own station, so put everyone else behind 'See who's where'
Everyone uses the full roster to find each other, so keep it fully open
Show it fully open for directors/editors and folded for counselors

ownerQuestions.question: How should people move around the app?
ownerQuestions.why: Today there are four different ways in and out (open-in-place cards, a bottom sheet, a full-screen chat, and a game section that appears at the bottom of the page). One-handed use needs one predictable pattern.
options: One scrolling home page with a fixed order; every detail opens as a bottom sheet you swipe away
A small bottom tab bar (Now · Scores · Chat), each tab one simple screen
Keep the current single page, but cut the boxes down and make game details open as a sheet

ownerQuestions.question: How often do counselors actually use Memory Verse, Meal Cleanup and Quick Points?
ownerQuestions.why: They currently get the same size and weight as Standings. If they're occasional, they can move lower or into the schedule without anyone missing them.
options: Daily, keep them on the home page but below the scoreboard
Occasionally, move them to a 'More' list or into the schedule sheet
The verse matters for camp culture, so give it a morning spotlight on the home screen and file the rest lower

ownerQuestions.question: What role should emoji play in the look of the app?
ownerQuestions.why: Emoji are currently the main icons on almost every line and in the table headers. Keeping them for team and station identity only would make the camp's personality stand out instead of turning into noise.
options: Keep emoji for teams and elective stations only; use plain words or simple icons everywhere else
Replace the interface emoji with one consistent icon set; teams keep their shields and colors
Keep them everywhere, because the playful look is part of the camp

lenses.lens: Director / game leader (editor): scoring the game happening right now under time pressure, posting announcements, fixing things
lenses.summary: For a director, the home page is a counselor's reading page with editor switches scattered through it, so the main job (scoring the game happening right now) never reaches the first screen. At 6:15pm on Tuesday the director sees their team card, a strip that says "Evening competition" (tapping it opens the schedule, not the games), a Chat card that is half "Hide from viewers" switch, and five rows that all look the same. Recording a podium result takes 9 taps plus a scroll past the morning's finished games. When the game opens, it appears below all five collapsed rows, and Back drops you at the top of the page. Some of the pieces are right: the red LIVE card, the full-screen pattern Chat already uses, and the compact podium form. But the page is arranged by type of data (Competitions, Standings, Cleanup, Verse, Points), not by what a director needs at this minute.

problems.problem: Nothing on the director's first screen leads to the game happening now. The 'Happening now' strip knows it is game time, but tapping it opens the schedule sheet, and the games in that sheet can't be tapped.
problems.evidence: Measured at Tue 6:15pm (?now=2-1815): the now-banner is a single line, '🏅 Evening competition 📅 Full schedule ›' (nowBannerHtml returns .now-slim for type 'games', app.js ~782). The schedule sheet lists games as plain <span class="sched-game-chip"> (app.js 934–935) with no click handler. With Competitions closed, the first screen is the team card, the slim strip, the Chat card and five closed rows (scratchpad layout/editor/gametime-first.png).
problems.impact: Every game starts with a hunt. Path to a podium result: open Competitions (1), scroll (the first evening game sits at y=967 on an 844px screen, under two finished morning brackets), tap the game (2), pick Gold, Silver and Bronze (open + choose each = 6), Save (1). That is 9 taps plus a scroll, and at least 3 of them are only navigation.

problems.problem: An opened game appears AFTER the whole accordion, below Competitions, Standings, Cleanup, Verse and Quick Points, instead of in place of the list. Back then lands at the top of the page, not at the list you left.
problems.evidence: index.html line 261: #game-view sits outside and after <jelly-accordion>. Measured for Musical Chairs at 10:30: after the auto-scroll, the game's top is at y=385, because the page is too short to scroll further (max scroll is 402). The top 45% of the screen is five closed card headers, and 'Start Bracket' sits at the bottom edge (layout/editor/tap2-game-open.png; shots/editor-game-open.png). Back sets scrollY to 0 and reopens Competitions (renderGameView + back-btn handler, app.js 5524–5560). No 'next game' link exists.
problems.impact: Where the game ends up on screen depends on how long the page is, so the director can't build muscle memory. Between games the loop is Back, then scroll down from the top past the team card and chat, then find the next game. That is the slowest step in a camp day with five games.

problems.problem: Every synced change rebuilds the open game and the LIVE card from scratch. Animations restart and things you opened snap shut while you are mid-game. This is the same family of glitch as the progress bar.
problems.evidence: Measured with Playwright. With a game open, one unrelated synced change (a bonus point landing) gives a new back-pill node whose 'back-pill-in' slide animation restarts at 0ms, recreates the medal <jelly-select>s, and closes an open 'How to play' (same=false, open=false). The LIVE card's infinite 'live-pulse' halo resets from 2433ms to 0 because renderLiveHome writes wrap.innerHTML on every renderAll (app.js 5718). renderGameView does view.innerHTML = html unconditionally (app.js 5562). applyRemoteState calls renderAll for any real change (app.js 2641).
problems.impact: A game leader reading the rules aloud loses the open rules every time another director saves anything. The back button twitches in from the left again and again. The red LIVE halo stutters every time anyone scores, so it looks broken exactly when the app is busiest.

problems.problem: The LIVE shortcut, the one good one-tap way back into a running game, only exists for brackets and live-ranked tallies. Half of junior's games and every senior game never get it.
problems.evidence: liveHomeGames() (app.js 5636) only counts tournament brackets and liveRankings tallies with a score in. Junior's default week has 11 placement, 5 tournament and 6 tally+liveRankings games, so 11 of 22 never surface. All 5 of senior's seeded games per day are placement. Placement drafts aren't counted.
problems.impact: The behavior isn't consistent: for some games the app 'remembers' what's on, and for others it doesn't. Senior directors get none of the benefit.

problems.problem: Controls only editors use (a set-once moderation switch, the announcement link, the quick-game link) sit inside the content and look just as heavy as the content.
problems.evidence: Six full-width '🙈 Hide from viewers' rows (index.html 160–252). The Chat card isn't collapsible, so its switch is always on the home screen: about 68px of the 127px Chat card, above the fold at game time. In every opened card the switch is the first thing, above the content (shots/editor-card-standings.png, -verse.png, -bonus.png). '📣 Post an announcement' is a small grey text link at the top-left, above the team card (renderAnnouncements, app.js 7537). '⚡ Quick game' is a link at the end of the day list.
problems.impact: Prime space on the first screen goes to a preference that is set maybe once a week. Meanwhile the one broadcast control a director needs fast looks like a stray caption.

problems.problem: There are three different ways to broadcast, each in a different place with a different lifetime. Settings (week builder, notice board, members, alerts, history) is reachable only from a small footer link.
problems.evidence: (1) The 📣 composer at the top of home (state.announcements, 1h / 3h / all-day options; layout/editor/announce-open.png). (2) Chat's Announcements channel, which also puts a banner at the top for 15 minutes (CHAT_BANNER_MS). (3) The Notice board, at Settings → Set up the week → Notice. renderFooter (app.js 1853–1872) holds the only '⚙️ Settings' button, at the very bottom of a page whose length changes with whichever card is open (about 2000px down with Verse open).
problems.impact: Under pressure, a director has to remember which of three tools to use and where each one lives. Fixing something (a game's rounds, a member's access) starts with scrolling to the bottom of the page.

problems.problem: Giving points is split across three separate panels, each with its own Mon–Fri picker. The single-open accordion and the 5-minute idle collapse keep closing the panel the director was using.
problems.evidence: Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse and Quick Points are separate jelly-collapsibles. Each repeats an explanation paragraph and its own day chips (shots/editor-card-cleanup.png, -verse.png, -bonus.png). <jelly-accordion single> means opening Cleanup closes Competitions. collapseCardsForIdle (app.js 7792) closes every panel after 5 minutes without input. In verse and cleanup, every row's '0' chip is solid blue, so 'zero' is the loudest thing in the card.
problems.impact: After lunch, giving cleanup points means leaving the games list. Coming back 5 minutes later means reopening everything. A director can't see at a glance who has already been given points, because the solid-blue zeros look like awards.

problems.problem: On a laptop at the scoring table, the page is the same phone column in the middle of the screen.
problems.evidence: shots/home-editor-desktop.png and layout/editor/desktop-game-open.png: a column about 608px wide on a 1280px screen with nothing on either side. An open game and the standings can't be seen together.
problems.impact: Less important than the phone problems, but an editor at a desk gets no benefit from the bigger screen.

keep: The red LIVE card at the top of home: one tap back into a running bracket. It's the right idea; extend it to every game type and stop rebuilding it on every change.
The full-screen takeover already used for Chat and the week builder (body.chat-open / body.builder-open hides everything else). It is the right container for an open game.
The podium entry form: three gold, silver and bronze rows plus one Save, which fits on one screen once you're there.
Making the 'Happening now' strip one line during game blocks. The instinct is right; it just needs to point at the games instead of the schedule.
Day tabs that default to today with the 'Tue •' marker.
Editor controls are hidden for viewers in one central place (html.view-only CSS), and the own-team guard lives in canScoreRound. One place to change either.

The v183 in-place refresh approach (setHtmlIfChanged; nudging the progress bar instead of rebuilding it) and the ladder-ball in-place refresh for rung taps. Apply the same approach to the game view and the LIVE card.
Back to the list via a labeled pill ('← Tuesday games') rather than an unlabeled arrow.
lenses.direction: Order the director's screen by what's happening now, not by type of data. (1) First on screen at game time, for editors: a 'Now playing' block for the current schedule block (the 10:00 Team competitions or the 6:00 Evening competition). It lists that block's games as large rows marked Not started, In progress or Done ✓, with the next unscored game styled as the main button ('Score Scatterball →'). Match block to session by time. It replaces both the one-line strip and the need to open Competitions; any game in progress, not only brackets, shows there with its LIVE state. Outside game blocks it falls back to the normal 'Happening now'. (2) Opening a game becomes a full-screen takeover, like Chat. It gets a fixed top bar with '← Games', the game name and 'Next game →'. The game no longer appears after the accordion. Back puts you back where you were, and the view is patched in place so the rules, the back button and the selects don't reset when someone else saves. (3) Move every editor-only control out of the content into one place: a slim editor bar pinned at the top or bottom with 📣 Announce (a real button), + Points and ⚙️ Settings. 'Hide from viewers' becomes one 'What counselors see' list of six switches inside Settings. (4) Combine Cleanup, Verse and Quick Points into one 'Points' area with one day picker. Verse reading can stay a viewer card. (5) Turn off the idle collapse for editors, or have it remember the last open panel. The single-open accordion can stay for viewers, but Competitions shouldn't have to compete with four other identical rows for a director. Navigation model for editors: three destinations (Now / Games / Points), with Standings and Chat a tap away. Counselors keep the reading-first page.
aiHabitsSpotted: Identical rounded white cards stacked vertically for every region (same border, radius and shadow), so the most-used panel (Competitions) has exactly the same weight as Quick Points.
Everything-is-a-collapsible: a single-open accordion plus an idle timer that closes everything again after 5 minutes.
Emoji as the icon system: 🙈 on all six hide switches, 📣 📋 🛠️ ⚙️ 📅 📍 in labels, and an emoji before every station name and team.
Pill badges everywhere: 'Bracket' and 'Podium pick' on every game card, the '4TH PLACE' pill, pill-shaped day tabs, pill kid-name chips, and solid-blue pill '0' chips.
The colored left-border stripe on the Happening Now card (the stock 'callout' look).
Explanation paragraphs at the top of every card ('Each day's memory verse — pick a day to read it, and record points…'), repeated on every visit, above the actual content.
Decorative motion: the back pill slides in, the LIVE card pulses forever, joySlideIn/joyStagger. Because the views rebuild on every sync, these replay as glitches.
Everything centered in one narrow column on desktop, with no layout for wider screens.
Settings tucked into the footer next to the version number and data timestamp.

ownerQuestions.question: Should directors get their own home page, or the same page as counselors with editor tools added on top?
ownerQuestions.why: Right now the counselor page is the base and editor controls are scattered through it. That is the root cause of most of the clutter and of the scoring hunt.
options: Same page for everyone; editor tools collected into one editor bar and moved out of the cards
A separate 'director home' (Now playing / Games / Points) for editors; counselors keep the reading page
A toggle editors can flip between 'Run the games' and 'See what counselors see'

ownerQuestions.question: During a game block, what should be the first thing a director sees?
ownerQuestions.why: This decides whether scoring takes 1 tap to reach or 3, and whether the 'Happening now' strip turns into a game list.
options: A list of this block's games with their status (Not started / In progress / Done)
Only the next unscored game, with one big 'Score it' button
The live board of whichever game is in progress, with the others underneath
Leave it as the schedule; directors open Competitions themselves

ownerQuestions.question: How is scoring split among staff during a block?
ownerQuestions.why: If each game leader only ever scores their own game, the app should remember 'my game' and open straight to it. If one person scores everything, a 'Next game →' flow matters more.
options: One scorekeeper records every game
Each game leader records only their own game
It varies by day or by game

ownerQuestions.question: Where should the 'Hide from viewers' switches live?
ownerQuestions.why: Today there are six of them in the content, and Chat's is always on the home screen. Moving them is the biggest single reduction in clutter.
options: One 'What counselors see' list inside Settings
A small ⋯ menu on each card
Only visible after tapping an 'Edit layout' button

ownerQuestions.question: Do you want three ways to broadcast (📣 announcement, the Chat Announcements channel, the Notice board), or fewer?
ownerQuestions.why: They live in three places with three different lifetimes (1h–all day, a 15-minute banner, until you take it down). Under pressure, a director has to remember which tool to use and where it is.
options: Keep all three, but put them behind one 'Announce' button that asks how long it should stay up
Retire the 📣 composer and use the Chat Announcements channel for quick messages; keep the Notice board for the big structured message
Keep things as they are; only make the 📣 link a proper button

ownerQuestions.question: Should Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse and Quick Points become one 'Points' area for directors?
ownerQuestions.why: All three are 'give team X some points'. Each has its own panel, explanation and day picker, and opening one closes the games list.
options: Merge all three into one Points area with one day picker
Merge Cleanup and Verse points; keep Quick Points separate
Keep three panels, but stop the accordion closing the others and stop the idle auto-close for editors

ownerQuestions.question: Do directors ever score from a laptop or tablet at a table, or only from phones?
ownerQuestions.why: If laptops are used, the game and the standings can sit side by side instead of in a narrow phone column. If phones only, that work can be skipped.
options: Phones only
Sometimes a laptop or tablet at the scoring table
The TV page covers big screens; don't bother

lenses.lens: Senior visual / graphic designer: hierarchy, type, color, spacing, team identity, emoji load, motion
lenses.summary: The top third of the page makes sense: a card for your team with the camper-drawn shield, then a "Happening now" panel that changes through the day. Both ideas are right. Below that, the page is a stack of six white rows that all look the same (Chat, Competitions, Current Standings, Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse, Quick Points). They all start closed, and they close again after 5 minutes of no use. So an app called Camp Scoreboard shows no scores on the first screen except "4TH PLACE 22 pts", and that number is the smallest grey text on the card. In light mode the page background and the cards are both pure white, so the boxes nearly disappear. Emoji, pill badges, sparkle effects and look-alike rounded boxes are doing the job that hierarchy, team colors and the shields should do. My advice: rebuild it as a "now + standings" screen with the shields as the team identity, and move the reference material (cleanup rota, verse, quick points) to a second level.

problems.problem: The order of importance is upside down: the scoreboard is not on the home screen, and every section has the same visual weight
problems.evidence: home-viewer-light-firstscreen.png: the first 844px is the follow card, then ~405px of electives, then the Chat and Competitions rows. Standings is the 3rd row of a collapsed accordion. applyCardDefaults() (app.js ~8139) closes every card on every load, collapseCardsForIdle() closes them again after 5 min, and the accordion is single-open (jelly-accordion single), so you can never see Standings next to Competitions. During game time (layout/counselor/games-first.png) the screen is 9 stacked boxes and the only score shown is '22 pts'.
problems.impact: Counselors outdoors have to tap and scroll for the one thing the app is named for. A glance at the page tells you nothing about the competition.

problems.problem: Look-alike accordion rows, with section titles as loud as the main heading
problems.evidence: Five jelly-collapsibles plus the Chat row: each 58px tall with a 15px gap, about 440px of plain navigation. The card h2 is 18.4px/800, exactly the same as .follow-team-name on phones (styles.css 3320, measured 18.4px/800). The rows carry no summary: Quick Points (usually 'No bonus points yet', viewer-card-bonus.png) gets the same billing as Current Standings.
problems.impact: It reads as a generic template. Nothing tells you which section matters right now, and 'Meal Cleanup' shouts as loud as your team's name.

problems.problem: Light mode has no structure: the page background and the cards are the same white
problems.evidence: Measured: body rgb(255,255,255) and .card rgb(255,255,255), with a border of rgb(236,236,239) (~1.2:1). Jelly's background-default token overrides the intended #f4f6f9 fallback. 29 rules use var(--color-bg) as an inset tile, and all of them vanish in light mode. The elective station rows are boxed in dark (home-viewer-dark.png) but flat in light (home-viewer-light.png). styles.css:363 even says the Hide row swaps to --color-bg 'for the contrast', which is zero in light.
problems.impact: In sunlight the boxes dissolve into a white sheet. Light and dark became two different designs by accident.

problems.problem: The team identity is underused, and the team colors can't be told apart
problems.evidence: Shields appear only on the followed team's card (and on the TV page). Standings, live boards, the cleanup rota and matchups all use emoji (🦊🦃🍁🎃🦅🚜). Four of the six junior accents sit within hue 9 to 33 degrees (fox #e2672b, turkey #9c6420, maple #c23b22, pumpkin #e07d10). Pumpkin is 2.95:1 and fox 3.38:1 on white, yet .board-tally-score uses the accent as the score's text color. The camps.js comment says the accents 'never sit side by side', but the Big Board puts them side by side. Senior teams ARE colors (Red/Blue/Green/Gold), yet standings rows are tinted by medal, and 'Gold Team' #b8860b collides with medal gold #96690a.
problems.impact: The most authentic, least generic asset in the app (kids' drawings) does almost no work, and color can't carry team identity at a glance.

problems.problem: The same color means different things
problems.evidence: viewer-card-standings.png: the peach wash means 'your team' (the fox card at top) and also means '3rd place' (bronze row #fbe9de, Pumpkins) on the same screen. Blue #3355ff is used for the Now label, the Now left stripe, the progress bar, the selected day chip, links, your-row outline, the electives card tint, and the selected '0' button on every team's points row (editor-card-verse.png shows six filled blue zeros).
problems.impact: Color stops carrying meaning. The eye gets pulled to six zeros and a stripe instead of to leaders and changes.

problems.problem: Emoji are the main visual language, including as table headers, and the standings table is clipped on phones
problems.evidence: I counted 59 emoji in the main column with standings open. Column headers are 🥇🥈🥉📖🧽. The footer reads '📋 … 🛠️ … ⚙️', buttons are '📋 Copy scores & points', and editor rows are '🙈 Hide'. At 390px the table's scrollWidth is 348 against 316 visible, so the 🧽 column sits off the edge with no hint. At 360px (layout/designer/standings-360.png) 📖 and 🧽 are gone and bronze is half-clipped, while names wrap to three lines ('Methodic / Mediocre / Maples', rows 93px tall).
problems.impact: Everything gets the same playful decoration, so nothing stands out. On common Android widths the scoreboard is partly hidden.

problems.problem: There is no type scale, and the hero number is tiny
problems.evidence: I measured 34 distinct size/weight combos on one screen. styles.css uses about 30 font sizes (0.62 to 3.4rem, with 0.78/0.8/0.82/0.85/0.88/0.9/0.92/0.95 all present) and weights 400/500/600/640/700/800. On the team card, points are 13.6px/600 muted grey (.follow-points) and rank is an 11.5px uppercase pill, while the 112px shield and the chores line ('Next meal cleanup') take the space.
problems.impact: Without a deliberate scale, everything competes and the numbers that matter look like small print.

problems.problem: Editor settings take more space than editor actions
problems.evidence: home-editor-light.png and editor-card-*.png: '🙈 Hide from viewers' (a ~66px row with a large switch) is the first thing inside every opened card and is always visible under Chat. '📣 Post an announcement' is a 0.78rem muted grey link at the top (styles.css:4212), the smallest text on the page. Verse scoring is 36 round buttons.
problems.impact: Directors scroll past a once-a-week setting five times, and the broadcast action looks like a footnote.

problems.problem: Views open in the wrong place, and there are layout artifacts
