problems.evidence: editor-game-open.png: tapping a game inside Competitions (row 2) shows #game-view after the whole accordion, below Quick Points. On the Big Board, .big-board.viewer has min-height:55vh with justify-content:center, so a 3-team tally floats in ~200px of empty box above and below (layout/counselor/announce-live-full.png). The TV page's 'Press → or tap to begin' overlaps 'Loading standings…' and the 🎪 spinner (tv-standings.png).
problems.impact: You tap one place and the result appears somewhere else, and the empty frames look broken.

problems.problem: Decorative motion everywhere, which makes the glitches stand out
problems.evidence: The 'JOY LAYER' in styles.css ~5760 and app.js ~8023: particle sparkles on every button and card-header tap, a 16-particle ✨⭐🎉💫 burst on every data save (joyCelebrate via touchData), a 0.93→1.05 spring on every tappable, and a staggered rise of card contents layered on jelly-collapsible's own spring. LIVE cards pulse forever, and renderLiveHome writes wrap.innerHTML directly (not setHtmlIfChanged), so they are re-created on every sync. The 'Happening now' progress bar is an unlabeled ~200px bar with no '25 min left', a low-information element that became the most visible thing when it glitched.
problems.impact: The motion carries no information, so real changes (a score landing, a rank moving) can't stand out, and every re-render shows as flicker.

problems.problem: The senior camp gets a weaker version of the junior design
problems.evidence: senior-home-viewer.png: with no crest, the main card falls back to a 🔴 emoji plus 'Red Team' on a pink wash. The layout depends on art that only junior has.
problems.impact: Teens get a plainer, more childish-looking version of the junior app rather than a design of their own.

keep: The camper-drawn team shields. They are the best visual asset in the app; expand their use rather than shrink it.
The time-aware 'Happening now' idea, especially the electives list showing where each kid is right now.
The live game taking over the top of the home screen during games (homeBoardGame). Right instinct: the game IS what's happening.
The 'Your team' personalization, including the team set by the person's account ('YOUR TEAM') and the next-matchup line.
Small human details in standings: rank-change arrows (↑2 / ↓3) and the catch-up line ('Foxes needs 2 golds (8 pts) to catch Maples').
TEAM_ABBREV short names (Foxes, Turkey, Maples…) already exist; use them to stop three-line wraps.
The notice board concept: one big composed message instead of six announcements.
The setHtmlIfChanged / nudge-don't-rebuild discipline in render code (renderNowBanner, renderFollowCard).
The dark theme's inset-tile structure. It shows what light mode was meant to look like.
Day chips with a today dot, and the TV page's large shield-led presentation as a reference for the phone's team identity.
lenses.direction:
Rebuild home as a 'now + standings' scoreboard with a clear top-to-bottom order of importance, and move reference material down a level.

FIRST ON SCREEN:
- A slim team bar in the team's own color: small shield, short name, rank as a big numeral ('4th'), points as a large tabular number, and one line for 'Up next'. Move the chores line and the 'tell us who you are' prompt out of the hero.
- Directly under it, one NOW module that changes with the day:
  - electives: where my kids are;
  - competitions: the live board, or today's games with results inline;
  - otherwise: the current block with 'ends 2:00 · 25 min left' as text, replacing the unlabeled bar (or making it a full-width hairline).

SECOND:
- Standings, always open, never an accordion. A compact 6-row (4 for senior) leaderboard: shield thumbnail, short name, big points.
- Medals as a small secondary line ('2G · 2S · 1B'). Verse and cleanup folded into points, with tap-for-breakdown.
- No horizontal scroll. Your row marked in your team color, not app blue. Rank shown by the numeral, not by gold/silver/bronze row fills.

THIRD:
- Today's games as a plain list showing the winner's shield inline.
- Tapping a game opens a full-screen view with a Back button, like the Chat takeover, never appended below the page.

FOURTH (reference):
- Meal cleanup, Memory verse and Quick points become one-line summaries in a 'Today's jobs / More' section, e.g. 'Cleanup: Breakfast Maples · Lunch Pumpkins · Supper Turkey'.
- Chat moves to a header or tab icon with an unread badge instead of a full-width row.

NAVIGATION:
- I'd recommend a 4-tab bottom bar on phones (Now · Standings · Games · Chat, with More in a header menu). Glancing, reading and talking are different jobs, and tabs end the everything-collapses habit.
- The alternative is a single scroll in the fixed order above with no accordions.

VISUAL SYSTEM:
- Warm off-white page with white surfaces, or no cards at all: small section labels and hairline dividers, with card chrome only for live or interactive modules.
- One type scale (roughly 12/14/16/20/32 px plus tabular display numerals for scores) and two weights.
- Neutral chrome and one action color. Team colors only for team identity, re-picked so the six are distinct. Medals only as medal marks.
- A shield wherever a team appears in a list. Emoji kept for schedule blocks and as the fallback when there is no art.

EDITORS:
- Hide-from-viewers switches move to Settings or an 'Edit home' mode.
- 'Post announcement' becomes a real button at the top for editors.

MOTION:
- Only for state changes: a score landing, a rank moving, the clock.
- Remove the sparkles, the springs on every tap and the staggered reveals.

SENIOR:
- Its own restrained scoreboard look built on the flag colors, which become the identity system that junior's shields are.
aiHabitsSpotted: Identical white rounded cards (16px radius, 1px border, soft shadow) stacked at a uniform 15px gap: a one-size-fits-all card stack
Everything collapsible: a 5-panel single-open accordion, closed on every load and closed again when idle, plus a 'How to play' disclosure inside game view
An emoji before nearly every label, button, row, column header and footer item (59 in the main column with standings open)
Emoji used as table column headers (🥇🥈🥉📖🧽) instead of designed labels
Pills and chips for everything: kid-name chips, uppercase rank pill, 'Bracket'/'Podium pick' badges, LIVE pill, a full-width grey 'Notify me' pill that looks disabled
Tiny uppercase letter-spaced accent 'eyebrow' ('HAPPENING NOW') plus a 4px colored left stripe on the card
A generic saturated product blue (#3355ff) as the only accent, unrelated to any team or to camp
A muted explainer paragraph under every section header ('Each day's memory verse — pick a day to read it…')
A radial-gradient wash plus a drop-shadowed illustration on the hero card
Confetti and sparkle particles on taps and saves, spring overshoot on every press, staggered fade-up reveals
Default underlined blue text links ('Change', 'Tell us who you are') mixed with designed buttons
About 30 font sizes and 6 weights with no scale: sizes nudged ad hoc (0.78/0.8/0.82/0.85/0.88rem)
Medal colors used as row fills (gold/silver/bronze bands) instead of team identity

ownerQuestions.question: When a counselor pulls out their phone at a random moment, what is the ONE thing the first screen must answer?
ownerQuestions.why: Today the top screen is your team card plus the electives list, and the scores are hidden in a closed row. The whole layout follows from this answer.
options: How my team is doing: rank, points, and the full standings right there
What's happening now and where my kids should be (scores one tap away)
It depends on the time of day: schedule and kids during electives, scores and live games during competitions
The game being played right now if there is one, otherwise the standings

ownerQuestions.question: How should people move around the app on a phone?
ownerQuestions.why: The current single-open accordion is the main reason the page looks generic and hides things. A real navigation model replaces it.
options: A bottom tab bar: Now · Standings · Games · Chat (verse, cleanup, quick points under More)
One scrolling page in a fixed order with nothing collapsed, so it's longer but everything is visible

lenses.lens: Information architect: inventory of every home region, frequency × importance, navigation model, junior/senior, editor/viewer, desktop/TV, time of day
lenses.summary: Partly. The top of the page works: your team, the "Happening now" banner, and the live game that takes over when one is running. It's also the only part that changes with the camp day. Everything below it is a fixed menu of six equal sections: Chat, then five collapsed rows (Competitions, Current Standings, Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse, Quick Points). That menu looks the same at breakfast, Bible study, competitions, lights-out and Sunday registration. It closes on every page load and closes itself again after 5 minutes idle, so the things people use most (standings, today's games, whatever meal or verse is happening now) cost taps on every visit. It's worst at the busiest time. During competition blocks the banner shrinks to one line, and podium-pick games (11 of junior's 22, all of senior's) never appear on the home page, so the home page says nothing about what's being played. My recommendation: a home page that follows the schedule, standings that are always visible in short form, and a few fixed destinations in place of the accordion.

problems.problem: The home page doesn't change through the day, but camp does. Five collapsed rows are a constant menu, and only the banner moves.
problems.evidence: Screenshots from the IA run (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Camp/0f7c2075-f70d-5c41-9f9f-e6ae084416ea/scratchpad/layout/ia/): v-tue-0815-breakfast-first, v-tue-0915-bible-first, v-wed-1030-games-first, v-tue-2245-night-first and v-sun-1430-arrival-first all show the same Chat card plus the same five rows in the same order. applyCardDefaults() removes [open] on every load (app.js ~8139). collapseCardsForIdle() closes everything after IDLE_COLLAPSE_MS = 5 min (app.js ~7790). The accordion is <jelly-accordion single>, so opening Standings closes Competitions.
problems.impact: Every visit starts from zero. The frequent destinations each cost 1–3 taps every time, plus a spring expand/collapse animation each time, so motion is doing the job of navigation. It also feeds the 'things keep reloading/animating' feeling. A counselor can't see standings and today's games at once.

problems.problem: Competition blocks, the peak use time, show the least on the home page.
problems.evidence: nowBannerHtml() returns a one-line .now-slim ('🏅 Team competitions') for type:'games' blocks (app.js ~775). Today's games sit behind Competitions ▸ → day tab → game. The live slot only fills for brackets or liveRankings tallies (liveHomeGames, app.js 5632). Junior has 11 placement games out of 22 and senior's seeds are all placement (camps.js 570), and placement games never appear there. s-tue-1030-games-first.png (senior, mid-competition) shows the team strip, one line, and the menu.
problems.impact: Counselors herding a team and directors running a game get nothing on the home page about which games are on, what's next, or what just finished. Senior camp, with four games blocks a day, gets this every block.

problems.problem: In a scoreboard app, the scoreboard starts collapsed, and when opened it's hard to read on a phone.
problems.evidence: Current Standings is the third collapsed row. index.html 192 and the styles.css comment at line 696 confirm the team strip exists 'so viewers keep the watch essentials even with Current Standings collapsed'. The follow card shows only your own rank and points. viewer-card-standings.png: an 8-column table at 390px wraps team names to 3 lines ('Particularly / Perilous / Pumpkins'), and the useful catch-up line ('needs 2 golds to catch…') is at the very bottom.
problems.impact: The question every counselor and camper asks ('where are we, who's ahead, by how much?') takes a tap and a scroll, and the 'by how much' is the last thing on the card.

problems.problem: A game opens underneath the menu, and four navigation models coexist on one page.
problems.evidence: #game-view is placed AFTER the accordion in index.html (line 261). renderGameView folds every card and scrolls (app.js 5513–5531). editor-game-open.png shows the game below 6 collapsed rows. Probe: state.ui.day and ui.gameId persist across reloads, so reopening on Wednesday shows Monday's 'Shields' game at y=681, not scrolled to (v-reload-with-open-game-first.png), and the Competitions tab stays on Monday. The four models are: accordion (cards), append-below (game), full-screen takeover (chat, week builder), and bottom sheets (schedule, settings, members, alerts, history).
problems.impact: No consistent idea of 'where am I / how do I get back'. The accordion forgets what was open while the game view and day tab remember, so the app is inconsistent about what it remembers.

problems.problem: Nothing limits how tall the message stack above 'now' can get.
problems.evidence: Render order: notice board → what's-new → announcements (+ chat-announcement banners) → team → now. v-wed-1030-all-full.png: a posted notice is ~1,270px, then two announcements, so the team card starts ~1,540px down and the live board ~1,720px (two full screens). Notices have no expiry by design.
problems.impact: While a notice is posted (e.g. send-off cleanup left up), live scores, the schedule and your team are two screens down for everyone.

problems.problem: Rarely used editor controls take up prime space, while the frequent editor tasks are scattered.
problems.evidence: A 'Hide from viewers' switch is the first row inside every card, and it's permanently visible on the non-collapsible Chat card, about 70px of an editor's first screen (home-editor-light-firstscreen.png). There are four broadcast tools in four places: '📣 Post an announcement' (small grey link, top), Notice (Settings → Set up the week → Notice tab), the Chat Announcements channel, and Director alerts (Settings → Phone alerts). Set up the week, Who can sign in and Change history can only be reached through the '⚙️ Settings' text in the footer, below every card.
problems.impact: Directors scroll past a switch they use maybe once a week, and have to remember which of four tools reaches people and how.

problems.problem: Point-earning moments follow the schedule, but the cards for them don't.
problems.evidence: Cleanup points (after each meal, 3×/day), verse points (1×/day around Bible study) and quick points each get their own same-weight card with their own day picker. At 8:15 the banner shows the breakfast cleanup team inline (v-tue-0815-breakfast-first.png), but awarding takes Meal Cleanup ▸ → day chip → meal. At 9:15 Bible study the banner doesn't show the verse at all (v-tue-0915-bible-first.png).
problems.impact: The timing is already in DAY_SCHEDULE, yet each award is a hunt through a card. That's easy to forget and easy to do on the wrong day.

problems.problem: Counselors' own phone alerts are buried.
problems.evidence: 📲 Phone alerts (the feature that buzzes a closed phone, built for every member) can only be reached via footer '⚙️ Settings' → Phone alerts. The in-page '🔕 Notify me' button hides itself once it's on (updateNotifyButton, app.js 3261).
problems.impact: The feature that matters most to people who aren't watching the app is the hardest one to find.

problems.problem: On junior afternoons the full electives roster is the biggest thing on screen, and 'you' is optional.
problems.evidence: home-viewer-light-firstscreen.png: roughly 400px of every station and every counselor chip, plus the break list. Your own station is only highlighted after '🙋 Tell us who you are' inside the team card.
problems.impact: A counselor's question is 'where am I working, am I on break?' and a director's is 'is every station covered?'. The same block answers both, and neither quickly.

problems.problem: The live board was sized for a full screen but sits inside a home-page slot.
problems.evidence: .big-board.viewer has min-height:55vh and is centred vertically (styles.css 5650). With 3 tally rows the home board is 464px tall with ~130px of blank space above and below (v-wed-1030-live-full.png, e-desktop-wed-live-first.png).
problems.impact: It pushes Chat and the menu off-screen with empty space, and reads as broken.

problems.problem: Desktop, tablet and TV aren't planned for.
problems.evidence: home-editor-desktop.png: a single ~608px column at 1280 wide. current-standings.html is a 6th→1st reveal show, junior-only, and is linked only from stalling.html (Settings → Stalling with Patrick). There's no ambient live-score display for a TV during games, and tv-standings.png shows 'Press → to begin' overlapping 'Loading standings…'.
problems.impact: A scorer's tablet or a dining-hall TV gets a stretched phone page or a hidden reveal deck.

problems.problem: There's no global context, and senior gets junior's menu with empty sections.
problems.evidence: There's no header: no camp name, day or date at the top. 'Senior Camp' appears only in the footer, and junior shows no label at all. senior-home-viewer.png: the team card shrinks to name + rank, and the same five rows include the empty rota (TBA) and placeholder verses. Dual-camp staff can't tell which camp they're in at a glance.
problems.impact: Easy to act in the wrong camp. Empty sections carry the same weight as real ones.

keep: The 'Happening now' banner, driven by DAY_SCHEDULE in camp time, with Up next, the cleanup team shown inline at meals, and a tap through to the full schedule sheet. It's the seed of a schedule-driven home page
A live game taking over the top of the home page when one is running (homeBoardGame), with the schedule banner giving way. That instinct is right and should apply to every game format
The team card idea: rank, points, next matchup and next cleanup, with the team set from the person's account (adoptMemberTeam) rather than picked by hand
The notice board as one structured message with a 'your team' callout, which is better than six separate announcements
Day tabs that open on today and say when you're looking at another day
Chat as a full-screen page with an unread badge on the home card; that's the right model for game detail too
Editors and counselors share one layout (editors see what counselors see), plus the own-team scoring guard
Re-renders that change nothing leave the page untouched (setHtmlIfChanged and the in-place progress bar nudge). Keep that discipline in any new structure
lenses.direction:
How often each thing is needed and how much it matters, read from DAY_SCHEDULE and the roles:

- **Needed most and matters most:** what's on now and next (every block, about every 45 minutes); my team's place and how far it is from the next team; live and just-finished games during games blocks (junior 2 a day, senior 4); urgent announcements; chat.
- **Middle:** the full standings (after each games block and in the evening); the electives roster (3 times each junior afternoon); whose meal cleanup it is (3 times a day); the verse (once a day).
- **Rarely:** the Quick Points ledger; other days' games; the verse and cleanup lists for the whole week.
- **Editors, needed most (only during set windows):** scoring the current game; cleanup points after each meal; verse points once a day.
- **Editors, rarely:** hiding sections from viewers; Set up the week; Who can sign in; Change history.

Recommended layout, top to bottom:

1. **A thin header.** Camp and day ('Junior · Wed'), a chat button with the unread count, and a Settings or Director button. This replaces the Settings link in the footer.
2. **A messages strip that can't grow past about a third of the screen.** It shows the newest announcement plus '2 more'. A posted notice shows as its headline and your team's line ('Foxes → Linger a While'); tap to open the full card.
3. **A 'Now' area whose content depends on the kind of block that's on:**
   - Games block: this session's games as a list marked live, up next or done, with results. The live board sits inline, sized to its content. Placement games show up here too.
   - Meal: whose cleanup it is, and for editors the award buttons for this meal.
   - Bible study: today's verse, and for editors the 0–5 points per team.
   - Electives: your station and break first, with all stations one tap away.
   - Evening: today's results and how the standings moved.
   - Sunday: team assignments. Saturday: the notice.
4. **Short standings, always open.** One line per team (6 for junior, 4 for senior), your team marked, and a gap line ('22 pts — 8 behind Maples'). This takes over from the 160px team card as the place your team shows.
5. **'Later today':** the next 2–3 blocks.

Getting around:

- A bar of 4–5 fixed destinations: **Now · Games · Standings · Chat · More**.
  - Games: day tabs, then a game.
  - Standings: the full table, a medal breakdown, and a link to a TV mode.
  - More: verse, the cleanup list, the Quick Points ledger, the full schedule.
- A game, chat and the week builder each open as a full-screen page with Back. That makes one model instead of four.
- Drop the single-open accordion, closing everything on each load, and the 5-minute idle collapse.

For directors:

- One Director menu holding: one 'Tell everyone' place (banner, buzz phones, pin as a notice), Set up the week, Members, History, and a single 'What viewers see' list. That list replaces the six hide switches inside the cards.
- Phone alerts goes in the header or More, where counselors can find it.

Wider screens:

- At about 900px and up, use two columns: Now or the open game on the left, standings and messages on the right.
- Add a live board mode for a TV, separate from the end-of-week reveal show, for both camps.

Senior uses the same layout. Sections with no data stay hidden until someone fills them.

Everything is a collapsible: a single-open accordion, collapse on every load, and an idle auto-collapse, so motion stands in for structure
Emoji as the main icons: every heading, row, label and status (💬 📣 🧽 📖 🙈 ⚙️ 🛠️ 📋 ⏭️ 🔴 🥇), including table column headers
Pills and chips everywhere: the rank pill ('4TH PLACE'), format badges on every game card ('Bracket', 'Podium pick'), a LIVE pill, and a chip for every counselor name in the roster
Small uppercase spaced-out labels above things ('HAPPENING NOW', 'THEME VERSE · HARVEST OF THE HEART', 'TEAM TOTALS · 3/6 IN')
A coloured stripe down the left edge of the Now card and the verse card
A tinted hero card for the team with a big crest, worth more on screen than the standings it summarises
Explanatory grey paragraphs at the top of every card ('Each day's memory verse — pick a day to read it…', 'Only counts games saved in this app…')
A centred board with a fixed min-height that floats a few rows in empty space
'tap to open ›' and 'Full schedule ›' hints in place of affordances that are clear on their own

synth.plainAssessment: Partly. The top of the page has the right ideas: your team's card with the shield the campers drew, a "Happening now" panel that follows the camp schedule, and a live game that takes over the top of the screen while it's being played. Below that, the page is a fixed menu of six look-alike boxes (Chat, Competitions, Standings, Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse, Quick Points). The menu is the same at breakfast, at game time and at lights-out, and every box closes each time the app opens and closes again after 5 minutes. So an app called Camp Scoreboard shows no scoreboard on its first screen. Finding out who's winning takes a scroll and a tap every time, and your own team's points are the smallest grey text on its card. It is weakest at the busiest time of day. During a competition block, "Happening now" shrinks to one line ("Team competitions") that doesn't say which game, where or against whom, and podium-pick games (half of junior's, all of senior's) never appear on the home page. For directors it doesn't work at game time: recording a result takes about 9 taps plus a scroll, the game opens at the bottom of the page under the closed boxes, and the screen is full of "Hide from viewers" switches you use about once a week, while "Post an announcement" is the smallest text on the page. The progress-bar flicker you reported is fixed, but the same kind of glitch remains in two places. An open game and the red LIVE card are rebuilt every time anyone saves anything, so "How to play" snaps shut, the back button slides in again and the LIVE glow restarts. That can be fixed now, without waiting for a redesign. The look also relies on habits that make apps feel machine-made: identical rounded boxes, an emoji on nearly every line, sparkles on every tap, and in light mode the boxes are white on a white page, so they nearly disappear in sunlight. All four reviewers point the same way: a first screen that follows the camp day, a short standings list that is always visible right under it, everything else one tap away as its own screen, and director tools gathered in one place. Before anything is drawn, there are some choices only you can make, and I'll ask them one at a time.

topProblems.problem: The scoreboard isn't on the home screen, and it closes itself again.
topProblems.whyItMatters: "Who's winning, and by how much?" is the question counselors ask most. Right now every check costs a scroll and a tap, so they'll ask a director instead.
topProblems.evidence: Current Standings is the second of five closed rows in a single-open accordion (index.html:173, 192). applyCardDefaults (app.js:8139) closes every card on each load. collapseCardsForIdle closes them again after IDLE_COLLAPSE_MS = 5 min (app.js:7790). During Elective 1 the Standings header sits at y=954 on an 844px screen. The team card shows only your own rank, as an 11.5px pill, and points as 13.6px grey text. The motivating line ('needs 2 golds (8 pts) to catch Maples') sits under an 8-column table. At 390px that table cuts off the cleanup column, and at 360px it drops two columns and wraps team names to three lines.

topProblems.problem: The page doesn't change with the camp day, and competition time shows the least.
topProblems.whyItMatters: During games blocks, the peak hour, counselors moving their team around and directors running a game get nothing from the home page about what's on, where, or what just finished.
topProblems.evidence: The same Chat card and five rows, in the same order, appear at breakfast, Bible study, games, lights-out and Sunday arrival (scratchpad layout/ia/v-*-first.png). For games blocks nowBannerHtml returns a one-line .now-slim 'Team competitions' (app.js ~775). Tapping it opens the schedule sheet, where game names are plain spans that can't be tapped (app.js 934-935). The LIVE slot only fills for brackets and live-ranked tallies (liveHomeGames, app.js:5632). Podium-pick games (11 of junior's 22, and all 5 of senior's per day) never appear on home.

topProblems.problem: Scoring the game happening right now takes about 9 taps plus a scroll, and the game opens at the bottom of the page.
topProblems.whyItMatters: There are five games a day. The trip between games (back, scroll, find the next one) is the slowest step in a director's day.
topProblems.evidence: The path is: open Competitions, scroll past the morning's finished games (the first evening game is at y=967), tap the game, then open and choose Gold, Silver and Bronze (6 taps), then Save. #game-view sits after the whole accordion (index.html:261), so the game opens below five closed rows (shots/editor-game-open.png). Back sets the scroll to 0 and reopens Competitions (app.js ~5524-5560). There is no 'next game' link.

topProblems.problem: An open game and the red LIVE card are rebuilt from scratch on every synced change. This is the same kind of glitch as the progress bar.
topProblems.whyItMatters: It happens exactly when the app is busiest. A game leader reading the rules aloud loses them whenever another director saves anything, and the LIVE glow stutters every time anyone scores.
topProblems.evidence: renderGameView writes view.innerHTML = html unconditionally (app.js:5567). renderLiveHome writes wrap.innerHTML on every renderAll (app.js:5688), instead of using setHtmlIfChanged like the panels fixed in v183. Measured: one unrelated bonus point landing restarts the back pill's slide-in, recreates the medal pickers and closes an open 'How to play'. The LIVE pulse resets from about 2.4s to 0. This is not a layout decision and can be fixed now.

topProblems.problem: Everything has the same visual weight, and the actual answers are the smallest text on screen.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Outdoors, small grey text is the first thing sunlight washes out. Nothing tells the eye where to look first.
topProblems.evidence: The five row titles are 18.4px/800, the same size and weight as your team's name. 'Up next', elective times and points are 13-14px muted grey. styles.css uses about 30 font sizes and 6 weights with no scale. In light mode the page and the cards are both pure white with a ~1.2:1 border, so the boxes nearly vanish (compare home-viewer-light.png with home-viewer-dark.png). Quick Points usually opens to 'No bonus points yet.' yet gets the same billing as Standings.

topProblems.problem: Much of the first screen goes to content that doesn't change, and 'what's next' disappears exactly when it's needed.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Half of a counselor's first screen is used up before it says what's happening now, and your own station appears twice.
topProblems.evidence: At 1:30pm the team card (140px), My electives (151px) and a full-width grey 'Notify me' bar all come before Happening Now, which starts at y=393. During an elective, Happening Now spends about 406px listing all six stations' rosters. There is no 'Up next' line in elective blocks (next=null, app.js:796). My electives stays up all morning for electives three hours away.

topProblems.problem: There are four different ways to go deeper into the app, so 'back' means something different each time.
topProblems.whyItMatters: A one-handed user can't build a mental map, and a tap's result shows up in an unexpected place.
topProblems.evidence: The four ways are: boxes that open in place (a single-open accordion), bottom sheets (schedule, settings, members, alerts, history), full-screen takeovers (chat, week builder), and a game added below the page. The app also isn't consistent about what it remembers. The accordion forgets what was open, while the open game and the day tab survive a reload: reopening on Wednesday showed Monday's game at y=681.

topProblems.problem: Director-only controls sit inside the content, while the tools directors need fast are scattered.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Prime space goes to a setting changed about once a week, and the action directors need under pressure looks like a footnote.
topProblems.evidence: A 'Hide from viewers' row is the first thing inside every opened card, and it takes up about 68px of the always-visible Chat card (home-editor-light-firstscreen.png). 'Post an announcement' is a 0.78rem grey link (styles.css:4212). There are four broadcast tools in four places: the banner composer, the Chat Announcements channel (15-minute banner), the Notice board under Settings > Set up the week, and Director alerts under Settings > Phone alerts. Settings itself can only be reached from the footer. Cleanup, verse and quick points each have their own card and day picker, and every team's '0' button is solid blue, so zeros look like awards.

topProblems.problem: Nothing limits how tall the messages above 'now' can get, and the live board is padded with empty space.
topProblems.whyItMatters: The most time-sensitive things end up two screens down, or framed by blank space that looks like a loading failure.
topProblems.evidence: A posted notice (~1,270px) plus two announcements pushes the team card ~1,540px down and the live board ~1,720px down (v-wed-1030-all-full.png). Notices have no expiry by design. `.big-board.viewer { min-height: 55vh; justify-content: center }` (styles.css:5650) gives a 3-team board about 120-130px of blank space above and below, so the first score row lands at y≈710.

topProblems.problem: The look relies on generic habits, and the teams' own identity (shields, colors) does little of the work.
topProblems.whyItMatters: When everything is decorated, nothing stands out, and real moments like a medal or a team moving up can't be celebrated differently from tapping a tab.
topProblems.evidence: There are 59 emoji in the main column with standings open, including the table column headers. Pills are used for rank, for game format ('Bracket', 'Podium pick') and around every counselor's name. Every tap throws a sparkle burst and every save throws confetti (the 'Joy layer', commit fef2eef, app.js ~8005-8110). Shields appear only on your own team's card; lists use emoji instead. Four of six junior team colors sit within hue 9-33°, and pumpkin (2.95:1 on white) is used as score text. Peach means both 'your team' and '3rd place'. Senior shows a red circle emoji where the shield would go.

keep: The camper-drawn team shields, the most authentic asset in the app. Use them wherever a team appears, not only on your own card.

'Happening now' driven by the real schedule in camp time, with 'Up next' (including the meal's dish and the cleanup team) and a tap through to a full-week schedule that opens on NOW. This is the seed of a home page that follows the day.
A live game taking over the top of the home screen while it runs. The idea is right; extend it to every game format, size it to its content, and stop rebuilding it.
Personalisation from the account: the app opens on your team (adoptMemberTeam), says 'YOUR TEAM', and highlights your own name in the station roster.
The human details in standings: movement arrows (up 2 / down 3), counselor names under each team, and the 'needs 2 golds (8 pts) to catch Maples' sentence. Move that sentence up, not out.
The Notice board as one structured message with a 'your team' callout, and announcements at the top that can be dismissed and expire on their own.
Game rows that show the medal result inline, so finished games need no tap, and the compact podium form (Gold/Silver/Bronze plus one Save).
The full-screen takeover already used for Chat and the week builder. It's the right container for an open game.
Day tabs that open on today, and the labelled back pill ('Tuesday games') rather than a bare arrow.
Editor controls hidden centrally for viewers (html.view-only), and the own-team scoring guard kept in one function (canScoreRound).
The discipline that re-renders which change nothing don't touch the page (setHtmlIfChanged, nudging the progress bar). Any new layout must keep it.
Short team names (TEAM_ABBREV) and the dark theme's inset-tile structure, which shows what light mode was meant to look like.

directions.name: A. Follow the day: one page, nothing folds (recommended)
directions.description:
Top to bottom:
1. A thin header: camp and day ('Junior · Wed'), Chat with its unread count, and a Director button for editors.
2. A messages strip capped at about a third of the screen: the newest announcement plus 'N more'. A posted notice shows its headline and your team's line.
3. A 'Now' block whose content depends on the kind of block that's on:
   - games: this block's games marked live, up next or done, with results inline and a Score button for directors;
   - electives: your station or break, now and next, with everyone else's a tap away;
   - meals: whose cleanup it is, with award buttons for directors;
   - Bible study: today's verse and its points.
4. A short standings list that is always open, one line per team with your row marked, plus the gap sentence.
5. 'Later today'.
A game, Chat and the full standings each open as their own full screen with Back (and 'Next game' for directors). The accordion and the 5-minute auto-close go. The team card shrinks to a slim strip (shield, rank number, points, gap to the team ahead).
directions.pros: Answers the 5-second glance on one screen. Uses one way of going deeper. Grows from pieces that already work (Happening now, the live takeover, the Chat takeover). The same page serves counselors and directors, with role-aware buttons. Senior gets the same frame with no electives line.
directions.cons: The Now block has many variants (games, electives, meals, Bible study, evening, Sunday, Saturday), so it is the most design and test work. Naming the right games for a block depends on Project 2 attaching games to schedule blocks. Until then it falls back to today's Morning/Evening guess.

directions.name: B. Bottom tab bar
directions.description: Four or five fixed tabs: Now · Games · Standings · Chat (· More). Now holds the schedule-following block plus short standings. Games holds the day tabs and the games. Standings holds the full table and medal breakdown. More holds the verse, the cleanup list, the quick points ledger and the full schedule.
directions.pros: Every destination is always one thumb-tap away. It ends the everything-collapses habit, gives Chat a permanent home, and makes a good place for a director menu.
directions.cons: It adds a permanent bar to a 390px screen. It splits 'now' from 'scores' unless the Now tab duplicates standings. It's more to build and test in a no-build app, and a tab bar alone doesn't fix the game-time problem.

directions.name: C. Separate director home
directions.description: Editors open to 'Now playing / Games / Points', with the current block's games and Score buttons at the top. Counselors keep a reading-first page.
directions.pros: Fastest possible scoring. Director clutter (hide switches, award buttons) disappears entirely from the counselor view.
directions.cons: Two home pages to design, maintain and test. Directors stop seeing what counselors see. Many editors are also counselors on a team, so they'd keep switching.

directions.name: D. Minimum fix, no redesign
directions.description:
Keep today's page, but:
- Standings always open; no auto-close.
- A game opens as its own full screen.
- Hide switches move into Settings, and 'Post an announcement' becomes a real button.
- The live board is sized to its content.
- The game view and LIVE card get the same no-rebuild fix as v183.
directions.pros: Small, low-risk, can ship this week, and doesn't collide with Project 2. Removes the worst friction and the remaining glitches.
directions.cons: It's still a stack of look-alike boxes that doesn't change with the day. Game time stays thin for counselors, and podium games still never appear on home.

synth.disagreements:
Verdict: the counselor, designer and IA reviewers said 'partly'; the director reviewer said 'does not'. My call is 'partly'. The top-of-page ideas are sound and worth keeping, but for a director at game time the page really doesn't work, and that comes through clearly in the problems above.

How to get around: the designer recommended a 4-tab bar (Now · Standings · Games · Chat). The IA reviewer recommended 5 tabs with More. The counselor reviewer preferred one scrolling page with sheets, with a 3-tab bar as a fallback. The director reviewer proposed director-specific destinations (Now / Games / Points). My call: all four agree on what the first screen must hold (what's on now, plus a short always-visible standings list); they differ only on how you reach everything else. I lean toward one page with full-screen detail screens and a thin header (Chat, Director). A tab bar would separate 'now' from 'scores', which a glance needs together, and it's more to build in a no-build app. Tabs remain a fair choice, so it's question 3.

Detail screens: the counselor reviewer wanted a game to open as a bottom sheet. The director, designer and IA reviewers wanted a full screen, like Chat. My call: full screen for a game and Chat, because scoring needs the full height and a fixed Back / Next game bar. Bottom sheets only for short reference (schedule, verse, cleanup list).

Separate director home: the director reviewer wanted one; the IA reviewer explicitly listed 'editors and counselors share one layout' as something to keep. My call: one shared page with a role-aware Now block (directors see Score and award buttons on the same rows), plus one Director menu for everything else. Directors are often counselors too, and two homes double the upkeep. Question 4.

Team card: the counselor and designer reviewers wanted it shrunk to a strip; the IA reviewer wanted it folded into the standings list. My call: a slim strip (shield, rank number, points, gap to the team ahead), with your row also marked in standings. The 'next meal cleanup' line moves into the Now block at meal times.

Cleanup / verse / quick points: the director reviewer wanted one merged Points page; the IA reviewer wanted each shown at its moment in the schedule; the designer wanted one-line summaries. My call: both. Show each at its moment (after a meal: cleanup team plus award buttons; Bible study: verse plus points), and put everything else on one Points page. Question 8.

Standings always visible: three reviewers said yes. But the counselor and IA reviewers spotted the 'Hide from viewers' switch, and commit 6565113 says it was added 'for suspense before an awards reveal'. So 'always' can't be unconditional. My call: visible by default, with a reveal stretch directors switch on. Question 2.

Emoji: the designer wanted nearly all removed; the counselor reviewer wanted them kept for teams and stations. My call: the middle ground (stations, schedule blocks, and teams with no shield), but it's your taste. Question 10.

Motion: the designer wanted sparkles and confetti removed, and the director reviewer showed decorative motion replaying as glitches. The sparkle layer was added in an earlier Claude session (commit fef2eef, July 24) with no recorded request from you. My call: motion only for real changes (a medal, a team moving up). Question 11.

Team colors: raised by the designer, but Project 2 already includes a measured 12-color palette with your decisions 13 and 14, so I have not re-asked it.

Senior: the designer wanted a look of its own; the IA reviewer wanted the same layout with empty sections hidden. My call: the same frame with empty sections hidden, and the flag colors (plus Project 2's optional team photo) as identity. Question 13.

Big screens: the director reviewer ranked a laptop layout low; the IA reviewer wanted two columns plus a live TV mode. My call: phone first, and ask. Question 12.

interviewQuestions.question: When a counselor pulls out their phone for five seconds, what should the first screen answer?
interviewQuestions.why: Right now the first screen tries to answer everything equally (team card, electives list, a menu of closed boxes). Every other layout choice follows from this one.

options.label: Whatever is happening now (recommended)
options.description: The top changes through the day: today's games and live scores during competitions, where you're working during electives, whose cleanup it is at meals. A short standings list always sits right under it.

options.label: Who's winning
options.description: The standings and how far my team is behind are always at the top; the schedule comes after.

options.label: Where I need to be
options.description: My own now-and-next schedule first; scores are one tap away.

options.label: Keep today's order
options.description: Team card, then Happening now, then the list of sections, just tidied up.

interviewQuestions.question: Should counselors see the standings without tapping?
interviewQuestions.why: Today Standings closes every time the app opens and closes again after 5 minutes. There's also a switch to hide it from counselors, added for suspense before the awards reveal, so 'always visible' might not be what you want all week.

options.label: Always, near the top
options.description: A short one-line-per-team list on the home screen all week long.

options.label: Always, except a reveal stretch (recommended)
options.description: Visible all week; directors flip one switch to hide it before the end-of-week reveal (today's switch, kept).

options.label: Only my team's place and gap
options.description: Home shows 'Foxes 4th, 8 pts behind Maples'; the full table is one tap away.

options.label: Keep it one tap away
options.description: But once opened it stays open instead of closing itself.

interviewQuestions.question: How should people move around the app?
interviewQuestions.why: Today there are four different ways in and out: boxes that open in place, sheets that slide up, a full-screen Chat, and a game that appears at the bottom of the page. One-handed use needs one predictable pattern.

options.label: One page, nothing folds (recommended)
options.description: A fixed-order home with nothing collapsing; a game, Chat or the full standings open as their own full screen with a Back button, like Chat does now.

options.label: Tabs along the bottom
options.description: Now · Games · Standings · Chat, each a simple screen; verse, cleanup and quick points under a More menu.

options.label: Keep the folding boxes
options.description: But stop them closing themselves, and open a game in its own screen instead of at the bottom of the page.

interviewQuestions.question: Should directors get their own home screen, or the same one as counselors?
interviewQuestions.why: Today the counselor page is the base and director controls are scattered through it: six 'Hide from viewers' switches, a tiny announcement link, and Settings in the footer. That causes most of the director clutter.

options.label: Same page, director tools in one place (recommended)
options.description: Everyone sees the same screen; directors also get Score buttons on today's games and one Director menu at the top (announce, points, settings, what counselors can see).

options.label: A separate director home
options.description: Directors open to Now playing / Games / Points; counselors keep a reading page.

options.label: A switch for directors
options.description: Directors flip between 'Run the games' and 'See what counselors see'.

interviewQuestions.question: How is scoring shared among staff during a competition block?
interviewQuestions.why: If each game leader scores only their own game, the app should remember 'my game' and open straight to it. If one person scores everything, a 'Next game' button matters more.

options.label: One scorekeeper does everything
options.description: One person records every game in the block.

options.label: Each leader scores their own game
options.description: Whoever runs a game records it.

options.label: It varies
options.description: Depends on the day or the game.

interviewQuestions.question: During a games block, what should a director see first?
interviewQuestions.why: This decides whether scoring is one tap away or about nine. Today it's a one-line 'Team competitions' that opens the schedule, and podium-pick games never show on the home page.

options.label: This block's games with their status (recommended)
options.description: Each game as a row marked Not started / In progress / Done, with a Score button; counselors see the same rows with results.

options.label: Just the next game to score
options.description: One big 'Score Scatterball' button; the other games are a tap away.

options.label: The live board first
options.description: Whichever game is in progress, with the others listed underneath.

interviewQuestions.question: During an elective, what does a counselor need to see?
interviewQuestions.why: The full who's-at-which-station list is the biggest thing on the screen every junior afternoon (about 400px), and it repeats the 'My electives' card above it.

options.label: My station or my break first (recommended)
options.description: One line for where I am now and next; everyone else's stations a tap away. Directors see the full list open.

options.label: Everyone's stations, mine highlighted
options.description: The full list as now, with the duplicate 'My electives' card removed.

options.label: Everyone's stations, as now
options.description: No change.

interviewQuestions.question: Where should Meal Cleanup, Memory Verse and Quick Points live?
interviewQuestions.why: Each gets a box as big as Standings, with its own day picker, even though counselors read them about once a day and Quick Points is usually empty.

options.label: Show each at its moment (recommended)
options.description: After a meal the home screen shows whose cleanup it was (with award buttons for directors), and at Bible study it shows the verse. The rest lives on one Points page.

options.label: One Points page
options.description: All three together under one day picker, off the home screen.

options.label: Keep three boxes
options.description: Lower on the page, and they stop closing each other.

interviewQuestions.question: How many ways should directors have to tell everyone something?
interviewQuestions.why: There are four today, in four places, each lasting a different time: the announcement banner (1 hour to all day), the Chat Announcements channel (15-minute banner), the Notice board (until taken down) and Director phone alerts.

options.label: One 'Tell everyone' button (recommended)
options.description: One box with choices: show a banner (and for how long), buzz phones, or pin it as the big notice.

options.label: Use Chat for quick messages
options.description: Retire the banner composer, since Chat Announcements already shows a banner; keep the Notice board for big structured messages.

options.label: Keep all four
options.description: Just make 'Post an announcement' a real button.

interviewQuestions.question: How much emoji should stay?
interviewQuestions.why: There's an emoji on almost every heading, button, row and table column header (59 on one screen). It's playful, but it puts everything at the same level and is a common sign of a machine-made look.

options.label: Teams, stations and schedule only (recommended)
options.description: Keep emoji for elective stations, schedule blocks, and teams without a shield; use plain words on headings, buttons and table headers.

options.label: One simple icon set
options.description: Replace the interface emoji with consistent drawn icons; teams keep their shields and colors.

options.label: Keep them everywhere
options.description: The playful look is part of camp.

interviewQuestions.question: What celebration and motion do you want?
interviewQuestions.why: Every tap throws sparkles and every save throws confetti, so a medal or a team moving up looks the same as tapping a day tab. The constant motion also makes glitches easier to notice.

options.label: Celebrate only real moments (recommended)
options.description: Medals awarded, a team moving up, final results. Nothing on ordinary taps.

options.label: A small press effect only
options.description: Buttons respond to touch, with no sparkles or confetti anywhere.

options.label: Keep the sparkles and confetti
options.description: No change.

interviewQuestions.question: Will anyone use this on a laptop, tablet or TV during camp?
interviewQuestions.why: Wide screens get the phone column in the middle. Project 2 already plans a laptop layout for setup and a TV standings page for both camps; this question is about the rest of the day.

options.label: Phones only
options.description: Don't spend effort on big screens beyond what Project 2 already plans.

options.label: A laptop or tablet at the scoring table
options.description: Two columns: the game on the left, standings and messages on the right.

options.label: A TV with live scores during games
options.description: An always-on board for both camps, separate from the end-of-week reveal show.

options.label: TV only for the reveal (as now)
options.description: No change.

interviewQuestions.question: Should senior camp's home look different from junior's?
interviewQuestions.why: Senior has no electives, four games blocks a day, placeholder cleanup and verse data, and no shield art, so it gets junior's layout with a red circle emoji where the shield goes.

options.label: Same layout, empty sections hidden (recommended)
options.description: Flag colors, plus Project 2's optional team photo, take the shield's place; sections with no data stay hidden until someone fills them in.

options.label: A bolder sports-scoreboard look for teens
options.description: Bigger numbers, fewer decorations, its own style.

options.label: Exactly like junior
options.description: No change.

synth.project2Overlap:
Project 2 (spec at /home/user/Camp/docs/build-notes/setup-rebuild-spec.md) explicitly leaves the home redesign out of scope (§2.2). It does build the 'home-screen seam' (§9.4): stable accessors such as gamesForBlock(dow, bid), gamesForDay, weekDays, teamAccentVars and teamCrestSrc, plus a seam.test.js check that stops renderers reading the camps.js constants directly. The redesign should sit on top of that seam.

Where the two overlap:
(1) Games attached to schedule blocks (game.blockId) are exactly what the recommended 'Now' block needs to name the current block's games. Without it, the home page can only use today's Morning/Evening guess. Build order: Project 2's schedule and games stage first, then the redesign. Alternatively, build the redesign on the accessors with the guess as a fallback.
(2) Project 2 decision Q19 (date-aware Happening Now, naming games inside Happening Now) is deferred to the redesign. Questions 1 and 6 here answer it.
(3) The team-color problem the designer raised is already covered by Project 2's measured 12-color palette (Appendix A) and its decisions Q13/Q14. The senior-identity gap is partly covered by the optional team photo (Q17). Don't ask those twice.
(4) TV page for both camps (G12) and the laptop two-pane layout at ≥900px for setup: question 12 should reuse the same breakpoint and the TV work, adding a live-scores mode only if wanted.
(5) Project 2 adds home entry points that the new navigation must find a place for: 'Change today's plan' from the schedule sheet (the rainy-Wednesday moment), 'Add games' on an empty day, the setup checklist hub under Settings > Set up the week, plus a sync line, an undo pill and a 'who's here' tag. If the redesign moves Settings into a header Director menu (question 4), these move with it.
(6) Cleanup, verse and electives become editable data in Project 2, so 'show each at its moment' (question 8) reads them through the same accessors.

Recommended sequencing:
- Fix the remaining rebuild glitches now (game view, LIVE card). They don't depend on either project.
- Optionally ship the minimum fix (direction D: standings open, no auto-close, live board sized to content).
- Ask these layout questions before Project 2's 27 decisions, as PROGRESS.md already plans.
- Build Project 2's data stages, then draw and build the redesign on the seam.
